  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (point< a b)
      (or (< (fst a) (fst b))
          (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (< (snd a) (snd b)))))
    (define (ordered-pair pts)
      (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
        (if (point< b a) (list b a) (list a b))))
    (define colors (filter (lambda (color) (= (length (find-color g color)) 2)) (grid-colors g 0)))
    (define records
      (sort
        (map (lambda (color)
               (let ((pts (ordered-pair (find-color g color))))
                 (list color (first pts) (second pts))))
             colors)
        (lambda (x y) (point< (second x) (second y)))))
    (define (range-between a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (range a (- b 1) -1)))
    (define (clear-path? cells a b)
      (all?
        (lambda (p)
          (or (same-pos? p a) (same-pos? p b) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 0)))
        cells))
    (define (segment rec)
      (let* ((color (first rec))
             (a (second rec))
             (b (third rec))
             (cells
              (cond
                [(= (fst a) (fst b))
                 (map (lambda (c) (list (fst a) c color)) (range-between (snd a) (snd b)))]
                [(= (snd a) (snd b))
                 (map (lambda (r) (list r (snd a) color)) (range-between (fst a) (fst b)))]
                [else (list)])))
        (if (clear-path? cells a b) cells (list))))
    (paint-cells g (flatmap segment records))))

title: Translate a source shape from the red anchor to the green anchor
written_solution: Treat the red(2) cell as a source anchor and the green(3) cell as a target anchor. Copy the blue(1) shape by the translation vector from the red(2) anchor to the green(3) anchor, and draw the translated copy in cyan(8). Keep the original shape and anchors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((source (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))))
         (src (first (find-color g 2)))
         (dst (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first dst) (first src)))
         (dc (- (second dst) (second src))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr))
                   (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 8)
                   out)))
           g
           (obj-cells source))))

title: Rotate a shape around a pivot according to the control code
written_solution: The maroon(9) cell is the anchor. The cyan(8) shape is the source. A single control cell with value 1, 2, 3, or 4 chooses a transform (1 → identity, 2 → 90° clockwise, 3 → 180°, 4 → 90° counter-clockwise) applied around the anchor. Stamp the rotated copy in red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 8)) (objects g 0))))
         (pivot (first (find-color g 9)))
         (code (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4)))) (grid-cells g))))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let* ((dr (- (first p) (first pivot)))
                    (dc (- (second p) (second pivot)))
                    (nrnc (cond [(= code 1) (list (+ (first pivot) dr) (+ (second pivot) dc))]
                                [(= code 2) (list (+ (first pivot) dc) (- (second pivot) dr))]
                                [(= code 3) (list (- (first pivot) dr) (- (second pivot) dc))]
                                [else (list (- (first pivot) dc) (+ (second pivot) dr))]))
                    (nr (first nrnc))
                    (nc (second nrnc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 2)
                   out)))
           g
           (obj-cells shape))))

title: Output the sorted sizes of the red components
written_solution: Look only at red(2) connected components. Measure the size of each red(2) component, sort those sizes from smallest to largest, and output a single-row grid whose entries are exactly those sizes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (list (sort (map obj-size (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))) <)))

title: Fill chambers that contain exactly one seed
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Partition the grid into chambers of non-wall cells. If a chamber contains exactly one seed cell of blue(1), 2, 3, or 4, fill every background cell in that chamber with that seed's color. Chambers with zero or multiple seeds stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (out g))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 5))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define chamber (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([step 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! chamber (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) chamber))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ step 1))))
        (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4)))) chamber)))
          (when (= (length seeds) 1)
            (let ((color (at g (first (first seeds)) (second (first seeds)))))
              (for ([p (in-list chamber)])
                (when (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
                  (set! out (set-cell out (first p) (second p) color)))))))))
    out))

title: Draw rectangle borders from opposite-corner markers
written_solution: For each color that appears exactly twice as a diagonal pair of opposite corners, draw the full axis-aligned rectangle border connecting those two corners in that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border a b)
      (let* ((r1 (min (first a) (first b)))
             (r2 (max (first a) (first b)))
             (c1 (min (second a) (second b)))
             (c2 (max (second a) (second b))))
        (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                                (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                (positions-in-rect r1 c1 r2 c2))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))))])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (and (= (length pts) 2)
                 (not (= (first (first pts)) (first (second pts))))
                 (not (= (second (first pts)) (second (second pts)))))
            (paint-cells out (rect-border (first pts) (second pts)) color)
            out)))))

title: Recolor the component with the unique vertical-symmetry status
written_solution: All blue(1) components are compared by vertical reflection after normalization. Exactly one component disagrees with the others in whether it is vertically symmetric. Recolor that odd-one-out component to red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (reflect-v cells)
      (let* ((s (norm cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second s)))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) s))))
    (define comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))
    (define flags (map (lambda (obj) (equal? (norm (obj-cells obj)) (reflect-v (obj-cells obj)))) comps))
    (define true-count (count-where (lambda (v) v) flags))
    (define false-count (- (length flags) true-count))
    (if (and (> true-count 0) (> false-count 0) (or (= true-count 1) (= false-count 1)))
        (let* ((target-flag (= true-count 1))
               (pairs (map list comps flags))
               (target (first (first (filter (lambda (p) (equal? (second p) target-flag)) pairs)))))
          (paint-cells g (obj-cells target) 2))
        g)))

title: Fill each blank cell with the nearer seed color
written_solution: There is one red(2) seed (2) and one green(3) seed (3). For every background cell, compare Manhattan distance to the two seeds. Fill the cell with the nearer seed's color; if the distances tie, leave it background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((s2 (first (find-color g 2)))
         (s3 (first (find-color g 3))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let ((d2 (+ (abs (- r (first s2))) (abs (- c (second s2)))))
                  (d3 (+ (abs (- r (first s3))) (abs (- c (second s3))))))
              (cond [(< d2 d3) 2] [(< d3 d2) 3] [else 0])))))))

title: Mark the cells that lie on every shortest path through a maze
written_solution: Walls are gray(5); start is red(2); goal is green(3). Mark every cell that lies on at least one shortest path from start to goal through non-wall cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (record-of p records)
      (find-first (lambda (rec) (same-pos? p (first rec))) records))
    (define (set-record-count p new-count records)
      (map
        (lambda (rec)
          (if (same-pos? p (first rec))
              (list (first rec) (second rec) new-count)
              rec))
        records))
    (define (neighbors p)
      (filter
        (lambda (n)
          (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
            (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5)))))
        (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (fst p) (fst d)) (+ (snd p) (snd d)))) cardinal-deltas)))
    (define (dist-count start)
      (let loop ((queue (list start)) (records (list (list start 0 1))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            records
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (cur-rec (record-of cur records))
                   (cur-dist (second cur-rec))
                   (cur-count (third cur-rec)))
              (let update ((ns (neighbors cur)) (q restq) (recs records))
                (if (empty? ns)
                    (loop q recs)
                    (let* ((n (first ns))
                           (nd (+ cur-dist 1))
                           (hit (record-of n recs)))
                      (cond
                        [(not hit)
                         (update (cdr ns) (append q (list n)) (append recs (list (list n nd cur-count))))]
                        [(= (second hit) nd)
                         (update (cdr ns) q (set-record-count n (+ (third hit) cur-count) recs))]
                        [else (update (cdr ns) q recs)]))))))))
    (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
           (goal (first (find-color g 3)))
           (from-start (dist-count start))
           (from-goal (dist-count goal))
           (goal-rec (record-of goal from-start)))
      (if (not goal-rec)
          g
          (let ((D (second goal-rec))
                (total (third goal-rec)))
            (grid-from-fn h w
              (lambda (r c)
                (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
                       (p (list r c))
                       (rs (record-of p from-start))
                       (rg (record-of p from-goal)))
                  (if (and (= v 0)
                           rs rg (= (+ (second rs) (second rg)) D)
                           (= (* (third rs) (third rg)) total))
                      8
                      v)))))))))

title: Fill the band between nested frames selected by the control number
written_solution: The yellow(4) frames are nested. The control cell has value 1 or 2. If it is k, fill the band between the k-th frame from the outside and the next inner frame with cyan(8), leaving the frames themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame-area obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)
           (> (obj-h obj) 2)
           (> (obj-w obj) 2)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define frames (sort (filter frame? (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (> (frame-area a) (frame-area b)))))
    (define control (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 1 2))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define outer (nth frames (- control 1)))
    (define inner (nth frames control))
    (define (strictly-inside? obj r c)
      (and (> r (obj-r1 obj)) (< r (obj-r2 obj)) (> c (obj-c1 obj)) (< c (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (inside-bbox? obj r c)
      (and (>= r (obj-r1 obj)) (<= r (obj-r2 obj)) (>= c (obj-c1 obj)) (<= c (obj-c2 obj))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (cell-at g r c) 0)
                 (strictly-inside? outer r c)
                 (not (inside-bbox? inner r c)))
            8
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Stamp the intersection of two transformed copies of a source shape
written_solution: The source shape is cyan(8). Two control cells with values blue(1)..yellow(4) specify two transforms: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → flip vertical, yellow(4) → flip horizontal. Apply both transforms to the normalized source shape and stamp only the cells that the two transformed copies share, using red(2), at the maroon(9) anchor cell as the top-left origin.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define source (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 8)) (objects g 0))))
    (define shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells source)))
    (define codes (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
    (define (flip-cells-ud cells)
      (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- (fst p)) (snd p))) cells)))
    (define (transform code cells)
      (cond
        [(= code 1) (normalize-cells cells)]
        [(= code 2) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw cells))]
        [(= code 3) (normalize-cells (flip-cells-lr cells))]
        [else (flip-cells-ud cells)]))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define a (transform (first codes) shape))
    (define b (transform (second codes) shape))
    (define overlap (filter (lambda (p) (pos-in? p b)) a))
    (define stamp-cells
      (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (fst anchor) (fst p)) (+ (snd anchor) (snd p)))) overlap))
    (paint-cells g stamp-cells 2)))

title: Mark wall-constrained equidistant cells between two seeds
written_solution: Walls are gray(5); seeds are 2 and 3. Using shortest-path distance through non-wall cells, mark every background cell whose distance to the two seeds is equal with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (hash-has-key? da (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? db (cons r c))
                 (= (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c))))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Translate a shape by the sum of two independent vectors
written_solution: The source shape is blue(1). The vector from red(2) to green(3) is one motion, and the vector from yellow(4) to magenta(6) is another. Add those two vectors, then stamp a translated copy of the blue(1) shape in cyan(8) using the summed motion. Keep the original shape and markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))))
         (p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
         (p3 (first (find-color g 3)))
         (p4 (first (find-color g 4)))
         (p6 (first (find-color g 6)))
         (dr (+ (- (first p3) (first p2)) (- (first p6) (first p4))))
         (dc (+ (- (second p3) (second p2)) (- (second p6) (second p4)))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr))
                   (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 8)
                   out)))
           g
           (obj-cells shape))))

title: Recolor every instance of the shape class that appears an odd number of times
written_solution: Normalize all blue(1) connected components by translation only. One normalized shape class appears an odd number of times while the others appear an even number of times. Recolor every component in that odd-frequency class to red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list comps)])
      (let ((freq (count-where (lambda (other) (equal? (norm (obj-cells obj)) (norm (obj-cells other)))) comps)))
        (if (= (modulo freq 2) 1)
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 2)
            out)))))

title: Fill each chamber with the majority gate color on its boundary
written_solution: Each black(0) chamber is enclosed by nonzero cells. Look at the boundary cells in colors blue(1)..yellow(4) touching that chamber: if exactly one such color appears, fill the chamber with that color; otherwise leave it black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (out g))
    (define (mode-unique vals)
      (let* ((colors (remove-duplicates vals))
             (ranked (sort (map (lambda (color) (list color (count-where (lambda (v) (= v color)) vals))) colors)
                           (lambda (a b) (> (second a) (second b))))))
        (cond [(empty? ranked) #f]
              [(= (length ranked) 1) (first (first ranked))]
              [(> (second (first ranked)) (second (second ranked))) (first (first ranked))]
              [else #f])))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c))) (= (at g r c) 0))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define chamber (list))
        (define boundary (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([step 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! chamber (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) chamber))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                    (cond [(and (= (at g nr nc) 0) (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                           (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                           (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))]
                          [(and (>= (at g nr nc) 1) (<= (at g nr nc) 4))
                           (set! boundary (cons (at g nr nc) boundary))])))))
            (bfs (+ step 1))))
        (let ((color (mode-unique boundary)))
          (when color
            (set! out (paint-cells out chamber color))))))
    out))

title: Recolor the endpoints of green paths
written_solution: Every green(3) cell with exactly one green(3) cardinal neighbor becomes red(2). green(3) cells with two or more green(3) neighbors stay green(3), and background stays unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 3)
               (= (count-where (lambda (d)
                                 (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                                   (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g nr nc) 3))))
                               cardinal-deltas)
                  1))
          2
          (at g r c)))))

title: Fill the centers of red Xs
written_solution: Whenever a black(0) cell has red(2) diagonal neighbors in all four diagonal directions, fill that center cell with blue(1). Nothing else changes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (all? (lambda (d) (= (safe-at g (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)) 0) 2)) diagonal-deltas))
          1
          (at g r c)))))

title: Recolor orange components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Find every orange(7) component. If a component touches exactly one outer border of the grid, recolor the whole component to cyan(8). Components touching zero borders or two or more borders stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((h (rows g)) (w (cols g)))
    (define (side-count obj)
      (+ (if (= (obj-r1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-r2 obj) (- h 1)) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c2 obj) (- w 1)) 1 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 7) (= (side-count o) 1))) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8))))

title: Shift red singletons one cell to the right
written_solution: Every isolated red(2) singleton moves one cell to the right. Its old cell becomes black(0). In these examples the destination is always empty.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (isolated-red? p)
      (and (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)
           (= (count-where (lambda (d) (= (safe-at g (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d)) 0) 2)) cardinal-deltas) 0)))
    (define base
      (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
        (lambda (r c)
          (if (and (= (at g r c) 2) (isolated-red? (list r c)))
              0
              (at g r c)))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((r (first p)) (c (+ (second p) 1)))
               (if (and (< c (cols g)) (= (at g r c) 0))
                   (set-cell out r c 2)
                   out)))
           base
           (filter isolated-red? (find-color g 2)))))

title: Recolor blue T-junction centers
written_solution: A blue(1) cell becomes yellow(4) exactly when it has blue(1) neighbors in three of the four cardinal directions. Plus-shape centers with four neighbors do not change.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 1)
               (= (count-where (lambda (d) (= (safe-at g (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)) 0) 1)) cardinal-deltas) 3))
          4
          (at g r c)))))

title: Recolor exact magenta dominoes
written_solution: Find every 4-connected magenta(6) component of size exactly 2. Recolor those size-2 dominoes to orange(7). Larger or smaller magenta(6) components stay magenta(6).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 6) (= (obj-size o) 2))) (objects g 0))])
    (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 7)))

title: Complete 2x2 green almost-squares
written_solution: Whenever a 2x2 window contains exactly three green(3) cells and one black(0) cell, fill the missing corner with green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let loop ((out g))
    (let* ((hits (filter (lambda (p)
                           (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
                                  (cells (list (list r c) (list (+ r 1) c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
                                  (vals (map (lambda (q) (at out (first q) (second q))) cells)))
                             (and (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 3)) vals) 3)
                                  (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1))))
                         (positions-in-rect 0 0 (- (rows g) 2) (- (cols g) 2)))))
      (if (empty? hits)
          out
          (loop
            (foldl (lambda (p acc)
                     (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
                            (cells (list (list r c) (list (+ r 1) c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
                            (zeros (filter (lambda (q) (= (at acc (first q) (second q)) 0)) cells)))
                       (if (= (length zeros) 1)
                           (set-cell acc (first (first zeros)) (second (first zeros)) 3)
                           acc)))
                   out hits))))))

title: Solidify each object's bounding box
written_solution: For each connected nonzero object, compute its tight bbox and fill that entire rectangle with the object's own color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
    (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (obj-color obj))))

title: XOR two shapes after top-left alignment
written_solution: Take the blue(1) object and the red(2) object. Crop each to its tight bbox and align both shapes to the top-left corner. Output cyan(8) in every cell occupied by exactly one of the two aligned shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (define s1 (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
    (define s2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
    (define b1 (bbox-of-cells s1))
    (define b2 (bbox-of-cells s2))
    (define out-h (max (if b1 (+ 1 (third b1)) 0) (if b2 (+ 1 (third b2)) 0)))
    (define out-w (max (if b1 (+ 1 (fourth b1)) 0) (if b2 (+ 1 (fourth b2)) 0)))
    (define res (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p s2))) s1)
                        (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p s1))) s2)))
    (if (empty? res)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (paint-cells (empty-grid out-h out-w 0) res 8))))

title: Recolor components by size parity
written_solution: Each connected nonzero component is recolored by its size: odd-sized components become green(3) and even-sized components become cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
    (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (if (= (modulo (obj-size obj) 2) 1) 3 8))))

title: Rotate the object 90° clockwise around the pivot
written_solution: Treat the red(2) cell as a anchor. Rotate every other nonzero cell 90° clockwise around that anchor and output only the rotated object on an otherwise black(0) grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((pivot (first (find-color g 2)))
         (pr (first pivot))
         (pc (second pivot)))
    (foldl (lambda (cell out)
             (let* ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell))
                    (dr (- r pr)) (dc (- c pc))
                    (nr (+ pr dc)) (nc (- pc dr)))
               (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 2)) (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)))
                   (set-cell out nr nc v)
                   out)))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           (grid-cells g))))

title: Fill the bounding rectangle of each color's markers
written_solution: For each non-background color separately, take all cells of that color and fill the tight bounding rectangle spanning them, using that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (non-bg-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (empty? cells)
          out
          (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
            (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) color))))))

title: Extract the object nearest the control marker
written_solution: Ignore the control marker 9. Among the remaining objects, choose the one whose nearest cell is closest in Manhattan distance to the marker. Output only that chosen object, cropped to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((marker (first (find-color g 9)))
         (objs (objects (set-cell g (first marker) (second marker) 0) 0))
         (best (first (sort objs
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (let ((da (apply min (map (lambda (p) (pos-manhattan p marker)) (obj-cells a))))
                                    (db (apply min (map (lambda (p) (pos-manhattan p marker)) (obj-cells b)))))
                                (cond [(not (= da db)) (< da db)]
                                      [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                                      [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))))
         (cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells best)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) cells (obj-color best))))

title: Complete each object to 180° symmetry in its own box
written_solution: For each connected object, look only inside its own bbox. Add the cells needed so that the object becomes 180-degree rotationally symmetric within that box.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
    (foldl (lambda (p acc)
             (let ((rr (- (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) (first p)))
                   (cc (- (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (second p))))
               (set-cell acc rr cc (obj-color obj))))
           out (obj-cells obj))))

title: Control cell chooses OR, XOR, or AND
written_solution: Crop the blue(1) object and red(2) object to their own bounding boxes and align them to the top-left. The control cell selects the merge rule: 3 → OR, 4 → XOR, and 5 → AND. Paint the resulting aligned shape in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (define a (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
    (define b (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
    (define ba (bbox-of-cells a))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells b))
    (define out-h (max (if ba (+ 1 (third ba)) 0) (if bb (+ 1 (third bb)) 0)))
    (define out-w (max (if ba (+ 1 (fourth ba)) 0) (if bb (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0)))
    (define ctrl (at g 0 0))
    (define res
      (cond [(= ctrl 3) (remove-duplicates (append a b))]
            [(= ctrl 4) (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p b))) a)
                                (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p a))) b))]
            [(= ctrl 5) (filter (lambda (p) (has? p b)) a)]
            [else (list)]))
    (if (empty? res)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (paint-cells (empty-grid out-h out-w 0) res 8))))

title: Control cell chooses the template rotation
written_solution: Take the blue(1) template, crop it to its bbox, and rotate it according to the control cell: 2 → 0°, 3 → 90° clockwise, 4 → 180°, and 5 → 270° clockwise. Output the rotated template in cyan(8), cropped to fit.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ()
    ;; Sort normalized cells deterministically so repeated rotations are stable.
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))

    ;; The unique marker color 2..5 encodes zero through three clockwise turns.
    (define ctrl
      (find-first
        (lambda (value)
          (or (= value 2) (= value 3) (= value 4) (= value 5)))
        (apply append g)))
    (define turns (- ctrl 2))
    (define cells
      (let loop ((remaining turns) (shape (norm (find-color g 1))))
        (if (zero? remaining)
            shape
            (loop (- remaining 1) (rot shape)))))

    ;; Return only the transformed blue template, cropped and recolored cyan.
    (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
      (paint-cells
        (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0)
        cells
        8))))

title: Fill each frame by the largest enclosed object
written_solution: Each gray(5) rectangular frame contains several small colored objects. For each frame, find the largest enclosed object by cell count and fill the entire interior of that frame with the winner's color, keeping the gray(5) border.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((out0 (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 5) 5 0)))))
    (for/fold ([out out0]) ([frame (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0))])
      (let* ((inside (bbox-interior-cells frame))
             (inners (filter (lambda (o)
                               (and (not (= (obj-color o) 5))
                                    (all? (lambda (p)
                                            (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 frame)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 frame))
                                                 (> (second p) (obj-c1 frame)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 frame))))
                                          (obj-cells o))))
                             (objects g 0))))
        (if (empty? inners)
            out
            (let ((best (first (sort inners (lambda (a b)
                                             (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                                   [else (> (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))))
              (paint-cells out inside (obj-color best))))))))

title: Voronoi-fill the chamber from its seeds
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. Nonzero non-wall cells are colored seeds. Fill every reachable empty cell with the color of the nearest seed, measuring distance through open cells; when distances tie, the smaller color wins.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define seeds (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))) (grid-positions g)))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue)) (r (first p)) (c (second p)) (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define seed-dists (map (lambda (p) (list p (at g (first p) (second p)) (dist-from p))) seeds))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (= (at g r c) 5)
            5
            (let* ((p (list r c))
                   (cands (filter (lambda (sd) (hash-has-key? (third sd) p)) seed-dists)))
              (if (empty? cands)
                  0
                  (second (first (sort cands
                                       (lambda (a b)
                                         (let ((da (hash-ref (third a) p)) (db (hash-ref (third b) p)))
                                           (if (= da db) (< (second a) (second b)) (< da db))))))))))))))

title: Extract the nth-largest object
written_solution: The top-left control cell gives a rank n. Ignore that control cell, sort the remaining objects by size from largest to smallest, take the nth object, and output it alone cropped to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((n (at g 0 0))
         (g2 (set-cell g 0 0 0))
         (objs (sort (objects g2 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                             [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
         (target (list-ref objs (- n 1)))
         (cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells target)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) cells (obj-color target))))

title: Complete 90° rotational symmetry around the pivot
written_solution: The red(2) cell is the rotation center. Every blue(1) cell must be completed into its full 4-way orbit under 90-degree rotations around that anchor. Keep the anchor and paint all rotated copies blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((pivot (first (find-color g 2)))
         (pr (first pivot))
         (pc (second pivot)))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let* ((dr0 (- (first p) pr)) (dc0 (- (second p) pc))
                    (rots (list (list dr0 dc0) (list dc0 (- dr0)) (list (- dr0) (- dc0)) (list (- dc0) dr0))))
               (foldl (lambda (d acc)
                        (let ((nr (+ pr (first d))) (nc (+ pc (second d))))
                          (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                              (set-cell acc nr nc 1)
                              acc)))
                      out rots)))
           g (find-color g 1))))

title: Fill each compartment with its majority marker color
written_solution: Gray(5) walls partition the grid into compartments. Inside each compartment, count the colored markers; then fill the entire compartment with the majority marker color, leaving the walls intact.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (not (= v 5)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (for/fold ([out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 5) 5 0)))]) ([comp comps])
      (let* ((counts (map (lambda (color) (list color (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) color)) comp))) (list 2 3 4)))
             (best (first (sort counts (lambda (a b) (if (= (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)) (> (second a) (second b))))))))
        (if (= (second best) 0)
            out
            (paint-cells out comp (first best)))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (f14-border-cells r0 c0 r1 c1) (for*/list ((r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))) (c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))) #:when (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))) (list r c))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((obj (in-list (objects g 0)))) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (paint-cells out (f14-border-cells (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) (obj-color obj))))))

title: Fill Diagonal Spans Between Matching Endpoints

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-colors-reading grid) (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (map (lambda (p) (at grid (first p) (second p))) (grid-positions grid))))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((color (in-list (e8b-colors-reading g)))) (let ((cells (find-color g color))) (if (= (length cells) 2) (let* ((a (first cells)) (b (second cells)) (dr (- (first b) (first a))) (dc (- (second b) (second a)))) (if (and (= (abs dr) (abs dc)) (not (= dr 0))) (let ((sr (if (> dr 0) 1 -1)) (sc (if (> dc 0) 1 -1))) (paint-cells out (map (lambda (k) (list (+ (first a) (* sr k)) (+ (second a) (* sc k)))) (range (+ (abs dr) 1))) color)) out)) out)))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g r c))) (if (= v 0) out (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((dr (in-list (list -1 0 1))) (dc (in-list (list -1 0 1)))) (let ((nr (+ r dr)) (nc (+ c dc))) (if (and (not (and (= dr 0) (= dc 0))) (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))) (set-cell acc nr nc v) acc))))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-list< a b) (cond ((empty? a) #f) ((< (first a) (first b)) #t) ((> (first a) (first b)) #f) (else (e8b-list< (rest a) (rest b))))) (define (s17b-object-crop grid obj) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))) (let ((obj (first (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b))) (e8b-list< (list (- (obj-size a)) (first ba) (second ba)) (list (- (obj-size b)) (first bb) (second bb))))))))) (s17b-object-crop g obj))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (s17b-object-crop grid obj) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))) (let* ((key (at g 0 0)) (work (set-cell g 0 0 0)) (obj (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) key)) (objects work 0))))) (upscale (s17b-object-crop work obj) 2))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define dirs4 (list (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((seed (in-list (find-color g 2)))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((d (in-list dirs4))) (let loop ((r (+ (first seed) (first d))) (c (+ (second seed) (second d))) (cur acc)) (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g r c) 0)) (loop (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)) (set-cell cur r c 8)) cur))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-paste grid pat top left) (for*/fold ((out grid)) ((r (in-range (rows pat))) (c (in-range (cols pat)))) (let ((v (at pat r c)) (rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c))) (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr cc (rows out) (cols out))) (set-cell out rr cc v) out)))) (define (f14b-hstack-center grids (gap 1)) (if (empty? grids) (list (list)) (let* ((h (apply max (map rows grids))) (w (+ (apply + (map cols grids)) (* gap (- (length grids) 1))))) (let loop ((xs grids) (left 0) (out (empty-grid h w 0))) (if (empty? xs) out (let* ((piece (first xs)) (top (quotient (- h (rows piece)) 2))) (loop (rest xs) (+ left (cols piece) gap) (e8b-paste out piece top left)))))))) (define (s17b-object-crop grid obj) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))) (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (s17b-object-crop g obj))) (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (< (first a) (first b)))))) (f14b-hstack-center (map second items) 1))))

program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((divider (first (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (v) (= v 5)) (row g r))) (range (rows g))))) (top (subgrid g 0 0 (- divider 1) (- (cols g) 1))) (bottom (subgrid g (+ divider 1) 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))) (grid-from-fn (rows top) (cols top) (lambda (r c) (if (and (not (= (at top r c) 0)) (not (= (at bottom r c) 0))) 8 0))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (nonzero-cells grid) (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))) (grid-positions grid))) (define (crop-nonzero grid) (let ((cells (nonzero-cells grid))) (if (empty? cells) (list (list 0)) (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))))) (define (t13c-transform grid code) (cond ((= code 1) grid) ((= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)) ((= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)) ((= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)) ((= code 5) (flip-lr grid)) (else grid))) (let* ((h (rows g)) (w (cols g)) (marker-info (first (filter (lambda (entry) (= (at g (first entry) (second entry)) 9)) (list (list 0 0 1) (list 0 (- w 1) 2) (list (- h 1) (- w 1) 3) (list (- h 1) 0 4))))) (work (set-cell g (first marker-info) (second marker-info) 0)) (obj (crop-nonzero work))) (t13c-transform obj (third marker-info)))))

title: Straight Terminal Links
written_solution: For each color, find its two endpoints. If they share a row, fill all cells between them horizontally; if they share a column, fill vertically.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
              (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
                     (paint-cells out (map (lambda (c) (list (first a) c))
                                           (range (min (second a) (second b)) (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))) color)]
                    [(= (second a) (second b))
                     (paint-cells out (map (lambda (r) (list r (second a)))
                                           (range (min (first a) (first b)) (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))) color)]
                    [else out]))
            out)))))

title: Complete the Rectangle
written_solution: For each color, take the bbox of its given corner cells and draw the full border of that axis-aligned rectangle.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let* ((pts (find-color g color))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells pts)))
        (paint-cells out
                     (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                                             (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                             (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
                     color)))))

title: Left-Pack Every Row
written_solution: For every row, remove the zeros, keep the remaining colors in their original order, and place them flush to the left with zeros filling the rest.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g r))))
        (if (< c (length vals)) (list-ref vals c) 0)))))

title: Mirror Across the Guide Wall
written_solution: The full column of maroon(9)s is a mirror axis. Reflect every nonzero non-maroon(9) cell across that column. Keep the original object and the maroon(9) axis.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((gc (first (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range gc)])
      (let ((v (at g r c)) (mc (- (* 2 gc) c)))
        (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9)) (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g)))
            (set-cell out r mc v)
            out)))))

title: Count to a Bar
written_solution: Count all nonzero marker cells and output a single row whose length equals that count, filled with the marker color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (map third (grid-cells g)))))
    (list (make-list (length vals) (first vals)))))

title: Fill the Enclosed Hole
written_solution: Find zero regions that do not touch the outside border. If such a region is enclosed by a single surrounding color, fill the whole interior with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash)) (out g))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (when (and (= (at g r c) 0) (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c))))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define region (list))
        (define border #f)
        (define neigh (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! region (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) region))
              (when (or (= (car cur) 0) (= (cdr cur) 0) (= (car cur) (- (rows g) 1)) (= (cdr cur) (- (cols g) 1)))
                (set! border #t))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                    (cond [(and (= (at g nr nc) 0) (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                           (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                           (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))]
                          [(not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                           (set! neigh (cons (at g nr nc) neigh))])))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (let ((colors (remove-duplicates neigh)))
          (when (and (not border) (= (length colors) 1))
            (set! out (paint-cells out region (first colors)))))))
    out))

title: Stamp the Corner Motif
written_solution: Take the top-left 2×2 block as the source motif. Remove the 9 markers and paste the motif with each marker acting as the motif's top-left anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((motif (subgrid g 0 0 1 1))
         (markers (find-color g 9))
         (cleared (paint-cells g markers 0)))
    (for/fold ([out cleared]) ([p (in-list markers)])
      (for*/fold ([cur out]) ([dr (in-range 2)] [dc (in-range 2)])
        (let ((v (at motif dr dc)) (r (+ (first p) dr)) (c (+ (second p) dc)))
          (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)))
              (set-cell cur r c v)
              cur))))))

title: Commanded L-Links
written_solution: The top-left command chooses row-first or column-first routing. Connect each same-colored terminal pair with an L-shaped Manhattan path using that bend policy.

(let* ((cmd (at g 0 0)) (colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (remove-duplicates (map third (grid-cells g)))))) (define endpoint-colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v cmd))) colors)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((color (in-list endpoint-colors))) (let ((pts (find-color g color))) (if (= (length pts) 2) (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))) (paint-cells (paint-cells out (if (= cmd 1) (map (lambda (c) (list (first a) c)) (range (min (second a) (second b)) (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))) (map (lambda (r) (list r (second a))) (range (min (first a) (first b)) (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1)))) color) (if (= cmd 1) (map (lambda (r) (list r (second b))) (range (min (first a) (first b)) (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))) (map (lambda (c) (list (first b) c)) (range (min (second a) (second b)) (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1)))) color)) out)))))

title: Guide-Color Crop
written_solution: Read the nonzero guide color from the top row, find the object of that color in the main grid, and output its tight bounding-box crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((guide (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g))))
         (cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (> r 0) (= v guide)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Checkerboard Frame Fill
written_solution: For each rectangular border, keep the frame itself and fill its interior with a checkerboard of frame color and zero, starting with the frame color at the interior's top-left cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)))
    (for/fold ([cur out]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (for*/fold ([acc cur]) ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]
                              [c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))])
        (cond [(or (= r (obj-r1 obj)) (= r (obj-r2 obj)) (= c (obj-c1 obj)) (= c (obj-c2 obj)))
               (set-cell acc r c (obj-color obj))]
              [else
               (set-cell acc r c (if (= (modulo (+ (- r (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1)) (- c (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1))) 2) 0)
                                     (obj-color obj)
                                     0))])))))

title: Area Equality Matrix
written_solution: Sort the objects by row-major order. Output a 3×3 matrix with cyan(8) when two objects have the same number of cells and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                           (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                           (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
         (areas (map obj-size objs))
         (n (length objs)))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (= (list-ref areas r) (list-ref areas c)) 8 0)))))

title: Rank-by-Area Extract
written_solution: Count the 9 markers in the top row to get rank k. Sort the objects below by area from smallest to largest and output the tight crop of the kth object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((k (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 9)) (first g)))
         (objs (sort (filter (lambda (o)
                               (and (not (= (obj-color o) 9))
                                    (all? (lambda (p) (> (first p) 0)) (obj-cells o))))
                             (objects g 0))
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-h a) (obj-h b))) (< (obj-h a) (obj-h b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-w a) (obj-w b))) (< (obj-w a) (obj-w b))]
                             [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
         (obj (list-ref objs (- k 1))))
    (grid-from-fn (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) r)) (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) c)))
          (if (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj)) (at g rr cc) 0))))))

title: Normalized Shape XOR
written_solution: Crop the two objects to their own bounding boxes, align both crops to the top-left of a shared canvas, and output 8 exactly where one occupancy mask is on and the other is off.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                           (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                           (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
         (a (first objs))
         (b (second objs))
         (h (max (obj-h a) (obj-h b)))
         (w (max (obj-w a) (obj-w b))))
    (define (occupied? obj r c)
      (member? (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) r) (+ (obj-c1 obj) c)) (obj-cells obj)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (equal? (occupied? a r c) (occupied? b r c))) 8 0)))))

title: Legend-Ordered Assembly
written_solution: Treat the nonzero top row as an ordering legend. Crop the matching objects and concatenate them left to right in legend order with one background separator column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
         (objs (filter (lambda (o) (all? (lambda (p) (> (first p) 0)) (obj-cells o))) (objects g 0))))
    (define (find-obj color) (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) objs)))
    (define crops (map find-obj legend))
    (define H (apply max (map obj-h crops)))
    (define W (+ (apply + (map obj-w crops)) (- (length crops) 1)))
    (grid-from-fn H W
      (lambda (r c)
        (let loop ([remaining crops] [offset 0])
          (cond [(empty? remaining) 0]
                [(and (>= c offset) (< c (+ offset (obj-w (first remaining)))))
                 (let* ((obj (first remaining))
                        (rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) r))
                        (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) (- c offset))))
                   (if (and (< r (obj-h obj)) (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj))) (at g rr cc) 0))]
                [else (loop (rest remaining) (+ offset (obj-w (first remaining)) 1))]))))))

title: Overlapping Routed Links
written_solution: Use the command-selected bend policy to connect every same-colored terminal pair. Any cell traversed by multiple routed paths becomes overlap cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (remove-duplicates (map third (grid-cells g)))))
         (endpoint-colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v cmd))) colors)))
    (define counts (make-hash))
    (define paints (make-hash))
    (define (mark! p color)
      (hash-update! counts (cons (first p) (second p)) add1 0)
      (hash-set! paints (cons (first p) (second p)) (if (> (hash-ref counts (cons (first p) (second p))) 1) 8 color)))
    (define (range-between a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (reverse (range b (+ a 1)))))
    (for ([color (in-list endpoint-colors)])
      (define pts (find-color g color))
      (when (= (length pts) 2)
        (define a (first pts))
        (define b (second pts))
        (define first-leg
          (if (= cmd 1)
              (map (lambda (c) (list (first a) c)) (range-between (second a) (second b)))
              (map (lambda (r) (list r (second a))) (range-between (first a) (first b)))))
        (define second-leg
          (if (= cmd 1)
              (map (lambda (r) (list r (second b))) (range-between (first a) (first b)))
              (map (lambda (c) (list (first b) c)) (range-between (second a) (second b)))))
        (for ([p (in-list (append first-leg (rest second-leg)))])
          (mark! p color))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([key (in-list (hash-keys paints))])
      (set-cell out (car key) (cdr key) (hash-ref paints key)))))

title: Translation Analogy
written_solution: Colors 2 and 3 show the same shape before and after a translation. Compute that translation vector and apply it to the yellow(4) object on a background output grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((bb2 (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (bb3 (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first bb3) (first bb2)))
         (dc (- (second bb3) (second bb2))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 4))])
      (set-cell out (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc) 4))))

title: Nested Frame Depth Map
written_solution: Find the rectangular frames and count, for every grid cell, how many frame bounding boxes contain it. Output that containment depth as the new color, leaving outside cells at 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((objs (objects g 0)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (count-where (lambda (o) (and (>= r (obj-r1 o)) (<= r (obj-r2 o))
                                      (>= c (obj-c1 o)) (<= c (obj-c2 o))))
                     objs)))))

title: Symmetry Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: Crop the three objects, ignore their colors, and compare their binary shapes up to any rotation or reflection. Output 8 where two objects are dihedrally equivalent and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                             (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                             (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define (shape-key cells)
      (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells)
                         (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-lr cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) norm))))
    (define keys
      (map (lambda (o)
             (remove-duplicates
              (append* (map (lambda (k)
                              (let ((rot (rotate (obj-cells o) k)))
                                (list (shape-key rot) (shape-key (rotate (reflect-lr (obj-cells o)) k)))))
                            (list 0 1 2 3)))))
           objs))
    (define base-keys (map (lambda (o) (shape-key (normalize-cells (obj-cells o)))) objs))
    (define n (length objs))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list-ref base-keys c) (list-ref keys r)) 8 0)))))

title: Command Composition Transform
written_solution: Read the nonzero command strip from the top row left to right, crop the lower object, and apply the listed transforms in sequence: rotate, flip, or transpose.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((cmds (let loop ([cs (first g)] [out (list)])
                (cond [(empty? cs) (reverse out)]
                      [(= (first cs) 0) (reverse out)]
                      [else (loop (rest cs) (cons (first cs) out))]))))
    (define cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (> r 0) (not (= v 0))))))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
    (define cur (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
    (for ([cmd (in-list cmds)])
      (set! cur (cond [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw cur)]
                      [(= cmd 2) (flip-lr cur)]
                      [(= cmd 3) (flip-ud cur)]
                      [else (transpose cur)])))
    cur))

title: Chamber Ownership Fill
written_solution: Treat 9 as an impassable wall. For each open chamber, if it contains exactly one marker color, fill the whole chamber with that color while keeping walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash)) (out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 9) 9 0)))))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (= (at g r c) 9) (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define region (list))
        (define colors (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! region (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) region))
              (when (not (= (at g (car cur) (cdr cur)) 0))
                (set! colors (cons (at g (car cur) (cdr cur)) colors)))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 9))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (define fill-colors (remove-duplicates colors))
        (for ([p (in-list region)])
          (cond [(and (= (length fill-colors) 1) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))
                 (set! out (set-cell out (first p) (second p) (first fill-colors)))]
                [(not (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))
                 (set! out (set-cell out (first p) (second p) (at g (first p) (second p))))]))))
    out))

title: Hole-Count Packing
written_solution: Count the enclosed holes in each object's tight crop, sort the objects by hole count from fewest to most, and pack the cropped shapes left to right with one background separator column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                             (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                             (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define (crop-object obj)
      (grid-from-fn (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)
