                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define frames
      (filter (lambda (o) (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))) (objects g 0)))
    (define frame (first (sort frames (lambda (a b)
                                        (if (= (* (- (obj-h a) 2) (- (obj-w a) 2))
                                               (* (- (obj-h b) 2) (- (obj-w b) 2)))
                                            (> (obj-color a) (obj-color b))
                                            (> (* (- (obj-h a) 2) (- (obj-w a) 2))
                                               (* (- (obj-h b) 2) (- (obj-w b) 2))))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                          [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
      (if (= (at out r c) 0) (set-cell out r c (obj-color frame)) out))))

title: Legend-Ordered Pack
written_solution: Read the distinct nonzero colors in the top row from left to right, extract the component of each color from the body of the grid, crop those components tightly, and pack them left-to-right in legend order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g))))
         (objs (filter (lambda (o) (all? (lambda (p) (> (first p) 0)) (obj-cells o))) (objects g 0))))
    (define (find-obj color) (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) objs)))
    (define crops (map find-obj legend))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let loop ([remaining crops] [offset 0])
          (cond [(empty? remaining) 0]
                [(and (>= r 1) (>= c offset) (< c (+ offset (obj-w (first remaining)))))
                 (let* ((obj (first remaining)) (rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) (- r 1))) (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) (- c offset))))
                   (if (and (< (- r 1) (obj-h obj)) (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj))) (at g rr cc) 0))]
                [else (loop (rest remaining) (+ offset (obj-w (first remaining)) 1))]))))))

title: Select by Rank, Then Transform
written_solution: Ignore the two command cells, rank the remaining components by descending area, select the k-th largest one, crop it tightly, and apply the transform given by the second command.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((k (at g 0 0))
         (cmd (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))
         (clean (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                  (lambda (r c) (if (or (and (= r 0) (= c 0)) (and (= r 0) (= c (- (cols g) 1)))) 0 (at g r c)))))
         (objs (sort (objects clean 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                           (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))
                           (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (obj (list-ref objs (- k 1)))
         (crop (grid-from-fn (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)
                 (lambda (r c)
                   (let ((rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) r)) (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) c)))
                     (if (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj)) (at clean rr cc) 0))))))
    (cond [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw crop)]
          [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 crop)]
          [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr crop)]
          [else (flip-ud crop)])))

title: Rotation-Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: Order the components by color, normalize their shapes, and build a square matrix where entry (i,j) is 8 exactly when components i and j have the same shape up to rotation; otherwise it is 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pos< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b))
          (< (second a) (second b))
          (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (canon cells)
      (sort (normalize-cells cells) pos<))
    (define (rot-canon cells)
      (canon (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define (rotation-match? a b)
      (let loop ([cur (canon a)] [k 0])
        (cond [(>= k 4) #f]
              [(equal? cur (canon b)) #t]
              [else (loop (rot-canon cur) (+ k 1))])))
    (define objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (obj-color a) (obj-color b))) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]
                    [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                    [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
    (define n (length objs))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (rotation-match? (obj-cells (list-ref objs r))
                             (obj-cells (list-ref objs c)))
            8
            0)))))

title: Seeded Chamber Fill
written_solution: Treat 9s as hard walls. For each colored seed, flood-fill through zeros inside its reachable chamber and recolor that chamber with the seed color, leaving unseeded chambers unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                         (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9)))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (define (seed-region seed)
      (let ((sr (first seed)) (sc (second seed)) (sv (third seed)))
        (connected-region g sr sc
          (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 9)) (or (= v 0) (= v sv))))
          4)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([seed (in-list seeds)])
      (paint-cells out (seed-region seed) (third seed)))))

title: Stamp the Extracted Template
written_solution: Extract the connected non-8 template anchored at the top-left corner, then stamp that template onto a background canvas with its top-left aligned to each anchor cell of cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-cells base cells)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
             (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb))
             (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb)))
        (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (- r1 r0)) (+ 1 (- c1 c0))
          (lambda (r c)
            (let ((rr (+ r0 r)) (cc (+ c0 c)))
              (if (member? (list rr cc) cells) (at base rr cc) 0))))))
    (define (paste-nonzero out pat top left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                  [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                  #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
        (let ((rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c)))
          (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows acc) (cols acc))
              (set-cell acc rr cc (at pat r c))
              acc))))
    (let* ((template-cells
             (connected-region g 0 0
               (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8))))
               4))
           (template (crop-cells g template-cells))
           (anchors (find-color g 8)))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
                ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
        (paste-nonzero out template (first anchor) (second anchor))))))

title: Pack by Hole Count
written_solution: Extract and crop each component, count its enclosed zero regions, sort the components from fewest holes to most, and pack them vertically with one background row between successive crops.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (count-nonzero-grid grid) (count-where (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells grid))) (define (min-nonzero grid) (apply min (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells grid))))) (define (zero-component-count crop) (let loop ((remaining (filter-cells crop (lambda (r c v) (= v 0)))) (holes 0)) (if (empty? remaining) holes (let* ((p (first remaining)) (region (connected-region crop (first p) (second p) (lambda (r c v) (= v 0)) 4)) (touches-border? (any? (lambda (q) (or (= (first q) 0) (= (second q) 0) (= (first q) (- (rows crop) 1)) (= (second q) (- (cols crop) 1)))) region))) (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining) (if touches-border? holes (+ holes 1))))))) (define (paste-nonzero out pat top left) (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((r (in-range (rows pat))) (c (in-range (cols pat))) #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0))) (let ((rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c))) (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows acc) (cols acc)) (set-cell acc rr cc (at pat r c)) acc)))) (define (pack-vertical crops) (let loop ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)) (remaining crops) (top 0)) (if (empty? remaining) out (loop (paste-nonzero out (first remaining) top 0) (rest remaining) (+ top (rows (first remaining)) 1))))) (let* ((entries (map (lambda (obj) (let ((crop (crop-object g obj))) (list (zero-component-count crop) crop))) (objects g 0))) (ordered (map second (sort entries (lambda (a b) (let ((ha (first a)) (hb (first b)) (ca (second a)) (cb (second b))) (cond ((not (= ha hb)) (< ha hb)) ((not (= (count-nonzero-grid ca) (count-nonzero-grid cb))) (< (count-nonzero-grid ca) (count-nonzero-grid cb))) (else (< (min-nonzero ca) (min-nonzero cb)))))))))) (pack-vertical ordered))))

title: Corner-Command Tiling
written_solution: Ignore the four command cells, crop the central motif, transform it according to the top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right commands, and place those four variants into a 2×2 tiled output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (crop-cells base cells)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
             (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb))
             (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb)))
        (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (- r1 r0)) (+ 1 (- c1 c0))
          (lambda (r c)
            (let ((rr (+ r0 r)) (cc (+ c0 c)))
              (if (member? (list rr cc) cells) (at base rr cc) 0))))))
    (define (paste-nonzero out pat top left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                  [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                  #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
        (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) (at pat r c))))
    (let* ((h (rows g))
           (w (cols g))
           (codes (list (at g 0 0) (at g 0 (- w 1)) (at g (- h 1) 0) (at g (- h 1) (- w 1))))
           (ignore (list (list 0 0) (list 0 (- w 1)) (list (- h 1) 0) (list (- h 1) (- w 1))))
           (motif-cells
             (filter-cells g
               (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (member? (list r c) ignore))))))
           (motif (crop-cells g motif-cells))
           (variants (map (lambda (code) (transform-code motif code)) codes))
           (cell-h (apply max (map rows variants)))
           (cell-w (apply max (map cols variants))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (* 2 cell-h) (* 2 cell-w) 0)])
                ([variant (in-list variants)] [idx (in-naturals)])
        (paste-nonzero out variant (* (quotient idx 2) cell-h) (* (modulo idx 2) cell-w))))))

title: Zone Commands: Transform and Pack
written_solution: Associate each component with the nearest top-row command by horizontal zone, transform each component according to its assigned code, then sort the transformed components by area and pack them left-to-right on a background canvas.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (transform-code grid code) (cond ((= code 1) (rotate-cw grid)) ((= code 2) (rotate-180 grid)) ((= code 3) (flip-lr grid)) (else (flip-ud grid)))) (define (count-nonzero-grid grid) (count-where (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells grid))) (define (min-nonzero grid) (apply min (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells grid))))) (define (nearest-command obj commands) (let loop ((remaining (rest commands)) (best (first commands)) (best-dist (abs (- (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (* 2 (first (first commands))))))) (if (empty? remaining) best (let* ((candidate (first remaining)) (dist (abs (- (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (* 2 (first candidate)))))) (if (< dist best-dist) (loop (rest remaining) candidate dist) (loop (rest remaining) best best-dist)))))) (define (paste-nonzero out pat top left) (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((r (in-range (rows pat))) (c (in-range (cols pat))) #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0))) (let ((rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c))) (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows acc) (cols acc)) (set-cell acc rr cc (at pat r c)) acc)))) (define (pack-horizontal crops) (let loop ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)) (remaining crops) (left 0)) (if (empty? remaining) out (loop (paste-nonzero out (first remaining) 1 left) (rest remaining) (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1))))) (let* ((commands (filter identity (for/list ((c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g 0 c))) (if (= v 0) #f (list c v)))))) (clean (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= r 0) 0 (at g r c))))) (transformed (map (lambda (obj) (transform-code (crop-object clean obj) (second (nearest-command obj commands)))) (objects clean 0))) (ordered (sort transformed (lambda (a b) (cond ((not (= (count-nonzero-grid a) (count-nonzero-grid b))) (> (count-nonzero-grid a) (count-nonzero-grid b))) (else (< (min-nonzero a) (min-nonzero b)))))))) (pack-horizontal ordered))))

title: Infer A→B, Apply It to C
written_solution: Extract the three framed inner patterns. Determine which allowed transform maps A to B, then apply that same transform to C and output the transformed third pattern.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 9)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
    (define inners
      (map (lambda (obj)
             (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                      (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
           (take frames 3)))
    (define A (first inners))
    (define B (second inners))
    (define C (third inners))
    (define code
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code A t) B)) (list 1 2 3 4))))
        (if hit hit 1)))
    (transform-code C code)))

title: Nearest-Seed Fill with Ties
written_solution: For every zero cell inside the grid, compute Manhattan distance to each colored seed. Fill the cell with the unique nearest seed color, or with cyan(8) if the nearest distance is tied. Keep the seeds and the maroon(9) border unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                         (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9)))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at g r c)))
          (if (not (= v 0))
              v
              (let* ((distances
                       (map (lambda (seed)
                              (list (+ (abs (- r (first seed))) (abs (- c (second seed))))
                                    (third seed)))
                            seeds))
                     (best (apply min (map first distances)))
                     (colors (remove-duplicates
                               (map second (filter (lambda (d) (= (first d) best)) distances)))))
                (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 8))))))))

title: Recolor by Nesting Depth
written_solution: Detect all rectangular 9-frames. For each nonzero, non-frame marker cell, count how many frame interiors contain it, and recolor that marker with the resulting nesting depth while leaving the frames untouched.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 9)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define frames (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at g r c)))
          (if (or (= v 0) (= v 9))
              v
              (count-where
                (lambda (obj)
                  (and (> r (obj-r1 obj)) (< r (obj-r2 obj))
                       (> c (obj-c1 obj)) (< c (obj-c2 obj))))
                frames)))))))

title: Ray-Overlap Map
written_solution: From each seed, project inclusive rays along the four cardinal directions until a wall blocks them. Count how many projected paths touch each cell and output 8 exactly where that count is at least two, with maroon(9) walls preserved.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                         (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9)))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (define (clear-row? r c1 c2)
      (for/and ([c (in-range (min c1 c2) (+ (max c1 c2) 1))])
        (not (= (at g r c) 9))))
    (define (clear-col? c r1 r2)
      (for/and ([r (in-range (min r1 r2) (+ (max r1 r2) 1))])
        (not (= (at g r c) 9))))
    (define (visible? seed r c)
      (let ((sr (first seed)) (sc (second seed)))
        (or (and (= sr r) (clear-row? r sc c))
            (and (= sc c) (clear-col? c sr r)))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (cond [(= (at g r c) 9) 9]
              [(>= (count-where (lambda (seed) (visible? seed r c)) seeds) 2) 8]
              [else 0])))))

title: Area Comparison Matrix
written_solution: Order the components by color and compute their areas. Build a square matrix whose entry is 1 when the row component is smaller, 2 when the two areas are equal, and 3 when the row component is larger.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs
           (sort (objects g 0)
                 (lambda (a b)
                   (cond [(not (= (obj-color a) (obj-color b))) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]
                         [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                         [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
         (n (length objs)))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((a (obj-size (list-ref objs r)))
              (b (obj-size (list-ref objs c))))
          (cond [(< a b) 1]
                [(= a b) 2]
                [else 3]))))))

title: Ranked Component with Composed Transforms
written_solution: Ignore the command markers, rank the components by descending area, select the k-th largest one, crop it tightly, and apply the first commanded transform followed by the second one.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (transform-code grid code) (cond ((= code 1) (rotate-cw grid)) ((= code 2) (rotate-180 grid)) ((= code 3) (flip-lr grid)) (else (flip-ud grid)))) (let* ((w (cols g)) (k (at g 0 0)) (t1 (at g 0 (- w 2))) (t2 (at g 0 (- w 1))) (clean (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (or (and (= r 0) (= c 0)) (and (= r 0) (= c (- w 2))) (and (= r 0) (= c (- w 1)))) 0 (at g r c))))) (objs (sort (objects clean 0) (lambda (a b) (cond ((not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))))))) (target (crop-object clean (list-ref objs (- k 1))))) (transform-code (transform-code target t1) t2))))

title: Fill seeded rows
written_solution: Each row that contains a nonzero seed is filled completely with that seed color. Rows with no nonzero cells stay all black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g r))))
        (if (empty? colors) 0 (first colors))))))

title: Expand singletons into pluses
written_solution: Every isolated nonzero cell grows into a plus of radius 1 in its own color: center plus the four cardinal neighbors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (x) (not (= (third x) 0))) (grid-cells g)))])
    (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
      (if (empty? (filter (lambda (d)
                            (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                              (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                                   (= (at g nr nc) v))))
                          cardinal-deltas))
          (paint-cells out
                       (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
                               (cons (list r c)
                                     (map (lambda (d) (list (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))) cardinal-deltas)))
                       v)
          out))))

title: Erase border-touching objects
written_solution: Delete every connected object that touches any outer border of the grid. Keep only objects that are fully interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (if (empty? (filter (lambda (p)
                          (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- (rows g) 1))
                              (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- (cols g) 1))))
                        (obj-cells obj)))
        out
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 0))))

title: Turn solid rectangles into outlines
written_solution: Replace every nonzero component by the outline of its tight bbox, in the component's color, on a black(0) background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (append (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
              (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj)))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (border-cells obj) (obj-color obj)))))

title: Shift everything one step down-right
written_solution: Move every nonzero cell one row down and one column right. The old positions become black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
            ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (x) (not (= (third x) 0))) (grid-cells g)))])
    (let ((r (+ (first cell) 1)) (c (+ (second cell) 1)))
      (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
          (set-cell out r c (third cell))
          out))))

title: Transpose the square grid
written_solution: Reflect the whole square grid across its main top-left to bottom-right diagonal.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (transpose g))

title: Fill one-cell gaps
written_solution: If a black(0) cell sits exactly between two equal nonzero colors horizontally or vertically, fill that gap with the shared color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (cols g))])
    (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
        out
        (let* ((horiz (and (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
                           (= (at g r (- c 1)) (at g r (+ c 1)))
                           (not (= (at g r (- c 1)) 0))))
               (vert (and (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1))
                          (= (at g (- r 1) c) (at g (+ r 1) c))
                          (not (= (at g (- r 1) c) 0)))))
          (if (and horiz (or (not vert) (= (at g r (- c 1)) (at g (- r 1) c))))
              (set-cell out r c (at g r (- c 1)))
              (if vert
                  (set-cell out r c (at g (- r 1) c))
                  out))))))

title: Crop the color named by the marker
written_solution: The top-left marker cell names the target color. Ignore the marker itself, collect all cells of that color, and output their tight bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((marker (at g 0 0))
         (cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (= (first p) 0) (= (second p) 0))))
                        (find-color g marker)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)

title: Draw each object’s bounding box
written_solution: Replace every nonzero component by the outline of its tight bbox, in the component's color, on a black(0) background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (append (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
              (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj)))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (border-cells obj) (obj-color obj)))))

title: Rotate the object by the corner key
written_solution: The value in the top-left corner is a rotation key: 1 → rotate the main object 90° clockwise, 2 → 180°, and 3 → 270° clockwise. Output the cropped rotated object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((key (at g 0 0))
         (obj (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0))))
    (if (= key 1)
        (rotate-cw obj)
        (if (= key 2) (rotate-180 obj) (rotate-ccw obj)))))

title: Swap the left and right objects
written_solution: There are exactly two objects. Exchange their positions by placing each object at the other object’s original top-left anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
         (a (first objs))
         (b (second objs)))
    (define (shifted obj top left)
      (map (lambda (p) (list (+ top (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj)))
                             (+ left (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj)))))
           (obj-cells obj)))
    (paint-cells
      (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (shifted a (obj-r1 b) (obj-c1 b)) (obj-color a))
      (shifted b (obj-r1 a) (obj-c1 a))
      (obj-color b))))

title: Recolor by size rank
written_solution: Rank the three objects by size. Recolor the smallest object red(2), the middle object yellow(4), and the largest object cyan(8), while keeping every shape in place.

(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))
         (palette (list 2 4 8)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list objs)] [i (in-naturals)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (list-ref palette i)))))

title: Corner marker selects a quadrant
written_solution: The inner 4×4 body is divided into four 2×2 quadrants. A corner marker outside the body selects which quadrant to output: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g))
         (body (subgrid g 1 1 (- h 2) (- w 2)))
         (bh (rows body))
         (bw (cols body))
         (hh (quotient bh 2))
         (hw (quotient bw 2))
         (corner (first (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)))
                                (list (list 0 0) (list 0 (- w 1)) (list (- h 1) 0) (list (- h 1) (- w 1)))))))
    (cond [(and (= (first corner) 0) (= (second corner) 0)) (subgrid body 0 0 (- hh 1) (- hw 1))]
          [(= (first corner) 0) (subgrid body 0 hw (- hh 1) (- bw 1))]
          [(= (second corner) 0) (subgrid body hh 0 (- bh 1) (- hw 1))]
          [else (subgrid body hh hw (- bh 1) (- bw 1))])))

title: Apply column gravity
written_solution: Within each column, slide all nonzero cells straight down to the bottom while preserving their top-to-bottom order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (gravity g "down"))

title: Stack objects vertically by area
written_solution: Extract every object, crop each one tightly, sort them from largest area to smallest, and stack them top-to-bottom with one background row between neighboring shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))
         (shapes (map (lambda (obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))) objs))
         (out-h (+ (apply + (map rows shapes)) (max 0 (- (length shapes) 1))))
         (out-w (apply max (map cols shapes))))
    (let pack ([remaining shapes] [top 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                         (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) c v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ top (rows shape) 1) next))))))

title: Place objects into matching-color frames
written_solution: Match each loose object to the empty frame of the same color, then move the cropped object into the center of that frame’s interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj))
             (w (obj-w obj))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))

    (define (floor-half x)
      (if (>= x 0) (quotient x 2) (- 0 (quotient (+ (- 0 x) 1) 2))))
    (define objs (objects g 0))

    (define shapes (filter (lambda (obj) (not (frame? obj))) objs))
    (define with-frames

    (for/fold ([out with-frames]) ([frame (in-list frames)])
      (let* ((obj (first (filter (lambda (candidate) (= (obj-color candidate) (obj-color frame))) shapes)))

        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
          (let ((v (at shape r c)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) v) acc)))))))

title: Repeat the template once per marker
written_solution: Count the nonzero markers in the top row. Crop the template object below, then output that many horizontal copies of the template with one background column between copies.

            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols shape) 1) next))))))

    (define (frame? obj)

        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)

title: Reflect the marked-side object across the divider
written_solution: A full gray(5) line is the mirror. The red(2) marker(2) tells you which side contains the source object. Copy that side's non-marker, non-divider cells by reflection across the divider, keeping the original source object.

(rule!
  (let* ((vert (find-first (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (horiz (find-first (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g))))
         (marker (first (find-color g 2))))
    (define mirrored
      (cond
        [(not (eq? vert #f))
         (let ((left-side (< (second marker) vert)))
           (foldl (lambda (cell out)
                    (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
                      (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 2)) (not (= v 5)) (equal? (< c vert) left-side))
                          (let ((nc (- (* 2 vert) c)))
                            (if (and (in-bounds? r nc (rows g) (cols g)) (not (= nc vert)))
                                (set-cell out r nc v)
                                out))
                          out)))
                  g (grid-cells g)))]
        [(not (eq? horiz #f))
         (let ((top-side (< (first marker) horiz)))
           (foldl (lambda (cell out)
                    (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
                      (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 2)) (not (= v 5)) (equal? (< r horiz) top-side))
                          (let ((nr (- (* 2 horiz) r)))
                            (if (and (in-bounds? nr c (rows g) (cols g)) (not (= nr horiz)))
                                (set-cell out nr c v)
                                out))
                          out)))
                  g (grid-cells g)))]
        [else g]))
    (set-cell mirrored (first marker) (second marker) 0)))

title: Move the magenta object one step in the marker's direction
written_solution: A single direction marker tells how to move the magenta(6) object: blue(1)=left, red(2)=up, green(3)=right, yellow(4)=down. Output only the shifted object.

  (let* ((marker (find-first (lambda (p)

                      [(= mcolor 2) (list -1 0)]

written_solution: Take the red(2) object and the green(3) object, align their bounding boxes by top-left corner, and output only the overlapping cells in cyan(8) on a background grid.

written_solution: Blue(1) markers on the top border select columns. Red(2) markers on the left border select rows. Put green(3) cells at every selected row/column intersection in an otherwise background output.

  (let* ((cols1 (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 1)) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (rows2 (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r 0) 2)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (apply append (map (lambda (r) (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) cols1)) rows2))
                 3)))

title: Recolor the symmetry outsider
written_solution: Most yellow(4) objects are the same shape up to rotation or reflection. Find the one object outside that symmetry class and recolor it to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0)))
    (define (canon obj)
      (first (sort (map (lambda (cells) (format "~s" cells)) (all-transforms (obj-cells obj))) string<?)))
    (define keyed (map (lambda (o) (list (canon o) o)) objs))
    (define odd
      (let loop ((remaining keyed))
        (cond [(empty? remaining) #f]
              [(= (count-where (lambda (x) (equal? (first x) (first (first remaining)))) keyed) 1)
               (second (first remaining))]
              [else (loop (rest remaining))])))
    (if odd (paint-cells g (obj-cells odd) 8) g)))

title: Fill the annulus between two nested frames
written_solution: A large yellow(4) frame(4) surrounds a smaller blue(1) frame(1). Fill every cell inside the outer frame but outside the inner frame with cyan(8), while keeping both frames unchanged.
