  (let* ((outer (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))
                             (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (inner (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                             (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (ob (obj-bbox outer))
         (ib (obj-bbox inner))
         (cells (filter (lambda (p)
                          (not (and (>= (first p) (first ib)) (<= (first p) (third ib))
                                    (>= (second p) (second ib)) (<= (second p) (fourth ib)))))
                        (positions-in-rect (+ (first ob) 1) (+ (second ob) 1) (- (third ob) 1) (- (fourth ob) 1)))))
    (paint-cells g cells 8)))

title: Copy rotated template shapes from control markers
written_solution: The green(3) template near the corner must be copied at each control marker. Marker color gives the rotation: blue(1)=0°, red(2)=90°, yellow(4)=180°, magenta(6)=270°. Place each rotated copy with the marker as the top-left of its bbox, and output only the copies.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define template
      (let* ((templates (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0)))
             (best (first (sort templates (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
        (norm (obj-cells best))))
    (define (rot-n cells k)
      (let loop ((i k) (x cells))
        (if (= i 0) x (loop (- i 1) (rot x)))))
    (define (turns color) (cond [(= color 1) 0] [(= color 2) 1] [(= color 4) 2] [else 3]))
    (foldl (lambda (m out)
             (let* ((color (at g (first m) (second m)))
                    (shape (rot-n template (turns color)))
                    (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first m) (first p)) (+ (second m) (second p)))) shape)))
               (paint-cells out placed 3)))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           (filter (lambda (p)
                     (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                       (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 4) (= v 6))))
                   (grid-positions g)))))

title: Fill each walled compartment from its seed
written_solution: Gray(5) walls divide the grid into chambers. Each chamber contains one colored seed. Fill all black(0) cells in a chamber with that seed's color, without crossing the walls.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (p)
                         (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                           (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3) (= v 4))))
                       (grid-positions g))))
    (foldl (lambda (seed out)
             (let* ((color (at g (first seed) (second seed)))
                    (region (connected-region g (first seed) (second seed) (lambda (r c v) (or (= v 0) (= v color))))))
               (foldl (lambda (p acc)
                        (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) color)
                            acc))
                      out region)))
           g seeds)))

title: Recolor the elbow of each red L-triomino
written_solution: For each red(2) component that forms a 3-cell L, identify the corner cell where the two arms meet and recolor only that elbow to yellow(4). Leave every other cell unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 2)) out
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (rs (map fst cells))
             (cs (map snd cells)))
        (if (or (not (= (length cells) 3)) (= (min-list rs) (max-list rs)) (= (min-list cs) (max-list cs)))
          out
          (let ((elbow (find-first (lambda (p)
            (= (count-where (lambda (q)
                 (= (+ (abs (- (fst p) (fst q))) (abs (- (snd p) (snd q)))) 1))
               cells) 2)) cells)))
            (if elbow (set-cell out (fst elbow) (snd elbow) 4) out))))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Fill the gap between aligned blue endpoints
written_solution: Whenever two blue(1) endpoints lie on the same row or column with only zeros between them, fill the cells between them with red(2). Keep the endpoints blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((row-filled
    (reduce (lambda (out r)
      (let ((cols1 (filter (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r c) 1)) (range 0 w))))
        (if (= (length cols1) 2)
          (let ((c1 (first cols1)) (c2 (second cols1)))
            (if (all? (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r c) 0)) (range (+ c1 1) c2))
              (reduce (lambda (acc c) (set-cell acc r c 2)) out (range (+ c1 1) c2))
              out))
          out)))
      g (range 0 h))))
    (reduce (lambda (out c)
      (let ((rows1 (filter (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 1)) (range 0 h))))
        (if (= (length rows1) 2)
          (let ((r1 (first rows1)) (r2 (second rows1)))
            (if (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 0)) (range (+ r1 1) r2))
              (reduce (lambda (acc r) (set-cell acc r c 2)) out (range (+ r1 1) r2))
              out))
          out)))
      row-filled (range 0 w))))

title: Turn solid green rectangles into cyan-outlined blocks
written_solution: Find every solid green(3) rectangle. Recolor its perimeter to cyan(8) while leaving its interior green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 3)) out
      ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of obj
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             ;; Top edge (row r1)
             (r0 (first bb))
             ;; Left edge (col c1)
             (c0 (second bb))
             ;; Bottom edge (row r2)
             (r1 (third bb))
             ;; Right edge (col c2)
             (c1 (fourth bb)))
        (reduce (lambda (acc r)
          (reduce (lambda (acc2 c)
            (if (and (= (cell-at g r c) 3)
                     (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1)))
              (set-cell acc2 r c 8)
              acc2))
            acc (range c0 (+ c1 1))))
          out (range r0 (+ r1 1))))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Complete the missing corner of each 2×2 blue square
written_solution: If a 2×2 window contains exactly three blue(1) cells and one empty cell, fill the missing corner with red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out r)
    (reduce (lambda (acc c)
      (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
             (blue-count (count-where (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 1)) cells))
             (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 0)) cells)))
        (if (and (= blue-count 3) (= (length zeros) 1))
          (set-cell acc (fst (first zeros)) (snd (first zeros)) 2)
          acc)))
      out (range 0 (- w 1))))
    g (range 0 (- h 1))))

title: Recolor the endpoints of diagonal magenta segments
written_solution: Each magenta(6) diagonal line keeps its interior, but its two endpoints are recolored to blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 6)) out
      (let* ((cells (sort-by (obj-cells obj) (lambda (p) (fst p))))
             (first-cell (first cells))
             (last-cell (nth cells (- (length cells) 1))))
        (set-cell (set-cell out (fst first-cell) (snd first-cell) 1)
                  (fst last-cell) (snd last-cell) 1))))
    g (objects-8 g 0)))

title: Fill the centers of hollow 3×3 yellow rings
written_solution: Every hollow 3×3 yellow(4) ring gets its center filled with red(2). All other cells stay the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((pattern (list 4 4 4 4 0 4 4 4 4)))
      (fold-cells g g
        (lambda (out r c v)
          (let ((vals (if (and (<= r (- h 3)) (<= c (- w 3)))
                          (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p)))
                               (positions-in-rect r c (+ r 2) (+ c 2)))
                          (list))))
            (if (equal? vals pattern)
                (set-cell out (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 2)
                out))))))

title: Recolor the border-touching orange component
written_solution: Among the orange(7) components, recolor the one that touches the outer border to green(3). Leave the interior orange(7) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
           (w (cols g))
           (orange (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 7)) (objects g 0))))
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj orange])
        (if (any? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- h 1)) (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- w 1)))) (obj-cells obj))
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
            out))))

title: Fill the interior of the unique hollow rectangle
written_solution: Among the cyanless magenta(6) rectangles, the hollow frame is special: fill its interior with cyan(8), while solid magenta(6) blocks remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1) (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b)) (all? (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)))
    (let ((frames (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0))))
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj frames])
        (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
               (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb)) (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb))
               (border (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)))
          (if (same-cells? (obj-cells obj) border)
              (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1)) 8)
              out))))))

title: Move the smallest blue object by the red→green vector
written_solution: Use the vector from the red(2) marker to the green(3) marker. Take the smallest blue(1) component, erase it from its original location, and redraw it translated by that vector in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((red (first (find-color g 2)))
         (green (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first green) (first red)))
         (dc (- (second green) (second red)))
         (target (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                              (lambda (a b)
                                (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                                    (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                        (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                                        (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                                    (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))))
    (define cleared (paint-cells g (obj-cells target) 0))
    (for/fold ([out cleared]) ([p (in-list (obj-cells target))])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) dr)) (c (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Fill the chamber containing the most red seeds
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. Count the red(2) seeds in each chamber and fill the background cells of the chamber with the largest seed count using cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (best-cells (list))
        (best-count -1))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 5))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define cells (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (let ((cnt (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) cells)))
          (when (> cnt best-count)
            (set! best-count cnt)
            (set! best-cells cells)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list best-cells)])
      (if (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
          (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
          out))))

title: Recolor the candidate that is a mirror image of the source
written_solution: The blue(1) source shape defines the pattern. Among the red(2) candidates, recolor the one whose normalized shape is a reflected version of the source (not merely a rotation) to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (shape-key cells) (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define source (find-color g 1))
    (define rotations (map (lambda (k) (shape-key (rotate source k))) (list 0 1 2 3)))
    (define dihedral
      (remove-duplicates
       (append* (map (lambda (k)
                       (let ((rot (rotate source k)))
                         (list (shape-key rot) (shape-key (reflect-h rot)))))
                     (list 0 1 2 3)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((key (shape-key (obj-cells obj))))
        (if (and (member? key dihedral) (not (member? key rotations)))
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8)
            out)))))

title: Count the components of colors 1, 2, and 3
written_solution: Count how many connected components there are of blue(1), red(2), and green(3). Output a 3-row chart where row i contains that many cells of color i, packed from the left.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (count-components color)
      (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) (objects g 0))))
    (let* ((n1 (count-components 1))
           (n2 (count-components 2))
           (n3 (count-components 3))
           (ww (max 1 n1 n2 n3)))
      (grid-from-fn 3 ww
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((cnt (cond [(= r 0) n1] [(= r 1) n2] [else n3]))
                (color (+ r 1)))
            (if (< c cnt) color 0)))))))

title: Crop the blue component whose size matches the marker count
written_solution: Count the red(2) markers. Find the blue(1) component having exactly that many cells, then output only that component cropped to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((k (length (find-color g 2)))
           (target (find-first (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 1) (= (obj-size o) k))) (objects g 0))))
      (if target
          (let* ((bb (obj-bbox target))
                 (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb)) (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb))
                 (cells (obj-cells target)))
            (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (- r1 r0)) (+ 1 (- c1 c0))
              (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list (+ r0 r) (+ c0 c)) cells) 1 0))))
          '((0)))))

title: Mark zero cells that touch both blue and red objects
written_solution: Find the background cells that are 4-connected to at least one blue(1) cell and also to at least one red(2) cell. Recolor those interface cells to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define h (rows g))
    (define w (cols g))
    (define (touches? color r c)
      (any? (lambda (d)
               (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                 (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (= (at g nr nc) color))))
             cardinal-deltas))
    (fold-cells g g
      (lambda (out r c v)
        (if (and (= v 0) (touches? 1 r c) (touches? 2 r c))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Highlight the union of all shortest paths through a maze
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. Between the start marker red(2) and the goal marker green(3), mark every empty cell that belongs to at least one shortest path with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dg (dist-from goal))
    (define D (hash-ref ds (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 999999))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (< D 999999)
                 (hash-has-key? ds (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? dg (cons r c))
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c)) (hash-ref dg (cons r c))) D))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Mark cells equidistant from two maze markers
written_solution: With gray(5) as walls, compute shortest-path distance from each empty cell to the red(2) marker and to the green(3) marker. If the cell is equidistant to both, paint it cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (hash-has-key? da (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? db (cons r c))
                 (= (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c))))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Stamp a control-selected transform of the source shape
written_solution: The blue(1) source shape is transformed according to the control marker: red(2) → identity, green(3) → 90° clockwise, yellow(4) → flip horizontal, magenta(6) → flip vertical. Stamp the transformed copy in cyan(8) with its normalized top-left corner anchored at the maroon(9) marker.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-v cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) norm))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define source (find-color g 1))
    (define control (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 2 3 4 6))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
    (define shape (cond [(= control 2) (normalize-cells source)]
                        [(= control 3) (rotate source 1)]
                        [(= control 4) (reflect-h source)]
                        [else (reflect-v source)]))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list shape)])
      (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (first p)))
            (c (+ (second anchor) (second p))))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Output the normalized XOR of the blue and red shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1) and red(2) shapes by translating each to its own bounding-box origin, overlay them, and output the cells that belong to exactly one of the two shapes. Use cyan(8) in the cropped output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape1 (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (shape2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (xor (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p shape2))) shape1)
                      (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p shape1))) shape2))))
    (if (empty? xor)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells xor))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Fill the selected band between nested frames
written_solution: There are three nested magenta(6) frames. The control marker selects which empty band to fill: 2 → the band between the outer and middle frame, 3 → the band between the middle and inner frame, and 4 → the interior of the innermost frame. Fill the selected region with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 6)
                                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define control (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 2 3 4))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define depth (cond [(= control 2) 0] [(= control 3) 1] [else 2]))
    (if (< depth (length frames))
        (let* ((selected (list-ref frames depth))
               (inner (and (< (+ depth 1) (length frames)) (list-ref frames (+ depth 1)))))
          (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 selected) 1) (obj-r2 selected))]
                                [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 selected) 1) (obj-c2 selected))])
            (if (and (= (at out r c) 0)
                     (or (not inner)
                         (not (and (>= r (obj-r1 inner)) (<= r (obj-r2 inner))
                                   (>= c (obj-c1 inner)) (<= c (obj-c2 inner))))))
                (set-cell out r c 8)
                out)))
        g)))

title: Highlight shortest paths from start to checkpoint to goal
written_solution: Using gray(5) as walls, first consider shortest paths from red(2) to yellow(4), then shortest paths from yellow(4) to green(3). Recolor every empty cell that belongs to at least one shortest path in either segment with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 4)))
         (cgoal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define (union-between s t)
      (let* ((ds (dist-from s))
             (dt (dist-from t))
             (D (hash-ref ds (cons (first t) (second t)) 999999)))
        (filter (lambda (p)
                  (and (hash-has-key? ds (cons (first p) (second p)))
                       (hash-has-key? dt (cons (first p) (second p)))
                       (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons (first p) (second p)))
                             (hash-ref dt (cons (first p) (second p))))
                          D)))
                (grid-positions g))))
    (define cells (remove-duplicates (append (union-between a b) (union-between b cgoal))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list cells)])
      (if (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
          (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
          out))))

title: Output the normalized intersection of three shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1), red(2), and green(3) shapes by translating each to its own bounding-box origin. Output the cells common to all three normalized shapes, using cyan(8) in a cropped grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape1 (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (shape2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (shape3 (normalize-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (inter (filter (lambda (p) (and (member? p shape2) (member? p shape3))) shape1)))
    (if (empty? inter)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells inter))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Mark the interior of straight blue segments
written_solution: Every blue(1) cell that lies strictly inside a straight horizontal or vertical blue(1) segment becomes red(2). Endpoints stay blue(1) and background stays unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((left (= (safe-at g r (- c 1) 0) 1))
            (right (= (safe-at g r (+ c 1) 0) 1))
            (up (= (safe-at g (- r 1) c 0) 1))
            (down (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) c 0) 1)))
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 1)
                 (or (and left right (not up) (not down))
                     (and up down (not left) (not right))))
            2
            (at g r c))))))

title: Fill one-cell vertical green gaps
written_solution: Whenever two green(3) cells appear in the same column with exactly one empty cell between them, fill that middle cell with red(2). Everything else stays as it is.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (= (at g r c) 0) (= (at g (- r 1) c) 3) (= (at g (+ r 1) c) 3))
          2
          (at g r c)))))

title: Recolor yellow components that touch exactly two borders
written_solution: Find every yellow(4) component and count how many grid borders it touches. If it touches exactly two borders, recolor that whole component to cyan(8). Leave the other yellow(4) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((h (rows g)) (w (cols g)))
    (define (side-count obj)
      (+ (if (= (obj-r1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-r2 obj) (- h 1)) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c2 obj) (- w 1)) 1 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 4) (= (side-count o) 2))) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8))))

title: Shift magenta singletons down-right
written_solution: Every magenta(6) singleton moves one cell diagonally down-right. The original magenta(6) cells disappear, while the gray(5) obstacles stay fixed.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl (lambda (p out)
           (let ((nr (+ (first p) 1)) (nc (+ (second p) 1)))
             (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                 (set-cell out nr nc 6)
                 out)))
         (paint-cells g (find-color g 6) 0)
         (find-color g 6)))

title: Recolor exact cyan line triominoes
written_solution: Look at each cyan(8) component. If it has exactly three cells and those three cells form a straight horizontal or vertical line, recolor that component to orange(7). Leave every other cyan(8) component unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o)
                                      (and (= (obj-color o) 8)
                                           (= (obj-size o) 3)
                                           (or (= (obj-r1 o) (obj-r2 o)) (= (obj-c1 o) (obj-c2 o)))))
                                    (objects g 0))])
    (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 7)))

title: Complete green 2x2 squares from diagonal pairs
written_solution: Whenever a 2x2 block contains two green(3) cells on one diagonal and the other two cells are empty, fill the missing two cells with green(3) to complete the square.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))] [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((a (at g r c)) (b (at g r (+ c 1))) (d (at g (+ r 1) c)) (e (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
      (cond
        [(and (= a 3) (= e 3) (= b 0) (= d 0))
         (set-cell (set-cell out r (+ c 1) 3) (+ r 1) c 3)]
        [(and (= b 3) (= d 3) (= a 0) (= e 0))
         (set-cell (set-cell out r c 3) (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 3)]
        [else out]))))

title: Recolor the smallest red component
written_solution: Among all red(2) connected components, find the unique smallest one by cell count and recolor it to blue(1). The other red(2) components stay red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((candidates (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))
         (target (first (sort candidates
                              (lambda (a b)
                                (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                      [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                                      [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))))
    (paint-cells g (obj-cells target) 1)))

title: Complete horizontal mirror symmetry in each box
written_solution: For every connected object, use its own tight bbox as a mirror box. Keep the original cells and add their left-right reflections inside that same box, in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
    (foldl (lambda (p acc)
             (set-cell acc (first p) (- (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (second p)) (obj-color obj)))
           out (obj-cells obj))))

title: Rotate each object 90° clockwise in its box
written_solution: Treat each object independently. Take its tight square bbox, rotate the object 90° clockwise inside that box, and output only the rotated version of each object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rot cells) (sort (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw cells)) cell<?))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
      (paint-cells out
                   (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) (first p)) (+ (obj-c1 obj) (second p))))
                        (rot (obj-cells obj)))
                   (obj-color obj)))))

title: Move the object by the source-to-target vector
written_solution: There is one non-marker object plus a source marker red(2) and a destination marker green(3). Compute the vector from red(2) to green(3), translate the object by that vector, and remove the markers and the original object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Red (2) is the source marker and green (3) is the destination marker.
  (let* ((src (first (find-color g 2)))
         (dst (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first dst) (first src)))
         (dc (- (second dst) (second src))))
    ;; Copy only payload cells to a blank grid, shifted by the 2->3 vector.
    (foldl (lambda (cell out)
             (let* ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell))
                    (nr (+ r dr)) (nc (+ c dc)))
               (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 2)) (not (= v 3))
                        (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)))
                   (set-cell out nr nc v)
                   out)))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           (grid-cells g))))

title: Extract the widest object
written_solution: Compare the objects by the width of their tight bounding boxes. Select the unique widest object, crop to its own bbox, and output just that cropped object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (first (sort (objects g 0)
                              (lambda (a b)
                                (let ((wa (obj-w a)) (wb (obj-w b)))
                                  (if (= wa wb) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) (> wa wb)))))))
         ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of target
         (bb (obj-bbox target)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Union two shapes after top-left alignment
written_solution: Take the shape made by blue(1) and the shape made by red(2). Normalize both to their own top-left corners, overlay them, and output the union as green(3) in the minimal bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((union-cells (remove-duplicates (append (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)) (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells union-cells)))
    (if bb
        (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) union-cells 3)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0))))

title: Complete main-diagonal symmetry in each box
written_solution: For each object, look at its tight square bbox and reflect the object across that box's main diagonal. Keep the original cells and add the reflected ones in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
    (foldl (lambda (p acc)
             (let ((nr (+ (obj-r1 obj) (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj))))
                   (nc (+ (obj-c1 obj) (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj)))))
               (set-cell acc nr nc (obj-color obj))))
           out (obj-cells obj))))

title: Complete 90° rotational symmetry in each box
written_solution: For each object, use its tight square bbox and add the 90°, 180°, and 270° rotations of the object's cells inside that same box. The result is the full 4-way rotational closure of each object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (objects g 0)])
      (let loop ((k 0) (shape (norm (obj-cells obj))) (acc out))
        (if (= k 4)
            acc
            (loop (+ k 1)
                  (rot shape)
                  (paint-cells acc
                               (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) (first p)) (+ (obj-c1 obj) (second p)))) shape)
                               (obj-color obj))))))))

title: Control-select a rank, then transform and extract
written_solution: The top-left control cell chooses which object to select by size rank: 1 → smallest, 2 → middle, 3 → largest. The top-right control cell chooses the transformation: 4 → identity, 5 → horizontal mirror, 6=90° clockwise. Select the chosen object, apply the chosen transform, and output only that transformed object as a tight crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (hmirror cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells)) (cmax (apply max (map second n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- cmax (second p)))) n))))
    (define rank (at g 0 0))
    (define transform (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define objs (sort (filter (lambda (o) (or (= (obj-color o) 7) (= (obj-color o) 8) (= (obj-color o) 9))) (objects g 0))
                       (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))
    (define target (cond [(= rank 1) (first objs)]
                         [(= rank 2) (list-ref objs (quotient (length objs) 2))]
                         [else (last objs)]))
    (define cells0 (norm (obj-cells target)))
    (define cells (cond [(= transform 4) cells0]
                        [(= transform 5) (hmirror cells0)]
                        [else (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells0))]))
    (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
      (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) cells (obj-color target)))))

title: Fill chambers only when exactly one seed is present
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Split the non-wall area into chambers. If a chamber contains exactly one colored seed, flood-fill the whole chamber with that seed's color. If it contains zero seeds or more than one seed, leave the chamber empty. Keep the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (not (= v 5)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (for/fold ([out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 5) 5 0)))]) ([comp comps])
      (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3)))) comp)))
        (if (= (length seeds) 1)
            (paint-cells out comp (at g (first (first seeds)) (second (first seeds))))
            out)))))

title: Reflect blue seeds across both pivot axes
written_solution: The red(2) anchor 2 defines a horizontal and a vertical reflection axis through its row and column. For every blue(1) seed cell, add its reflections across the anchor row, the anchor column, and both at once. Keep the anchor unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((pivot (first (find-color g 2)))
         (pr (first pivot))
         (pc (second pivot)))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((targets (list p (list (- (* 2 pr) (first p)) (second p))
                                  (list (first p) (- (* 2 pc) (second p)))
                                  (list (- (* 2 pr) (first p)) (- (* 2 pc) (second p))))))
               (foldl (lambda (q acc)
                        (if (pos-in-bounds? q (rows g) (cols g))
                            (set-cell acc (first q) (second q) 1)
                            acc))
                      out targets)))
           g (find-color g 1))))

title: Subtract the aligned second shape from the first
written_solution: Extract the blue(1) shape and the red(2) shape, normalize both to their own top-left corners, and subtract the second from the first. Output the remaining cells as green(3) in a tight crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (b (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (c (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p b))) a)))
    (if (empty? c)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells c))
               (norm (normalize-cells c))
               (bb2 (bbox-of-cells norm)))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb2)) (+ 1 (fourth bb2)) 0) norm 3)))))

title: Copy the template to anchors with reflection controls
written_solution: The yellow(4) object is the template. Each anchor color selects how to copy it: 1 → identity, 2 → horizontal mirror, 3 → vertical mirror. For every anchor, place the corresponding transformed copy of the template with the anchor as the copy's top-left corner. The output contains only the copies, not the original template or the anchors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (hmirror cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells)) (cmax (apply max (map second n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- cmax (second p)))) n))))
    (define (vmirror cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells)) (rmax (apply max (map first n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (- rmax (first p)) (second p))) n))))
    (define template (norm (find-color g 4)))
    (foldl (lambda (anchor out)
             (let* ((color (at g (first anchor) (second anchor)))
                    (shape (cond [(= color 1) template] [(= color 2) (hmirror template)] [else (vmirror template)]))
                    (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)))
               (paint-cells out placed 4)))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3)))) (grid-positions g)))))

title: Extract the most deeply enclosed object
written_solution: Gray(5) rectangles are frames. For every non-frame object, count how many frames strictly enclose it. Select the object with the greatest enclosure depth and output only that object's tight crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define frames (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0)))
    (define objs (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) 5))) (objects g 0)))
    (define (depth obj)
      (count-where (lambda (fr)
                     (all? (lambda (p)
                             (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 fr)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 fr))
                                  (> (second p) (obj-c1 fr)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 fr))))
                           (obj-cells obj)))
                   frames))
    (define target (first (sort objs (lambda (a b)
                                       (let ((da (depth a)) (db (depth b)))
                                         (if (= da db) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) (> da db)))))))
    (let* ((cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells target)))
           (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
      (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) cells (obj-color target)))))

title: Paint color-matched row/column intersections
written_solution: Markers on the top row choose columns and markers on the left column choose rows. Paint an interior cell only when its row marker color matches its column marker color, and use that shared color at the intersection. Keep the border markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((row-marks (filter (lambda (r) (let ((v (at g r 0))) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3)))) (range 1 (rows g))))
         (col-marks (filter (lambda (c) (let ((v (at g 0 c))) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3)))) (range 1 (cols g)))))
    (foldl (lambda (r out)
             (foldl (lambda (c acc)
                      (if (= (at g r 0) (at g 0 c))
                          (set-cell acc r c (at g r 0))
                          acc))
                    out col-marks))
           (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
             (lambda (r c)
               (if (or (and (= c 0) (member? r row-marks)) (and (= r 0) (member? c col-marks)))
                   (at g r c)
                   0)))
           row-marks)))

title: Complete three blue rectangle corners with a red fourth corner
written_solution: Look for blue(1) cells that occupy exactly three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Add a red(2) cell at the missing fourth corner. Leave every other cell unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((ones (find-color g 1)))
    (define (has-one? p) (member? p ones))
    (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r1 (in-range (rows g))] [r2 (in-range (+ r1 1) (rows g))]
                          [c1 (in-range (cols g))] [c2 (in-range (+ c1 1) (cols g))])
      (let* ((corners (list (list r1 c1) (list r1 c2) (list r2 c1) (list r2 c2)))
             (present (filter has-one? corners))
             (missing (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-one? p))) corners)))
        (if (and (= (length present) 3) (= (length missing) 1)
                 (= (at out (first (first missing)) (second (first missing))) 0))
            (set-cell out (first (first missing)) (second (first missing)) 2)
            out)))))

title: Fill horizontal gaps between red endpoints with yellow
written_solution: In any row where two red(2) endpoints have only background cells between them, keep the red(2) endpoints and fill the interior gap with yellow(4). Process every qualifying row.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out r)
    (let ((reds (filter (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r c) 2)) (range 0 w))))
      (if (= (length reds) 2)
        (let ((c1 (first reds)) (c2 (second reds)))
          (if (all? (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r c) 0)) (range (+ c1 1) c2))
            (reduce (lambda (acc c) (set-cell acc r c 4)) out (range (+ c1 1) c2))
            out))
        out)))
    g (range 0 h)))

title: Fill the centers of hollow blue 3x3 frames
written_solution: Find every hollow 3x3 blue(1) square whose border is blue(1) and whose center is background. Fill just the center cell with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out r)
    (reduce (lambda (acc c)
      (if (and (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)) 0)
               (= (cell-at g r c) 1)
               (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 1)
               (= (cell-at g r (+ c 2)) 1)
               (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) c) 1)
               (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) (+ c 2)) 1)
               (= (cell-at g (+ r 2) c) 1)
               (= (cell-at g (+ r 2) (+ c 1)) 1)
               (= (cell-at g (+ r 2) (+ c 2)) 1))
        (set-cell acc (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 8)
        acc))
      out (range 0 (- w 2))))
    g (range 0 (- h 2))))

title: Crop to the tight bounding box of the colored object
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (if bb
        (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
        (empty-grid 1 1 0))))

title: Recolor 7-components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Examine each connected orange(7) component. If it touches exactly one of the four grid borders, recolor the whole component green(3). Components touching zero borders or multiple borders stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 7)) out
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (top (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) cells))
             (bottom (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) (- h 1))) cells))
             (left (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) 0)) cells))
             (right (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) (- w 1))) cells))
             (touch-count (+ (if top 1 0) (if bottom 1 0) (if left 1 0) (if right 1 0))))
        (if (= touch-count 1)
          (recolor-cells out cells 3)
          out))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Mirror the left half across the central divider
written_solution: A vertical line of gray(5) cells is the divider. Copy every nonzero cell from the left side to its mirror position on the right side. Keep the original left side and the divider.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((divs (filter (lambda (c)
                        (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5))
                              (range 0 h)))
                      (range 0 w))))
    (if (empty? divs)
        g
        (let ((divider (first divs)))
          (cellmap g (r c v)
            (let ((src-c (- (* 2 divider) c)))
              (if (and (> c divider)
                       (in-bounds? r src-c h w)
                       (!= (at g r src-c) 0)
                       (!= (at g r src-c) 5))
                  (at g r src-c)
                  v)))))))

title: Recolor the smallest connected component to maroon
written_solution: Find all nonzero connected components. The smallest one by area is recolored maroon(9). All larger components keep their original colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort-by (objects g 0) (lambda (obj) (obj-size obj))))
         (small (first objs)))
    (recolor-cells g (obj-cells small) 9)))

title: Copy the 2-shape by the marker vector as a 3-shape
written_solution: Take the connected shape made of red(2). The vector from marker 8 to marker 9 tells you where to copy it. Stamp a translated copy of the whole shape in green(3) while keeping the original shape and the markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
         (p8 (first (find-color g 8)))
         (p9 (first (find-color g 9)))
         (dr (- (first p9) (first p8)))
         (dc (- (second p9) (second p8))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr))
                   (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 3)
                   out)))
           g
           (obj-cells shape))))

title: Fill each frame interior with a count-coded color
written_solution: Each hollow frame is made of yellow(4). Count how many red(2) markers lie strictly inside that frame. Fill the frame interior with magenta(6) for one marker, orange(7) for two markers, and cyan(8) for three markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ()
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (and (>= (- (obj-r2 obj) (obj-r1 obj)) 2)
               (>= (- (obj-c2 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) 2)
               (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?)))
          (let* ((inside (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
                 (cnt (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) inside)))
            (paint-cells out inside (+ 5 cnt)))
          out))))

title: Flood each wall chamber from its unique seed
written_solution: Gray(5) walls partition the grid into chambers. If a chamber contains exactly one seed color among 1, 2, or 3, fill all background cells in that chamber with that seed color. Leave walls and seed cells in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (out g))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 5))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define chamber (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([step 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! chamber (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) chamber))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ step 1))))
        (let ((seed-colors (remove-duplicates
                            (filter (lambda (v) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 3)))
                                    (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) chamber)))))
          (when (= (length seed-colors) 1)
            (for ([p (in-list chamber)])
              (when (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
                (set! out (set-cell out (first p) (second p) (first seed-colors)))))))))
    out))

title: Stamp a rotated copy of the template at the anchor
written_solution: The magenta(6) component is the template. the unique control cell 1/2/3/4 chooses rotation by 0/90/180/270 degrees. Rotate the template accordingly and stamp the rotated copy in green(3) with its top-left corner at the cyan(8) anchor cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define shape (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 8)))
    (define ctrl (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4)))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p))))
                        (rotate shape (- ctrl 1))))
    (paint-cells g placed 3)))

title: Fill the overlap of two rectangles implied by corner pairs
written_solution: Two blue(1) cells are opposite corners of one rectangle, and two red(2) cells are opposite corners of another. Infer both filled rectangles and color their overlapping region cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((p1 (find-color g 1))
        (p2 (find-color g 2)))
    (if (and (= (length p1) 2) (= (length p2) 2))
        (let* ((ar0 (min (first (first p1)) (first (second p1))))
               (ar1 (max (first (first p1)) (first (second p1))))
               (ac0 (min (second (first p1)) (second (second p1))))
               (ac1 (max (second (first p1)) (second (second p1))))
               (br0 (min (first (first p2)) (first (second p2))))
               (br1 (max (first (first p2)) (first (second p2))))
               (bc0 (min (second (first p2)) (second (second p2))))
               (bc1 (max (second (first p2)) (second (second p2))))
               (r0 (max ar0 br0))
               (r1 (min ar1 br1))
               (c0 (max ac0 bc0))
               (c1 (min ac1 bc1)))
          (if (and (<= r0 r1) (<= c0 c1))
              (paint-cells g (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1) 8)
              g))
        g)))

title: Output component colors sorted by size
written_solution: Find every connected nonzero component and measure its area. Produce a single output row listing the component colors from largest component to smallest component.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((comps (sort (objects g 0)
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                            (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))
                            (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (list (map obj-color comps))))

title: Bridge each aligned equal-color pair
written_solution: For each color that appears exactly twice in the grid, if the two cells are aligned horizontally or vertically and the cells between them are empty, fill the gap with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
              (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
                     (let* ((r (first a)) (lo (min (second a) (second b))) (hi (max (second a) (second b))))
                       (if (all? (lambda (c) (= (at out r c) 0)) (range (+ lo 1) hi))
                           (paint-cells out (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (+ lo 1) hi)) color)
                           out))]
                    [(= (second a) (second b))
                     (let* ((c (second a)) (lo (min (first a) (first b))) (hi (max (first a) (first b))))
                       (if (all? (lambda (r) (= (at out r c) 0)) (range (+ lo 1) hi))
                           (paint-cells out (map (lambda (r) (list r c)) (range (+ lo 1) hi)) color)
                           out))]
                    [else out]))
            out)))))

title: Mark the union of all shortest paths in the maze
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls, red(2) is the start, and green(3) is the goal. Mark every empty cell that lies on at least one shortest path from red(2) to green(3) with cyan(8). Keep the walls and endpoints unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dg (dist-from goal))
    (define goal-key (cons (first goal) (second goal)))
    (define D (hash-ref ds goal-key 999999))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (< D 999999)
                 (hash-has-key? ds (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? dg (cons r c))
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c)) (hash-ref dg (cons r c))) D))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Wall-constrained three-seed Voronoi fill
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Seeds of colors 1, 2, and 3 compete for each reachable empty cell. Fill a cell with the color of its nearest seed, but leave it empty if two or more seeds are tied for nearest.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 3)))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist-from seed)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first seed) (second seed))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define dists (map (lambda (s) (list (third s) (dist-from s))) seeds))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((vals (map (lambda (item) (list (hash-ref (second item) (cons r c) 999999) (first item))) dists))
                   (best (apply min (map first vals)))
                   (hits (filter (lambda (p) (= (first p) best)) vals)))
              (if (and (< best 999999) (= (length hits) 1)) (second (first hits)) 0)))))))

title: Fill the band selected by the nested-frame control
written_solution: Three nested frames of yellow(4) appear in the grid. The control cell 1/2/3 selects which region to fill: 1 fills the band between the outer and middle frames, 2 fills the band between the middle and inner frames, and 3 fills the inside of the innermost frame. Use cyan(8) for the filled region.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define ctrl (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 3)))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)
                                       (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define idx (- ctrl 1))
    (define selected (and (< idx (length frames)) (list-ref frames idx)))
    (define inner (and (< (+ idx 1) (length frames)) (list-ref frames (+ idx 1))))
    (if selected
        (let* ((inside (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 selected) 1) (+ (obj-c1 selected) 1)
                                          (- (obj-r2 selected) 1) (- (obj-c2 selected) 1)))
               (fillable (filter (lambda (p)
                                    (and (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                                         (or (eq? inner #f)
                                             (not (and (>= (first p) (obj-r1 inner)) (<= (first p) (obj-r2 inner))
                                                       (>= (second p) (obj-c1 inner)) (<= (second p) (obj-c2 inner)))))))
                                  inside)))
          (paint-cells g fillable 8))
        g)))

title: Trace a right-moving mirror beam
written_solution: The beam starts at the red(2) source and initially moves to the right. Slash mirrors (3) and backslash mirrors (4) reflect it, and walls (5) stop it. Mark every empty traversed cell with cyan(8) while leaving the source, mirrors, and walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; The lone red source launches one beam immediately to its right.
  (let* ((source (first (find-color g 2))))
    ;; Slash and backslash mirrors redirect the current ray differently.
    (define (slash dr dc) (list (- 0 dc) (- 0 dr)))
    (define (backslash dr dc) (list dc dr))
    ;; Paint only traversed black cells; the first gray wall ends the trace.
    (let loop ([out g] [r (first source)] [c (+ (second source) 1)] [dr 0] [dc 1] [seen (list)] [fuel 500])
      (if (or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) (member? (list r c dr dc) seen) (= (at out r c) 5))
          out
          (let* ((v (at out r c))
                 (nd (cond [(= v 3) (slash dr dc)]
                           [(= v 4) (backslash dr dc)]
                           [else (list dr dc)]))
                 (next-out (if (= v 0) (set-cell out r c 8) out)))
            (loop next-out (+ r (first nd)) (+ c (second nd)) (first nd) (second nd) (cons (list r c dr dc) seen) (- fuel 1)))))))

title: Apply a transform and translation to the template
written_solution: The magenta(6) component is the template. The vector from blue(1) marker to red(2) marker tells where its transformed copy should go. A control color chooses the transformation: green(3) → identity, yellow(4) → 90° clockwise, orange(7) → flip horizontal, cyan(8) → flip vertical. Stamp the transformed copy in maroon(9) at the translated position.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define shape (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))))
    (define p1 (first (find-color g 1)))
    (define p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define ctrl (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (or (= v 3) (= v 4) (= v 7) (= v 8)))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define dr (- (first p2) (first p1)))
    (define dc (- (second p2) (second p1)))
    (define r0 (apply min (map first shape)))
    (define c0 (apply min (map second shape)))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) cells))))
    (define (reflect-v cells)
      (let ((w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells))))
    (define base (norm shape))
    (define transformed (cond [(= ctrl 4) (rot90 base)]
                              [(= ctrl 7) (reflect-h base)]
                              [(= ctrl 8) (reflect-v base)]
                              [else base]))
    (paint-cells g (map (lambda (p) (list (+ r0 dr (first p)) (+ c0 dc (second p)))) transformed) 9)))

title: Fill each chamber by boundary-color majority
written_solution: For each black(0) chamber, count the cardinally touching boundary cells in colors blue(1) through yellow(4), including repeated occurrences. Fill the whole chamber with the unique most frequent boundary color. If the highest count is tied (or there is no marker), leave the chamber black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Mutable lookup table for seen
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (out g))
    (define (mode-unique vals)
      (let* ((colors (remove-duplicates vals))
             (ranked (sort (map (lambda (color) (list color (count-where (lambda (v) (= v color)) vals))) colors)
                           (lambda (a b) (> (second a) (second b))))))
        (cond [(empty? ranked) #f]
              [(= (length ranked) 1) (first (first ranked))]
              [(> (second (first ranked)) (second (second ranked))) (first (first ranked))]
              [else #f])))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c))) (= (at g r c) 0))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define chamber (list))
        (define boundary (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([step 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! chamber (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) chamber))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                    (cond [(and (= (at g nr nc) 0) (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                           (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                           (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))]
                          [(and (>= (at g nr nc) 1) (<= (at g nr nc) 4))
                           (set! boundary (cons (at g nr nc) boundary))])))))
            (bfs (+ step 1))))
        (let ((color (mode-unique boundary)))
          (when color (set! out (paint-cells out chamber color))))))
    out))

title: Mark maze cells equidistant from the two seeds
written_solution: Walls are gray(5), and seeds are colors 1 and 2. Mark every empty cell that is reachable from both seeds and has exactly the same maze distance to each seed. Use cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 1)))
         (b (first (find-color g 2))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (hash-has-key? da (cons r c))
                 (= (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c) 999999)))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Horizontal sandwich fill
written_solution: Whenever a row contains color–zero–same color with exactly one zero between them, fill that zero with the matching color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1)))) (if (and (= (at g r c) 0) (not (= (at g r (- c 1)) 0)) (= (at g r (- c 1)) (at g r (+ c 1)))) (set-cell out r c (at g r (- c 1))) out))))

title: Complete the missing square corner
written_solution: Whenever a 2×2 block contains exactly three cells of the same non-background color and one empty cell, fill the empty corner with that color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))) (c (in-range (- (cols g) 1)))) (let* ((cells (positions-in-rect r c (+ r 1) (+ c 1))) (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells)) (nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals))) (if (and (= (length nz) 3) (= (length (remove-duplicates nz)) 1) (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1)) (let ((miss (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)))) (set-cell out (first miss) (second miss) (first nz))) out)))))

title: Fill the row between matching endpoints
written_solution: If a row has exactly two nonzero cells, both the same color, and all cells between them are 0, fill the entire segment from the left endpoint to the right endpoint with that color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (let ((nz (filter (lambda (cv) (not (= (second cv) 0))) (map (lambda (c) (list c (at g r c))) (range (cols g)))))) (if (and (= (length nz) 2) (= (second (first nz)) (second (second nz))) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ (first (first nz)) 1) (first (second nz))))) (paint-cells out (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (first (first nz)) (+ (first (second nz)) 1))) (second (first nz))) out)))))

title: X-center fill
written_solution: If a black(0) cell has the same non-background color on all four diagonal neighbors, fill the center with that color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))) (c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1)))) (let ((vals (list (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) (- c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))) (if (and (= (at g r c) 0) (not (= (first vals) 0)) (= (length (remove-duplicates vals)) 1)) (set-cell out r c (first vals)) out)))))

title: Extend exact dominoes
written_solution: Every row segment of exact length 2 is extended one cell to the right, provided the next cell is 0. Longer runs are left alone.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (f4-horizontal-runs grid) (apply append (for/list ((r (in-range (rows grid)))) (let loop ((c 0) (acc (list))) (cond ((>= c (cols grid)) (reverse acc)) ((= (at grid r c) 0) (loop (+ c 1) acc)) (else (let* ((v (at grid r c)) (end (let walk ((cc c)) (if (and (< (+ cc 1) (cols grid)) (= (at grid r (+ cc 1)) v)) (walk (+ cc 1)) cc)))) (loop (+ end 1) (cons (list r c end v) acc))))))))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((run (in-list (f4-horizontal-runs g)))) (let ((r (first run)) (c1 (third run)) (v (fourth run))) (if (and (= (+ 1 (- c1 (second run))) 2) (< (+ c1 1) (cols g)) (= (at g r (+ c1 1)) 0)) (set-cell out r (+ c1 1) v) out)))))

title: Highlight 2×2 block anchors
written_solution: For every solid 2×2 block of the same non-background color, recolor only its top-left cell to cyan(8) and leave the other three cells unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))) (c (in-range (- (cols g) 1)))) (let ((v (at g r c))) (if (and (not (= v 0)) (= (at g r (+ c 1)) v) (= (at g (+ r 1) c) v) (= (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)) v)) (set-cell out r c 8) out)))))

title: Horizontal symmetrization
written_solution: Reflect every nonzero cell across the horizontal midline of the grid. Keep the original cells; add the mirrored copies.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Overlay the UP-DOWN mirror onto the grid: every non-zero cell also
 ;; lands at its vertically mirrored position.
 (overlay g (flip-ud g)))

title: Recolor the rightmost object
written_solution: Find the component whose cells extend farthest to the right, and recolor that entire object to cyan(8). Leave all other objects as they are.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-list< a b) (cond ((empty? a) #f) ((< (first a) (first b)) #t) ((> (first a) (first b)) #f) (else (e8b-list< (rest a) (rest b))))) (define (e8b-list> a b) (e8b-list< b a)) (let* ((chosen (first (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (e8b-list> (list (apply max (map second (obj-cells a))) (obj-size a) (- (apply min (map first (obj-cells a))))) (list (apply max (map second (obj-cells b))) (obj-size b) (- (apply min (map first (obj-cells b))))))))))) (paint-cells g (obj-cells chosen) 8))))

title: Draw every object's bounding-box border
written_solution: Each nonzero component is a solid axis-aligned rectangle. For every component, keep only its bbox border in the component's color and clear the interior.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (f14-border-cells r0 c0 r1 c1) (for*/list ((r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))) (c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))) #:when (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))) (list r c))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((obj (in-list (objects g 0)))) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (paint-cells out (f14-border-cells (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) (obj-color obj))))))

title: Bridge aligned same-color objects
