title: Recolor red components that touch exactly two borders
written_solution: Inspect each red(2) component. Count which of the four outer borders of the grid it touches. If it touches exactly two distinct borders, recolor the whole component to green(3). Leave red(2) components that touch only one border, three borders, or no border unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((touches (remove-duplicates
                      (append* (map (lambda (p)
                                      (append (if (= (first p) 0) (list 1) (list))
                                              (if (= (first p) (- h 1)) (list 2) (list))
                                              (if (= (second p) 0) (list 3) (list))
                                              (if (= (second p) (- w 1)) (list 4) (list))))
                                    (obj-cells obj))))))
        (if (= (length touches) 2)
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
            out)))))

title: Fill the centers of diagonal X patterns
written_solution: Look at every empty cell as the center of a 3×3 window. If the four diagonal positions are yellow(4) and the four orthogonal neighbors are still background, then that center belongs to an X pattern and should become cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
               (= (safe-at g (- r 1) (- c 1) 0) 4)
               (= (safe-at g (- r 1) (+ c 1) 0) 4)
               (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) (- c 1) 0) 4)
               (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 0) 4)
               (= (safe-at g (- r 1) c 0) 0)
               (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) c 0) 0)
               (= (safe-at g r (- c 1) 0) 0)
               (= (safe-at g r (+ c 1) 0) 0))
          8
          (at g r c)))))

title: Mark the endpoints of straight blue lines
written_solution: Each blue(1) component is a straight horizontal or vertical line. Recolor only its two endpoint cells to orange(7). Keep the interior cells of the line blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((rs (remove-duplicates (map first (obj-cells obj))))
           (cs (remove-duplicates (map second (obj-cells obj)))))
      (cond [(= (length rs) 1)
             (let ((r (first rs)))
               (paint-cells out (list (list r (apply min cs)) (list r (apply max cs))) 7))]
            [(= (length cs) 1)
             (let ((c (first cs)))
               (paint-cells out (list (list (apply min rs) c) (list (apply max rs) c)) 7))]
            [else out]))))

title: Fill single horizontal gaps in magenta runs
written_solution: Whenever a background cell has magenta(6) immediately on its left and right, fill that one-cell gap with magenta(6). Nothing else changes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
               (= (at g r (- c 1)) 6)
               (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 6))
          6
          (at g r c)))))

title: Recolor the smallest green component
written_solution: Find all green(3) connected components and compare their sizes. The unique smallest one is recolored to yellow(4). Larger green(3) components stay green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))))
    (if (empty? comps)
        g
        (paint-cells g (obj-cells (first (sort comps (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))) 4))))

title: Add center dots to odd hollow rectangles
written_solution: Every red(2) object that is a thin hollow rectangle with odd height and odd width gets a single cyan(8) dot at its exact center. Other red(2) shapes are left alone.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (and (= (modulo (obj-h obj) 2) 1)
               (= (modulo (obj-w obj) 2) 1)
               (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?)))
          (set-cell out (quotient (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) 2)
                       (quotient (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) 2)
                       8)
          out))))

title: Mirror a colored block across a vertical divider
written_solution: The full-height maroon(9) column is the mirror axis. Copy every non-divider colored cell to its reflected position on the opposite side of that divider, keeping the same color. The original block stays in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((divs (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (if (empty? divs)
        g
        (let ((div (first divs)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (grid-cells g))])
            (let* ((r (first cell))
                   (c (second cell))
                   (v (third cell))
                   (mc (- (* 2 div) c)))
              (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9))
                       (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g))
                       (not (= mc div))
                       (= (at out r mc) 0))
                  (set-cell out r mc v)
                  out)))))))

title: Copy a green shape by the marker vector
written_solution: Use the vector from the red(2) marker to the blue(1) marker. Copy every green(3) cell by that same vector and recolor the translated copy orange(7). Keep the original shape and the markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((red (find-color g 2))
         (blue (find-color g 1)))
    (if (and (= (length red) 1) (= (length blue) 1))
        (let* ((r0 (first (first red)))
               (c0 (second (first red)))
               (r1 (first (first blue)))
               (c1 (second (first blue)))
               (dr (- r1 r0))
               (dc (- c1 c0)))
          (foldl (lambda (p out)
                   (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr))
                         (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
                     (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                         (set-cell out nr nc 7)
                         out)))
                 g
                 (find-color g 3)))
        g)))

title: Fill the rectangle whose width matches the marker count
written_solution: Count the red(2) markers. Among the hollow yellow(4) rectangles, choose the one whose outer width equals that count. Fill only its interior with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define k (length (find-color g 2)))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (and (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))
               (= (obj-w obj) k))
          (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                                              (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1))
                       8)
          out))))

title: Flood-fill the seed chamber inside the walls
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. Starting from the one colored seed cell, flood-fill through background cells only within its connected chamber. Recolor that reachable chamber with the seed's own color and leave walls untouched.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                         (let ((v (third cell)))
                           (or (= v 2) (= v 3) (= v 4) (= v 6) (= v 7) (= v 8))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (if (empty? seeds)
        g
        (let* ((seed (first seeds))
               (color (third seed))
               (seen (make-hash)))
          (define queue (list (cons (first seed) (second seed))))
          (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
          (let bfs ([step 0])
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (let ((cur (first queue)))
                (set! queue (rest queue))
                (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                  (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                        (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                    (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                               (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                               (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                      (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                      (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
              (bfs (+ step 1))))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([key (in-list (hash-keys seen))])
            (if (= (at g (car key) (cdr key)) 0)
                (set-cell out (car key) (cdr key) color)
                out))))))

title: Mark the bounding-box corners of the largest blue component
written_solution: Find the largest blue(1) component. Compute its bbox and place red(2) dots at the four bbox corners. The rest of the grid stays the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))))
    (if (empty? comps)
        g
        (let ((obj (first (sort comps (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
          (paint-cells g (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                               (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj))
                               (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                               (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
                       2)))))

title: Apply orthogonal closure to each red component
written_solution: For each red(2) component, record every row it occupies and every column it occupies. Inside that component's own bbox, fill every intersection of an occupied row and an occupied column, recoloring the whole closure green(3). This is an orthogonal-closure operation.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((rs (remove-duplicates (map first (obj-cells obj))))
           (cs (remove-duplicates (map second (obj-cells obj))))
           (cells (for*/list ([r (in-list rs)] [c (in-list cs)])
                    (list r c))))
      (paint-cells out cells 3))))

title: Rotate an anchored source shape onto the target
written_solution: The source object is the connected shape made from green(3) cells plus one red(2) anchor cell. Count the blue(1) control dots: 1 → identity, 2 → 90° clockwise, 3 → 180°, 4 → 90° counter-clockwise. Rotate the whole anchored source around its anchor, place the anchor on the cyan(8) target cell, and draw the copied shape in orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((anchors (find-color g 2))
         (targets (find-color g 8))
         (k (length (find-color g 1))))
    (if (and (= (length anchors) 1) (= (length targets) 1) (>= k 1))
        (let* ((anchor (first anchors))
               (target (first targets))
               (seen (make-hash)))
          (define (allowed? r c) (or (= (at g r c) 2) (= (at g r c) 3)))
          (define queue (list (cons (first anchor) (second anchor))))
          (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
          (let bfs ([step 0])
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (let ((cur (first queue)))
                (set! queue (rest queue))
                (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                  (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                        (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                    (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                               (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                               (allowed? nr nc))
                      (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                      (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
              (bfs (+ step 1))))
          (define offsets
            (map (lambda (key) (list (- (car key) (first anchor)) (- (cdr key) (second anchor))))
                 (hash-keys seen)))
          (define (rot offs)
            (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- 0 (first p)))) offs))
          (define final
            (let loop ([i 0] [offs offsets])
              (if (= i (- k 1)) offs (loop (+ i 1) (rot offs)))))
          (foldl (lambda (p out)
                   (let ((nr (+ (first target) (first p)))
                         (nc (+ (second target) (second p))))
                     (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                         (set-cell out nr nc 7)
                         out)))
                 g
                 final))
        g)))

title: Extract the hole of the single-hole red component
written_solution: Among the red(2) components, find the one that encloses exactly one hole. Output only that hole region, colored cyan(8), on an otherwise background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((regions (find-0-regions g 0)))
    (define (holes obj)
      (filter (lambda (reg)
                (all? (lambda (p)
                        (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                             (> (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                      reg))
              regions))
    (define candidates
      (filter (lambda (item) (= (length (second item)) 1))
              (map (lambda (obj) (list obj (holes obj)))
                   (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))))
    (if (empty? candidates)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (let* ((best (first (sort candidates (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size (first a)) (obj-size (first b)))))))
               (hole (first (second best))))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) hole 8)))))

title: Select a component by size rank, transform it, and stamp it
written_solution: Sort the blue(1) components by size from smallest to largest. The number of red(2) markers chooses which rank to take. The number of green(3) markers chooses the transform: 1 → identity, 2 = 90°, 3 = 180°, 4 → left-right mirror. Normalize the chosen component to its own bbox, apply the selected transform, then stamp it with its top-left corner at the cyan(8) target. Output only the stamped orange(7) shape.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Objects whose color is blue(1)
  (let* ((comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))
         ;; Count of red(2) cells
         (k (length (find-color g 2)))
         ;; Count of green(3) cells
         (t (length (find-color g 3)))
         ;; Positions of every cyan(8) cell
         (targets (find-color g 8)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p)
                              (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
                                (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))))
                            cells)))
    (define (rot180 cells) (rot90 (rot90 cells)))
    (define (flip-h cells)
      (let ((w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells))))
    (if (and (not (empty? comps)) (not (empty? targets)) (>= k 1) (<= k (length comps)) (>= t 1) (<= t 4))
        ;; Position of the first cyan(8) cell
        (let* ((target (first targets))
               (obj (list-ref (sort comps (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))) (- k 1)))
               ;; Same shape, translated so its bbox starts at (0,0)
               (shape0 (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
               (shape (cond [(= t 1) shape0] [(= t 2) (rot90 shape0)] [(= t 3) (rot180 shape0)] [else (flip-h shape0)]))
               (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first target) (first p)) (+ (second target) (second p)))) shape)))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 7))
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))))

title: Fill by nearest seed inside the wall maze
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. Red(2) and green(3) are the two seeds. For each empty cell, compare its shortest-path distance to each seed while respecting walls. Color it by the nearer seed; if both distances are equal, leave it black(0). Keep the seeds and walls as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (or (= (third cell) 2) (= (third cell) 3))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist-from seed)
      ;; Mutable lookup table for dist
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first seed) (second seed))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc)))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define dists (map (lambda (s) (list s (dist-from s))) seeds))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((hits (filter (lambda (item) (hash-has-key? (second item) (cons r c))) dists))
                   (bestd (if (empty? hits) #f (apply min (map (lambda (item) (hash-ref (second item) (cons r c))) hits)))))
              (if (eq? bestd #f)
                  0
                  (let* ((best (filter (lambda (item) (= (hash-ref (second item) (cons r c)) bestd)) hits))
                         (colors (remove-duplicates (map (lambda (item) (third (first item))) best))))
                    (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 0)))))))))

title: Stamp the anchored symmetric difference of two shapes
written_solution: There are two anchored source shapes: a red(2) shape with one maroon(9) anchor and a blue(1) shape with its own maroon(9) anchor. Convert both shapes into offset sets relative to their anchors, take the symmetric difference of those offset sets, then stamp that result in green(3) with the cyan(8) target acting as the new anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define target (find-color g 8))
    (define (allowed r c) (or (= (at g r c) 1) (= (at g r c) 2) (= (at g r c) 9)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (p) (allowed (first p) (second p))) (grid-positions g)))])
      (when (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons (first cell) (second cell))))
        (define queue (list (cons (first cell) (second cell))))
        (define comp (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([step 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! comp (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) comp))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                             (allowed nr nc))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ step 1))))
        (set! comps (cons comp comps))))
    (define (vals comp) (remove-duplicates (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) comp)))
    (define red-comp (first (filter (lambda (comp) (and (member? 9 (vals comp)) (member? 2 (vals comp)) (not (member? 1 (vals comp))))) comps)))
    (define blue-comp (first (filter (lambda (comp) (and (member? 9 (vals comp)) (member? 1 (vals comp)) (not (member? 2 (vals comp))))) comps)))
    (define red-anchor (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 9)) red-comp)))
    (define blue-anchor (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 9)) blue-comp)))
    (define rset (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first red-anchor)) (- (second p) (second red-anchor)))) red-comp))
    (define bset (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first blue-anchor)) (- (second p) (second blue-anchor)))) blue-comp))
    (define sym (filter (lambda (p) (and (not (equal? p (list 0 0)))
                                         (not (and (member? p rset) (member? p bset)))))
                        (append rset bset)))
    (if (empty? target)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (let* ((t (first target))
               (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first t) (first p)) (+ (second t) (second p)))) sym)))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 3)))))

title: Fill the selected band between nested frames
written_solution: The yellow(4) frames are nested. Count the red(2) markers to get an index k from outside to inside. Fill the kth empty band with cyan(8): the region inside frame k but outside the next inner frame. If k points to the innermost frame, fill its interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (obj)
                      (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)
                           (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define k (length (find-color g 2)))
    (if (and (>= k 1) (<= k (length frames)))
        (let* ((cur (list-ref frames (- k 1)))
               (nxt (if (< k (length frames)) (list-ref frames k) #f))
               (interior (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 cur) 1) (+ (obj-c1 cur) 1) (- (obj-r2 cur) 1) (- (obj-c2 cur) 1)))
               (fillable (filter (lambda (p)
                                    (and (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                                         (or (eq? nxt #f)
                                             (not (and (>= (first p) (obj-r1 nxt)) (<= (first p) (obj-r2 nxt))
                                                       (>= (second p) (obj-c1 nxt)) (<= (second p) (obj-c2 nxt)))))))
                                  interior)))
          (paint-cells g fillable 8))
        g)))

title: Draw a Manhattan shell around the green shape
written_solution: Count the red(2) markers to get a radius k. Keep the green(3) source shape, then color cyan(8) every background cell whose Manhattan distance from the source shape is exactly k. This is a Manhattan-shell construction.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((k (length (find-color g 2)))
         (cells (find-color g 3)))
    (if (or (empty? cells) (< k 1))
        g
        (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
          (let ((d (apply min (map (lambda (q) (+ (abs (- (first p) (first q))) (abs (- (second p) (second q))))) cells))))
            (if (and (= d k) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))
                (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                out))))))

title: Trace the beam through slash and backslash mirrors
written_solution: The emitter is the red(2) cell, and the adjacent blue(1) cell gives the initial direction. March one step at a time. Slash mirrors (3) and backslash mirrors (4) reflect the direction, gray(5) cells stop the beam, and every traversed background cell is painted cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((src (find-color g 2))
         (arr (find-color g 1)))
    (define (slash dr dc) (list (- 0 dc) (- 0 dr)))
    (define (backslash dr dc) (list dc dr))
    (if (and (= (length src) 1) (= (length arr) 1))
        (let* ((s (first src))
               (a (first arr))
               (dr (- (first a) (first s)))
               (dc (- (second a) (second s))))
          (if (not (= (+ (abs dr) (abs dc)) 1))
              g
              (let loop ([out g] [r (+ (first a) dr)] [c (+ (second a) dc)] [dr dr] [dc dc] [fuel 500])
                (if (or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) (= (at g r c) 5))
                    out
                    (let* ((v (at g r c))
                           (nd (cond [(= v 3) (slash dr dc)]
                                     [(= v 4) (backslash dr dc)]
                                     [else (list dr dc)]))
                           (next-out (if (= v 0) (set-cell out r c 8) out)))
                      (loop next-out (+ r (first nd)) (+ c (second nd)) (first nd) (second nd) (- fuel 1)))))))
        g)))

title: Use the legend to color each chamber
written_solution: Read a legend from the top two rows: every nonzero label color in row 0 maps to the fill color directly beneath it in row 1. In the chamber area below, each chamber contains one label cell. Fill the background of that chamber with the mapped color while preserving the label cell and the gray(5) walls.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define mapping
      (filter (lambda (p) (and (not (= (first p) 0)) (not (= (second p) 0))))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))]) (list (at g 0 c) (at g 1 c)))))
    (define (mapped v)
      (let ((hit (filter (lambda (p) (= (first p) v)) mapping)))
        (if (empty? hit) #f (second (first hit)))))
    (define seen-global (make-hash))
    (define out g)
    (for* ([r (in-range 2 (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((v (at g r c)))
        (when (and (not (eq? (mapped v) #f)) (not (hash-has-key? seen-global (cons r c))))
          (define fill (mapped v))
          (define seen (make-hash))
          (define queue (list (cons r c)))
          (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
          (hash-set! seen-global (first queue) #t)
          (let bfs ([step 0])
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (let ((cur (first queue)))
                (set! queue (rest queue))
                (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                  (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                        (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                    (when (and (>= nr 2) (< nr (rows g)) (>= nc 0) (< nc (cols g))
                               (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                               (or (= (at g nr nc) 0) (= (at g nr nc) v)))
                      (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                      (hash-set! seen-global (cons nr nc) #t)
                      (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
              (bfs (+ step 1))))
          (for ([key (in-list (hash-keys seen))])
            (when (= (at out (car key) (cdr key)) 0)
              (set! out (set-cell out (car key) (cdr key) fill)))))))
    out))

title: Fill Between Matching Endpoints
written_solution: Each color appears exactly twice as the endpoints of a horizontal or vertical segment. Fill every cell on that segment, inclusive, with the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (grid-colors g 0)))
    (define (segment a b color)
      (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
             (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b))
                                     (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
               (list (first a) c color))]
            [(= (second a) (second b))
             (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b))
                                     (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
               (list r (second a) color))]
            [else (list (list (first a) (second a) color)
                        (list (first b) (second b) color))]))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (paint-cells out (segment (first cells) (second cells) color))
            out)))))

title: Complete 2×2 Corners
written_solution: Every nonzero motif is a 2×2 block with one missing corner. If three cells in a 2×2 window share the same non-background color and one cell is 0, fill the 0 with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (window-fill curr r c)
      (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
             (vals (map (lambda (p) (at curr (first p) (second p))) cells))
             (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (at curr (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells))
             (nonzeros (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
        (if (and (= (length zeros) 1)
                 (= (length nonzeros) 3)
                 (all? (lambda (v) (= v (first nonzeros))) nonzeros))
            (list (first zeros) (first nonzeros))
            #f)))
    (define (step curr)
      (for*/fold ([acc (list curr #f)])
                 ([r (in-range (- (rows curr) 1))]
                  [c (in-range (- (cols curr) 1))])
        (let ((hit (window-fill curr r c)))
          (if hit
              (list (set-cell (first acc) (first (first hit)) (second (first hit)) (second hit)) #t)
              acc))))
    (let loop ([curr g])
      (let ((next (step curr)))
        (if (second next) (loop (first next)) (first next))))))

title: Main-Diagonal Mirror Add
written_solution: Reflect every nonzero cell across the main diagonal and keep the union of original and reflected cells. Diagonal cells stay where they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (at g r c))
            (ref (at g c r)))
        (if (and (= v 0) (not (= ref 0))) ref v)))))

title: Column Gravity Down
written_solution: Within each column, slide all nonzero cells straight down to the bottom while preserving their top-to-bottom order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (gravity g "down"))

title: Crop And Rotate Right
written_solution: Take the minimal bbox containing the object, discard the surrounding black(0) background, and rotate the cropped object 90° clockwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (rotate-cw (crop-to-content g)))

title: Glyph Broadcast From Anchors
written_solution: Find the red(2) source glyph, normalize it to its bbox, and copy that same shape to every green(3) anchor. The copies are recolored to green(3) and the original source is not kept.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((source (find-color g 2))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells source))
         (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) source))
         (anchors (find-color g 3)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
      (paint-cells out
        (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)) 3)) norm)))))

title: Bounding-Box Corners
written_solution: For each non-background color, compute the bbox covering all cells of that color and keep only the four corners of that box in the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g color)))
           (corners (list (list (first bb) (second bb) color)
                          (list (first bb) (fourth bb) color)
                          (list (third bb) (second bb) color)
                          (list (third bb) (fourth bb) color))))
      (paint-cells out corners))))

title: Fill Rectangles From Four Corners
written_solution: Every color marks the four corners of a rectangle. Fill the entire rectangle, including its interior, with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 4)
          (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
            (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) color))
          out))))

title: Legend-Selected Crop
written_solution: The top-left cell selects a target color. Keep only cells of that color and crop the result to its tight bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((selector (at g 0 0))
         (cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (= (first p) 0) (= (second p) 0))))
                        (find-color g selector)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Diagonal Reflection By Command
written_solution: A guide marker chooses which diagonal to reflect across: one command means the main diagonal, the other the anti-diagonal. Remove the guide and output the union of the object with its reflection.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (base (set-cell (set-cell g 0 0 0) 0 (- (cols g) 1) 0)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at base r c))
              (ref (if (= cmd 1)
                       (at base c r)
                       (at base (- (rows g) 1 c) (- (cols g) 1 r)))))
          (if (not (= v 0)) v ref))))))

title: Directional Gravity By Guide
written_solution: The guide color specifies a gravity direction: down, up, left, or right. Remove the guide, then compress all nonzero cells along that direction while preserving their order within each line.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (work (set-cell g 0 0 0)))
    (cond [(= cmd 1) (gravity work "down")]
          [(= cmd 2) (gravity work "up")]
          [(= cmd 3) (gravity work "left")]
          [else (gravity work "right")])))

title: Seeded Chamber Fill
written_solution: Each hollow rectangle is a chamber, and each chamber contains a colored seed. Preserve the border, then fill the chamber interior with the seed's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= (obj-size obj) 8)
             (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define rects
      (filter rect-border?
              (apply append
                (map (lambda (color) (objects (keep-only g color) 0)) (grid-colors g 0)))))
    (define with-borders
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list rects)])
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj))))
    (for/fold ([out with-borders]) ([obj (in-list rects)])
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (seeds (filter (lambda (p)
                              (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                                (and (not (= v 0))
                                     (not (member p (obj-cells obj))))))
                            (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                                               (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))))
        (if (empty? seeds)
            out
            (paint-cells out
                         (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                                            (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1))
                         (at g (first (first seeds)) (second (first seeds)))))))))

title: Recolor Broadcast Component
written_solution: Find the multicolor source component, normalize its shape, and copy that shape to every anchor cell. Each copy is recolored uniformly to the anchor's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (components-allowed allowed)
      (define visited (make-hash))
      (define comps (list))
      (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
        (when (and (member (at g r c) allowed)
                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
          (define queue (list (list r c)))
          (define cells (list))
          (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
          (define (bfs)
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (define p (first queue))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons p cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (member (at g nr nc) allowed)
                           (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
              (bfs)))
          (bfs)
          (set! comps (cons (reverse cells) comps))))
      (reverse comps))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)))
    (let* ((source (first (sort (filter (lambda (cells) (> (length cells) 1))
                                        (components-allowed (list 2 4)))
                                (lambda (a b) (> (length a) (length b))))))
           (norm (normalize source))
           (anchors (filter (lambda (cell) (member (third cell) (list 6 7 8 9))) (grid-cells g))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
        (paint-cells out
          (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p))
                                 (+ (second anchor) (second p))
                                 (third anchor)))
               norm))))))

title: Guided L-Paths
written_solution: Read command 1 or 2 at the top-left cell. For every other nonzero color, take its two markers in row-major order. Command 1 connects them with a horizontal-then-vertical L path; command 2 uses vertical-then-horizontal. Process colors by their first marker's row-major order, so later colors overwrite earlier ones at intersections, and clear the command cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((cmd (at g 0 0)))
    (define (hseg r c1 c2 color)
      (for/list ([c (in-range (min c1 c2) (+ (max c1 c2) 1))]) (list r c color)))
    (define (vseg c r1 r2 color)
      (for/list ([r (in-range (min r1 r2) (+ (max r1 r2) 1))]) (list r c color)))
    (let ((colors (remove-duplicates
                    (map third
                         (filter (lambda (cell)
                                   (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                                        (not (and (= (first cell) 0) (= (second cell) 0)))))
                                 (grid-cells g))))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list colors)])
        (let ((cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (= (first p) 0) (= (second p) 0))))
                             (find-color g color))))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (let ((a (first cells)) (b (second cells)))
              (if (= cmd 1)
                  (paint-cells out (append (hseg (first a) (second a) (second b) color)
                                           (vseg (second b) (first a) (first b) color)))
                  (paint-cells out (append (vseg (second a) (first a) (first b) color)
                                           (hseg (first b) (second a) (second b) color)))))
            out))))))

title: Command-Rotated Broadcast
written_solution: Extract the multicolor source component, then for every command-anchor pair, rotate the source by the commanded amount and place a copy with its bounding-box origin at the anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (components-allowed allowed)
      (define visited (make-hash))
      (define comps (list))
      (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
        (when (and (member (at g r c) allowed)
                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
          (define queue (list (list r c)))
          (define cells (list))
          (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
          (define (bfs)
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (define p (first queue))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons (list (first p) (second p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (member (at g nr nc) allowed)
                           (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
              (bfs)))
          (bfs)
          (set! comps (cons (reverse cells) comps))))
      (reverse comps))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)) (third p))) cells)))
    (define (transform cells t)
      (let* ((raw (map (lambda (p)
                         (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)) (v (third p)))
                           (cond [(= t 1) (list c (- r) v)]
                                 [(= t 2) (list (- r) (- c) v)]
                                 [(= t 3) (list (- c) r v)]
                                 [else (list r c v)])))
                       cells))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells raw)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)) (third p))) raw)))
    (let* ((source (first (sort (filter (lambda (cells) (> (length cells) 1))
                                        (components-allowed (list 5 6 7)))
                                (lambda (a b) (> (length a) (length b))))))
           (norm (normalize source))
           (anchors (filter (lambda (cell)
                              (and (= (third cell) 9)
                                   (> (second cell) 0)
                                   (member (at g (first cell) (- (second cell) 1)) (list 1 2 3 4))))
                            (grid-cells g))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
        (paint-cells out
          (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p))
                                 (+ (second anchor) (second p))
                                 (third p)))
               (transform norm (- (at g (first anchor) (- (second anchor) 1)) 1))))))))

title: Symmetry Analogy Transfer
written_solution: Two exemplar components of red(2) show an input-output transformation under a rotation or reflection. Infer that transform from the exemplar pair and apply it to the green(3) query component; output only the transformed query.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)
              (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))))
    (define (transform cells t)
      (let* ((raw (map (lambda (p)
                         (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
                           (cond [(= t 1) (list c (- r))]
                                 [(= t 2) (list (- r) (- c))]
                                 [(= t 3) (list (- c) r)]
                                 [(= t 4) (list r (- c))]
                                 [(= t 5) (list (- r) c)]
                                 [(= t 6) (list c r)]
                                 [(= t 7) (list (- c) (- r))]
                                 [else (list r c)])))
                       cells)))
        (normalize raw)))
    (let* ((examples (sort (objects (keep-only g 2) 0)
                           (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
           (a (first examples))
           (b (second examples))
           (q (first (objects (keep-only g 3) 0)))
           (a-norm (normalize (obj-cells a)))
           (b-norm (normalize (obj-cells b)))
           (t (first (filter (lambda (i) (equal? (transform a-norm i) b-norm)) (range 0 8))))
           (q-cells (transform (normalize (obj-cells q)) t))
           (bb (bbox-of-cells q-cells)))
      (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                               (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)
                               0)
                   q-cells
                   3))))

title: Translation Analogy Transfer
written_solution: The two yellow(4) exemplar components are the same shape at two different positions. Infer the translation vector from the first exemplar to the second, then translate the green(3) query component by that same vector.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((examples (sort (objects (keep-only g 4) 0)
                         (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
         (a (first examples))
         (b (second examples))
         (q (first (objects (keep-only g 3) 0)))
         (dr (- (obj-r1 b) (obj-r1 a)))
         (dc (- (obj-c1 b) (obj-c1 a))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list (obj-cells q))])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) dr)) (c (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 3)
            out)))))

title: Hole-Count Recolor
written_solution: Every component starts as red(2). Recolor each component according to how many holes it encloses: 0 holes becomes green(3), 1 hole becomes yellow(4), 2 holes becomes gray(5), and 3 or more holes becomes magenta(6).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((two (keep-only g 2))
         (objs (objects two 0)))
    (define (hole-color obj)
      (let ((holes (topo-count-holes two obj 0)))
        (cond [(= holes 0) 3]
              [(= holes 1) 4]
              [(= holes 2) 5]
              [(= holes 3) 6]
              [else 9])))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list objs)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (hole-color obj)))))

title: Fill Only The Max-Seed Frames
written_solution: Each rectangular frame contains some number of seed dots. Keep all borders, but fill the interior only for those frame(s) that contain the maximum number of seeds; frames with fewer seeds remain hollow.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define rects
      (filter rect-border?
              (apply append
                (map (lambda (color) (objects (keep-only g color) 0))
                     (filter (lambda (color) (not (= color 8))) (grid-colors g 0))))))
    (define scored
      (map (lambda (obj)
             (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                    (inside (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                                               (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))
                    (count8 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 8)) inside)))
               (list obj count8)))
           rects))
    (define max-count (apply max (map second scored)))
    (define with-borders
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([item (in-list scored)])
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells (first item)) (obj-color (first item)))))
    (for/fold ([out with-borders]) ([item (in-list scored)])
      (let* ((obj (first item))
             (bb (obj-bbox obj)))
        (if (= (second item) max-count)
            (paint-cells out
                         (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                                            (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1))
                         (obj-color obj))
            out)))))

title: Normalized Shape Subtraction
written_solution: Crop and normalize the green(3) source shape and the gray(5) mask shape to their own bounding boxes, overlay them at the same top-left origin, subtract every masked cell from the source, and output the remaining source shape cropped tightly.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)))
    (let* ((src (first (objects (keep-only g 3) 0)))
           (mask (first (objects (keep-only g 5) 0)))
           (src-norm (normalize (obj-cells src)))
           (mask-norm (normalize (obj-cells mask)))
           (kept (filter (lambda (p) (not (member p mask-norm))) src-norm))
           (bb (bbox-of-cells kept)))
      (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                               (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)
                               0)
                   (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb))
                                          (- (second p) (second bb))))
                        kept)
                   3))))

title: Voronoi Fill Inside A Frame
written_solution: Inside the rectangular frame, fill every interior cell with the color of the nearest seed using Manhattan distance. Seeds remain as they are, the border stays blue(1), and ties remain black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frame (first (objects (keep-only g 1) 0)))
         (bb (obj-bbox frame))
         (seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                          (let ((v (third cell)))
                            (and (not (= v 0))
                                 (not (= v 1))
                                 (> (first cell) (first bb))
                                 (< (first cell) (third bb))
                                 (> (second cell) (second bb))
                                 (< (second cell) (fourth bb)))))
                        (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist cell r c)
      (+ (abs (- (first cell) r)) (abs (- (second cell) c))))
    (define (nearest-color r c)
      (let* ((ds (map (lambda (cell) (dist cell r c)) seeds))
             (m (apply min ds))
             (colors (remove-duplicates
                       (map third
                            (filter (lambda (cell) (= (dist cell r c) m)) seeds)))))
        (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 0)))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]
                [c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
      (if (= (at g r c) 1)
          out
          (set-cell out r c (nearest-color r c))))))

title: Mark the endpoints of vertical red segments
written_solution: Find each red(2) component that is a straight vertical line. Recolor exactly its top and bottom endpoint cells to blue(1) and leave the rest of the grid unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 2) (= (obj-c1 o) (obj-c2 o)) (>= (obj-size o) 2))) (objects g 0))])
    (set-cell (set-cell out (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj) 1)))

title: Complete missing corners of 2x2 yellow squares
written_solution: Look at every 2x2 window. If it contains exactly three yellow(4) cells and one background(0), fill the missing corner with red(2). Leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))] [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
           (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
           (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)))
      (if (and (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 4)) vals) 3) (= (length zeros) 1))
          (set-cell out (first (first zeros)) (second (first zeros)) 2)
          out))))

title: Fill the centers of hollow green pluses
written_solution: Whenever a background(0) cell has green(3) neighbors above, below, left, and right, fill that center cell with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
               (all? (lambda (d) (= (at g (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d))) 3)) cardinal-deltas))
          8
          (at g r c)))))

title: Recolor orange components touching exactly one border
written_solution: Find each orange(7) component. If it touches exactly one grid border, recolor the whole component to gray(5). Components touching zero borders or two or more borders stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define h (rows g))
    (define w (cols g))
    (define (side-count obj)
      (+ (if (= (obj-r1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-r2 obj) (- h 1)) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c2 obj) (- w 1)) 1 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 7) (= (side-count o) 1))) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 5))))

title: Reflect the left pattern across a vertical divider
written_solution: Find the full-height divider made of maroon(9). For every blue(1) cell on one side, copy a mirrored cell across the divider and paint the reflected copy cyan(8). Keep the original pattern and divider.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((axis (first (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
         (ones (find-color g 1)))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((mc (- (* 2 axis) (second p))))
               (if (and (in-bounds? (first p) mc (rows g) (cols g)) (not (= mc axis)))
                   (set-cell out (first p) mc 8)
                   out)))
           g ones)))

title: Copy a cyan object by a marker vector
written_solution: There is one cyan(8) object, one red(2) marker, and one green(3) marker. Compute the vector from red(2) to green(3), then copy the cyan(8) object by that vector and paint the translated copy blue(1). Keep the original object and markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first b) (first a)))
         (dc (- (second b) (second a))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr)) (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 1)
                   out)))
           g (find-color g 8))))

title: Crop the largest purple object
written_solution: Among all purple(6) connected components, select the largest one. Output only its minimal bbox, keeping its shape but recoloring it to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (shape-key obj) (format "~s" (sort (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)) cell<?)))
    (define objs (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))
    (define best
      (first (sort objs (lambda (a b)
                          (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                [else (string>? (shape-key a) (shape-key b))])))))
    (define cells (sort (normalize-cells (obj-cells best)) cell<?))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) cells 8)))

title: Recolor L-triominoes by orientation
written_solution: Every blue(1) object is a three-cell L-triomino. Recolor each whole object according to its orientation: top-left corner shape → red(2), top-right → green(3), bottom-left → yellow(4), bottom-right → cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (tri-color cells)
      (let ((n (norm cells)))
        (cond [(equal? n (list (list 0 0) (list 0 1) (list 1 0))) 2]
              [(equal? n (list (list 0 0) (list 0 1) (list 1 1))) 3]
              [(equal? n (list (list 0 0) (list 1 0) (list 1 1))) 4]
              [(equal? n (list (list 0 1) (list 1 0) (list 1 1))) 8]
              [else #f])))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
      (let ((color (tri-color (obj-cells obj))))
        (if color (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color) out)))))

title: Connect aligned equal-color marker pairs
written_solution: For each color that appears as exactly two aligned markers, fill the straight horizontal or vertical segment between them with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list '(2 3 4))])
    (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length pts) 2)
          (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))
                 (r1 (first a)) (c1 (second a)) (r2 (first b)) (c2 (second b)))
            (cond
              [(= r1 r2) (paint-cells out (for/list ([c (in-range (min c1 c2) (+ 1 (max c1 c2)))]) (list r1 c)) color)]
              [(= c1 c2) (paint-cells out (for/list ([r (in-range (min r1 r2) (+ 1 (max r1 r2)))]) (list r c1)) color)]
              [else out]))
          out))))

title: Fill the overlap of red and green bounding boxes
written_solution: Take the bbox of all red(2) cells and the bbox of all green(3) cells. Output a background grid of the same size, and fill only the rectangular overlap of those two boxes with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((reds (find-color g 2))
         (greens (find-color g 3)))
    (if (or (empty? reds) (empty? greens))
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((ra (bbox-of-cells reds))
               (gb (bbox-of-cells greens))
               (rr0 (max (first ra) (first gb)))
               (cc0 (max (second ra) (second gb)))
               (rr1 (min (third ra) (third gb)))
               (cc1 (min (fourth ra) (fourth gb))))
          (if (and (<= rr0 rr1) (<= cc0 cc1))
              (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (positions-in-rect rr0 cc0 rr1 cc1) 8)
              (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))))))

title: Rotate a template by control and stamp it at an anchor
written_solution: Treat the blue(1) shape as a template. The control marker chooses a rotation; the orange(7) cell gives the placement anchor. Output a background grid containing the rotated template anchored at the orange(7) cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 2))) 2]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 3]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 4]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 6]
                       [else 2]))
    (define times (cond [(= ctrl 2) 0] [(= ctrl 3) 1] [(= ctrl 4) 2] [else 3]))
    (define shape
      (let loop ((k times) (cells (norm (find-color g 1))))
        (if (= k 0) cells (loop (- k 1) (rot cells)))))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 7)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)
                 8)))

title: Fill the interiors of marked frames
written_solution: Each hollow yellow(4) frame may contain a single colored marker inside it. If a frame contains exactly one nonzero, non-frame color, fill all background interior cells of that frame with the marker's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                    (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (hollow-rect? obj)
      (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
        (and (>= (- (third bb) (first bb)) 2)
             (>= (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 2)
             (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?)
                     (sort (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) cell<?)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 4) (hollow-rect? o))) (objects g 0))])
      (let* ((inside (bbox-interior-cells obj))
             (markers (filter (lambda (p)
                                (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                                  (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 4)))))
                              inside)))
        (if (= (length (remove-duplicates (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) markers))) 1)
            (let ((fill (at g (first (first markers)) (second (first markers)))))
              (foldl (lambda (p acc)
                       (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
                           (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) fill)
                           acc))
                     out inside))
            out)))))

title: Pack objects sorted by area into a row
written_solution: Find all blue(1) objects, normalize them, sort them by area from smallest to largest, recolor them to cyan(8), and pack them left-to-right into a cropped output with a single background column between consecutive shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm obj) (sort (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)) cell<?))
    ;; Retain each blue object's normalized crop, dimensions, true area, and
    ;; a deterministic normalized-shape key for the rule's tie-break.
    (define (entry obj)
      (let* ((cells (norm obj))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (list cells (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb))
              (obj-size obj) (format "~s" cells))))
    ;; Sort by cell area, not scan order or bounding-box area.
    (define entries
      (sort (map entry (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (list-ref a 3) (list-ref b 3)))
                     (< (list-ref a 3) (list-ref b 3))]
                    [else (string<? (list-ref a 4) (list-ref b 4))]))))
    (if (empty? entries)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((out-h (apply max (map second entries)))
               (out-w (+ (foldl + 0 (map third entries))
                         (max 0 (- (length entries) 1)))))
          ;; Pack normalized crops left-to-right, top-aligned, with one zero
          ;; column between consecutive cyan objects.
          (let loop ((remaining entries)
                     (cur-c 0)
                     (out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)))
            (if (empty? remaining)
                out
                (let* ((e (first remaining))
                       (cells (first e))
                       (w (third e)))
                  (loop (rest remaining)
                        (+ cur-c w 1)
                        (paint-cells
                         out
                         (map (lambda (p)
                                (list (first p) (+ cur-c (second p))))
                              cells)
                         8)))))))))

title: Reflect one quadrant across a cross divider
written_solution: A full maroon(9) row and a full maroon(9) column divide the grid into four quadrants. A blue(1) shape appears in exactly one quadrant. Reflect that shape across the row, across the column, and across both, and paint the three reflected copies cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((sep-row (first (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g)))))
         (sep-col (first (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
                    (mr (- (* 2 sep-row) r))
                    (mc (- (* 2 sep-col) c))
                    (targets (list (list r mc) (list mr c) (list mr mc))))
               (foldl (lambda (q acc)
                        (if (and (pos-in-bounds? q (rows g) (cols g))
                                 (not (= (first q) sep-row))
                                 (not (= (second q) sep-col)))
                            (set-cell acc (first q) (second q) 8)
                            acc))
                      out targets)))
           g (find-color g 1))))

title: Mark all cells on any shortest path
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls. Between the red(2) start and green(3) goal, compute all shortest 4-neighbor paths. Mark every background(0) cell that lies on at least one shortest path with cyan(8), keeping walls and markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue)) (r (first p)) (c (second p)) (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define s (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define t (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define ds (dist-from s))
    (define dt (dist-from t))
    (if (not (hash-has-key? ds t))
        g
        (let ((target (hash-ref ds t)))
          (foldl (lambda (p out)
                   (if (and (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                            (hash-has-key? ds p)
                            (hash-has-key? dt p)
                            (= (+ (hash-ref ds p) (hash-ref dt p)) target))
                       (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                       out))
                 g (grid-positions g))))))

title: Wall-constrained three-seed Voronoi fill
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls. Every background cell belongs to the nearest seed by maze distance among red(2), green(3), and yellow(4). Fill it with that seed's color; if two or more seeds tie for the minimum distance, fill it with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue)) (r (first p)) (c (second p)) (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define colors (list 2 3 4))
    (define dists (map (lambda (color) (list color (dist-from (first (find-color g color))))) colors))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((p (list r c))
                   (vals (filter (lambda (cd) (hash-has-key? (second cd) p)) dists)))
              (if (empty? vals)
                  0
                  (let* ((mind (apply min (map (lambda (cd) (hash-ref (second cd) p)) vals)))
                         (winners (filter (lambda (cd) (= (hash-ref (second cd) p) mind)) vals)))
                    (if (> (length winners) 1) 8 (first (first winners)))))))))))

title: Select the kth nested frame by marker count
written_solution: Count the red(2) markers. Among the nested hollow yellow(4) frames, ordered from outermost to innermost, recolor the kth frame border to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                    (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (hollow-rect? obj)
      (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
        (and (>= (- (third bb) (first bb)) 2)
             (>= (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 2)
             (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?)
                     (sort (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) cell<?)))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 4) (hollow-rect? o))) (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define k (length (find-color g 2)))
    (if (and (>= k 1) (<= k (length frames)))
        (paint-cells g (obj-cells (list-ref frames (- k 1))) 8)
        g)))

title: Combine two shapes with op and transform controls
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1) shape and the red(2) shape. First transform the red(2) shape according to its transform control: orange(7)=identity, cyan(8)=90°, maroon(9)=flip vertical. Then combine the two normalized shapes according to the operation control: green(3)=union, yellow(4)=intersection, magenta(6)=xor. Output the cropped result in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define (flip-v cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells)) (cmax (apply max (map second n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- cmax (second p)))) n))))
    (define a (norm (find-color g 1)))
    (define b0 (norm (find-color g 2)))
    (define op (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 0]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 1]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 2]
                     [else 0]))
    (define tr (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 7))) 0]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 8))) 1]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 9))) 5]
                     [else 0]))
    (define b (cond [(= tr 1) (rot b0)] [(= tr 5) (flip-v b0)] [else b0]))
    (define (has? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (define res0
      (cond [(= op 0) (remove-duplicates (append a b))]
            [(= op 1) (filter (lambda (p) (has? p b)) a)]

title: Trace a beam through mirrors and walls

Mark every background cell visited by the beam with cyan(8).

(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (arrow (first (find-color g 1))))

               (dc (- (second arrow) (second start)))

title: Transform and repeat-stamp a template

Output only the repeated stamps in maroon(9) on a background grid.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define (flip-v cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells)) (cmax (apply max (map second n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- cmax (second p)))) n))))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 2))) 2]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 3]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 4]
                       [else 2]))
    (define times (cond [(= ctrl 2) 0] [(= ctrl 3) 1] [else 2]))
    (define shape-rot
      (let loop ((k times) (cells (norm (find-color g 1))))
        (if (= k 0) cells (loop (- k 1) (rot cells)))))
    (define shape (if (empty? (find-color g 6)) shape-rot (flip-v shape-rot)))

    (define nxt (first (find-color g 8)))

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (not (= v 5)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (define (winner comp)
      (let* ((counts (map (lambda (color)
                            (list color (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) color)) comp)))
                          (list 1 2 3)))

        (if (= (second (first sorted)) 0)

                (first (first sorted))))))
    (foldl (lambda (comp out)

                                (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) fill)
                                acc))
                          out comp)

title: Odd Candidate Under Dihedral Room-Motif Equivalence
skills: shape normalization, dihedral equivalence, odd-one-out detection
written_solution: Normalize the motif in each chamber up to rotation and reflection. Three of the candidate rooms belong to the same equivalence class, while one does not. Output a strip marking the odd chamber with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Walls (1/7/9) partition the board into rooms, each stamped with a
 ;; motif. Compare motifs up to rotation/flip and emit a 1-row strip
 ;; (one cell per room, reading order): cyan(8) marks the rooms whose
 ;; motif matches no other room's.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (wall? v) (member? v (list 1 7 9)))
     (define rooms
       (sort (objects (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
                                          (if (wall? (at g r c)) 0 1)))
                      0)
             (lambda (a b) (or (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (and (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                    (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))))
     (define (spin p t)  ;; the 8 dihedral images of a cell
       (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
         (cond ((= t 0) (list r c))
               ((= t 1) (list c (- r)))
               ((= t 2) (list (- r) (- c)))
               ((= t 3) (list (- c) r))
               ((= t 4) (list r (- c)))
               ((= t 5) (list (- c) (- r)))
               ((= t 6) (list (- r) c))
               (else (list c r)))))
     (define (dihedral cells)  ;; the motif's 8 normalized variants
       (if (empty? cells)
           (list (list))
           (remove-duplicates
            (for/list ((t (in-range 8)))
              (let* ((raw (map (lambda (p) (spin p t)) cells))
                     (mr (min-of first raw))
                     (mc (min-of second raw)))
                (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) mr)
                                             (- (second p) mc)))
                           raw)
                      cell<))))))
     (define sets
       (map (lambda (room)
              (dihedral
               (filter (lambda (x) x)
                       (map (lambda (p)
                              (and (not (zero? (at g (first p)
                                                   (second p))))
                                   (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 room))
                                         (- (second p)
                                            (obj-c1 room)))))
                            (obj-cells room)))))
            rooms))
     (define uniques  ;; room indices whose set intersects only itself
       (map first
            (filter (lambda (pair)
                      (= 1 (count-if
                            (lambda (s)
                              (any? (lambda (v) (member? v s))
                                    (second pair)))
                            sets)))
                    (enumerate-list sets))))
     (grid-from-fn 1 (length rooms)
                   (lambda (r c) (if (member? c uniques) 8 0))))))
