title: Learn Motif-to-Fill Mapping from Example Rooms
skills: room-level analogical transfer, motif recognition, learned mapping
written_solution: Use the example rooms to infer which motif corresponds to which chamber-fill color. Then inspect the background query rooms, identify their motifs, and fill each query chamber with the color associated with that motif.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Walls (1/7/9) partition the grid into 4-connected rooms. EXAMPLE
 ;; rooms hold a majority fill color (not 0/6): each maps its motif —
 ;; the room's magenta(6) cells normalized to its bbox origin — to that
 ;; fill. Rooms with no majority fill are QUERIES: paint each one
 ;; entirely with the fill its motif maps to. Everything else passes
 ;; through unchanged.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (wall? v) (member? v (list 1 7 9)))
     (define rooms
       (sort (objects (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
                                          (if (wall? (at g r c)) 0 1)))
                      0)
             (lambda (a b)
               (or (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                   (and (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                        (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))))
     (define (motif room)
       (sort (filter values
                     (map (lambda (p)
                            (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 6)
                                (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 room))
                                      (- (second p) (obj-c1 room)))
                                #f))
                          (obj-cells room)))
             cell<))
     (define (fill-of room)
       ;; majority color of the room excluding 0/6 (ties -> larger), else #f
       (let* ((vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p)))
                         (obj-cells room)))
              (cnt (lambda (col) (count-if (lambda (v) (= v col)) vals)))
              (ranked (sort (unique (filter (lambda (v)
                                              (and (> v 0) (not (= v 6))))
                                            vals))
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (or (> (cnt a) (cnt b))
                                  (and (= (cnt a) (cnt b)) (> a b)))))))
         (if (and (pair? ranked)
                  (> (cnt (first ranked)) (quotient (length vals) 2)))
             (first ranked)
             #f)))
     (define infos
       (map (lambda (room) (list room (motif room) (fill-of room))) rooms))
     (define mapping (filter (lambda (i) (third i)) infos))
     (for/fold ((out g)) ((i (in-list infos)))
       (if (third i)
           out
           (paint-cells out (obj-cells (first i))
                        (third (find (lambda (e) (equal? (second e) (second i)))
                                     mapping))))))))

title: Recolor exact 3x3 blue squares
written_solution: Find every blue(1) component that is a solid 3x3 square. Recolor the whole square to green(3). Leave all other blue(1) shapes unchanged.

(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 9) (= (obj-h obj) 3) (= (obj-w obj) 3))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
        out)))

title: Complete blue 2x2 squares from L-shapes
written_solution: Look at every 2x2 window. If it contains exactly three blue(1) cells and one background cell, fill the background cell with green(3). Leave existing blue(1) cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range 0 (- (rows g) 1))] [c (in-range 0 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
           (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
           (ones (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 1)) vals))
           (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)))
      (if (and (= ones 3) (= (length zeros) 1))
          (set-cell out (first (first zeros)) (second (first zeros)) 3)
          out))))

title: Mark the centers of exact length-5 orange bars
written_solution: Find each orange(7) component that is a straight horizontal or vertical bar of exactly length 5. Recolor its middle cell to cyan(8). Leave all other orange(7) bars unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 7) (= (obj-size o) 5))) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((rs (remove-duplicates (map first (obj-cells obj))))
           (cs (remove-duplicates (map second (obj-cells obj)))))
      (cond [(and (= (length rs) 1) (= (length cs) 5))
             (set-cell out (first rs) (list-ref (sort cs <) 2) 8)]
            [(and (= (length cs) 1) (= (length rs) 5))
             (set-cell out (list-ref (sort rs <) 2) (first cs) 8)]
            [else out]))))

title: Reflect singletons across the anti-diagonal
written_solution: For every nonzero cell, also place the same color at its reflection across the anti-diagonal of the square grid. Keep the original cells too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((n (rows g)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (grid-cells g))])
      (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
        (if (not (= v 0))
            (set-cell out (- n 1 c) (- n 1 r) v)
            out)))))

title: Complete rectangles from three corner markers
written_solution: Each color marks three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Add the missing fourth corner in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g)))])
    (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length pts) 3)
          (let* ((rs (sort (remove-duplicates (map first pts)) <))
                 (cs (sort (remove-duplicates (map second pts)) <)))
            (if (and (= (length rs) 2) (= (length cs) 2))
                (let* ((corners (for*/list ([r (in-list rs)] [c (in-list cs)]) (list r c)))
                       (missing (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p pts))) corners)))
                  (if (= (length missing) 1)
                      (set-cell out (first (first missing)) (second (first missing)) color)
                      out))
                out))
          out))))

title: Recolor exact blue 2x3 rectangles
written_solution: Find every blue(1) component that is a solid 2x3 or 3x2 rectangle. Recolor that whole rectangle to red(2). Leave other blue(1) shapes alone.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 6)
             (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
             (or (and (= (obj-h obj) 2) (= (obj-w obj) 3))
                 (and (= (obj-h obj) 3) (= (obj-w obj) 2))))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 2)
        out)))

title: Fill the centers of red diamonds
written_solution: Whenever a background cell has red(2) cells directly above, below, left, and right of it, fill that center cell with yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
               (= (at g (- r 1) c) 2)
               (= (at g (+ r 1) c) 2)
               (= (at g r (- c 1)) 2)
               (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 2))
          4
          (at g r c)))))

written_solution: Treat each blue(1) solid rectangle as an object. Recolor squares to cyan(8), wider-than-tall rectangles to red(2), and taller-than-wide rectangles to green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (if (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj)
                     (cond [(= (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)) 8]
                           [(> (obj-w obj) (obj-h obj)) 2]
                           [else 3]))
        out)))

        (p2 (find-color g 2)))
    (if (and (= (length p1) 2) (= (length p2) 2))
        (let* ((r0b (min (first (first p1)) (first (second p1))))
               (r1b (max (first (first p1)) (first (second p1))))
               (c0b (min (second (first p1)) (second (second p1))))
               (c1b (max (second (first p1)) (second (second p1))))
               (r0r (min (first (first p2)) (first (second p2))))
               (r1r (max (first (first p2)) (first (second p2))))
               (c0r (min (second (first p2)) (second (second p2))))
               (c1r (max (second (first p2)) (second (second p2))))

               (rb (min r1b r1r))
               (ca (max c0b c0r))
               (cb (min c1b c1r)))

title: Extract the unique translated shape
written_solution: All purple(6) objects are translated copies of shapes. Three belong to one shape class and one belongs to a different class. Extract the unique shape and crop it to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))
    (define target
      (find-first (lambda (obj)
                    (= (count-where (lambda (other) (equal? (norm (obj-cells obj)) (norm (obj-cells other)))) comps) 1))
                  comps))
    (if target
        (let* ((shape (norm (obj-cells target)))
               (bb (bbox-of-cells shape)))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) shape 6))
        (empty-grid 1 1 0))))

title: Connect matched color pairs with L-paths
written_solution: Each non-background color appears exactly twice. For each color, connect the lexicographically earlier point to the later one by going horizontally first and then vertically. Output only those colored L-paths on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))))
    (define (l-path a b)
      (let* ((r1 (first a)) (c1 (second a)) (r2 (first b)) (c2 (second b))
             (stepc (if (>= c2 c1) 1 -1))
             (stepr (if (>= r2 r1) 1 -1))

             (vpart (map (lambda (r) (list r c2)) (range (+ r1 stepr) (+ r2 stepr) stepr))))

        (if (= (length pts) 2)

      (let* ((color (+ r 1))

        (if (< c n) color 0)))))

title: Trace the shortest path through the checkpoint
written_solution: Walls are gray(5), the start is red(2), the checkpoint is green(3), and the goal is yellow(4). Find the shortest path from start to checkpoint and then from checkpoint to goal, avoiding walls, and color the whole path cyan(8). Keep the walls.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define start (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define check (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define goal (first (find-color g 4)))
    (define (path a b)
      (define parent (make-hash))
      (define seen (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first a) (second a))))
      (define goal-key (cons (first b) (second b)))
      (define found #f)
      (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (or found (empty? queue))
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (when (equal? cur goal-key) (set! found #t))
            (unless found
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (hash-set! parent (cons nr nc) cur)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc)))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      (if (not found)
          (list)
          (let trace ([cur goal-key] [acc (list)])
            (let ((next-acc (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) acc)))
              (if (equal? cur (cons (first a) (second a)))
                  next-acc
                  (trace (hash-ref parent cur) next-acc))))))
    (let* ((base (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 5) 5 0))))
           (p (append (path start check) (path check goal))))
      (paint-cells base p 8))))

title: Scale and rotate the template from controls
written_solution: The top-left control cell chooses the scale (1 or 2). The next control cell chooses the rotation (0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees). Extract the orange(7) template, apply both transforms, and stamp the result with its top-left corner at the cyan(8) anchor on an otherwise background canvas.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define scale (if (= (at g 0 0) 1) 1 2))
    (define rot (cond [(= (at g 0 1) 3) 0] [(= (at g 0 1) 4) 1] [(= (at g 0 1) 5) 2] [else 3]))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 8)))
    (define obj (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 7)) (objects g 0))))
    (define (scale-shape cells k)

       (append* (map (lambda (p)
                       (for*/list ([dr (in-range k)] [dc (in-range k)])
                         (list (+ (* (first p) k) dr) (+ (* (second p) k) dc))))
                     cells))))
    (define (rot90 cells)

        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)

        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define shape (rotate (scale-shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)) scale) rot))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)

title: Fill the chamber whose seed count matches the control
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. The control value in the top-left tells you how many red(2) seeds a target chamber contains. Find the chamber with exactly that many red(2) seeds and fill all of its non-wall cells with cyan(8). Keep the walls.

        (seen (make-hash)))

      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 5) (and (= r 0) (= c 0)))
        (hash-set! seen (cons r c) #t)

          (define cells (list))
          (define seeds 0)

            (unless (empty? queue)

                (set! queue (rest queue))

                               (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))

(rule!

title: Apply Whole-Object Gravity Inside Each Frame

          (cond [(or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)))) (reverse path)]
                [(= (at g nr nc) 5) (reverse path)]
                [(and (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                      (not (and mirrors? (or (= (at g nr nc) 6) (= (at g nr nc) 7)))))
                 (reverse path)]
                [else
                 (let* ((v (at g nr nc))
                        (nd (turn v dr dc)))
                   (loop nr nc (first nd) (second nd) (- fuel 1) (cons (list nr nc) path)))]))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([seed (in-list (find-color g 2))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (trace (first seed) (second seed) #f))])
        (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 7)
            acc)))))

title: Fill Row Intervals
written_solution: In each row, look for a color that appears exactly twice. When the two copies of that color bound an all-zero gap, fill from the left endpoint to the right endpoint inclusive with that same color. Rows without such a pair stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (for/fold ([acc out]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (let ((cols-for-color
             (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) color)) (range 0 (cols g)))))
        (if (and (= (length cols-for-color) 2)
                 (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0))
                       (range (+ (first cols-for-color) 1) (second cols-for-color))))
            (paint-cells acc
                         (for/list ([c (in-range (first cols-for-color) (+ (second cols-for-color) 1))])
                           (list r c))
                         color)
            acc)))))

title: Crop the Active Bounding Box
written_solution: Ignore the background and locate the minimal bbox that contains every nonzero cell. The output is simply that rectangle cropped out of the input, preserving the colors and relative positions inside it.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (crop-to-content g 0))

title: Move Shape to Anchor
written_solution: There is one real object and one anchor marker blue(1). Compute the object's bbox, then translate every object cell by the vector that moves the bbox's top-left corner onto the anchor cell. Output only the translated object on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((anchor (first (find-color g 1)))
         (cells (filter (lambda (p)
                          (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                            (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 1)))))
                        (grid-positions g)))
         (color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
         (dr (- (first anchor) (first bb)))
         (dc (- (second anchor) (second bb))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list cells)])
      (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr)) (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out nr nc color)
            out)))))

title: Keep Only Internal Objects
written_solution: Decompose the grid into connected nonzero objects. Any object that touches the top, bottom, left, or right boundary is discarded. The output is a background grid containing only the components that stay strictly inside the frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (if (any? (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- (rows g) 1))
                    (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- (cols g) 1))))
              (obj-cells obj))
        out
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj)))))

title: Paint Aligned Midpoints
written_solution: Each relevant color appears exactly twice. If the pair is horizontally or vertically aligned and the gap has a single center cell, paint that center cell cyan(8). The original markers remain in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 2)
          (let* ((a (first cells))
                 (b (second cells))
                 (r1 (first a)) (c1 (second a))
                 (r2 (first b)) (c2 (second b)))
            (cond [(and (= r1 r2) (= (modulo (abs (- c1 c2)) 2) 0))
                   (set-cell out r1 (quotient (+ c1 c2) 2) 8)]
                  [(and (= c1 c2) (= (modulo (abs (- r1 r2)) 2) 0))
                   (set-cell out (quotient (+ r1 r2) 2) c1 8)]
                  [else out]))
          out))))

title: Most-Frequent Color Bar
written_solution: Count the number of cells for every non-background color and select the unique most frequent one. The output is otherwise background, except that the bottom row begins with a horizontal bar in that winning color whose length equals its cell count.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (count-color (lambda (color)
                        (count-where (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color)) (grid-cells g))))
         (best (first (sort colors
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (if (= (count-color a) (count-color b))
                                  (< a b)
                                  (> (count-color a) (count-color b)))))))
         (n (count-color best)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([c (in-range 0 (min n (cols g)))])
      (set-cell out (- (rows g) 1) c best))))

title: One-Mirror Beam
written_solution: Trace a beam from the red(2) source travelling right. The beam reflects off two intervening reflectors before reaching the goal; paint every traversed empty cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (turn v dr dc)
      (cond [(= v 6)
             (cond [(and (= dr 0) (= dc 1)) (list -1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr 0) (= dc -1)) (list 1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr -1) (= dc 0)) (list 0 1)]
                   [else (list 0 -1)])]
            [(= v 7)
             (cond [(and (= dr 0) (= dc 1)) (list 1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr 0) (= dc -1)) (list -1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr -1) (= dc 0)) (list 0 -1)]
                   [else (list 0 1)])]
            [else (list dr dc)]))
    (define (trace r c)
      (let loop ([rr r] [cc c] [dr 0] [dc 1] [fuel (* (rows g) (cols g) 8)] [path (list)])
        (let ((nr (+ rr dr)) (nc (+ cc dc)))
          (cond [(or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)))) (reverse path)]
                [(= (at g nr nc) 5) (reverse path)]
                [(and (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                      (not (or (= (at g nr nc) 6) (= (at g nr nc) 7))))
                 (reverse path)]
                [else
                 (let* ((v (at g nr nc))
                        (nd (turn v dr dc)))
                   (loop nr nc (first nd) (second nd) (- fuel 1) (cons (list nr nc) path)))]))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([seed (in-list (find-color g 2))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (trace (first seed) (second seed)))])
        (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 8)
            acc)))))

title: Seeded Room Fill
written_solution: Find every rectangular gray(5) frame. Each one contains a single nonzero seed that determines the chamber's fill color. Fill all zero cells strictly inside the frame with that seed color, while keeping the frame and seed itself.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 obj)) (c1 (obj-c1 obj))
             (r2 (obj-r2 obj)) (c2 (obj-c2 obj))
             (h (+ 1 (- r2 r1))) (w (+ 1 (- c2 c1)))
             (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2)))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
             (= (obj-size obj) perim)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                         (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (objects (keep-only g 5) 0))])
      (if (frame? obj)
          (let* ((inner (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                                           (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
                 (seeds (remove-duplicates
                         (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                                 (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) inner)))))
            (if (= (length seeds) 1)
                (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list inner)])
                  (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
                      (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) (first seeds))
                      acc))
                out))
          out))))

title: Two-Row Recolor Legend
written_solution: The first two rows form a legend: every nonzero entry in row 0 maps to the nonzero entry directly beneath it in row 1. Recolor every occurrence of those old colors in the rows below according to that legend. Any body color not named in the legend stays unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((mapping (make-hash)))
    (for ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((old (at g 0 c)) (new (at g 1 c)))
        (when (and (not (= old 0)) (not (= new 0)))
          (hash-set! mapping old new))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at g r c)))
          (if (< r 2) v (hash-ref mapping v v)))))))

title: Pick the Object with Area N
written_solution: The top row encodes a number N as the count of blue(1) dots. Among the connected body objects, exactly one has area N. Output a background grid with that object alone, recolored cyan(8), in its original position.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0)))
         (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (chosen (find-first (lambda (obj) (= (obj-size obj) target))
                             (objects (keep-only body 3) 0))))
    (if (eq? chosen #f)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                     (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) 1) (second p))) (obj-cells chosen))
                     8))))

title: Column Gravity Compression
written_solution: Treat each column as a stack under gravity. Remove the zero gaps, keep the nonzero values in their original top-to-bottom order, and place them flush against the bottom of the column. Do this independently for every column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (gravity g "down" 0))

title: Downward Color Shadows
written_solution: For each colored source cell, copy its color straight down through consecutive zeros. The projection stops before any nonzero blocker or wall gray(5), and the original cells remain. The result is a set of vertical same-color shadows.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g g
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (or (= v 0) (= v 5))
          out
          (let smear ([rr (+ r 1)] [acc out])
            (if (and (< rr (rows g)) (= (at g rr c) 0))
                (smear (+ rr 1) (set-cell acc rr c v))
                acc))))))

title: Two-Panel Difference Mask
written_solution: The grid contains two same-size panels separated by a vertical gray(5) divider. Compare the panels cell by cell. The output is a single panel-sized mask whose cells are cyan(8) exactly where the two inputs differ and black(0) where they match.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((div (first (filter (lambda (c)
                              (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                            (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) div
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) (at g r (+ div 1 c)))) 8 0)))))

title: Two-Mirror Beam Maze
written_solution: Trace a beam from the red(2) source travelling right. The beam reflects off two intervening reflectors before reaching the goal; paint every traversed empty cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (turn v dr dc)
      (cond [(= v 6)
             (cond [(and (= dr 0) (= dc 1)) (list -1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr 0) (= dc -1)) (list 1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr -1) (= dc 0)) (list 0 1)]
                   [else (list 0 -1)])]
            [(= v 7)
             (cond [(and (= dr 0) (= dc 1)) (list 1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr 0) (= dc -1)) (list -1 0)]
                   [(and (= dr -1) (= dc 0)) (list 0 -1)]
                   [else (list 0 1)])]
            [else (list dr dc)]))
    (define (trace r c)
      (let loop ([rr r] [cc c] [dr 0] [dc 1] [fuel (* (rows g) (cols g) 8)] [path (list)])
        (let ((nr (+ rr dr)) (nc (+ cc dc)))
          (cond [(or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)))) (reverse path)]
                [(= (at g nr nc) 5) (reverse path)]
                [(and (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                      (not (or (= (at g nr nc) 6) (= (at g nr nc) 7))))
                 (reverse path)]
                [else
                 (let* ((v (at g nr nc))
                        (nd (turn v dr dc)))
                   (loop nr nc (first nd) (second nd) (- fuel 1) (cons (list nr nc) path)))]))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([seed (in-list (find-color g 2))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (trace (first seed) (second seed)))])
        (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 8)
            acc)))))

title: Rotation-Coded Template Stamps
written_solution: The input contains one template made of green(3) and several anchor markers blue(1). The cell immediately left of each anchor is a rotation code: 2 → 0°, 4 → 90°, 6 → 180°, and 9 → 270°. Normalize the template, rotate it as requested for each anchor, and stamp the rotated copy in cyan(8) starting at the anchor cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pt< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (normalize pts)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells pts))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb)))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) r0) (- (second p) c0))) pts) pt<)))
    (define (rot1 pts)
      (let ((maxr (apply max (map first pts))))
        (normalize (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- maxr (first p)))) pts))))
    (define (rotate pts k)
      (let loop ([n (modulo k 4)] [acc pts])
        (if (= n 0) acc (loop (- n 1) (rot1 acc)))))
    (define (code-rot v)
      (cond [(= v 2) 0] [(= v 4) 1] [(= v 6) 2] [(= v 9) 3] [else #f]))
    (define base (normalize (find-color g 3)))
    (fold-cells g (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
      (lambda (out r c v)
        (if (and (= v 1) (> c 0))
            (let ((rot (code-rot (at g r (- c 1)))))
              (if (eq? rot #f)
                  out
                  (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (rotate base rot))])
                    (let ((rr (+ r (first p))) (cc (+ c (second p))))
                      (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g))
                          (set-cell acc rr cc 8)
                          acc)))))
            out)))))

title: Extract the Unpaired Shape
written_solution: Group cells into connected objects and compare their shapes after removing translation. Every repeated shape occurs exactly twice except one. Keep only that unique shape, in its original position, recolored to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pt< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (normalize pts)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells pts))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb)))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) r0) (- (second p) c0))) pts) pt<)))
    (define objs (objects g 0))
    (define sigs
      (foldl (lambda (obj acc)
               (let ((sig (normalize (obj-cells obj))))
                 (if (member sig acc) acc (append acc (list sig)))))
             (list) objs))
    (define target-sig
      (first (filter (lambda (sig)
                       (= (count-where (lambda (obj) (equal? (normalize (obj-cells obj)) sig)) objs) 1))
                     sigs)))
    (define target
      (first (filter (lambda (obj) (equal? (normalize (obj-cells obj)) target-sig)) objs)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells target) 8)))

title: Three-Panel Majority Merge
written_solution: Parse the three side-by-side panels and compare them position by position. For each cell location, find whether some non-background color is supported by at least two of the three panels. The output is a single panel that keeps only those majority-supported nonzero cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((divs (filter (lambda (c)
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                       (range 0 (cols g))))
         (d1 (first divs))
         (d2 (second divs)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) d1
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((a (at g r c))
              (b (at g r (+ d1 1 c)))
              (x (at g r (+ d2 1 c))))
          (cond [(and (not (= a 0)) (or (= a b) (= a x))) a]
                [(and (not (= b 0)) (= b x)) b]
                [else 0]))))))

title: Legend-Driven Room Repaint
written_solution: This combines a legend step with a chamber-filling step. The top two rows define how seed colors should be translated into output colors. Each framed chamber contains one seed color from that legend; fill the chamber interior with the mapped output color rather than the original seed color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((mapping (make-hash)))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 obj)) (c1 (obj-c1 obj))
             (r2 (obj-r2 obj)) (c2 (obj-c2 obj))
             (h (+ 1 (- r2 r1))) (w (+ 1 (- c2 c1)))
             (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2)))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
             (= (obj-size obj) perim)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                         (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((old (at g 0 c)) (new (at g 1 c)))
        (when (and (not (= old 0)) (not (= new 0)))
          (hash-set! mapping old new))))
    (let ((body (subgrid g 2 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))))
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (objects (keep-only body 5) 0))])
        (if (frame? obj)
            (let* ((inner (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                                             (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
                   (seeds (remove-duplicates
                           (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                                   (map (lambda (p) (at body (first p) (second p))) inner)))))
              (if (= (length seeds) 1)
                  (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list inner)])
                    (set-cell acc (+ (first p) 2) (second p) (hash-ref mapping (first seeds) (first seeds))))
                  out))
            out)))))

title: Complete the Missing Symmetric Quadrant
written_solution: The gray(5) row and column divide the grid into four equal quadrants. The nonempty quadrants are mirrored versions of the same underlying shape. Recover that canonical shape from any filled quadrant and place the correctly mirrored version into the unique missing quadrant.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pt< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (normalize pts)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells pts))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb)))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) r0) (- (second p) c0))) pts) pt<)))
    (define (mirror-h pts)
      (let ((maxc (apply max (map second pts))))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- maxc (second p)))) pts) pt<)))
    (define (mirror-v pts)
      (let ((maxr (apply max (map first pts))))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- maxr (first p)) (second p))) pts) pt<)))
    (define (orient idx pts)
      (cond [(= idx 1) (mirror-h pts)]
            [(= idx 2) (mirror-v pts)]
            [(= idx 3) (mirror-v (mirror-h pts))]
            [else pts]))
    (define divr (first (filter (lambda (r)
                                  (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g))))
                                (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (define divc (first (filter (lambda (c)
                                  (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                                (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (define qh divr)
    (define qw divc)
    (define quads (list (list 0 0 0)
                        (list 1 0 (+ divc 1))
                        (list 2 (+ divr 1) 0)
                        (list 3 (+ divr 1) (+ divc 1))))
    (define (quad-cells q)
      (let ((r0 (second q)) (c0 (third q)))
        (for*/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r0 qh))]
                    [c (in-range c0 (+ c0 qw))]
                    #:when (let ((v (at g r c))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
          (list (- r r0) (- c c0)))))
    (define source (first (filter (lambda (q) (not (empty? (quad-cells q)))) quads)))
    (define source-cells (quad-cells source))
    (define source-r0 (second source))
    (define source-c0 (third source))
    (define color (at g (+ source-r0 (first (first source-cells)))
                      (+ source-c0 (second (first source-cells)))))
    (define canon (orient (first source) (normalize source-cells)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([q (in-list quads)])
      (let ((cells (quad-cells q)))
        (if (not (empty? cells))
            out
            (let ((r0 (second q)) (c0 (third q)))
              (paint-cells out
                           (map (lambda (p) (list (+ r0 (first p)) (+ c0 (second p))))
                                (orient (first q) canon))
                           color)))))))

title: Count, Select, Move, Recolor
written_solution: This combines a counting selector with a transport step. The top row gives a target area N. Choose the body object of green(3) whose area is N, translate it so that its bbox's top-left corner lands on the anchor cell red(2), recolor it cyan(8), and output only the moved object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0)))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 2)))
         (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (chosen (find-first (lambda (obj) (= (obj-size obj) target))
                             (objects (keep-only body 3) 0))))
    (if (eq? chosen #f)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (let* ((abs-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) 1) (second p))) (obj-cells chosen)))
               (bb (bbox-of-cells abs-cells))
               (dr (- (first anchor) (first bb)))
               (dc (- (second anchor) (second bb))))
          (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list abs-cells)])
            (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr)) (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
              (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                  (set-cell out nr nc 8)
                  out)))))))

title: Mark the midpoint of odd blue segments
written_solution: Find each connected blue(1) component that forms a straight horizontal or vertical segment of odd length at least 3. Recolor only its middle cell to red(2) and leave every other cell unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
    (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
           (rs (map first cells))
           (cs (map second cells)))
      (if (and (>= (length cells) 3)
               (= (remainder (length cells) 2) 1)
               (or (= (min-list rs) (max-list rs)) (= (min-list cs) (max-list cs))))
          (let* ((sorted (sort cells (lambda (a b)
                                       (if (= (min-list rs) (max-list rs))
                                           (< (second a) (second b))
                                           (< (first a) (first b))))))
                 (mid (nth sorted (quotient (length sorted) 2))))
            (set-cell out (first mid) (second mid) 2))
          out))))

title: Complete the missing corner of a red rectangle
written_solution: The red(2) cells are three corners of one axis-aligned rectangle. Add the missing fourth corner as cyan(8); keep the original red(2) corners and all distractors unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((pts (find-color g 2))
         (rs (unique (map first pts)))
         (cs (unique (map second pts)))
         (corners (for*/list ([r rs] [c cs]) (list r c)))
         (missing (find-first (lambda (p) (not (member? p pts))) corners)))
    (if missing (set-cell g (first missing) (second missing) 8) g)))

title: Crop the smallest object
written_solution: Among all non-black(0) connected components, find the smallest one by number of cells. Output only the bounding-box crop of that object, preserving its original color pattern.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (objects g 0))
         (best (argmin (lambda (o) (+ (* 10000 (obj-size o))
                                      (* 1000 (obj-color o))
                                      (* 100 (obj-r1 o))
                                      (obj-c1 o)))
                       objs)))
    (crop-object g best)))

title: Recolor border-touching green components
written_solution: Find every green(3) component. If any cell of that component touches the outer border of the grid, recolor the whole component to yellow(4). Internal green(3) components stay green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))])
    (if (any? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- h 1)) (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- w 1)))) (obj-cells obj))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 4)
        out)))

title: Mirror magenta shapes across an orange divider
written_solution: A full orange(7) line acts as a mirror. Reflect every magenta(6) cell across that divider and draw the reflected copy in cyan(8), while keeping the divider and the original magenta(6) cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((div-row (find-first (lambda (r) (for/and ([c (range 0 w)]) (= (at g r c) 7))) (range 0 h)))
         (div-col (find-first (lambda (c) (for/and ([r (range 0 h)]) (= (at g r c) 7))) (range 0 w))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (find-color g 6)])
      (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
             (nr (if div-col r (- (* 2 div-row) r)))
             (nc (if div-col (- (* 2 div-col) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
            (set-cell out nr nc 8)
            out)))))

title: Fill between matching marker pairs
written_solution: Each non-black(0) color appears as a pair of markers on one row or one column. Fill every cell between the two markers with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (grid-colors g 0)])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 2)
          (let* ((a (first cells))
                 (b (second cells))
                 (r1 (first a)) (c1 (second a)) (r2 (first b)) (c2 (second b)))
            (cond [(= r1 r2) (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect r1 (min c1 c2) r1 (max c1 c2)) color)]
                  [(= c1 c2) (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (min r1 r2) c1 (max r1 r2) c1) color)]
                  [else out]))
          out))))

title: Fill the blue component's bounding box
written_solution: Find the blue(1) object, compute its bbox, and fill the entire box with cyan(8). Other colors remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Fill the tight bounding box of every blue (1) cell with cyan (8).
  ;; Painting the full rectangle replaces the blue cells and background gaps.
  (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 1))))
    (if bb
        (paint-cells g
                     (positions-in-rect
                      (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
                     8)
        g)))

title: Translate the red object by the marker vector
written_solution: Take the red(2) object and compute the vector from the blue(1) marker to the green(3) marker. Remove the original red(2) object and redraw it shifted by that vector in cyan(8), leaving the markers and distractors in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((obj (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
         (a (first (find-color g 1)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first b) (first a)))
         (dc (- (second b) (second a)))
         (cleared (paint-cells g (obj-cells obj) 0))
         (moved (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc))) (obj-cells obj))))
    (paint-cells cleared moved 8)))

title: Rotate the red object according to the control corner
written_solution: The blue(1) control marker sits in one grid corner and encodes a rotation: top-left = 0°, top-right = 90° clockwise, bottom-right = 180°, bottom-left = 270°. Rotate the red(2) object accordingly, normalize it to its own bbox, and output it in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (rmax (max-list (map first norm))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- rmax (first p)))) norm))))
    (define (rot cells k)
      (cond [(= k 0) (normalize-cells cells)]
            [(= k 1) (rot90 cells)]
            [(= k 2) (rot90 (rot90 cells))]
            [else (rot90 (rot90 (rot90 cells)))]))
    (define (crop-cells cells color)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm)))
        (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb))
          (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) color 0)))))
    (let* ((ctrl (first (find-color g 1)))
           (code (cond [(and (= (first ctrl) 0) (= (second ctrl) 0)) 0]
                       [(and (= (first ctrl) 0) (= (second ctrl) (- w 1))) 1]
                       [(and (= (first ctrl) (- h 1)) (= (second ctrl) (- w 1))) 2]
                       [else 3]))
           (obj (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
           (cells (rot (obj-cells obj) code)))
      (crop-cells cells 8))))

title: Flood-fill the chamber containing the seed
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. Starting from the red(2) seed, flood through empty black(0) cells in the same chamber and recolor those reachable background cells to cyan(8). Walls and the seed remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((seed (first (find-color g 2)))
         (region (connected-region g (first seed) (second seed) (lambda (r c v) (or (= v 0) (= v 2))) 4))
         (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) region)))
    (paint-cells g zeros 8)))

title: Count colored components into a bar row
written_solution: Count the number of connected components of red(2), green(3), and yellow(4). Output a single row: first that many 2s, then a 0 separator, then that many 3s, then 0, then that many 4s.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((n2 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
         (n3 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))))
         (n4 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))))
         (ww (+ n2 n3 n4 2)))
    (list (for/list ([c (range 0 ww)])
      (cond [(< c n2) 2]
            [(= c n2) 0]
            [(< c (+ n2 1 n3)) 3]
            [(= c (+ n2 1 n3)) 0]
            [else 4])))))

title: Fill the marked frame's interior with the marker color
written_solution: Several hollow yellow(4) frames are present. A single external marker lies directly beside one frame; use that marker's color to fill the interior of the adjacent frame, leaving the other frames unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1) (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b)) (all? (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)))
    (define (marker-for bb markers)
      (let ((r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb)) (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb)))
        (find-first
          (lambda (m)
            (let ((r (first m)) (c (second m)))
              (or (and (= r (- r0 1)) (<= c0 c) (<= c c1))
                  (and (= r (+ r1 1)) (<= c0 c) (<= c c1))
                  (and (= c (- c0 1)) (<= r0 r) (<= r r1))
                  (and (= c (+ c1 1)) (<= r0 r) (<= r r1)))))
          markers)))
    (let* ((frames (filter (lambda (o)
                             (and (= (obj-color o) 4)
                                  ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of o
                                  (let ((bb (obj-bbox o)))
                                    (same-cells? (obj-cells o) (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))
                           (objects g 0)))
           ;; Cells filtered out of every (r,c) position
           (markers (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 4))))) (grid-positions g)))
           (hit (find-first (lambda (o) (marker-for (obj-bbox o) markers)) frames)))
      (if hit
          ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of hit
          (let* ((bb (obj-bbox hit))
                 (marker (marker-for bb markers))
                 (fill (at g (first marker) (second marker)))
                 ;; Positions of every color 0 cell
                 (inside (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))
                                 (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1) (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))))
            (paint-cells g inside fill))
          g))))

title: Intersect row-spans and column-spans
written_solution: Red(2) marker pairs define horizontal spans on their rows, and green(3) marker pairs define vertical spans on their columns. Output a background grid with cyan(8) exactly where a chosen row span and a chosen column span overlap.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((row-spans
          (filter (lambda (span) span)
            (for/list ([r (range 0 h)])
              (let ((cs (for/list ([c (range 0 w)] #:when (= (at g r c) 2)) c)))
                (if (>= (length cs) 2) (list r (min-list cs) (max-list cs)) #f)))))
         (col-spans
          (filter (lambda (span) span)
            (for/list ([c (range 0 w)])
              (let ((rs (for/list ([r (range 0 h)] #:when (= (at g r c) 3)) r)))
                (if (>= (length rs) 2) (list c (min-list rs) (max-list rs)) #f))))))
    (foldl
      (lambda (row-span out)
        (foldl
          (lambda (col-span acc)
            (let ((r (first row-span)) (c0 (second row-span)) (c1 (third row-span))
                  (c (first col-span)) (r0 (second col-span)) (r1 (third col-span)))
              (if (and (<= c0 c) (<= c c1) (<= r0 r) (<= r r1))
                  (set-cell acc r c 8)
                  acc)))
          out
          col-spans))
      (empty-grid h w 0)
      row-spans)))

title: Pack objects left-to-right by size
written_solution: Extract every non-black(0) component, crop each one to its own bbox, sort them by size from smallest to largest, and concatenate those crops left-to-right with one background separator column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (piece obj)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm)))
        (list (obj-color obj) norm (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) (obj-size obj))))
    (define (piece< a b)
      (cond [(not (= (nth a 4) (nth b 4))) (< (nth a 4) (nth b 4))]
            [else (< (first a) (first b))]))
    (define pieces (sort (map piece (objects g 0)) piece<))
    (define widths (map (lambda (p) (nth p 3)) pieces))
    (define hh (if (empty? pieces) 1 (max-list (map (lambda (p) (nth p 2)) pieces))))
    (define ww (if (empty? pieces) 1 (+ (apply + widths) (max 0 (- (length pieces) 1)))))
    (first
      (foldl
        (lambda (p state)
          (let* ((out (first state))
                 (offset (second state))
                 (color (first p))
                 (cells (map (lambda (cell) (list (first cell) (+ offset (second cell)))) (second p)))
                 (painted (paint-cells out cells color)))
            (list painted (+ offset (nth p 3) 1))))
        (list (empty-grid hh ww 0) 0)
        pieces))))

title: Mark cells that lie on every shortest path
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls, red(2) as start, and green(3) as goal. Consider all shortest paths from start to goal through black(0) cells. Output a background grid with cyan(8) only on cells that belong to every shortest path.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (passable? r c) (member? (at g r c) (list 0 2 3)))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (passable? nr nc)
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dt (dist-from goal))
    (define D (hash-ref ds (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 999999))
    (define path-cells
      (sort (filter (lambda (p)
                      (and (passable? (first p) (second p))
                           (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons (first p) (second p)) 999999)
                                 (hash-ref dt (cons (first p) (second p)) 999999))
                              D)))
                    (grid-positions g))
            (lambda (a b) (< (hash-ref ds (cons (first a) (second a)))
                             (hash-ref ds (cons (first b) (second b)))))))
    (define cs (make-hash))
    (hash-set! cs (cons (first start) (second start)) 1)
    (for ([p (in-list path-cells)])
      (define cur (cons (first p) (second p)))
      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (let ((nr (+ (first p) (first d))) (nc (+ (second p) (second d))))
          (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                     (passable? nr nc)
                     (= (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc) 999999) (+ (hash-ref ds cur) 1))
                     (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc) 999999) (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc) 999999)) D))
            (hash-update! cs (cons nr nc) (lambda (x) (+ x (hash-ref cs cur 0))) 0)))))
    (define ct (make-hash))
    (hash-set! ct (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 1)
    (for ([p (in-list (sort path-cells (lambda (a b) (< (hash-ref dt (cons (first a) (second a)))
                                                         (hash-ref dt (cons (first b) (second b)))))))])
      (define cur (cons (first p) (second p)))
      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (let ((nr (+ (first p) (first d))) (nc (+ (second p) (second d))))
          (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                     (passable? nr nc)
                     (= (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc) 999999) (+ (hash-ref dt cur) 1))
                     (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc) 999999) (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc) 999999)) D))
            (hash-update! ct (cons nr nc) (lambda (x) (+ x (hash-ref ct cur 0))) 0)))))
    (define total (hash-ref cs (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 0))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (passable? r c)
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c) 999999) (hash-ref dt (cons r c) 999999)) D)
                 (= (* (hash-ref cs (cons r c) 0) (hash-ref ct (cons r c) 0)) total))
            8
            0)))))

title: Mark maze cells equidistant to both seeds
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. Compute the shortest-path distance from every reachable empty cell to the red(2) seed and to the green(3) seed. Output a background grid with cyan(8) wherever those two maze distances are equal.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (passable? r c) (member? (at g r c) (list 0 2 3)))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (passable? nr nc)
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (passable? r c)
                 (hash-has-key? da (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? db (cons r c))
                 (= (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c))))
            8
            0)))))

title: XOR one shape with a control-rotated second shape
written_solution: Normalize the red(2) shape and the green(3) shape to their own bounding boxes. The blue(1) corner control chooses a rotation for the green(3) shape. Rotate that green(3) shape, then output the cellwise XOR of the two normalized shapes as a cropped cyan(8) shape.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define ctrl (first (find-color g 1)))
    (define code (cond [(and (= (first ctrl) 0) (= (second ctrl) 0)) 0]
                       [(and (= (first ctrl) 0) (= (second ctrl) (- (cols g) 1))) 1]
                       [(and (= (first ctrl) (- (rows g) 1)) (= (second ctrl) (- (cols g) 1))) 2]
                       [else 3]))
    (define a (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
    (define b (rotate (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0)))) code))
    (define xor (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p b))) a)
                        (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p a))) b)))
    (if (empty? xor)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells xor))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Fill the depth-selected band between nested frames
written_solution: Sort the nested yellow(4) frames from outside to inside. The number of blue(1) markers selects a depth. If that depth is not the innermost frame, fill the band between that frame and the next inner frame with cyan(8); if it is the innermost frame, fill its interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 4)
                                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (- (obj-r2 a) (obj-r1 a)) (- (obj-c2 a) (obj-c1 a)))
                             (* (- (obj-r2 b) (obj-r1 b)) (- (obj-c2 b) (obj-c1 b)))))))
    (define k (length (find-color g 1)))
    (if (and (not (empty? frames)) (> k 0))
        (if (< k (length frames))
            (let ((outer (list-ref frames (- k 1)))
                  (inner (list-ref frames k)))
              (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 outer) 1) (obj-r2 outer))]
                                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 outer) 1) (obj-c2 outer))])
                (if (and (= (at out r c) 0)
                         (not (and (>= r (obj-r1 inner)) (<= r (obj-r2 inner))
                                   (>= c (obj-c1 inner)) (<= c (obj-c2 inner)))))
                    (set-cell out r c 8)
                    out)))
            (let ((inner (last frames)))
              (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 inner) 1) (obj-r2 inner))]
                                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 inner) 1) (obj-c2 inner))])
                (if (= (at out r c) 0) (set-cell out r c 8) out))))
        g)))

title: Trace a beam through mirrors
written_solution: A beam starts at the red(2) source and travels inward from the border. Gray(5) cells stop it. Backslash mirrors (6) and slash mirrors (7) turn it. Output a background grid with cyan(8) on every cell the beam visits.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((source (first (find-color g 2))))
    (define (start-dir)
      (cond [(= (first source) 0) (list 1 0)]
            [(= (first source) (- (rows g) 1)) (list -1 0)]
            [(= (second source) 0) (list 0 1)]
            [(= (second source) (- (cols g) 1)) (list 0 -1)]
            [else (list 0 1)]))
    (define (slash dr dc) (list (- 0 dc) (- 0 dr)))
    (define (backslash dr dc) (list dc dr))
    (let* ((d0 (start-dir)))
      (let loop ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]
                 [r (first source)] [c (second source)]
                 [dr (first d0)] [dc (second d0)] [fuel 500])
        (let ((nr (+ r dr)) (nc (+ c dc)))
          (if (or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))) (= (at g nr nc) 5))
              out
              (let* ((v (at g nr nc))
                     (next-out (set-cell out nr nc 8))
                     (nd (cond [(= v 7) (slash dr dc)]
                               [(= v 6) (backslash dr dc)]
                               [else (list dr dc)])))
                (loop next-out nr nc (first nd) (second nd) (- fuel 1)))))))))

title: Extract the odd shape up to dihedral symmetry
written_solution: All components are red(2). Most components are the same shape up to rotation/reflection, but one is different. Find the outlier, convert it to its canonical orientation under the dihedral group, and output that normalized shape in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (shape-key cells) (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-v cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) norm))))
    (define (variants cells)
      (remove-duplicates
       (append* (map (lambda (k)
                       (let ((rot (rotate cells k)))
                         (list (normalize-cells rot) (rotate (reflect-v cells) k))))
                     (list 0 1 2 3)))))
    (define (canonical cells)
      (first (sort (variants cells) (lambda (a b) (string<? (shape-key a) (shape-key b))))))
    (define comps (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))
    (define counts (make-hash))
    (for ([obj (in-list comps)])
      (hash-update! counts (shape-key (canonical (obj-cells obj))) add1 0))
    (define odd (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (hash-ref counts (shape-key (canonical (obj-cells o)))) 1)) comps)))
    (let* ((cells (canonical (obj-cells odd)))
           (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells))))
           (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
      (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) cells) 8 0))))))

title: Control-rotate and vector-shift the template
written_solution: Take the red(2) template, rotate it according to the blue(1) control corner, then translate it by the vector from the green(3) marker to the magenta(6) marker. Place the transformed template on a background grid in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])

title: Dual Legend Chooses Holes and Symmetry
written_solution: This puzzle combines two legends. The first header row gives the target number of holes by using one extra blue(1) cell, so 1→0 holes, 2→1 hole, and 3→2 holes. The second header row chooses the symmetry class with the code 1 vertical-only, 2 horizontal-only, 3 both, 4 none. The body object matching both conditions is cropped and recolored to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Two header rows spell a query: (count of 1s in row 0) - 1 = the
 ;; HOLE count, count of 2s in row 1 = the SYMMETRY class (1 -> 
 ;; left-right, 2 -> up-down, 3 -> both, else none). Scan the body
 ;; (rows 2+) in top-left order and answer with the first object
 ;; matching both, as its shape mask painted cyan(8).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (norm-cells obj)
       (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                              (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj))))
            (obj-cells obj)))
     (define (mask-of obj color)
       (paint-cells (empty-grid (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj) 0)
                    (norm-cells obj) color))
     (define (holes-of obj)  ;; enclosed 0-pockets of the shape mask
       (let ((mask (mask-of obj 1)))
         (length (filter (lambda (region)
                           (all? (lambda (p)
                                   (and (> (first p) 0)
                                        (< (first p) (- (rows mask) 1))
                                        (> (second p) 0)
                                        (< (second p)
                                           (- (cols mask) 1))))
                                 region))
                         (find-0-regions mask 0)))))
     (define (sym-class obj)  ;; up-down adds 1, left-right adds 2
       (let ((cells (norm-cells obj)))
         (+ (if (all? (lambda (p)
                        (member (list (- (obj-h obj) 1 (first p))
                                      (second p))
                                cells))
                      cells)
                1 0)
            (if (all? (lambda (p)
                        (member (list (first p)
                                      (- (obj-w obj) 1 (second p)))
                                cells))
                      cells)
                2 0))))
     (define holes-target
       (max (- (count-if (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0)) 1) 0))
     (define sym-target
       (let ((code (count-if (lambda (v) (= v 2)) (row g 1))))
         (cond ((= code 1) 2) ((= code 2) 1) ((= code 3) 3) (else 0))))
     (define target
       (find-first (lambda (o) (and (= (holes-of o) holes-target)
                                    (= (sym-class o) sym-target)))
                   (sort (objects (subgrid g 2 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)) 0)
                         (lambda (a b)
                           (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                               (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))))))
     (mask-of target 8))))

title: Feature Analogy Across Two Panels
written_solution: The left panel provides a reference object, highlighted in red(2). Its feature triple is transferred across the separator into the right panel, where the matching candidate is extracted, cropped, and recolored to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Two panels split by a full gray(5) column. The LEFT panel's red(2)
 ;; object defines a feature TRIPLE — (area, enclosed-hole count, symmetry
 ;; class: 0 none / 1 up-down / 2 left-right / 3 both). Output the first
 ;; (top-left order) RIGHT-panel object with the same triple, as its
 ;; cropped shape mask painted cyan(8).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (norm-cells obj)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
         (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb))
                                (- (second p) (second bb))))
              (obj-cells obj))))
     (define (mask-of obj color)
       (paint-cells (empty-grid (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj) 0)
                    (norm-cells obj) color))
     (define (holes-of obj)
       ;; enclosed 0-regions of the shape mask (none touching its border)
       (let ((mask (mask-of obj 1)))
         (length (filter (lambda (region)
                           (all? (lambda (p)
                                   (and (> (first p) 0)
                                        (< (first p) (- (rows mask) 1))
                                        (> (second p) 0)
                                        (< (second p) (- (cols mask) 1))))
                                 region))
                         (find-0-regions mask 0)))))
     (define (sym-class obj)
       (let ((cells (norm-cells obj)))
         (+ (if (all? (lambda (p) (member (list (- (obj-h obj) 1 (first p))
                                               (second p))
                                         cells))
                      cells)
                1 0)
            (if (all? (lambda (p) (member (list (first p)
                                               (- (obj-w obj) 1 (second p)))
                                         cells))
                      cells)
                2 0))))
     (define (triple obj)
       (list (obj-size obj) (holes-of obj) (sym-class obj)))
     (define seps
       (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5))
                                 (range 0 (rows g))))
               (range 0 (cols g))))
     (define ref (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (first seps) 1)))
     (define cand
       (subgrid g 0 (+ (first seps) 1) (- (rows g) 1)
                (if (> (length seps) 1)
                    (- (second seps) 1)
                    (- (cols g) 1))))
     (define target-feat
       (triple (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2))
                              (objects ref 0)))))
     (define target
       (first (filter (lambda (o) (equal? (triple o) target-feat))
                      (sort (objects cand 0)
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                                (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                                    (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                                         (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))))
     (mask-of target 8))))

title: Header Chooses Rank Within a Symmetry Class
written_solution: The first header row names a symmetry class using the code 1 vertical-only, 2 horizontal-only, 3 both, 4 none. After filtering the body objects to that class, the second header row gives the area rank to take. The selected object is then cropped and recolored to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Two header rows spell a query: count of 1s in row 0 = the SYMMETRY
 ;; class (1 -> left-right, 2 -> up-down, 3 -> both, else none), count
 ;; of 2s in row 1 = the RANK k. Among the body objects (rows 2+) with
 ;; that symmetry, ranked biggest-first (ties top-left), answer with
 ;; the k-th — its shape mask painted cyan(8).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (norm-cells obj)
       (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                              (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj))))
            (obj-cells obj)))
     (define (mask-of obj color)
       (paint-cells (empty-grid (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj) 0)
                    (norm-cells obj) color))
     (define (sym-class obj)  ;; up-down adds 1, left-right adds 2
       (let ((cells (norm-cells obj)))
         (+ (if (all? (lambda (p)
                        (member (list (- (obj-h obj) 1 (first p))
                                      (second p))
                                cells))
                      cells)
                1 0)
            (if (all? (lambda (p)
                        (member (list (first p)
                                      (- (obj-w obj) 1 (second p)))
                                cells))
                      cells)
                2 0))))
     (define sym-target
       (let ((code (count-if (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0))))
         (cond ((= code 1) 2) ((= code 2) 1) ((= code 3) 3) (else 0))))
     (define k (count-if (lambda (v) (= v 2)) (row g 1)))
     (define candidates  ;; matching symmetry, biggest first
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (sym-class o) sym-target))
                     (objects (subgrid g 2 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)) 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                   (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                       (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                       (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                   (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
     (mask-of (nth candidates (- k 1)) 8))))

title: Recolor left-right symmetric red components
written_solution: Look at every red(2) component by itself. If its shape is symmetric under a left-right mirror inside its own bbox, recolor the whole component to green(3). Leave asymmetric red(2) components and all other colors unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (hmirror cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second n)))))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) n) cell<?)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (equal? (norm (obj-cells obj)) (hmirror (obj-cells obj)))
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
          out))))

title: Fill diagonal gaps between yellow pairs
written_solution: Whenever two yellow(4) cells sit one step away from the same empty cell on a diagonal, fill that empty midpoint with cyan(8). Do this for both diagonal directions and keep everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (or (and (= (safe-at g (- r 1) (- c 1) 0) 4)
                        (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 0) 4))
                   (and (= (safe-at g (- r 1) (+ c 1) 0) 4)
                        (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) (- c 1) 0) 4))))
          8
          (at g r c)))))

title: Turn solid blue rectangles into hollow rectangles
written_solution: Every blue(1) object is a solid axis-aligned rectangle. Remove its interior cells and keep only the border, so each solid rectangle becomes a hollow rectangle.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (foldl (lambda (p acc)
             (if (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                      (> (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 obj)))
                 (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 0)
                 acc))
           out
           (obj-cells obj))))

title: Recolor the corner cell of each green L-triomino
written_solution: Among the green(3) size-3 objects, only the L-shaped triominoes change. In each L, the bend cell where the two arms meet becomes red(2). Straight size-3 lines stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (degree p cells)
      (count-where (lambda (d) (member? (list (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d))) cells))
                   cardinal-deltas))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o)
                                                 (and (= (obj-color o) 3)
                                                      (= (obj-size o) 3)
                                                      (= (obj-h o) 2)
                                                      (= (obj-w o) 2)))
                                               (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((corners (filter (lambda (p) (= (degree p (obj-cells obj)) 2)) (obj-cells obj))))
        (if (= (length corners) 1)
            (set-cell out (first (first corners)) (second (first corners)) 2)
            out)))))

title: Recolor orange components that touch a grid corner
written_solution: Check every orange(7) component. If any cell of that component sits in one of the four corners of the whole grid, recolor the entire component to blue(1). Other orange(7) components stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g))
         (corners (list (list 0 0) (list 0 (- w 1)) (list (- h 1) 0) (list (- h 1) (- w 1)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 7)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (any? (lambda (p) (member? p corners)) (obj-cells obj))
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 1)
          out))))

title: Recolor the smallest red component
written_solution: Compare the red(2) connected components by area. The unique smallest one becomes cyan(8); all larger red(2) components and any distractor colors stay as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((reds (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))
         (target (first (sort reds (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (paint-cells g (obj-cells target) 8)))

title: Grow a blue plus around each red singleton
written_solution: Each red(2) singleton grows a blue(1) orthogonal halo. Paint the up, down, left, and right neighbors blue(1) wherever those neighbor cells are empty. Keep the red(2) center and any blockers unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o)
                                      (and (= (obj-color o) 2)
                                           (= (obj-size o) 1)))
                                    (objects g 0)))]
              [d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
    (let* ((p (first (obj-cells obj)))
           (nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
           (nc (+ (second p) (second d))))
      (if (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
               (zero? (at g nr nc)))
          (set-cell out nr nc 1)
          out))))

title: Top legend remaps object colors
written_solution: The top two rows form a color legend: each nonzero source color in row 0 maps to the aligned nonzero target color in row 1. Recolor every object below the legend using that mapping, while leaving the legend rows themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((mapping
         (filter (lambda (p) (and (not (= (first p) 0)) (not (= (second p) 0))))
                 (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))]) (list (at g 0 c) (at g 1 c))))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (at g r c))
               (hit (filter (lambda (p) (= (first p) v)) mapping)))
          (if (and (>= r 2) (not (empty? hit)))
              (second (first hit))
              v))))))

title: Match objects to a template shape
written_solution: The unique cyan(8) template object shows the target shape. Any red(2) object whose normalized shape matches the template is recolored to green(3); non-matching red(2) objects stay red(2). The template itself stays cyan(8).
