(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define template (norm (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 8)) (objects g 0))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (equal? (norm (obj-cells obj)) template)
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
          out))))

title: Draw rectangle outlines from opposite-corner markers
written_solution: Each non-background color appears exactly twice as single markers. Treat those two cells as opposite corners of a rectangle and draw the rectangle outline in that same color, keeping the corner markers as part of the border.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (sort (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g)) <)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (let* ((a (first pts))
                   (b (second pts))
                   (r1 (min (first a) (first b)))
                   (r2 (max (first a) (first b)))
                   (c1 (min (second a) (second b)))
                   (c2 (max (second a) (second b)))
                   (cells (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                                                   (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                                  (positions-in-rect r1 c1 r2 c2))))
              (paint-cells out cells color))
            out)))))

title: Slide all objects rightward until the wall
written_solution: The gray(5) vertical line is a wall. Remove the colored objects on its left, then slide each whole object rigidly to the right until the next step would hit the wall or another settled object. Shapes and colors are preserved.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define movable
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (or (= (obj-color o) 2) (= (obj-color o) 3) (= (obj-color o) 4))) (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (obj-c2 a) (obj-c2 b))
                  (> (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                  (> (obj-c2 a) (obj-c2 b))))))
    (define cleared (foldl (lambda (obj acc) (erase-cells acc (obj-cells obj) 0)) g movable))
    (define occupied
      (for/set ([cell (in-list (grid-cells cleared))] #:when (= (third cell) 5))
        (cons (first cell) (second cell))))
    (define (blocked? cells occ)
      (any? (lambda (p)
              (or (not (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
                  (set-member? occ (cons (first p) (second p)))))
            cells))
    (define (shift cells) (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (+ (second p) 1))) cells))
    (define (slide-cells cells occ)
      (let loop ([cur cells])
        (let ((nxt (shift cur)))
          (if (blocked? nxt occ) cur (loop nxt)))))
    (let-values ([(out final-occ)
                  (for/fold ([out cleared] [occ occupied]) ([obj (in-list movable)])
                    (let* ((landed (slide-cells (obj-cells obj) occ))
                           (new-out (paint-cells out landed (obj-color obj)))
                           (new-occ (for/fold ([o occ]) ([p (in-list landed)])
                                      (set-add o (cons (first p) (second p))))))
                      (values new-out new-occ)))])
      out)))

title: Rotate each blue object using its control marker
written_solution: Each magenta(6) object has a control digit immediately above the top-left corner of its bbox. The digit says how much to rotate that object within its own square box: 1 → identity, 2 → 90° clockwise, 3 → 180°, and 4 → 270° clockwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (renorm cells) (normalize-cells cells))
    (define (rot90 cells h w) (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells)))
    (define (rot180 cells h w) (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells)))
    (define (rot270 cells h w) (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- w 1 (second p)) (first p))) cells)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))])
      (let* ((code (safe-at g (- (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-c1 obj) 0))
             (shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
             (hh (obj-h obj))
             (ww (obj-w obj))
             (tshape (cond [(= code 1) shape]
                           [(= code 2) (rot90 shape hh ww)]
                           [(= code 3) (rot180 shape hh ww)]
                           [else (rot270 shape hh ww)]))
             (cleared (erase-cells out (obj-cells obj) 0))
             (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) (first p)) (+ (obj-c1 obj) (second p)))) tshape)))
        (paint-cells cleared placed 6)))))

title: Recolor objects by number of holes
written_solution: Every object starts as magenta(6), but its final color depends on how many enclosed holes it contains. Components with no holes become red(2), components with one hole become green(3), and components with two or more holes become yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((n (topo-count-holes g obj 0))
           (color (cond [(= n 0) 2] [(= n 1) 3] [else 4])))
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color))))

title: Marker count selects the matching-size object
written_solution: Count the blue(1) markers in the top row. Then find the red(2) component below whose area equals that count and recolor that entire component to green(3). The other red(2) objects stay red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((target (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (= (obj-size obj) target)
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
          out))))

title: Fill the common interior of all hollow frames
written_solution: Each colored hollow rectangle contributes its interior region. Compute the overlap common to all of those interiors and fill exactly that common region with red(2), while leaving the original frames in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define frames
      (filter (lambda (obj)
                (and (not (= (obj-color obj) 8))
                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))))
              (objects g 0)))
    (if (empty? frames)
        g
        (let* ((first-interior (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 (first frames)) 1)
                                                  (+ (obj-c1 (first frames)) 1)
                                                  (- (obj-r2 (first frames)) 1)
                                                  (- (obj-c2 (first frames)) 1)))
               (common (filter (lambda (p)
                                  (all? (lambda (obj)
                                          (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                                               (> (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                                        frames))
                                first-interior)))
          (paint-cells g common 2)))))

title: Flood each chamber by distance modulo 3
written_solution: Use the seeds of red(2) as BFS sources and treat gray(5) cells as walls. Every reachable floor cell is recolored by its shortest-path distance modulo 3: distance 0 becomes green(3), distance 1 becomes yellow(4), and distance 2 becomes gray(5).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dist (make-hash)))
    (define queue (map (lambda (p) (cons (first p) (second p))) (find-color g 2)))
    (for ([p (in-list queue)]) (hash-set! dist p 0))
    (let bfs ([step 0])
      (unless (empty? queue)
        (let ((cur (first queue)))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
            (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                  (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
              (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                         (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc)))
                         (or (= (at g nr nc) 0) (= (at g nr nc) 2)))
                (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
        (bfs (+ step 1))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (hash-has-key? dist (cons r c))
            (let ((m (modulo (hash-ref dist (cons r c)) 3)))
              (cond [(= m 0) 3] [(= m 1) 4] [else 5]))
            (at g r c))))))

title: Stamp the common intersection of multiple shapes
written_solution: Normalize all red(2) objects to their own top-left corners and intersect their cell sets. The shared subshape is then stamped in green(3) starting at the anchor cell marked 9, and the output contains only that stamped result.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shapes (map (lambda (obj) (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
                      (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
         (base (first shapes))
         (common (filter (lambda (p) (all? (lambda (s) (member? p s)) shapes)) base))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
         (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) common)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 3)))

title: Compose multiple transforms from a control strip
written_solution: Take the unique blue(1) template and apply the bottom control-strip operations from left to right. Here blue(1) → 90° clockwise, red(2) → 180°, green(3) → flip horizontal, yellow(4) → flip vertical. Stamp the final transformed shape in green(3) at the maroon(9) anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define template (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
    (define (renorm cells) (normalize-cells cells))
    (define (rot90 cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells)) w h))
    (define (rot180 cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells)) h w))
    (define (flip-h cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells)) h w))
    (define (flip-v cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) cells)) h w))
    (define start (list (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)) (obj-h template) (obj-w template)))
    (define ops (filter (lambda (v) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4))) (row g (- (rows g) 1))))
    (define final
      (foldl (lambda (op state)
               (let ((cells (first state)) (hh (second state)) (ww (third state)))
                 (cond [(= op 1) (rot90 cells hh ww)]
                       [(= op 2) (rot180 cells hh ww)]
                       [(= op 3) (flip-h cells hh ww)]
                       [else (flip-v cells hh ww)])))
             start
             ops))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
    (define placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) (first final)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 3)))

title: Extract the hole of the selected hollow object
written_solution: the unique selector color in the top row tells you which hollow object to use. Find the non-singleton object with that same color, extract the shape of its hole region, normalize it, and stamp that hole pattern at the anchor in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((selector (first (filter (lambda (v) (and (>= v 2) (<= v 7))) (row g 0))))
         (target (first (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) selector) (> (obj-size o) 1))) (objects g 0))))
         (regions (find-0-regions g 0))
         (holes (append* (filter (lambda (reg)
                                   (all? (lambda (p)
                                           (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 target)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 target))
                                                (> (second p) (obj-c1 target)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 target))))
                                         reg))
                                 regions)))
         (shape (normalize-cells holes))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
         (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 8)))

title: Stamp dihedral variants of a template at local anchors
written_solution: Each anchor 9 has a control code immediately to its left. That code selects one of the 8 dihedral transforms of the template shape—identity, rotations, flips, and diagonal reflections. Stamp the chosen variant at each anchor in green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define template (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
    (define (renorm cells) (normalize-cells cells))
    (define (rot90 cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells)) w h))
    (define (rot180 cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells)) h w))
    (define (rot270 cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- w 1 (second p)) (first p))) cells)) w h))
    (define (flip-h cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells)) h w))
    (define (flip-v cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) cells)) h w))
    (define (flip-d cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (first p))) cells)) w h))
    (define (flip-a cells h w) (list (renorm (map (lambda (p) (list (- w 1 (second p)) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells)) w h))
    (define base (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)))
    (define (apply-code code)
      (cond [(= code 1) (list base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 2) (rot90 base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 3) (rot180 base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 4) (rot270 base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 5) (flip-h base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 6) (flip-v base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [(= code 7) (flip-d base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]
            [else (flip-a base (obj-h template) (obj-w template))]))
    (foldl (lambda (anchor out)
             (let* ((code (safe-at g (first anchor) (- (second anchor) 1) 0))
                    (shape (first (apply-code code)))
                    (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)))
               (paint-cells out placed 3)))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           (find-color g 9))))

title: Stamp the shape difference A minus B
written_solution: Normalize the red(2) A-shape and the yellow(4) B-shape to their own top-left corners. Subtract the B cells from the A cells and stamp the remaining difference shape at the maroon(9) anchor in magenta(6).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
         (b (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))))))
         (diff (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p b))) a))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
         (placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) diff)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) placed 6)))

title: Left-column row painters
written_solution: Look only at the leftmost column. If a row starts with a non-background color, repaint that entire row with that color. Rows whose first cell is 0 stay all 0.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (paint grid cells color) (for/fold ((out grid)) ((p (in-list cells))) (if (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) color) out))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (let ((color (at g r 0))) (if (= color 0) out (paint out (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (cols g))) color))))))

title: Fill horizontal same-color gaps
written_solution: Scan each row. Whenever two matching nonzero cells are separated by exactly one background cell, fill that background with the same color. Leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (- (cols g) 2)))) (let ((a (at g r c)) (b (at g r (+ c 1))) (d (at g r (+ c 2)))) (if (and (not (= a 0)) (= a d) (= b 0)) (set-cell out r (+ c 1) a) out)))))

title: Bottom-row up-left diagonals
written_solution: Ignore all rows except the last one. For each nonzero seed there, paint that color on the seed itself and on every cell reached by stepping one row up and one column left until you hit the border.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((color (at g (- (rows g) 1) c))) (if (= color 0) out (let loop ((k 0) (acc out)) (let ((r (- (- (rows g) 1) k)) (cc (- c k))) (if (or (< r 0) (< cc 0)) acc (loop (+ k 1) (set-cell acc r cc color))))))))))

title: Keep only border-touching components
written_solution: Find every nonzero component. Keep a component only if at least one of its cells touches the outer grid border. Erase the rest.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (paint grid cells color) (for/fold ((out grid)) ((p (in-list cells))) (if (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) color) out))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((obj (in-list (objects g 0)))) (if (any? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- (rows g) 1)) (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- (cols g) 1)))) (obj-cells obj)) (paint out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj)) out))))

title: Fill between row endpoints
written_solution: For each row, look for repeated occurrences of the same non-background color. Fill every cell from that color’s leftmost occurrence to its rightmost occurrence, inclusive.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (paint grid cells color) (for/fold ((out grid)) ((p (in-list cells))) (if (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) color) out))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((color (in-list (grid-colors (list (list-ref g r)) 0)))) (let ((cols-hit (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) color)) (range (cols g))))) (if (>= (length cols-hit) 2) (paint acc (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (apply min cols-hit) (+ (apply max cols-hit) 1))) color) acc))))))

title: Recolor each row by its header cell
written_solution: In every row, use the first cell as that row’s header color. Any nonzero cell elsewhere in the same row is rewritten to the header color, while 0s stay 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Each row's LEADING cell is a header: the row's non-zeros take its color
 ;; (an empty header leaves them unchanged).
 (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
   (let ((header (at g r 0)) (v (at g r c)))
     (if (= v 0) 0 (if (= header 0) v header))))))

title: Mirror rows around 9 anchors
written_solution: For each row containing a maroon(9), reflect every nonzero non-maroon(9) cell across that maroon(9)’s column. Keep the original cells too, so the final row becomes symmetric around the anchor.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (let ((anchors (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range (cols g))))) (if (empty? anchors) out (let ((a (first anchors))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g r c)) (mc (- (* 2 a) c))) (if (and (not (member? v (list 0 9))) (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g))) (set-cell acc r mc v) acc)))))))))

title: Hinge reflection around a 9 pivot
written_solution: Find the unique 9 anchor and the unique colored object. If the object lies entirely on one side of the anchor, reflect it across the anchor’s vertical or horizontal line and keep both the original and reflected copies.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((pivot (first (find-color g 9))) (pr (first pivot)) (pc (second pivot)) (objs (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? (at g (first p) (second p)) (list 0 9)))) (grid-positions g))) (rs (map first objs)) (cs (map second objs))) (cond ((empty? objs) g) ((or (< (apply max cs) pc) (> (apply min cs) pc)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((p (in-list objs))) (let ((mc (- (* 2 pc) (second p)))) (if (in-bounds? (first p) mc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out (first p) mc (at g (first p) (second p))) out)))) ((or (< (apply max rs) pr) (> (apply min rs) pr)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((p (in-list objs))) (let ((mr (- (* 2 pr) (first p)))) (if (in-bounds? mr (second p) (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out mr (second p) (at g (first p) (second p))) out)))) (else g)))))

title: Palette by component size
written_solution: Ignore the top row except as a palette. In the body, detect the three connected components, sort them from smallest to largest, and recolor them using the top-row colors in that same order.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (paint grid cells color) (for/fold ((out grid)) ((p (in-list cells))) (if (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) color) out))) (let* ((palette (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g))) (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))) (objs (sort (objects body 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))) (let ((base (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((c (in-range (cols g)))) (set-cell out 0 c (at g 0 c))))) (for/fold ((out base)) ((obj (in-list objs)) (i (in-naturals))) (paint out (map (lambda (p) (list (+ 1 (first p)) (second p))) (obj-cells obj)) (list-ref palette i)))))))

title: Sweep shapes through corridors
written_solution: Treat 8s as walls. For every nonzero non-wall cell, paint its color to the right along the same row until just before the next wall or the edge. Keep walls unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g r c))) (if (member? v (list 0 8)) out (let* ((walls (filter (lambda (wc) (and (> wc c) (= (at g r wc) 8))) (range (cols g)))) (stop (if (empty? walls) (cols g) (first walls)))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((x (in-range c stop))) (if (= (at acc r x) 0) (set-cell acc r x v) acc))))))))

title: Infer a transform from two panels and apply it to a third
written_solution: Split the input into three panels separated by full cyan(8) columns. Identify which geometric transform maps the first panel to the second; apply that same transform to the third panel and output it.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define transform-names (list 'id 'rot90 'rot180 'rot270 'flip-h 'flip-v 'transpose 'anti-transpose)) (define (anti-transpose-grid grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid))) (define (apply-transform-name name grid) (cond ((equal? name 'id) grid) ((equal? name 'rot90) (rotate-cw grid)) ((equal? name 'rot180) (rotate-180 grid)) ((equal? name 'rot270) (rotate-ccw grid)) ((equal? name 'flip-h) (flip-lr grid)) ((equal? name 'flip-v) (flip-ud grid)) ((equal? name 'transpose) (transpose grid)) (else (anti-transpose-grid grid)))) (define (split-full-sep-cols grid sep) (let* ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) sep)) (range (rows grid)))) (range (cols grid))))) (let loop ((cuts (append seps (list (cols grid)))) (start 0) (acc (list))) (if (empty? cuts) (reverse acc) (let ((c (first cuts))) (loop (rest cuts) (+ c 1) (cons (subgrid grid 0 start (- (rows grid) 1) (- c 1)) acc))))))) (define (transform-name-exact a b) (first (filter (lambda (name) (equal? (apply-transform-name name a) b)) transform-names))) (let* ((panels (split-full-sep-cols g 8)) (name (transform-name-exact (first panels) (second panels)))) (apply-transform-name name (third panels)))))

title: Translate an object by a guide vector
written_solution: Find marker green(3), marker yellow(4), and the remaining colored object. Compute the vector from green(3) to yellow(4), move the whole object by that vector, erase the original object, and keep the markers in place.

title: Vector shadow copy

title: Roomwise nearest-seed fill with ties blank
written_solution: gray(5) 5-cells are walls. Inside each connected chamber of non-wall cells, colored seeds spread through shortest paths. Fill each empty cell with the color of its uniquely nearest seed within that chamber. If two different seeds are tied for nearest, leave that cell empty.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Geodesic Voronoi: every empty cell takes the color of its NEAREST seed,
 ;; where distance flows through non-wall cells (gray 5 = wall). Cells tied
 ;; between different colors stay 0 — the black frontier lines.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define h (rows g))
     (define w (cols g))
     (define (dist-map seed)
       ;; single-source BFS -> grid of hop counts (-1 = unreachable)
       (let loop ((frontier (list seed))
                  (dist (set-cell (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) -1))
                                  (first seed) (second seed) 0))
                  (d 0))
         (if (null? frontier)
             dist
             (let ((next (filter (lambda (p)
                                   (and (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) h w)
                                        (!= (at g (first p) (second p)) 5)
                                        (= (at dist (first p) (second p)) -1)))
                                 (remove-duplicates
                                  (flatmap (lambda (p)
                                             (map (lambda (dd)
                                                    (list (+ (first p) (first dd))
                                                          (+ (second p) (second dd))))
                                                  cardinal-deltas))
                                           frontier)))))
               (loop next
                     (for/fold ((acc dist)) ((p (in-list next)))
                       (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) (+ d 1)))
                     (+ d 1))))))
     (define seed-maps
       (map (lambda (s) (cons (at g (first s) (second s)) (dist-map s)))
            (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? (at g (first p) (second p)) (list 0 5))))
                    (grid-positions g))))
     (cellmap g (r c v)
       (if (!= v 0)
           v
           (let ((reach (filter (lambda (x) (>= (first x) 0))
                                (map (lambda (m) (list (at (cdr m) r c) (car m)))
                                     seed-maps))))
             (if (null? reach)
                 0
                 (let* ((best (apply min (map first reach)))
                        (cols (remove-duplicates
                               (map second
                                    (filter (lambda (x) (= (first x) best)) reach)))))
                   (if (= (length cols) 1) (first cols) 0)))))))))

(s16-binop k p1 p2) p3)) (list 'union 'intersection 'xor))))) (s16-binop kind p4 p5))))

written_solution: Reflect every nonzero cell across the vertical midline of the grid. Keep the original cells; add the mirrored copies.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Overlay the LEFT-RIGHT mirror onto the grid: every non-zero cell also
 ;; lands at its horizontally mirrored position.
 (overlay g (flip-lr g)))

    (lambda (r c)
      (let ([vals (filter (lambda (v) (!= v 0)) (row g r))])
        (if (< c (length vals)) (list-ref vals c) 0)))))

title: Neutral Glyph Recolor
written_solution: The top row is a legend. Read its nonzero colors from left to right. The lower 3×3 motif is symbolic: replace every blue(1) with the first legend color, every red(2) with the second, and every green(3) with the third, then output only that recolored motif.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
         (template (subgrid g 2 1 4 3))
         (symbols (sort (remove-duplicates
                          (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0)))
                                  (map third (grid-cells template))))
                        <)))
    (define (mapped v)
      (if (= v 0)
          0
          (let loop ([remaining symbols] [idx 0])
            (cond [(empty? remaining) v]
                  [(= v (first remaining)) (list-ref legend idx)]
                  [else (loop (rest remaining) (+ idx 1))]))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows template) (cols template)
      (lambda (r c) (mapped (at template r c))))))

title: Diagonal Corners to Rectangle
written_solution: The two colored markers are opposite corners of a rectangle. Draw the full rectangle outline in the same color, spanning the rows and columns between those markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))
         (a (first cells))
         (b (second cells))
         (color (third a))
         (r0 (min (first a) (first b)))
         (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
         (c0 (min (second a) (second b)))
         (c1 (max (second a) (second b)))
         (outline
           (append
             (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r0 c))
             (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r1 c))
             (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c0))
             (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c1)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) outline color)))

title: Terminal Run Completion
written_solution: Whenever two cells of the same color lie on the same row or the same column and the cells in between are empty, fill the entire straight segment between them in that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define row-filled
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
        (for/fold ([acc out]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
          (let ((cols (map second
                           (filter (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color))
                                   (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))]) (list r c (at g r c)))))))
            (if (and (= (length cols) 2)
                     (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0))
                           (range (+ (apply min cols) 1) (apply max cols))))
                (paint-cells acc
                  (for/list ([c (in-range (apply min cols) (+ (apply max cols) 1))]) (list r c))
                  color)
                acc)))))
    (for/fold ([out row-filled]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
        (let ((rs (map first
                       (filter (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color))
                               (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))]) (list r c (at g r c)))))))
          (if (and (= (length rs) 2)
                   (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 0))
                         (range (+ (apply min rs) 1) (apply max rs))))
              (paint-cells acc
                (for/list ([r (in-range (apply min rs) (+ (apply max rs) 1))]) (list r c))
                color)
              acc))))))

title: Mirror Across the Guide
written_solution: Find the vertical guide made entirely of cyan(8). Reflect every nonzero non-guide cell across that guide, keeping the original object and adding its mirror image on the other side.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((guide-col
          (find-first (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 8)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                      (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))]
                #:when (let ((v (at g r c)))
                          (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)) (not (= c guide-col)))))
      (let ((mc (- (* 2 guide-col) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? r mc (rows out) (cols out))
            (set-cell out r mc (at g r c))
            out)))))

title: Seeded Interior Fill
written_solution: Identify the rectangular frame. Leave the frame unchanged and fill every empty interior cell with the color of the unique non-frame seed cell inside it.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define values (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define frame-color (mode-list values))
    (define frame-bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g frame-color)))
    (define seed (third (first (filter (lambda (cell)
                                         (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                                              (not (= (third cell) frame-color))))
                                       (grid-cells g)))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (+ (first frame-bb) 1) (third frame-bb))]
                [c (in-range (+ (second frame-bb) 1) (fourth frame-bb))])
      (if (= (at out r c) 0) (set-cell out r c seed) out))))

title: Crop the Largest Object
written_solution: Find all connected colored objects. Choose the largest one by area; if there is a tie, take the uppermost then leftmost. Output the tight crop of that object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((chosen
          (first
            (sort (objects g 0)
              (lambda (a b)
                (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                      [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                      [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Frequency Strip
written_solution: Count how many times each non-background color appears. Sort colors by descending count, breaking ties by smaller color number. Output a single row of those colors in that order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (entries (sort
                    (map (lambda (color)
                           (list color (count-where (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color)) (grid-cells g))))
                         colors)
                    (lambda (a b)
                      (cond [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (> (second a) (second b))]
                            [else (< (first a) (first b))])))))
    (list (for*/list ([entry (in-list entries)]
                      [_ (in-range (second entry))])
            (first entry)))))

title: Palette-Lift Strip Assembly
written_solution: The first row supplies a three-color palette. The second row is an ordered selector of keyed blocks. The lower bank maps each key to a 2×2 neutral block whose values 1/2/3 are symbolic. Recolor each selected block with the palette, then concatenate the recolored blocks in selector order.

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (lookup-symbol sym syms colors) (cond ((empty? syms) sym) ((= sym (first syms)) (first colors)) (else (lookup-symbol sym (rest syms) (rest colors))))) (define (palette-lift template legend) (let ((syms (grid-colors template 0))) (grid-from-fn (rows template) (cols template) (lambda (r c) (let ((v (at template r c))) (if (= v 0) 0 (lookup-symbol v syms legend))))))) (define (lookup-block key bank) (cond ((empty? bank) (list (list 0))) ((= key (first (first bank))) (second (first bank))) (else (lookup-block key (rest bank))))) (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0))) (selector (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 1))) (bank (for/list ((c (in-range (cols g))) #:when (not (= (at g 3 c) 0))) (list (at g 3 c) (subgrid g 4 c 5 (+ c 1))))) (blocks (map (lambda (key) (palette-lift (lookup-block key bank) legend)) selector))) (stack-grids 'horizontal blocks))))

title: Commanded Crop Transform
written_solution: Read the command in the top-left cell. Crop the unique object from the rest of the grid and apply the corresponding transform: blue(1) → 90° clockwise, red(2) → 180°, green(3) → 90° counter-clockwise, yellow(4) → flip horizontal, gray(5) → flip vertical.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (transpose grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (apply-transform (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0)) (at g 0 0))))

title: Chamber Majority Flood
written_solution: Treat cyan(8) as walls. Each enclosed chamber contains a few colored seeds. Determine the majority nonzero seed color inside each chamber and fill all background cells of that chamber with that majority color, keeping walls and original seeds unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (region-colors cells)
      (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8))))
              (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells)))
    (define (majority vals)
      (first
        (first
          (sort (map (lambda (color)
                       (list color (count-where (lambda (v) (= v color)) vals)))
                     (remove-duplicates vals))
                (lambda (a b)
                  (cond [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (> (second a) (second b))]
                        [else (< (first a) (first b))]))))))
    (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 8))))]
               [out g])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((start (first remaining))
                 (cells (connected-region g (first start) (second start)
                           (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 8))) 4))
                 (colors (region-colors cells))
                 (next-remaining (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p cells))) remaining)))
            (if (empty? colors)
                (loop next-remaining out)
                (let ((color (majority colors)))
                  (loop next-remaining
                        (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list cells)])
                          (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
                              (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) color)
                              acc))))))))))

title: Area–Hole Relation Matrix
written_solution: Split the input into three object panels. For each object compute its area and number of holes. Output a 3×3 relation matrix: diagonal cells are 5; use 6 if two objects share both area and hole count, 2 if they share only area, 3 if they share only hole count, and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-blank-cols grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (define (shape-area grid)
      (count-where (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells grid)))
    (define (hole-count grid)
      (let* ((occ (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) 1) (+ (second p) 1)))
                       (filter-cells grid (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))))
             (h (+ (rows grid) 2))
             (w (+ (cols grid) 2)))
        (define (free? r c) (not (member? (list r c) occ)))
        (let loop ([remaining (filter (lambda (p) (free? (first p) (second p)))
                                      (positions-in-rect 0 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)))]
                   [holes 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              holes
              (let* ((p (first remaining))
                     (region (connected-region (empty-grid h w 0) (first p) (second p)
                               (lambda (r c v) (free? r c)) 4))
                     (touches-edge? (any? (lambda (q)
                                            (or (= (first q) 0) (= (second q) 0)
                                                (= (first q) (- h 1)) (= (second q) (- w 1))))
                                          region)))
                (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining)
                      (if touches-edge? holes (+ holes 1))))))))
    (define (relation ai hi aj hj same-flag)
      (cond [(= same-flag 1) 5]
            [(and (= ai aj) (= hi hj)) 6]
            [(= ai aj) 2]
            [(= hi hj) 3]
            [else 0]))
    (let* ((panels (map crop-to-content (split-blank-cols g)))
           (infos (map (lambda (p) (list (shape-area p) (hole-count p))) panels))
           (n (length infos)))
      (grid-from-fn n n
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((a (nth infos r)) (b (nth infos c)))
            (relation (first a) (second a) (first b) (second b) (if (= r c) 1 0))))))))

title: Ranked Component Selection
written_solution: Ignore the top-left command cell and analyze the remaining colored objects. Command 1 selects the smallest-area component, 2 the largest-area component, 3 the widest component, and 4 the tallest component. Output the tight crop of the selected component.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define cmd (at g 0 0))
    (define clean (set-cell g 0 0 0))
    (define (better? a b)
      (cond [(= cmd 2)
             (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                   [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])]
            [(= cmd 3)
             (cond [(not (= (obj-w a) (obj-w b))) (> (obj-w a) (obj-w b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                   [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])]
            [(= cmd 4)
             (cond [(not (= (obj-h a) (obj-h b))) (> (obj-h a) (obj-h b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                   [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])]
            [else
             (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                   [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                   [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])]))
    (let ((chosen (first (sort (objects clean 0) better?))))
      (subgrid clean (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen)))))

title: Anchor Copies with Overlap
written_solution: Find the connected exemplar that contains cyan(8); that cyan(8) marks the exemplar origin. Copy the whole exemplar so that its origin lands on every other cyan(8) in the grid as well as on its original location. Overlay all copies in the original canvas. If two copies write different nonzero colors to the same cell, mark the overlap as maroon(9).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (nonzero-components grid)
      (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells grid (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))] [acc (list)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            (reverse acc)
            (let* ((start (first remaining))
                   (cells (connected-region grid (first start) (second start)
                            (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))) 4)))
              (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p cells))) remaining)
                    (cons cells acc))))))
    (define (contains-color? cells color)
      (any? (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) color)) cells))
    (define (component< a b)
      (let ((ba (bbox-of-cells a)) (bb (bbox-of-cells b)))
        (cond [(not (= (length a) (length b))) (> (length a) (length b))]
              [(not (= (first ba) (first bb))) (< (first ba) (first bb))]
              [else (< (second ba) (second bb))])))
    (define (overlay-one out template origin anchor)
      (let ((top (- (first anchor) (first origin)))
            (left (- (second anchor) (second origin))))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (rows template))]
                    [c (in-range (cols template))]
                    #:when (not (= (at template r c) 0)))
          (let ((rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c)) (v (at template r c)))
            (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows acc) (cols acc))
                (let ((old (at acc rr cc)))
                  (cond [(= old 0) (set-cell acc rr cc v)]
                        [(= old v) acc]
                        [else (set-cell acc rr cc 9)]))
                acc)))))
    (let* ((proto (first (sort (filter (lambda (cells)
                                         (and (> (length cells) 1) (contains-color? cells 8)))
                                       (nonzero-components g))
                                component<)))
           (bb (bbox-of-cells proto))
           (template (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
           (origin (first (find-color template 8)))
           (abs-origin (list (+ (first bb) (first origin)) (+ (second bb) (second origin))))
           (anchors (cons abs-origin (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p proto))) (find-color g 8)))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
        (overlay-one out template origin anchor)))))

title: Select a Panel, Then Transform It
written_solution: Below the header are multiple zero-separated panels. The first header number selects which panel to use (1-based). Crop that panel tightly and apply the transform given by the second header number using the same command code as in the commanded-crop task.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (transpose grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (split-blank-cols grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (let* ((select-idx (at g 0 0))
           (cmd (at g 0 1))
           (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
           (panel (crop-to-content (nth (split-blank-cols body) (- select-idx 1)))))
      (apply-transform panel cmd))))

title: Palette-Lift Matrix with Commands
written_solution: The top row is a three-color palette. The next 2×2 block chooses which keyed neutral 3×3 template to place in each output slot. The following 2×2 command block tells how to transform each chosen template. Recolor every chosen template with the palette, apply its local transform, and assemble the four resulting 3×3 blocks into a 2×2 output matrix.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (transpose grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (lookup-symbol sym syms colors)
      (cond [(empty? syms) sym]
            [(= sym (first syms)) (first colors)]
            [else (lookup-symbol sym (rest syms) (rest colors))]))
    (define (palette-lift template legend cmd)
      (let* ((pat (apply-transform template cmd))
             (syms (grid-colors pat 0)))
        (grid-from-fn (rows pat) (cols pat)
          (lambda (r c)
            (let ((v (at pat r c)))
              (if (= v 0) 0 (lookup-symbol v syms legend)))))))
    (define (lookup-block key bank)
      (cond [(empty? bank) (list (list 0))]
            [(= key (first (first bank))) (second (first bank))]
            [else (lookup-block key (rest bank))]))

            [(= cmd 3) (transpose grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]

              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid)))

              [else

written_solution: The two full-height divider columns split the input into three equal panels. For each cell position, check how many of the three panels contain a nonzero cell there. If at least two panels agree that the cell is occupied, place cyan(8) in the output; otherwise leave it black(0).

(lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range (rows g)))) (range (cols g)))) (d1 (first divs)) (d2 (second divs)) (p1 (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- d1 1))) (p2 (subgrid g 0 (+ d1 1) (- (rows g) 1) (- d2 1))) (p3 (subgrid g 0 (+ d2 1) (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))) (grid-from-fn (rows p1) (cols p1) (lambda (r c) (if (>= (+ (if (= (at p1 r c) 0) 0 1) (if (= (at p2 r c) 0) 0 1) (if (= (at p3 r c) 0) 0 1)) 2) 8 0))))))

title: Complete the Axis Span
written_solution: There are exactly two nonzero markers of the same color. They lie on one row or one column. Fill every cell from one marker to the other, inclusive, with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((pts (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         (a (first pts))
         (b (second pts))
         (color (at g (first a) (second a))))
    (define cells
      (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
             (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b))
                                     (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
               (list (first a) c))]
            [else
             (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b))
                                     (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
               (list r (second a)))]))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) cells color)))

title: Tight Crop of the Motif
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (crop-to-content g))

title: Mirror Across the Main Diagonal
written_solution: For every nonzero cell at row r and column c, copy the same color to position c,r. The result is the original pattern plus its mirror across the main diagonal.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((v (at g r c)))
      (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out c r v) out))))

title: Rotate the Motif by the Corner Command
written_solution: The top-left command chooses a rotation: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → 180°, yellow(4) → 90° counter-clockwise. Ignore the command cell itself, crop the remaining motif tightly, and output the rotated crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((code (at g 0 0)))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (apply-cmd (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0)) code)))

title: Fill the Hollow Rectangle
written_solution: The colored cells form a hollow axis-aligned rectangle. Keep the same bbox, but fill its entire interior and border with the rectangle's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         ;; Bounding box enclosing the cells
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
         (color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
                 color)))

title: Draw the X from Square Corners
written_solution: The four colored cells are the corners of a square. Draw both diagonals connecting opposite corners, using the same color as the markers, and leave everything else black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
         (color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells))))
         (side (- (third bb) (first bb))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([i (in-range (+ side 1))])
      (set-cell
        (set-cell out (+ (first bb) i) (+ (second bb) i) color)
        (+ (first bb) i) (- (fourth bb) i) color))))

title: Keep Only the Nonempty Rows
written_solution: Delete every all-zero row. The output is just the nonempty rows, preserved in the same order and with the same width as before.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (filter (lambda (r) (not (all? (lambda (v) (= v 0)) r))) g))

title: Crop the Largest Component
written_solution: Treat each disconnected nonzero object as one component. Select the component with the most cells and output its tight bbox, preserving its colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 0 1))))
         (objs (objects mask 0))
         (best (first (sort objs (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 best) (obj-c1 best) (obj-r2 best) (obj-c2 best))))

title: Assemble Components by Legend Order
written_solution: The top row lists the colors in the desired order. Below it, each listed color appears as exactly one component. Crop each component tightly and concatenate the crops from left to right with a single black(0) column between neighbors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((order (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0))))
    (define below (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define objs (objects below 0))
    (define (piece color)
      (let ((obj (first (reverse (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) objs)))))
        (subgrid below (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define pieces (map piece order))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows pieces)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols pieces)) (max 0 (- (length pieces) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining pieces] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((p (first remaining))
                 (next
                  (for*/fold ([acc out])
                             ([r (in-range (rows p))]
                              [c (in-range (cols p))])
                    (let ((v (at p r c)))
                      (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols p) 1) next))))))

title: Flood Each Chamber from Its Seed
written_solution: The wall color partitions the grid into chambers. Every chamber contains exactly one colored seed. Replace the zeros in that chamber with the seed color while leaving the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((zero-objs (objects (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                            (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 1 0)))
                           0)))
    (define (neighbor-colors obj)
      (remove-duplicates
        (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8))))
          (for*/list ([p (in-list (obj-cells obj))]
                      [d (in-list cardinal-deltas)]
                      #:when (in-bounds? (+ (first p) (first d))
                                         (+ (second p) (second d))
                                         (rows g) (cols g)))
            (at g (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d)))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list zero-objs)])
      (let ((colors (neighbor-colors obj)))
        (if (= (length colors) 1)
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (first colors))
            out)))))

title: Translate the Payload by the Anchor Vector
written_solution: One anchor marks the starting point and another marks the destination. Compute the offset from the first anchor to the second, remove the anchors, and copy the payload component after translating every one of its cells by that offset.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((src (first (reverse (find-color g 2))))
         (dst (first (reverse (find-color g 3))))
         (dr (- (first dst) (first src)))
         (dc (- (second dst) (second src)))
         (payload (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member (third cell) (list 0 2 3))))
                          (grid-cells g))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([cell (in-list payload)])
      (let ((rr (+ (first cell) dr))
            (cc (+ (second cell) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out rr cc (third cell))
            out)))))

title: Span Overlay with Crossings
written_solution: Each color appears exactly twice and those two markers define one horizontal or vertical span. Draw all such spans. Cells covered by only one span keep that span's color, while cells where two or more spans overlap become maroon(9).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (grid-colors g 0)))
    (define (span color)
      (let* ((pts (find-color g color))
             (a (first pts))
             (b (second pts)))
        (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
               (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b))
                                       (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
                 (list (first a) c))]
              [else
               (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b))
                                       (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
                 (list r (second a)))])))
    (define spans (map (lambda (color) (list color (span color))) colors))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((hits (filter (lambda (item) (member (list r c) (second item))) spans)))
          (cond [(empty? hits) 0]
                [(> (length hits) 1) 9]
                [else (first (first hits))]))))))

title: Histogram of Component Colors
written_solution: Count how many connected components exist for each non-background color. Sort the colors in ascending order. For each color, output a row containing that color repeated once per component, padded on the right with zeros to the maximum row length.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (counts (map (lambda (color)
                        (length (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))))
                      colors))
         (width (apply max counts)))
    (grid-from-fn (length colors) width
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (< c (nth counts r)) (nth colors r) 0)))))

title: Copy the Template into the Matching Frame
written_solution: Crop the non-frame template tightly. Among the empty rectangular frames, exactly one has an interior whose size matches the template. Copy the template into that frame's interior, aligned to the interior's top-left corner, and leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((template-cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (member v (list 0 8))))))
         (template-bb (bbox-of-cells template-cells))
         (template (subgrid g (first template-bb) (second template-bb)
                            (third template-bb) (fourth template-bb))))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 8)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define chosen
      (filter (lambda (obj) (and (rect-frame? obj)
                                 (= (- (obj-h obj) 2) (rows template))
                                 (= (- (obj-w obj) 2) (cols template))))
              (objects g 0)))
    (if (empty? chosen)
        g
        (let ((frame (first chosen)))
          (for*/fold ([out g])
                     ([r (in-range (rows template))]
                      [c (in-range (cols template))])
            (let ((v (at template r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0))
                  (set-cell out (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1 r) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1 c) v)
                  out)))))))

title: Transform Analogy Across Panels
written_solution: The first two panels show an example transform: panel B is panel A after a rotation or reflection. Detect which transform was used by comparing the cropped nonzero shapes in those panels, then apply that transform to the cropped shape in panel C and output the result.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (sep-col? c)
      (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define (split-panels)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols g)) (reverse panels)]
              [(sep-col? c) (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols g)) (sep-col? stop))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid g 0 c (- (rows g) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels))
           (a (first panels))
           (b (second panels))
           (c (third panels))
           (code (first (filter (lambda (k) (equal? (apply-cmd (crop-to-content a) k)
                                                    (crop-to-content b)))
                                (range 1 7)))))
      (apply-cmd (crop-to-content c) code))))

title: Recolor Nested Frames by Depth
written_solution: The grid contains several nested rectangular borders, all initially in blue(1). Sort those frame borders by decreasing bounding-box area so the outermost frame comes first. Recolor the outermost frame to red(2), the next one to green(3), then 4, and so on inward.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                              (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 1) 1 0)))
                             0)
                     (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)]
               [i (in-naturals 2)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) i))))

title: Voronoi Fill Inside the Frame
written_solution: The boundary gray(5) forms a closed frame. Interior zeros are assigned to the nearest seed by Manhattan distance. If a cell is tied between two or more seeds, color it cyan(8). Keep the seeds and the frame as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member (third cell) (list 0 5))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist seed r c) (+ (abs (- (first seed) r)) (abs (- (second seed) c))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((best (apply min (map (lambda (seed) (dist seed r c)) seeds)))
                   (hits (filter (lambda (seed) (= (dist seed r c) best)) seeds)))
              (if (= (length hits) 1) (third (first hits)) 8)))))))

title: Dihedral Equality Matrix
written_solution: Each disconnected object is one shape. Two shapes count as equal if one can be rotated or reflected to match the other. Order the objects by their top-left positions and output a square matrix with red(2) where a pair of shapes is dihedrally equivalent and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Build the output grid
  (let* ((mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 0 1))))
         ;; Objects sorted by bbox position
         (objs (sort (objects mask 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                           (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                           (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
         ;; Number of objects
         (n (length objs)))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (match-transform (obj-cells (nth objs r)) (obj-cells (nth objs c))) 2 0)))))

title: Overlap Count of Multiple Spans
written_solution: Each repeated color defines one horizontal or vertical span between its two markers. Count, for every cell, how many of these spans pass through it. Cells covered by exactly two spans become cyan(8), cells covered by three or more spans become maroon(9), and all other cells stay 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (grid-colors g 0)))
    (define (span color)
      (let* ((pts (find-color g color))
             (a (first pts))
             (b (second pts)))
        (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
               (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b))
                                       (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
                 (list (first a) c))]
              [else
               (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b))
                                       (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
                 (list r (second a)))])))
    (define spans (map (lambda (color) (span color)) colors))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((n (count-where (lambda (cells) (member (list r c) cells)) spans)))
          (cond [(= n 2) 8]
                [(>= n 3) 9]
                [else 0]))))))

title: Transfer a Color Mapping
written_solution: Panels A and B have the same shape layout, but B recolors A by a consistent palette mapping. Infer that mapping from corresponding nonzero cells, then apply the same color substitution to panel C's cropped pattern and output the recolored crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (sep-col? c)
      (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define (split-panels)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols g)) (reverse panels)]
              [(sep-col? c) (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols g)) (sep-col? stop))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid g 0 c (- (rows g) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (define (lookup v pairs)
      (cond [(empty? pairs) #f]
            [(= v (first (first pairs))) (second (first pairs))]
            [else (lookup v (rest pairs))]))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels))
           (a (first panels))
           (b (second panels))
           (c (crop-to-content (third panels)))
           (mapping
            (filter (lambda (pair) (not (= (first pair) 0)))
              (for*/list ([r (in-range (rows a))]
                          [col (in-range (cols a))])
                (list (at a r col) (at b r col))))))
      (grid-from-fn (rows c) (cols c)
        (lambda (r col)
          (let* ((v (at c r col))
                 (hit (lookup v mapping)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) hit 0)))))))

title: Compose Two Transform Commands
written_solution: The two command values on the top row specify two geometric transforms in order. Crop the motif below them, apply the first transform, then apply the second. Commands use the same code system as the unique-command rotation task, extended with gray(5) for flip horizontal and 6 for flip vertical.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((codes (take (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0)) 2))
         (motif (crop-to-content (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
