(let ((dummy 0)) (define (crop-by-bbox base cells) (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))) (subgrid base (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))) (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (obj-color obj) (crop-by-bbox g (obj-cells obj)))) (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (cond ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (> (first a) (first b))) (else (< (second a) (second b))))))) (crops (map third items)) (out-h (apply max (map rows crops))) (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))) (let loop ((out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)) (remaining crops) (left 0)) (if (empty? remaining) out (loop (paste out (first remaining) 0 left) (rest remaining) (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1)))))))

title: Normalized Overlap Map
written_solution: Take the red(2) pattern and the green(3) pattern, crop and normalize them to the same origin, then build a comparison grid: 8 for overlap, 2 for only the first, 3 for only the second.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (cells3 (normalize-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (both (append cells2 cells3)))
    (if (empty? both)
        (list (list 0))
        (let ((max-r (apply max (map first both)))
              (max-c (apply max (map second both))))
          (grid-from-fn (+ max-r 1) (+ max-c 1)
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((p (list r c)))
                (cond [(and (member? p cells2) (member? p cells3)) 8]
                      [(member? p cells2) 2]
                      [(member? p cells3) 3]
                      [else 0]))))))))

title: Anchor Vector Move
written_solution: The cyan(8) cell is the source anchor and the maroon(9) cell is the target anchor. Translate the whole ordinary object by the vector from cyan(8) to maroon(9) and discard the markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((anchor-hits (find-color g 8))
         (target-hits (find-color g 9))
         (anchor (if (empty? anchor-hits) #f (last anchor-hits)))
         (target (if (empty? target-hits) #f (last target-hits)))
         (obj-cells (filter (lambda (cell)
                              (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)) (not (= v 9)))))
                            (grid-cells g))))
    (if (or (eq? anchor #f) (eq? target #f))
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (let ((dr (- (first target) (first anchor)))
              (dc (- (second target) (second anchor))))
          (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
                    ([cell (in-list obj-cells)])
            (let ((nr (+ (first cell) dr)) (nc (+ (second cell) dc)))
              (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows out) (cols out))
                  (set-cell out nr nc (third cell))
                  out)))))))

title: Seeded Frames Fill
written_solution: Find every rectangular border. If a frame contains a non-border seed inside, fill its interior with the seed color while keeping the border itself intact.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define (first-seed frame)
      (find-first
        (lambda (cell)
          (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v (obj-color frame))))))
        (for*/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
          (list r c (at g r c)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((seed (first-seed frame)))
        (if seed
            (paint-cells out
              (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)
                                 (- (obj-r2 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1))
              (third seed))
            out)))))

title: Legend Motif Composer
written_solution: The left legend chooses a transform and the top legend chooses one motif from a small library. Compose those choices for every row/column pair and tile the transformed 3×3 motifs into the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (motif mid)
      (cond [(= mid 2) (list (list 2 0 0) (list 2 2 0) (list 2 2 2))]
            [(= mid 3) (list (list 3 0 0) (list 0 3 0) (list 0 0 3))]
            [else (list (list 0 4 0) (list 4 4 4) (list 0 4 0))]))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [else (flip-lr grid)]))
    (define row-keys (map (lambda (r) (at g r 0)) (range 1 (rows g))))
    (define col-keys (rest (first g)))
    (grid-from-fn (* 3 (length row-keys)) (* 3 (length col-keys))
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((tile-r (quotient r 3))
               (tile-c (quotient c 3))
               (rr (modulo r 3))
               (cc (modulo c 3))
               (tile (transform-code (motif (list-ref col-keys tile-c))
                                     (list-ref row-keys tile-r))))
          (at tile rr cc))))))

title: Nearest-Seed Partition
written_solution: Each background location is colored by the unique nearest seed under Manhattan distance. When two or more seeds are equally near, the cell remains 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((distances
                     (sort
                       (map (lambda (seed)
                              (list (+ (abs (- r (first seed))) (abs (- c (second seed))))
                                    (third seed)))
                            seeds)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (first a) (first b))
                             (< (second a) (second b))
                             (< (first a) (first b)))))))
              (cond [(empty? distances) 0]
                    [(and (>= (length distances) 2)
                          (= (first (first distances)) (first (second distances)))) 0]
                    [else (second (first distances))])))))))

title: Transform Analogy Transfer
written_solution: Split the input into three panels. Determine which geometric transform maps the first panel's cropped object to the second panel's cropped object, then apply that same transform to the third panel's object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 1)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                          (range 0 (cols grid)))))
        (let loop ([remaining (append seps (list (cols grid)))] [start 0] [panels (list)])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              (reverse panels)
              (let ((stop (first remaining)))
                (loop (rest remaining)
                      (+ stop 1)
                      (if (> stop start)
                          (cons (subgrid grid 0 start (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels)
                          panels)))))))
    (define (without-divider panel)
      (grid-from-fn (rows panel) (cols panel)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at panel r c) 1) 0 (at panel r c)))))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels g))
           (a (crop-to-content (without-divider (first panels))))
           (b (crop-to-content (without-divider (second panels))))
           (q (crop-to-content (without-divider (third panels))))
           (code (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code a t) b))
                                        (list 1 2 3 4 5 6))))
                   (if hit hit 1))))
      (transform-code q code))))

title: Nested Depth Borders
written_solution: Detect all nested rectangular borders. Recolor each border by its nesting depth: outermost becomes red(2), next becomes green(3), and so on inward.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (let ((border
              (remove-duplicates
                (append
                  (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
                  (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))
                  (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
                  (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj)))))))
        (and (= (obj-size obj) (length border))
             (all? (lambda (p) (member? p border)) (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define rects (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (= (at g r c) 0)
            0
            (+ 1
               (count-where
                 (lambda (obj)
                   (and (>= r (obj-r1 obj)) (<= r (obj-r2 obj))
                        (>= c (obj-c1 obj)) (<= c (obj-c2 obj))))
                 rects)))))))

title: Command Strip Replay
written_solution: Use the 3×3 motif on the left as a template. Read the command strip across the top and concatenate transformed copies of that motif in command order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define motif (subgrid g 1 0 3 2))
    (define cmds
      (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0)))
              (for/list ([c (in-range 3 (cols g))]) (at g 0 c))))
    (define (transform-command code)
      (cond [(= code 1) motif]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw motif)]
            [(= code 3) (flip-lr motif)]
            [else (rotate-180 motif)]))
    (define tiles (map transform-command cmds))
    (grid-from-fn 3 (apply + (map cols tiles))
      (lambda (r c)
        (let loop ([remaining tiles] [left 0])
          (let ((tile (first remaining)))
            (if (< c (+ left (cols tile)))
                (at tile r (- c left))
                (loop (rest remaining) (+ left (cols tile))))))))))

title: Shape Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: Order the disconnected objects by position, normalize each one by translation only, and fill an N×N matrix with cyan(8) exactly when two normalized shapes are identical.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pos< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (canon obj) (sort (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)) pos<))
    (define objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                  (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                  (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define norms (map canon objs))
    (define n (length objs))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (equal? (list-ref norms r) (list-ref norms c)) 8 0)))))

title: Color Analogy Transfer
written_solution: Split the three panels, crop away padding, and compare the first two panels to infer a color substitution table. Apply that same color map to the cropped query object in the third panel.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 1)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                          (range 0 (cols grid)))))
        (let loop ([remaining (append seps (list (cols grid)))] [start 0] [panels (list)])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              (reverse panels)
              (let ((stop (first remaining)))
                (loop (rest remaining)
                      (+ stop 1)
                      (if (> stop start)
                          (cons (subgrid grid 0 start (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels)
                          panels)))))))
    (define (without-divider panel)
      (grid-from-fn (rows panel) (cols panel)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at panel r c) 1) 0 (at panel r c)))))
    (define (color-map-from a b)
      (if (or (not (= (rows a) (rows b))) (not (= (cols a) (cols b))))
          #f
          (let loop ([cells (grid-positions a)] [mapping (list)])
            (if (empty? cells)
                mapping
                (let* ((p (first cells))
                       (va (at a (first p) (second p)))
                       (vb (at b (first p) (second p)))
                       (entry (find-first (lambda (item) (= (first item) va)) mapping)))
                  (cond [(and (= va 0) (= vb 0)) (loop (rest cells) mapping)]
                        [(or (= va 0) (= vb 0)) #f]
                        [(and entry (not (= (second entry) vb))) #f]
                        [(not (eq? entry #f)) (loop (rest cells) mapping)]
                        [else (loop (rest cells) (cons (list va vb) mapping))]))))))
    (define (apply-cmap grid cmap)
      (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid)
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((v (at grid r c)))
            (let ((entry (find-first (lambda (item) (= (first item) v)) cmap)))
              (if (or (= v 0) (not entry)) 0 (second entry)))))))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels g))
           (a (crop-to-content (without-divider (first panels))))
           (b (crop-to-content (without-divider (second panels))))
           (q (crop-to-content (without-divider (third panels))))
           (cmap (color-map-from a b)))
      (if (eq? cmap #f) q (apply-cmap q cmap)))))

title: Column Gravity Dots
written_solution: For each column, count the blue(1) cells. The output keeps the same height and width, but all blue(1) cells in a column have fallen straight down and stacked at the bottom. Only the number of blue(1) cells per column matters; their original row positions do not.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Per-column HISTOGRAM: count the blue(1) cells in each column and redraw
 ;; them as a bottom-aligned bar of that height.
 (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
   (let ((cnt (count-where (lambda (rr) (= (at g rr c) 1)) (range h))))
     (if (>= r (- h cnt)) 1 0)))))

title: Crop the Interior Rectangle
written_solution: The two yellow(4) markers define a crop window. Ignore the markers themselves and take the interior subgrid bounded by them. The output is exactly that interior rectangle, with its original colors and zeros preserved.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Crop to the INTERIOR of the yellow(4) frame (its bbox inset by 1).
 (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 4))))
   (subgrid g (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
            (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1))))

title: Solid Bounding Box
written_solution: There is one magenta(6) object. Replace it by its full bbox: the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that covers all of its cells. The output keeps the original grid size, clears everything else to black(0), and paints the entire box magenta(6).
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (object-color-cells grid color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects grid 0))) (let* ((obj (first (object-color-cells g 6))) (bb (obj-bbox obj))) (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (and (>= r (first bb)) (<= r (third bb)) (>= c (second bb)) (<= c (fourth bb))) 6 0))))))

title: Normalize Shape to Top-Left
written_solution: Take the unique green(3) component and ignore its absolute position. Normalize it by shifting it up and left until its bbox touches row 0 and column 0. The output is background except for that translated green(3) shape.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (object-color-cells grid color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects grid 0))) (define (normalize-paint grid cells color) (paint-cells grid (normalize-cells cells) color)) (let* ((obj (first (object-color-cells g 3)))) (normalize-paint (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells obj) 3))))

title: Topmost Cell in Each Column
written_solution: The rule is columnwise. In every column, preserve the first yellow(4) cell seen from the top and delete any additional yellow(4) cells below it. Columns with no yellow(4) stay empty.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Per column, keep only the FIRST yellow(4); everything else clears.
 (let ()
   (define (row-with-four c)
     (first (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 4)) (range h))))
   (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) (if (= r (row-with-four c)) 4 0)))))

title: Component Count Bar
written_solution: All nonzero cells are blue(1), but they form several disconnected objects. Count those connected components and output a 1-row grid whose length equals that count, filled with blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Output a 1xN row of 1s, N = the number of BLUE objects.
 (list (make-list (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1))
                                  (objects g 0)))
                  1)))

title: Row Majority Column

title: Recolor every full 2x2 red block
written_solution: Every cell that belongs to a complete 2x2 block of red(2) should become green(3). Lone red(2) cells and incomplete L-shapes stay red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (cell-at g r c) 2)
               (any?
                 (lambda (p)
                   (let ((r0 (first p))
                         (c0 (second p)))
                     (and (>= r0 0) (< r0 (- h 1))
                          (>= c0 0) (< c0 (- w 1))
                          (= (cell-at g r0 c0) 2)
                          (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) c0) 2)
                          (= (cell-at g r0 (+ c0 1)) 2)
                          (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1)) 2))))
                 (list (list r c)
                       (list (- r 1) c)
                       (list r (- c 1))
                       (list (- r 1) (- c 1)))))
          3
          (cell-at g r c)))))

title: Recolor blue components that touch the top border
written_solution: Find each blue(1) component. If any cell in that component touches the top row, recolor the entire component to yellow(4). Other blue(1) components stay blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      obj-cells
      (filter
        (lambda (obj)
          (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
               (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) (obj-cells obj))))
        (objects g 0)))
    4))

title: Fill hollow rectangles
written_solution: Each component of magenta(6) is a hollow axis-aligned rectangle. Fill the rectangle’s interior with magenta(6), turning the whole box solid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl
    (lambda (obj acc)
      (if (= (obj-color obj) 6)
          (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                 (r0 (first bb))
                 (c0 (second bb))
                 (r1 (third bb))
                 (c1 (fourth bb)))
            (if (and (< (+ r0 1) r1) (< (+ c0 1) c1))
                (paint-cells acc (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1)) 6)
                acc))
          acc))
    g
    (objects g 0)))

title: Mirror the left object across a vertical divider
written_solution: The full gray(5) column is a mirror axis. Copy every non-zero non-divider cell on the left side to its reflected position on the right side. Keep the original object too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((divider
          (find-first
            (lambda (c)
              (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 5)) (range h)))
            (range w))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (cond
          [(= c divider) 5]
          [(< c divider) (cell-at g r c)]
          [else
            (let ((mc (- (* 2 divider) c)))
              (if (and (>= mc 0) (< mc divider)
                       (not (= (cell-at g r mc) 0))
                       (not (= (cell-at g r mc) 5)))
                  (cell-at g r mc)
                  0))])))))

title: Extend every horizontal line of length 3
written_solution: Look for connected horizontal segments of cyan(8) that have exactly length 3. Extend each such segment by one cell on the left and one on the right if those cells are empty. Other 8-components do not change.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl
    (lambda (obj acc)
      (if (= (obj-color obj) 8)
          (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
                 (rs (map fst cells))
                 (cs (map snd cells))
                 (r0 (first rs))
                 (cmin (min-list cs))
                 (cmax (max-list cs))
                 (left (- cmin 1))
                 (right (+ cmax 1)))
            (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 3)
                     (= (length (unique rs)) 1)
                     (= (- cmax cmin) 2))
                (paint-cells
                  acc
                  (append
                    (if (and (>= left 0) (= (cell-at g r0 left) 0)) (list (list r0 left)) '())
                    (if (and (< right w) (= (cell-at g r0 right) 0)) (list (list r0 right)) '()))
                  8)
                acc))
          acc))
    g
    (objects g 0)))

title: Crop to the tight non-zero bounding box
written_solution: Ignore the surrounding black(0) background. Output only the smallest rectangle that contains every non-zero cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter
                  (lambda (p) (not (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 0)))
                  (grid-positions g)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Recolor the largest orange component
written_solution: Find all orange(7) connected components. Recolor only the largest one to red(2). Smaller orange(7) components stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((orange-objects (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 7)) (objects g 0)))
         (largest (first (sort orange-objects (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (paint-cells g (obj-cells largest) 2)))

title: Recolor line objects by orientation
written_solution: Every green(3) object is a straight line. Horizontal 3-lines become blue(1); vertical 3-lines become cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl
    (lambda (obj acc)
      (if (= (obj-color obj) 3)
          (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
                 (row-count (length (unique (map fst cells))))
                 (col-count (length (unique (map snd cells)))))
            (cond
              [(= row-count 1) (paint-cells acc cells 1)]
              [(= col-count 1) (paint-cells acc cells 8)]
              [else acc]))
          acc))
    g
    (objects g 0)))

title: Copy the object by the marker vector
written_solution: There are two marker cells of maroon(9). Read the translation vector from the first marker to the second marker (top-left to bottom-right in row-major order). Copy the non-marker object by that vector. Remove the 9 markers. Keep the original object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; The two maroon markers encode one row-major translation vector.
  (let* ((markers (find-color g 9))
         (p1 (first markers))
         (p2 (second markers))
         (dr (- (fst p2) (fst p1)))
         (dc (- (snd p2) (snd p1))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        ;; Pull from one vector-step behind; this overlays the shifted copy.
        (let* ((sr (- r dr))
               (sc (- c dc))
               (src-v (if (in-bounds? sr sc h w) (cell-at g sr sc) 0))
               (v (cell-at g r c)))
          (cond
            [(and (not (= src-v 0)) (not (= src-v 9))) src-v]
            ;; Otherwise retain original payload cells and erase both markers.
            [(and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9))) v]
            [else 0]))))))

title: Complete bilateral symmetry across the divider
written_solution: The gray(5) column is a mirror axis. Any colored cell on either side should also appear in the reflected position on the other side. So the output is the symmetric completion, not just a copy from one fixed side.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((divider
          (find-first
            (lambda (c)
              (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 5)) (range h)))
            (range w))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
               (mc (- (* 2 divider) c))
               (mv (if (in-bounds? r mc h w) (cell-at g r mc) 0)))
          (cond
            [(= c divider) 5]
            [(and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))) v]
            [(and (not (= mv 0)) (not (= mv 5))) mv]
            [else 0]))))))

title: Recolor hollow and solid orange objects differently
written_solution: For each orange(7) component, inspect its bbox. If it contains a genuine empty interior hole, recolor that component to yellow(4). If it is solid, recolor it to red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl
    (lambda (obj acc)
      (if (= (obj-color obj) 7)
          (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                 (r0 (first bb))
                 (c0 (second bb))
                 (r1 (third bb))
                 (c1 (fourth bb))
                 (cells (obj-cells obj))
                 (interior (if (and (< (+ r0 1) r1) (< (+ c0 1) c1))
                               (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1))
                               (list)))
                 (hollow
                   (any?
                     (lambda (p)
                       (and (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 0)
                            (not (member p cells))))
                     interior)))
            (paint-cells acc cells (if hollow 4 2)))
          acc))
    g
    (objects g 0)))

title: Connect matched markers in a row or column
written_solution: Markers of the same color that lie in the same row or the same column should be joined by a solid line of that color, including the endpoints.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (grid-colors g 0)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (not (= v 0))
              v
              (let ((fill-color
                      (find-first
                        (lambda (color)
                          (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
                            (or
                              (any?
                                (lambda (p1)
                                  (any?
                                    (lambda (p2)
                                      (and (= (fst p1) r) (= (fst p2) r)
                                           (<= (min (snd p1) (snd p2)) c)
                                           (<= c (max (snd p1) (snd p2)))))
                                    pts))
                                pts)
                              (any?
                                (lambda (p1)
                                  (any?
                                    (lambda (p2)
                                      (and (= (snd p1) c) (= (snd p2) c)
                                           (<= (min (fst p1) (fst p2)) r)
                                           (<= r (max (fst p1) (fst p2)))))
                                    pts))
                                pts))))
                        colors)))
                (if fill-color fill-color 0))))))))

title: Compress objects into a size-sorted strip
written_solution: Each component becomes a run of its own color whose length equals the component’s size. Sort the runs from largest to smallest, breaking size ties by smaller color number first, and separate runs by one black(0) cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((sorted-objs
           (sort (objects g 0)
             (lambda (a b)
               (cond
                 [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                 [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
         (row
           (cdr
             (flatmap
               (lambda (obj)
                 (cons 0 (for/list ([i (range (obj-size obj))]) (obj-color obj))))
               sorted-objs))))
    (list row)))

title: Recolor each gray frame by the marker inside it
written_solution: Every gray(5) hollow frame contains exactly one colored marker inside. Recolor the whole frame border to the marker’s color, then remove the marker, leaving the interior black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (foldl

title: Assemble the Mosaic by Edge Matching
skills: search, global arrangement, rotations, combinatorial assembly
written_solution: Rotate and permute the tiles until the touching edge-center colors match across both internal boundaries of a 2×2 mosaic. Output that assembled mosaic.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Four 3x3 tiles sit on a maroon(9) divider lattice. Reassemble them
 ;; as a 2x2 jigsaw: try every tile permutation and rotation until the
 ;; touching edge midpoints agree, then output the assembled board
 ;; (dividers included), lexicographically smallest solution first.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (flat grid) (apply append grid))
     (define (lex< a b)
       (cond ((empty? a) (not (empty? b)))
             ((empty? b) #f)
             ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b)))
             (else (lex< (rest a) (rest b)))))
     (define (remove-one x xs)
       (cond ((empty? xs) (list))
             ((equal? x (first xs)) (rest xs))
             (else (cons (first xs) (remove-one x (rest xs))))))
     (define (permutations-list xs)
       (if (empty? xs)
           (list (list))
           (flatmap (lambda (x)
                      (map (lambda (p) (cons x p))
                           (permutations-list (remove-one x xs))))
                    xs)))
     (define (segments n dividers)  ;; (start end-exclusive) spans
       (let loop ((ds (append dividers (list n))) (prev -1)
                  (acc (list)))
         (if (empty? ds)
             (reverse acc)
             (loop (rest ds) (first ds)
                   (if (> (- (first ds) prev 1) 0)
                       (cons (list (+ prev 1) (first ds)) acc)
                       acc)))))
     (define tiles
       (let ((rbs (segments h (filter (lambda (r)
                                        (all? (lambda (c)
                                                (= (at g r c) 9))
                                              (range 0 w)))
                                      (range 0 h))))
             (cbs (segments w (filter (lambda (c)
                                        (all? (lambda (r)
                                                (= (at g r c) 9))
                                              (range 0 h)))
                                      (range 0 w)))))
         (flatmap (lambda (rb)
                    (map (lambda (cb)
                           (subgrid g (first rb) (first cb)
                                    (- (second rb) 1)
                                    (- (second cb) 1)))
                         cbs))
                  rbs)))
     (define (rotk tile k)
       (cond ((= (modulo k 4) 1) (rotate-cw tile))
             ((= (modulo k 4) 2) (rotate-180 tile))
             ((= (modulo k 4) 3) (rotate-ccw tile))
             (else tile)))
     (define (assemble t0 t1 t2 t3)  ;; 2x2 with 1-wide 9 dividers
       (let ((th (rows t0)) (tw (cols t0)))
         (for*/fold ((out (empty-grid (+ (* 2 th) 1) (+ (* 2 tw) 1) 9)))
                    ((rr (in-range 2)) (cc (in-range 2))
                     (r (in-range th)) (c (in-range tw)))
           (set-cell out (+ (* rr (+ th 1)) r) (+ (* cc (+ tw 1)) c)
                     (at (nth (list t0 t1 t2 t3) (+ (* rr 2) cc))
                         r c)))))
     (define (edges-match? t0 t1 t2 t3)
       (and (= (at t0 1 2) (at t1 1 0))
            (= (at t2 1 2) (at t3 1 0))
            (= (at t0 2 1) (at t2 0 1))
            (= (at t1 2 1) (at t3 0 1))))
     (define candidates
       (filter (lambda (x) x)
               (for*/list ((perm (in-list (permutations-list
                                           (range 0 (length tiles)))))
                           (k0 (in-range 4)) (k1 (in-range 4))
                           (k2 (in-range 4)) (k3 (in-range 4)))
                 (let ((t0 (rotk (nth tiles (first perm)) k0))
                       (t1 (rotk (nth tiles (second perm)) k1))
                       (t2 (rotk (nth tiles (third perm)) k2))
                       (t3 (rotk (nth tiles (fourth perm)) k3)))
                   (and (edges-match? t0 t1 t2 t3)
                        (assemble t0 t1 t2 t3))))))
     (first (sort candidates (lambda (a b) (lex< (flat a) (flat b))))))))

(rule!

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

    (define (clean-row-between? r c1 c2)

    (define (clean-col-between? c r1 r2)

    (define row-runs
      (filter
        (lambda (run) (clean-row-between? (first run) (second run) (third run)))

title: Complete red diagonal pairs into green 2x2 squares

title: Mirror the left motif across a gray divider
written_solution: Find the full gray(5) vertical divider column. Copy every colored cell on its left side to the mirrored position on its right side, preserving each color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (full-col? c)
      (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 5)) (range 0 h)))
    (define divider (first (filter full-col? (range 0 w))))

      (filter
        (lambda (p)
          (let ((v (third p))) (and (< (second p) divider) (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
        (grid-cells g)))

        (if src (third src) #f)))
    (grid-from-fn h w

        (let ((mv (mirror-value r c)))
          (if mv mv (cell-at g r c)))))))

title: Copy the green object by the source-to-destination vector

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

      (if (empty? (cdr xs)) (first xs) (last-item (cdr xs))))

    (define dst (last-item (find-color g 1)))
    (define dr (- (fst dst) (fst src)))
    (define dc (- (snd dst) (snd src)))
    (define obj (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 3)) (objects g 0))))
    (define copied
      (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (fst p) dr) (+ (snd p) dc))) (obj-cells obj)))

      (any? (lambda (p) (and (= r (fst p)) (= c (snd p)))) copied))

      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c h w) (copied-cell? r c)) 8 (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Fill the marked frame with its marker color
written_solution: Several gray(5) rectangular frames appear. Exactly one frame contains exactly one colored marker in its interior. Fill the empty interior cells of that frame with the marker's color, and leave the other frames unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame-perimeter obj)
      (- (+ (* 2 (obj-h obj)) (* 2 (obj-w obj))) 4))
    (define (border-cell? obj p)
      (or (= (fst p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (fst p) (obj-r2 obj))
          (= (snd p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (snd p) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
           (> (obj-h obj) 1)
           (> (obj-w obj) 1)
           (= (obj-size obj) (frame-perimeter obj))
           (all? (lambda (p) (border-cell? obj p)) (obj-cells obj))))
    (define frames (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (define (interior-cells frame)
      (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (- (obj-r2 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1)))
    (define (marker-values frame)
      (filter
        (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
        (map (lambda (p) (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))) (interior-cells frame))))
    (define target
      (find-first (lambda (frame) (= (length (marker-values frame)) 1)) frames))
    (if (not target)
        g
        (let ((fill-color (first (marker-values target))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
                (if (and (= v 0)
                         (> r (obj-r1 target)) (< r (obj-r2 target))
                         (> c (obj-c1 target)) (< c (obj-c2 target)))

written_solution: The red(2) object is a template. The control cell magenta(6)/7/8/9 → rotate it by 0/90/180/270 degrees. Stamp the rotated template starting at the blue(1) anchor cell, using yellow(4) for the stamped copy.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define control
      (first (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 6 7 8 9))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define rot-count (- (third control) 6))
    (define template (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 1)))
    (define (rotate-n cells n)
      (if (= n 0)
          (normalize-cells cells)
          (rotate-n (rotate-cells-cw (normalize-cells cells)) (- n 1))))
    (define shape (rotate-n (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)) rot-count))
    (define stamp-cells
      (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (fst anchor) (fst p)) (+ (snd anchor) (snd p)))) shape))
    (paint-cells g stamp-cells 4)))

title: Connect matching color pairs with L-paths
written_solution: For each color that appears exactly twice, order the two endpoints lexicographically. Draw a path in that same color that goes horizontally along the first endpoint's row until it reaches the second endpoint's column, then vertically down or up to the second endpoint.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (point< a b)
      (or (< (fst a) (fst b))
          (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (< (snd a) (snd b)))))
    (define (ordered-pair pts)
      (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
        (if (point< b a) (list b a) (list a b))))
    (define (pair-record color)
      (let ((pts (ordered-pair (find-color g color))))
        (list color (first pts) (second pts))))
    (define (range-between a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (range a (- b 1) -1)))
    (define colors
      (filter (lambda (color) (= (length (find-color g color)) 2)) (grid-colors g 0)))
    (define records
      (sort (map pair-record colors)
            (lambda (x y) (point< (second x) (second y)))))
    (define (path-cells rec)
      (let* ((color (first rec))
             (a (second rec))
             (b (third rec)))
        (append
          (map (lambda (c) (list (fst a) c color)) (range-between (snd a) (snd b)))
          (map (lambda (r) (list r (snd b) color)) (range-between (fst a) (fst b))))))
    (paint-cells g (flatmap path-cells records))))

title: Recolor the candidate that matches the legend shape
written_solution: The blue(1) component is the legend shape. Compare every red(2) candidate component to the legend up to rotation. Recolor the unique matching candidate cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define legend
      (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))
    (define red-objs
      (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0)))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b))
           (all? (lambda (p) (has-cell? p b)) a)))
    ;; Normalize the candidate under all four quarter-turns. Reflections are
    ;; deliberately excluded from the matching relation.
    (define (rotations cells)
      (let* ((r0 (normalize-cells cells))
             (r1 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r0)))
             (r2 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r1)))
             (r3 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r2))))
        (list r0 r1 r2 r3)))
    (define legend-shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells legend)))
    (define (matches-legend? obj)
      (any? (lambda (shape) (same-cells? legend-shape shape))
            (rotations (obj-cells obj))))
    ;; Preserve the scene and recolor only red components in the legend's
    ;; rotation orbit.
    (define targets (filter matches-legend? red-objs))
    (paint-cells g (flatmap obj-cells targets) 8)))

title: Project arrow rays until they hit walls
written_solution: Each arrow cell 1/2/3/4 points up/right/down/left. From each arrow, paint a ray of orange(7) through background cells until the ray reaches a wall cell gray(5) or leaves the grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define arrows
      (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4))) (grid-cells g)))
    (define (direction color)
      (cond
        [(= color 1) (list -1 0)]
        [(= color 2) (list 0 1)]
        [(= color 3) (list 1 0)]
        [else (list 0 -1)]))
    (define (visible-from? cell tr tc)
      (let* ((d (direction (third cell)))
             (dr (first d))
             (dc (second d)))
        (let loop ((r (+ (first cell) dr))
                   (c (+ (second cell) dc)))
          (cond
            [(not (in-bounds? r c h w)) #f]
            [(= (cell-at g r c) 5) #f]
            [(and (= r tr) (= c tc)) #t]
            [else (loop (+ r dr) (+ c dc))]))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (cell-at g r c) 0)
                 (any? (lambda (cell) (visible-from? cell r c)) arrows))
            7
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Fill the selected band between nested frames
written_solution: Three gray(5) rectangular frames are nested. The control value 1/2/3 selects, respectively, the outer band between the outer and middle frames, the middle band between the middle and inner frames, or the innermost interior inside the inner frame. Fill the selected region with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (area obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
    (define (frame-perimeter obj)
      (- (+ (* 2 (obj-h obj)) (* 2 (obj-w obj))) 4))
    (define (border-cell? obj p)
      (or (= (fst p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (fst p) (obj-r2 obj))
          (= (snd p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (snd p) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
           (> (obj-h obj) 1)
           (> (obj-w obj) 1)
           (= (obj-size obj) (frame-perimeter obj))
           (all? (lambda (p) (border-cell? obj p)) (obj-cells obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort
        (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
        (lambda (a b) (> (area a) (area b)))))
    (define control-cell
      (find-first (lambda (p) (member? (third p) (list 1 2 3))) (grid-cells g)))
    (if (or (< (length frames) 3) (not control-cell))
        g
        (let* ((control (third control-cell))
               (outer (first frames))
               (mid (second frames))
               (inner (third frames)))
          (define (inside? r c obj)
            (and (> r (obj-r1 obj)) (< r (obj-r2 obj)) (> c (obj-c1 obj)) (< c (obj-c2 obj))))
          (define (selected? r c)
            (cond
              [(= control 1) (and (inside? r c outer) (not (inside? r c mid)))]
              [(= control 2) (and (inside? r c mid) (not (inside? r c inner)))]
              [else (inside? r c inner)]))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
                (if (and (= v 0) (selected? r c)) 8 v))))))))

title: Mark the cells that lie on every shortest path
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as blocked walls. Between the start cell red(2) and goal cell green(3), consider all shortest paths. Mark exactly the cells that belong to every shortest path with cyan(8), leaving the start and goal themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (record-of p records)
      (find-first (lambda (rec) (same-pos? p (first rec))) records))
    (define (set-record-count p new-count records)
      (map
        (lambda (rec)
          (if (same-pos? p (first rec))
              (list (first rec) (second rec) new-count)
              rec))
        records))
    (define (neighbors p)
      (filter
        (lambda (n)
          (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
            (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5)))))
        (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (fst p) (fst d)) (+ (snd p) (snd d)))) cardinal-deltas)))
    (define (dist-count start)
      (let loop ((queue (list start)) (records (list (list start 0 1))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            records
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (cur-rec (record-of cur records))
                   (cur-dist (second cur-rec))
                   (cur-count (third cur-rec)))
              (let update ((ns (neighbors cur)) (q restq) (recs records))
                (if (empty? ns)
                    (loop q recs)
                    (let* ((n (first ns))
                           (nd (+ cur-dist 1))
                           (hit (record-of n recs)))
                      (cond
                        [(not hit)
                         (update (cdr ns) (append q (list n)) (append recs (list (list n nd cur-count))))]
                        [(= (second hit) nd)
                         (update (cdr ns) q (set-record-count n (+ (third hit) cur-count) recs))]
                        [else (update (cdr ns) q recs)]))))))))
    (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
           (goal (first (find-color g 3)))
           (from-start (dist-count start))
           (from-goal (dist-count goal))
           (goal-rec (record-of goal from-start)))
      (if (not goal-rec)
          g
          (let ((D (second goal-rec))
                (total (third goal-rec)))
            (grid-from-fn h w
              (lambda (r c)
                (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
                       (p (list r c))
                       (rs (record-of p from-start))
                       (rg (record-of p from-goal)))
                  (if (and (not (= v 5)) (not (= v 2)) (not (= v 3))
                           rs rg (= (+ (second rs) (second rg)) D)
                           (= (* (third rs) (third rg)) total))
                      8
                      v)))))))))

title: Stamp dihedral variants of the prototype at multiple anchors
written_solution: The maroon(9) component is the exemplar. Every anchor is a magenta(6) cell with a control cell directly above it: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → flip horizontal, yellow(4) → flip horizontal then 90° clockwise. Stamp the transformed exemplar at each anchor in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define proto
      (first
        (filter
          (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) 9) (> (obj-size obj) 1)))
          (objects g 0))))
    (define shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells proto)))
    (define (transform code cells)
      (cond
        [(= code 1) (normalize-cells cells)]
        [(= code 2) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw cells))]
        [(= code 3) (normalize-cells (flip-cells-lr cells))]
        [else (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw (flip-cells-lr cells)))]))
    (define anchors
      (filter
        (lambda (p)
          (and (> (first p) 0)
               (= (third p) 6)
               (member? (cell-at g (- (first p) 1) (second p)) (list 1 2 3 4))))
        (grid-cells g)))
    (define stamp-cells
      (flatmap
        (lambda (a)
          (let* ((ar (first a))
                 (ac (second a))
                 (code (cell-at g (- ar 1) ac))
                 (shp (transform code shape)))
            (map (lambda (p) (list (+ ar (fst p)) (+ ac (snd p)))) shp)))
        anchors))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c h w) (pos-in? (list r c) stamp-cells))
            8
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Write the normalized XOR of two shapes into the output frame
written_solution: Normalize the red(2) shape and the green(3) shape to their own bounding boxes, align them at the same top-left corner, then compute the XOR of their occupied cells. Write that XOR shape in cyan(8) into the interior of the gray(5) output frame, aligned to the frame interior's top-left corner.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define (area obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
    (define (frame-perimeter obj)
      (- (+ (* 2 (obj-h obj)) (* 2 (obj-w obj))) 4))
    (define (border-cell? obj p)
      (or (= (fst p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (fst p) (obj-r2 obj))
          (= (snd p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (snd p) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
           (> (obj-h obj) 1)
           (> (obj-w obj) 1)
           (= (obj-size obj) (frame-perimeter obj))
           (all? (lambda (p) (border-cell? obj p)) (obj-cells obj))))
    (define red (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
    (define green (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 3)) (objects g 0))))))
    (define sxor
      (normalize-cells
        (append
          (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p green))) red)
          (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p red))) green))))
    (define frame
      (first
        (sort
          (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
          (lambda (a b) (> (area a) (area b))))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
               (local (list (- r (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1)) (- c (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)))))
          (if (and (> r (obj-r1 frame)) (< r (obj-r2 frame))
                   (> c (obj-c1 frame)) (< c (obj-c2 frame))
                   (has-cell? local sxor))
              8
              v))))))

title: Mark wall-constrained distance ties between the two seeds
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. For every empty cell, compare its shortest-path distance to the red(2) seed 2 and the green(3) seed 3. Recolor the cells whose two distances are equal and finite to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (record-of p records)
      (find-first (lambda (rec) (same-pos? p (first rec))) records))
    (define (neighbors p)
      (filter
        (lambda (n)
          (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
            (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5)))))
        (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (fst p) (fst d)) (+ (snd p) (snd d)))) cardinal-deltas)))
    (define (dist-records start)
      (let loop ((queue (list start)) (records (list (list start 0))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            records
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (cur-dist (second (record-of cur records))))
              (let update ((ns (neighbors cur)) (q restq) (recs records))
                (if (empty? ns)
                    (loop q recs)
                    (let ((n (first ns)))
                      (if (record-of n recs)
                          (update (cdr ns) q recs)
                          (update (cdr ns) (append q (list n)) (append recs (list (list n (+ cur-dist 1)))))))))))))
    (let* ((s2 (first (find-color g 2)))
           (s3 (first (find-color g 3)))
           (d2 (dist-records s2))
           (d3 (dist-records s3)))
      (grid-from-fn h w
        (lambda (r c)
          (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
                 (p (list r c))
                 (r2 (record-of p d2))
                 (r3 (record-of p d3)))
            (if (and (= v 0) r2 r3 (= (second r2) (second r3))) 8 v)))))))

title: Fill the bounding boxes of the odd-frequency shape class
written_solution: Group the red(2) components by normalized shape up to rotation. Exactly one shape class occurs an odd number of times. For every component in that odd-frequency class, fill its whole bbox with orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define red-objs (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0)))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b))
           (all? (lambda (p) (has-cell? p b)) a)))
    (define (rotations cells)
      (let* ((r0 (normalize-cells cells))
             (r1 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r0)))
             (r2 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r1)))
             (r3 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw r2))))
        (list r0 r1 r2 r3)))
    (define (same-rot-shape? a b)
      (let ((sa (normalize-cells (obj-cells a)))
            (rots (rotations (obj-cells b))))
        (any? (lambda (rb) (same-cells? sa rb)) rots)))
    (define (same-count obj)
      (count-where (lambda (other) (same-rot-shape? obj other)) red-objs))
    (define targets (filter (lambda (obj) (= (remainder (same-count obj) 2) 1)) red-objs))
    (define (inside-target-bbox? r c)
      (any?
        (lambda (obj)
          (and (>= r (obj-r1 obj)) (<= r (obj-r2 obj))
               (>= c (obj-c1 obj)) (<= c (obj-c2 obj))))
        targets))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (inside-target-bbox? r c) 7 (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Fill even-marker chambers with their majority color
written_solution: Gray(5) walls partition the grid into chambers. For each chamber, count the colored markers 1-4 inside it. If the chamber contains an even positive number of markers and one color is a strict majority, fill that chamber's background cells with the majority color. Chambers with odd counts or no markers remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (chamber start)
      (let loop ((queue (list start)) (seen (list)) (acc (list)))
        (if (empty? queue)
            acc
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (r (fst cur))
                   (c (snd cur)))
              (if (or (pos-in? cur seen) (= (cell-at g r c) 5))
                  (loop restq seen acc)
                  (let* ((new-seen (cons cur seen))
                         (neighbors
                           (filter
                             (lambda (n)
                               (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
                                 (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                      (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                      (not (pos-in? n new-seen)))))
                             (map (lambda (d) (list (+ r (fst d)) (+ c (snd d)))) cardinal-deltas))))
                    (loop (append restq neighbors) new-seen (cons cur acc))))))))
    (define marker-colors (list 1 2 3 4))
    (define (markers cells)
      (filter
        (lambda (v) (member? v marker-colors))
        (map (lambda (p) (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))) cells)))
    (define (majority markers)
      (if (empty? markers)
          #f
          (let* ((counts (map (lambda (color) (list color (count-where (lambda (v) (= v color)) markers))) marker-colors))
                 (max-count (max-list (map second counts)))
                 (winners (filter (lambda (entry) (= (second entry) max-count)) counts)))
            (if (= (length winners) 1) (first (first winners)) #f))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (= v 0)
              (let* ((cells (chamber (list r c)))
                     (ms (markers cells))
                     (maj (majority ms)))
                (if (and maj (> (length ms) 0) (= (remainder (length ms) 2) 0)) maj v))
              v))))))

written_solution: Find the maroon(9) cell and record the relative positions of all yellow(4) cells around it. Erase the template. For every red(2) in the grid, place yellow(4)s at those same relative offsets and keep the anchor itself as red(2).
