written_solution: Each red(2) source emits straight rays up, down, left, and right. The rays pass through zeros until the grid edge and paint those cells orange(7). The source cells themselves stay red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((starts (find-color g 2)))
    (define (draw-dir out start d)
      (let walk ([acc out] [r (+ (first start) (first d))] [c (+ (second start) (second d))])
        (cond [(not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) acc]
              [(not (= (at g r c) 0)) acc]
              [else (walk (set-cell acc r c 7) (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))])))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([start (in-list starts)]
                [d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
      (draw-dir out start d))))

title: Row Bridge
written_solution: Whenever a row contains exactly two blue(1) cells, fill the entire segment between them with blue(1), including the endpoints. Leave all other rows unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (let ((cols-hit (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))] #:when (= (at g r c) 1)) c)))
      (if (= (length cols-hit) 2)
          (paint-cells out
            (for/list ([c (in-range (apply min cols-hit) (+ (apply max cols-hit) 1))])
              (list r c))
            1)
          out))))

title: Missing Corner
written_solution: In any 2×2 block that has three copies of the same non-background color and one empty cell, fill the empty cell with that color. The examples are spaced so these local completions do not interfere with one another.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
           (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
           (nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
      (if (and (= (length nz) 3) (= (length (remove-duplicates nz)) 1))
          (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list cells)] [v (in-list vals)])
            (if (= v 0) (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) (first nz)) acc))
          out))))

title: Keep the Live Columns
written_solution: Delete every column that is entirely zero. Keep the remaining columns in their original left-to-right order and keep all rows unchanged, so the output is a thinner version of the input.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((keep (filter (lambda (c)
                        (not (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
                      (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))])
      (for/list ([c (in-list keep)])
        (at g r c)))))

title: Divider Mirror
written_solution: The full column of gray(5) cells is a mirror line. Copy every nonzero cell from the left side to the equally distant position on the right side, preserving its color. Keep the original left side and the divider unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((div (first (filter (lambda (c)
                              (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                            (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range div)])
      (let ((v (at g r c))
            (mc (- (* 2 div) c)))
        (if (and (not (member v (list 0 5))) (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r mc) 0))
            (set-cell out r mc v)
            out)))))

title: Solidify the Box
written_solution: Find all green(3) cells. Compute the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that contains them, then fill that entire rectangle with green(3). Everything else becomes black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 3))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
                 3)))

title: Readout Strip
written_solution: Read the nonzero cells in row-major order: top row to bottom row, and within each row left to right. Output a single row containing exactly those color values with no zeros between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (list (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))))

title: Seeded Frames
written_solution: Each rectangular frame made of blue(1) contains exactly one colored seed cell in its interior. Keep the frame itself, and fill the entire interior of that frame with the seed’s color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let ((seed
           (first (reverse (filter (lambda (v) (not (member v (list 0 1))))
                             (for*/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]
                                         [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))])
                               (at g r c)))))))
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]
                  [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))])
        (set-cell acc r c seed)))))

title: Rectangle Sort
written_solution: Each nonzero component is a solid rectangle. Crop each rectangle to its own bbox, sort the cropped rectangles by area from smallest to largest, and place them left-to-right with one background column between consecutive pieces.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                             (list (obj-size obj)
                                   (obj-r1 obj)
                                   (obj-c1 obj)
                                   (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                           (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                              [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                              [else (< (third a) (third b))]))))
         (rects (map fourth items))
         (out-h (apply max (map rows rects)))
         (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols rects)) (max 0 (- (length rects) 1)))))
    (let pack ([remaining rects] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((rect (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows rect))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols rect))])
                         (let ((v (at rect r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols rect) 1) next))))))

title: Largest Crop
written_solution: Find the largest orthogonally connected nonzero component in the grid. Output that component cropped tightly to its own bbox, preserving its exact shape and colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 0 1))))
         (objs (sort (objects mask 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                             [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
         (chosen (first objs)))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Chamber Rays
written_solution: Inside the rectangular wall of 1s, each colored source cell projects rays in the four cardinal directions. The rays keep the source’s own color and extend through zeros until just before they would hit the wall.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((starts (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member (third cell) (list 0 1)))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (draw-dir out start d)
      (let walk ([acc out] [r (+ (first start) (first d))] [c (+ (second start) (second d))])
        (cond [(not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) acc]
              [(= (at g r c) 1) acc]
              [(not (= (at g r c) 0)) (walk acc (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))]
              [else (walk (set-cell acc r c (third start)) (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))])))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([start (in-list starts)]
                [d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
      (draw-dir out start d))))

title: Pair Connectors
written_solution: Each non-background color appears exactly twice. If the two copies lie in the same row, fill the horizontal segment between them; if they lie in the same column, fill the vertical segment between them. Keep the endpoints themselves.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (remove-duplicates
                                         (map third
                                           (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0)))
                                                   (grid-cells g)))))])
    (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length pts) 2)
          (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
            (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
                   (paint-cells out
                     (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b))
                                             (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
                       (list (first a) c))
                     color)]
                  [(= (second a) (second b))
                   (paint-cells out
                     (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b))
                                             (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
                       (list r (second a)))
                     color)]
                  [else out]))
          out))))

title: BBox Overlap
written_solution: Take the bbox of all 2-cells and the bbox of all 3-cells. Compute the overlap of those two rectangles. Output only that overlap region as a solid rectangle of cyan(8), cropped to its own size.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((bb2 (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (bb3 (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (r0 (max (first bb2) (first bb3)))
         (c0 (max (second bb2) (second bb3)))
         (r1 (min (third bb2) (third bb3)))
         (c1 (min (fourth bb2) (fourth bb3))))
    (empty-grid (+ (- r1 r0) 1) (+ (- c1 c0) 1) 8)))

title: Marker Rotation Crop
written_solution: A single command color specifies how to rotate the main object after cropping it to its bbox: red(2) → identity, green(3) → 90° clockwise, yellow(4) → 180°, gray(5) → 90° counter-clockwise. The command cell itself does not appear in the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((cmd (at g 0 0)))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 2) grid]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [else (rotate-ccw grid)]))
    (let* ((cleaned (set-cell g 0 0 0))
           (mask (grid-from-fn (rows cleaned) (cols cleaned)
                   (lambda (r c) (if (= (at cleaned r c) 0) 0 1))))
           (objs (sort (objects mask 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                               [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                               [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
           (obj (first objs)))
      (apply-cmd (subgrid cleaned (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) cmd))))

title: Palette Mask Multiplication
written_solution: The top row gives a palette order. Elsewhere in the grid there is a single mask made of 1s. Crop that mask to its bbox, then repeat it once for each palette color, recoloring the mask with that color and arranging the copies left-to-right with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((palette (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (mask (grid-from-fn (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                             (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)
                 (lambda (r c)
                   (if (= (at g (+ (first bb) r) (+ (second bb) c)) 1) 1 0)))))
    (define copies
      (map (lambda (color)
             (grid-from-fn (rows mask) (cols mask)
               (lambda (r c) (if (= (at mask r c) 1) color 0))))
           palette))
    (define out-h (rows mask))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols copies)) (max 0 (- (length copies) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining copies] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((p (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows p))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols p))])
                         (let ((v (at p r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols p) 1) next))))))

title: Nested Depth Paint
written_solution: Every nonzero object is a rectangular frame of blue(1) nested inside larger frames. Recolor the outermost frame to red(2), the next frame to green(3), then 4, then 5, and so on as depth increases inward.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))
                              (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))]
                             [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                             [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))])))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)]
               [depth (in-naturals 2)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) depth))))

title: Hole Histogram
written_solution: Read the connected red(2) objects from left to right. For each object, count how many holes are enclosed inside it. Output a single row where each entry is hole-count plus one: solid objects become blue(1), one-hole objects become red(2), two-hole objects become green(3), and so on.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))
                     (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))))))
    (list (map (lambda (obj) (+ (topo-count-holes g obj 0) 1)) objs))))

title: Ray Clash Grid
written_solution: Every nonzero source projects rays up, down, left, and right through empty space until the boundary. background cells reached by exactly one source take that source’s color. background cells reached by two or more different source colors become cyan(8). Original source cells stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((sources (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (clear-between? src r c)
      (let ((sr (first src)) (sc (second src)))
        (cond [(= sr r)
               (all? (lambda (cc) (= (at g r cc) 0))
                     (range (+ (min sc c) 1) (max sc c)))]
              [(= sc c)
               (all? (lambda (rr) (= (at g rr c) 0))
                     (range (+ (min sr r) 1) (max sr r)))]
              [else #f])))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let ((hits (remove-duplicates
                          (map third
                            (filter (lambda (src) (clear-between? src r c)) sources)))))
              (cond [(= (length hits) 1) (first hits)]
                    [(>= (length hits) 2) 8]
                    [else 0])))))))

title: Perimeter Sort
written_solution: Crop each connected nonzero component to its bbox. Compute its orthogonal perimeter, sort the cropped pieces from largest perimeter to smallest, and stack them top-to-bottom with one background row between pieces.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (perimeter obj)
      (apply +
        (map (lambda (p)
               (count-where (lambda (d)
                              (not (member (list (+ (first p) (first d))
                                                 (+ (second p) (second d)))
                                           (obj-cells obj))))
                            cardinal-deltas))
             (obj-cells obj))))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (perimeter obj)
                                     (obj-r1 obj)
                                     (obj-c1 obj)
                                     (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (> (first a) (first b))]
                    [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                    [else (< (third a) (third b))]))))
    (define crops (map fourth items))
    (define out-h (+ (apply + (map rows crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (define out-w (apply max (map cols crops)))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [top 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((p (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows p))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols p))])
                         (let ((v (at p r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) c v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ top (rows p) 1) next))))))

title: Command-Rotated Template Strip
written_solution: The top row contains rotation commands in order: 2 → keep the template as-is, 3 → rotate it 90° clockwise, 4 → 180°, and 5 → 270° clockwise. Crop the unique template component below, apply those rotations in command order, and place the resulting copies left-to-right with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((cmds (filter (lambda (v) (member v (list 2 3 4 5))) (row g 0))))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 2) grid]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [else (rotate-ccw grid)]))
    (let* ((body (for/fold ([out g]) ([c (in-range (cols g))]) (set-cell out 0 c 0)))
           (mask (grid-from-fn (rows body) (cols body)
                   (lambda (r c) (if (= (at body r c) 0) 0 1))))
           (objs (sort (objects mask 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                               [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                               [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
           (obj (first objs))
           (template (subgrid body (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
           (copies (map (lambda (cmd) (apply-cmd template cmd)) cmds))
           (out-h (apply max (map rows copies)))
           (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols copies)) (max 0 (- (length copies) 1)))))
      (let pack ([remaining copies] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            out
            (let* ((p (first remaining))
                   (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                     ([r (in-range (rows p))]
                                      [c (in-range (cols p))])
                           (let ((v (at p r c)))
                             (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
              (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols p) 1) next)))))))

title: Normalized XOR
written_solution: Take the red(2) object and the green(3) object, crop each one to its own bbox, and align those two cropped occupancy masks at the top-left corner of a common canvas. Mark cyan(8) wherever exactly one mask has a filled cell, 0 where both masks agree, and then crop the result to its nonzero bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (mask color)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g color))))
        (grid-from-fn (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                      (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)
          (lambda (r c)
            (if (= (at g (+ (first bb) r) (+ (second bb) c)) color) 1 0)))))
    (let* ((a (mask 2))
           (b (mask 3))
           (h (max (rows a) (rows b)))
           (w (max (cols a) (cols b)))
           (xor-grid
            (grid-from-fn h w
              (lambda (r c)
                (let ((av (and (< r (rows a)) (< c (cols a)) (= (at a r c) 1)))
                      (bv (and (< r (rows b)) (< c (cols b)) (= (at b r c) 1))))
                  (if (or (and av (not bv)) (and bv (not av))) 8 0))))))
      (crop-to-content xor-grid))))

title: Mark the midpoint between two blue markers
written_solution: Find the two blue(1) markers that lie on the same row or column. Put a red(2) cell exactly at their midpoint and leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((pts (find-color g 1))) (let ((hit (first (filter (lambda (pair) (let ((a (first pair)) (b (second pair))) (or (and (= (first a) (first b)) (= (modulo (abs (- (second a) (second b))) 2) 0) (>= (abs (- (second a) (second b))) 2)) (and (= (second a) (second b)) (= (modulo (abs (- (first a) (first b))) 2) 0) (>= (abs (- (first a) (first b))) 2))))) (pairs pts))))) (if hit (let* ((a (first hit)) (b (second hit)) (mr (quotient (+ (first a) (first b)) 2)) (mc (quotient (+ (second a) (second b)) 2))) (set-cell g mr mc 2)) g))))

title: Recolor the endpoints of straight red segments
written_solution: Every red(2) component is a straight horizontal or vertical segment. Recolor just its two endpoints to yellow(4) and keep the interior cells red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 2)) out
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (rs (map fst cells))
             (cs (map snd cells))
             (r0 (min-list rs))
             (r1 (max-list rs))
             (c0 (min-list cs))
             (c1 (max-list cs)))
        (cond
          ((= r0 r1) (set-cell (set-cell out r0 c0 4) r0 c1 4))
          ((= c0 c1) (set-cell (set-cell out r0 c0 4) r1 c0 4))
          (else out)))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Fill the single missing cell in each green rectangle
written_solution: Each green(3) object is a solid rectangle missing exactly one cell. Locate the missing interior cell in each such rectangle and fill it with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 3)) out
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb))
             (r1 (third bb))
             (c1 (fourth bb)))
        (reduce (lambda (acc r)
          (reduce (lambda (acc2 c)
            (if (= (cell-at g r c) 0)
              (set-cell acc2 r c 8)
              acc2))
            acc (range c0 (+ c1 1))))
          out (range r0 (+ r1 1))))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Mirror the orange motif across the gray divider
written_solution: There is a full gray(5) separator row or column and an orange(7) motif on one side. Reflect that motif across the divider and draw the reflected copy in blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((full-rows (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g))))
         (full-cols (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (if (not (empty? full-rows))
        (let ((div (first full-rows)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 7))])
            (let ((rr (- (* 2 div) (first p))) (c (second p)))
              (if (and (in-bounds? rr c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out rr c) 0))
                  (set-cell out rr c 1)
                  out))))
        (let ((div (first full-cols)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 7))])
            (let ((r (first p)) (cc (- (* 2 div) (second p))))
              (if (and (in-bounds? r cc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r cc) 0))
                  (set-cell out r cc 1)
                  out)))))))

title: Connect the aligned magenta markers
written_solution: Two magenta(6) markers lie on the same row or column. Fill all cells strictly between them with cyan(8), keeping the markers themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Two magenta endpoints define one horizontal or vertical gap.
  (let* ((pts (find-color g 6))
         (p1 (first pts))
         (p2 (second pts))
         (r1 (fst p1))
         (c1 (snd p1))
         (r2 (fst p2))
         (c2 (snd p2)))
    ;; Preserve endpoints and decorations; paint only the strict interior cyan.
    (if (= r1 r2)
      (reduce (lambda (out c) (set-cell out r1 c 8)) g (range (+ (min c1 c2) 1) (max c1 c2)))
      (reduce (lambda (out r) (set-cell out r c1 8)) g (range (+ (min r1 r2) 1) (max r1 r2))))))

title: Crop to the tight bounding box of the nonzero pattern
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (if bb
        (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
        (empty-grid 1 1 0))))

title: Recolor blue components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Inspect each blue(1) component. If it touches exactly one outer border of the grid, recolor the whole component red(2); otherwise leave it blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 1)) out
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (top (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) cells))
             (bottom (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) (- h 1))) cells))
             (left (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) 0)) cells))
             (right (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) (- w 1))) cells))
             (touch-count (+ (if top 1 0) (if bottom 1 0) (if left 1 0) (if right 1 0))))
        (if (= touch-count 1)
          (recolor-cells out cells 2)
          out))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Rotate the green template into the gray frame using the control color
written_solution: A green(3) template sits outside a hollow gray(5) frame. The singleton control color chooses a rotation, and the rotated template is copied into the frame interior in cyan(8), aligned to the frame’s top-left interior corner.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define control
      (first (filter (lambda (color) (= (length (find-color g color)) 1)) (list 1 2 4 6))))
    (define k (cond [(= control 1) 0] [(= control 2) 1] [(= control 4) 2] [else 3]))
    (define template
      (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))
                              (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (define frame
      (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 5)
                                            (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))))
                           (objects g 0))
                   (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (rotate template k))])
      (let ((r (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1 (first p)))
            (c (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1 (second p))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r c) 0))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Take the Cartesian product of border row and column markers
written_solution: Blue(1) cells on the left border mark rows, and red(2) cells on the top border mark columns. Fill every marked row/column intersection with green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mark-rows (map fst (find-color g 1)))
         (mark-cols (map snd (filter (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) (find-color g 2)))))
    (reduce (lambda (out r)
      (reduce (lambda (acc c) (set-cell acc r c 3)) out mark-cols))
      g mark-rows)))

title: Recolor the orange component that touches both top and left
written_solution: Among the orange(7) components, exactly one touches both the top and the left border. Recolor that component cyan(8) and leave the others unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (reduce (lambda (out obj)
    (if (not (= (obj-color obj) 7)) out
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (touch-top (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) cells))
             (touch-left (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) 0)) cells)))
        (if (and touch-top touch-left)
          (recolor-cells out cells 8)
          out))))
    g (objects g 0)))

title: Draw the rectangle outline from two opposite green corners
written_solution: The two green(3) cells are opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Draw that rectangle’s outline in cyan(8), keeping the original green(3) corners.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((pts (find-color g 3)))
    (if (= (length pts) 2)
        (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))
               (r0 (min (first a) (first b))) (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
               (c0 (min (second a) (second b))) (c1 (max (second a) (second b))))
          (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))] [c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))])
            (if (and (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1)) (= (at out r c) 0))
                (set-cell out r c 8)
                out)))
        g)))

title: Translate the template by the sum of two marker vectors
written_solution: Use the vector from red(2) to green(3) and add the vector from yellow(4) to magenta(6). Copy the blue(1) template by that summed translation and draw the copy in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((template (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                                           (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
         (a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3)))
         (c (first (find-color g 4)))
         (d (first (find-color g 6)))
         (dr (+ (- (first b) (first a)) (- (first d) (first c))))
         (dc (+ (- (second b) (second a)) (- (second d) (second c)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list template)])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) dr)) (col (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r col (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r col) 0))
            (set-cell out r col 8)
            out)))))

title: Fill the chamber with the most seeds using its majority color
written_solution: Walls gray(5) partition the grid into chambers. Count the non-wall seed cells in each chamber; choose the chamber with the most seeds, then fill its background cells with that chamber’s majority seed color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (best-score #f)
        (best-cells (list))
        (best-color 0))
    (define (score-better? score old)
      (or (not old)
          (> (first score) (first old))
          (and (= (first score) (first old))
               (or (> (second score) (second old))
                   (and (= (second score) (second old))
                        (> (third score) (third old)))))))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 5))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define cells (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (let* ((seed-values (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0)))
                                    (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))))
          (unless (empty? seed-values)
            (define counts (make-hash))
            (for ([v (in-list seed-values)])
              (hash-update! counts v add1 0))
            (define top-color
              (first (sort (hash-keys counts)
                           (lambda (a b)
                             (if (= (hash-ref counts a) (hash-ref counts b))
                                 (< a b)
                                 (> (hash-ref counts a) (hash-ref counts b)))))))
            (define score (list (length seed-values) (hash-ref counts top-color) (- 0 top-color)))
            (when (score-better? score best-score)
              (set! best-score score)
              (set! best-cells cells)
              (set! best-color top-color))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list best-cells)])
      (if (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
          (set-cell out (first p) (second p) best-color)
          out))))

title: Recolor every candidate congruent to the reference under dihedral symmetry
written_solution: The blue(1) object is the reference shape. Recolor any red(2) object that matches it up to rotation or reflection to cyan(8), and leave the non-matching candidates unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (shape-key cells) (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define (all-keys cells)
      (remove-duplicates
       (append* (map (lambda (k)
                       (let ((rot (rotate cells k)))
                         (list (shape-key rot) (shape-key (reflect-h rot)))))
                     (list 0 1 2 3)))))
    (define ref (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                                        (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (define forms (all-keys ref))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (member? (shape-key (obj-cells obj)) forms)
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8)
          out))))

title: Fill the union of all shortest paths through the maze
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls, blue(1) as the start, and red(2) as the goal. Mark every empty cell that lies on at least one shortest path from start to goal with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 1)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 2))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dg (dist-from goal))
    (define D (hash-ref ds (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 999999))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (< D 999999)
                 (hash-has-key? ds (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? dg (cons r c))
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c)) (hash-ref dg (cons r c))) D))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Trace the reflecting beam
written_solution: The emitter blue(1) fires to the right. Mirror green(3) acts like '/', mirror yellow(4) acts like '\\', and wall gray(5) stops the beam. Mark every empty traversed cell with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((source (first (find-color g 1))))
    (define (slash dr dc) (list (- 0 dc) (- 0 dr)))
    (define (backslash dr dc) (list dc dr))
    (let loop ([out g] [r (first source)] [c (+ (second source) 1)] [dr 0] [dc 1] [seen (list)] [fuel 500])
      (if (or (= fuel 0) (not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) (member? (list r c dr dc) seen) (= (at g r c) 5))
          out
          (let* ((v (at g r c))
                 (nd (cond [(= v 3) (slash dr dc)]
                           [(= v 4) (backslash dr dc)]
                           [else (list dr dc)]))
                 (next-out (if (= v 0) (set-cell out r c 8) out)))
            (loop next-out (+ r (first nd)) (+ c (second nd)) (first nd) (second nd) (cons (list r c dr dc) seen) (- fuel 1)))))))

title: Fill the selected band of nested frames
written_solution: The grid contains nested frame outlines in magenta(6). The control blue(1), 2, or 3 selects which interior band to fill with cyan(8): outer band, middle band, or innermost core.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define control (first (filter (lambda (color) (= (length (find-color g color)) 1)) (list 1 2 3))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 6)
                                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (obj-h a) (obj-h b))
                  (> (obj-w a) (obj-w b))
                  (> (obj-h a) (obj-h b))))))
    (define idx (- control 1))
    (define selected (list-ref frames idx))
    (define inner (and (< (+ idx 1) (length frames)) (list-ref frames (+ idx 1))))
    (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 selected) 1) (obj-r2 selected))]
                          [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 selected) 1) (obj-c2 selected))])
      (if (and (= (at out r c) 0)
               (or (not inner)
                   (not (and (> r (obj-r1 inner)) (< r (obj-r2 inner))
                             (> c (obj-c1 inner)) (< c (obj-c2 inner))))))
          (set-cell out r c 8)
          out))))

title: Mark only the cells that are on every shortest path
written_solution: Again using walls 5, start 1, and goal 2, mark the background cells that lie on every shortest path from start to goal. These are the unavoidable shortest-path core cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 1)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 2))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dt (dist-from goal))
    (define D (hash-ref ds (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 999999))
    (define path-cells
      (sort (filter (lambda (p)
                      (and (hash-has-key? ds (cons (first p) (second p)))
                           (hash-has-key? dt (cons (first p) (second p)))
                           (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons (first p) (second p)))
                                 (hash-ref dt (cons (first p) (second p))))
                              D)))
                    (grid-positions g))
            (lambda (a b) (< (hash-ref ds (cons (first a) (second a)))
                             (hash-ref ds (cons (first b) (second b)))))))
    (define cs (make-hash))
    (hash-set! cs (cons (first start) (second start)) 1)
    (for ([p (in-list path-cells)])
      (define cur (cons (first p) (second p)))
      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (let ((nr (+ (first p) (first d))) (nc (+ (second p) (second d))))
          (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                     (hash-has-key? ds (cons nr nc))
                     (= (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc)) (+ (hash-ref ds cur) 1))
                     (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc)) (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc) 999999)) D)
                     (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
            (hash-update! cs (cons nr nc) (lambda (x) (+ x (hash-ref cs cur 0))) 0)))))
    (define ct (make-hash))
    (hash-set! ct (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 1)
    (for ([p (in-list (sort path-cells (lambda (a b) (< (hash-ref dt (cons (first a) (second a)))
                                                         (hash-ref dt (cons (first b) (second b)))))))])
      (define cur (cons (first p) (second p)))
      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (let ((nr (+ (first p) (first d))) (nc (+ (second p) (second d))))
          (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                     (hash-has-key? dt (cons nr nc))
                     (= (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc)) (+ (hash-ref dt cur) 1))
                     (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons nr nc) 999999) (hash-ref dt (cons nr nc))) D)
                     (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
            (hash-update! ct (cons nr nc) (lambda (x) (+ x (hash-ref ct cur 0))) 0)))))
    (define total (hash-ref cs (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 0))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c) 999999) (hash-ref dt (cons r c) 999999)) D)
                 (= (* (hash-ref cs (cons r c) 0) (hash-ref ct (cons r c) 0)) total))
            8
            (at g r c))))))

title: Transform the template, then translate it by the marker vector
written_solution: A control color chooses a symmetry transform of the blue(1) template, and the vector from orange(7) to maroon(9) tells where to move it. Stamp the transformed copy in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define template-obj (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                                      (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
    (define control (first (filter (lambda (color) (= (length (find-color g color)) 1)) (list 2 3 4 6))))
    (define shape (cond [(= control 2) (normalize-cells (obj-cells template-obj))]
                        [(= control 3) (rotate (obj-cells template-obj) 1)]
                        [(= control 4) (reflect-h (obj-cells template-obj))]
                        [else (rotate (obj-cells template-obj) 2)]))
    (define start (first (find-color g 7)))
    (define finish (first (find-color g 9)))
    (define dr (- (first finish) (first start)))
    (define dc (- (second finish) (second start)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list shape)])
      (let ((r (+ (obj-r1 template-obj) dr (first p)))
            (c (+ (obj-c1 template-obj) dc (second p))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r c) 0))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Find the odd shape out under dihedral equivalence
written_solution: All but one of the green(3) components belong to the same shape class up to rotation/reflection. Find the unique outlier and recolor it cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (shape-key cells) (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      ;; Same shape, translated so its bbox starts at (0,0)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define (canonical-key cells)
      (first (sort (append* (map (lambda (k)
                                   (let ((rot (rotate cells k)))
                                     (list (shape-key rot) (shape-key (reflect-h rot)))))
                                 (list 0 1 2 3)))
                   string<?)))
    ;; Mutable lookup table for groups
    (define groups (make-hash))
    (for ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0)))])
      (hash-update! groups (canonical-key (obj-cells obj)) (lambda (xs) (cons obj xs)) (list)))
    (define odd
      (first (append* (map (lambda (k)
                             (let ((xs (hash-ref groups k)))
                               (if (= (length xs) 1) xs (list))))
                           (hash-keys groups)))))
    (if odd (paint-cells g (obj-cells odd) 8) g)))

title: Output the normalized XOR of the two source shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1) and red(2) shapes to the top-left, take their symmetric difference, and output that resulting shape alone, drawn in cyan(8) and tightly cropped.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape1 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                                                        (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))))
         (shape2 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))
                                                        (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))))
         (xor (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (member? p shape1) (member? p shape2))))
                      (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p shape2))) shape1)
                              (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p shape1))) shape2)))))
    (if (empty? xor)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells xor))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Horizontal run endcaps
written_solution: For every row segment of red(2) with length at least 3, change only the first and last cell of that run to cyan(8). Leave the interior 2s and everything else unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (v1-run-end-row grid r c color) (let loop ((cc c)) (if (and (< (+ cc 1) (cols grid)) (= (at grid r (+ cc 1)) color)) (loop (+ cc 1)) cc))) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (cols g)))) (if (and (= (at g r c) 2) (or (= c 0) (not (= (at g r (- c 1)) 2)))) (let ((end (v1-run-end-row g r c 2))) (if (>= (+ 1 (- end c)) 3) (set-cell (set-cell out r c 8) r end 8) out)) out))))

title: Vertical domino promotion

title: In Each Frame, Choose by Size Rank, Transform, and Recenter
written_solution: Each frame contains a key cell and two candidate components. Key 1 → keep the smaller component; key 2 → keep the larger one. If the frame border is 9, rotate the chosen component by 180°; if the border is 8, keep its orientation. Then center the chosen crop inside the frame interior and erase everything else inside the frame.

(rule!
 ;; Cyan(8) and maroon(9) frames each hold small objects plus a KEY
 ;; dot: blue(1) keeps the frame's SMALLEST object, red(2) its LARGEST.
 ;; Redraw every frame with only the chosen object centered inside —
 ;; rotated 180 degrees inside maroon frames.

   (let ()
     (define (frame? o color)  ;; hollow rectangle outline, 3x3+
       (and (= (obj-color o) color)
            (>= (obj-h o) 3) (>= (obj-w o) 3)
            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define (stamp out pat top left)  ;; nonzero cells, clipped
       (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((r (range 0 (rows pat)))
                               (c (range 0 (cols pat))))
         (let ((v (at pat r c)))
           (if (and (> v 0) (in-bounds? (+ top r) (+ left c) h w))
               (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) v)
               acc))))
     (define (process out frame color)
       (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 frame)) (c1 (obj-c1 frame))
              (r2 (obj-r2 frame)) (c2 (obj-c2 frame))
              (key (find-first
                    (lambda (v) (member? v (list 1 2)))
                    (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p)))
                         (positions-in-rect (+ r1 1) (+ c1 1)
                                            (- r2 1) (- c2 1)))))
              (interior  ;; frame contents with key dots scrubbed
               (grid-from-fn (- r2 r1 1) (- c2 c1 1)
                             (lambda (rr cc)
                               (let ((v (at g (+ r1 1 rr)
                                            (+ c1 1 cc))))
                                 (if (or (= v 0)
                                         (member? v (list 1 2)))
                                     0 v)))))
              (objs (sort (objects interior 0)
                          (lambda (a b)
                            (let loop ((xs (list (obj-size a)
                                                 (obj-r1 a)
                                                 (obj-c1 a)))
                                       (ys (list (obj-size b)
                                                 (obj-r1 b)
                                                 (obj-c1 b))))
                              (cond ((null? xs) #f)
                                    ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
                                    ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
                                    (else (loop (rest xs)
                                                (rest ys))))))))
              (chosen (if (= key 1) (first objs) (last objs)))
              (crop (subgrid interior (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen)
                             (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen)))
              (oriented (if (= color 9) (rotate-180 crop) crop)))
         (stamp (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) color)
                oriented
                (+ r1 1 (quotient (- (rows interior)
                                     (rows oriented)) 2))
                (+ c1 1 (quotient (- (cols interior)
                                     (cols oriented)) 2)))))
     (for/fold ((out (empty-grid h w 0)))
               ((color (in-list (list 8 9))))
       (for/fold ((o2 out))
                 ((frame (sort (filter (lambda (o) (frame? o color))
                                       (objects g 0))
                               (lambda (a b)
                                 (or (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                     (and (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                          (< (obj-c1 a)
                                             (obj-c1 b))))))))
         (process o2 frame color))))))

    (define cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))))
    (define color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells))))
    (define reflected
      (map (lambda (p)
             (if (eq? guide-col #f)
                 (list (- (* 2 guide-row) (first p)) (second p))
                 (list (first p) (- (* 2 guide-col) (second p)))))
           cells))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells reflected))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb)))
                             (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb))) 0)
                 (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) reflected)
                 color)))

title: Frequency-Sorted Color Bar
written_solution: Count how many times each non-background color appears. Sort colors by descending count, breaking ties by smaller color number. Output a single row of those colors in that order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (entries (sort
                    (map (lambda (color)
                           (list color (count-where (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color)) (grid-cells g))))
                         colors)
                    (lambda (a b)
                      (cond [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (> (second a) (second b))]
                            [else (< (first a) (first b))])))))
    (list (for*/list ([entry (in-list entries)]
                      [_ (in-range (second entry))])
            (first entry)))))

title: Checker Fill Inside the Frame
written_solution: The most common non-background color is a rectangular frame, and the lone other color is the paint color. Preserve the frame, then fill the interior with a checkerboard of the paint color on even parity cells and 0 on odd parity cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (entries (map (lambda (color)
                         (list color (count-where (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color)) (grid-cells g))))
                       colors))
         (frame-color (first (first (sort entries (lambda (a b) (> (second a) (second b)))))))
         (paint-color (first (first (sort entries (lambda (a b) (< (second a) (second b)))))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g frame-color))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]
                [c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
      (set-cell out r c
        (if (= (modulo (+ (- r (+ (first bb) 1)) (- c (+ (second bb) 1))) 2) 0)
            paint-color
            0)))))

title: Select the Marked Motif
written_solution: Three 3×3 motifs are shown, and a single selector cell in the top row points to one of them by column position. Output only the selected 3×3 motif.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((selector-col (second (first (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0)))
                                             (grid-cells (list (row g 0)))))))
         (start (cond [(< selector-col 4) 1]
                      [(< selector-col 8) 5]
                      [else 9])))
    (subgrid g 2 start 4 (+ start 2))))

title: Lane Docking
written_solution: The maroon(9)s form walls and three independent horizontal lanes. In each lane, move the colored component right as a rigid object until the next step would hit the wall, then keep the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (can-move? board cells)
      (all? (lambda (p)
              (let ((nr (first p)) (nc (+ (second p) 1)))
                (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows board) (cols board))
                     (or (= (at board nr nc) 0) (member? (list nr nc) cells)))))
            cells))
    (define (shift-east cells)
      (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (+ (second p) 1))) cells))
    (define (slide board cells)
      (let loop ([cur cells])
        (if (can-move? board cur) (loop (shift-east cur)) cur)))
    (define walls (find-color g 9))
    (for/fold ([out (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) walls 9)])
              ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) 9))) (objects g 0)))])
      (let* ((board (paint-cells (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) walls 9)
                                 (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj)))
             (moved (slide board (obj-cells obj))))
        (paint-cells out moved (obj-color obj))))))

title: Pack Components by Area
written_solution: Find every connected nonzero component, crop it to its own bbox, sort the cropped objects by descending area and then ascending color, and pack them left-to-right with a single zero column between neighbors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pack-h grids gap)
      (let* ((h (apply max (map rows grids)))
             (w (+ (apply + (map cols grids)) (* gap (max 0 (- (length grids) 1))))))
        (let loop ([out (empty-grid h w 0)] [remaining grids] [left 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              out
              (let ((block (first remaining)))
                (loop (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                  ([r (in-range (rows block))]
                                   [c (in-range (cols block))]
                                   #:when (not (= (at block r c) 0)))
                        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at block r c)))
                      (rest remaining)
                      (+ left (cols block) gap)))))))
    (define sorted-objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
        (lambda (a b)
          (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
    (pack-h (map (lambda (o) (subgrid g (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o))) sorted-objs) 1)))

title: Legend Transform Strip
written_solution: Each header digit tells how to transform the motif underneath: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → flip horizontal, yellow(4) → 180°. Transform the three motifs accordingly and pack the resulting 3×3 panels into one horizontal strip with one black(0) column gap.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-command grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 1) grid]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (rotate-180 grid)]))
    (define (pack-h grids gap)
      (let* ((h (apply max (map rows grids)))
             (w (+ (apply + (map cols grids)) (* gap (max 0 (- (length grids) 1))))))
        (let loop ([out (empty-grid h w 0)] [remaining grids] [left 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              out
              (let ((block (first remaining)))
                (loop (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                  ([r (in-range (rows block))]
                                   [c (in-range (cols block))]
                                   #:when (not (= (at block r c) 0)))
                        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at block r c)))
                      (rest remaining)
                      (+ left (cols block) gap)))))))
    (let ((blocks (map (lambda (start)
                         (apply-command (subgrid g 2 start 4 (+ start 2))
                                        (at g 0 (+ start 1))))
                       (list 1 5 9))))
      (pack-h blocks 1))))

title: Nearest-Seed Chamber Fill
written_solution: Inside the rectangular frame, each zero cell considers the Manhattan distance to every seed. Collect the distinct colors represented among the nearest seeds. If exactly one nearest color remains, fill the cell with that color; if two or more different colors tie, leave the cell 0. Keep the seeds and the frame unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frame-bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 5)))
         (seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (and (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 5))))
                        (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist cell r c)
      (+ (abs (- r (first cell))) (abs (- c (second cell)))))
    (define (fill-value r c)
      (let* ((dmin (apply min (map (lambda (cell) (dist cell r c)) seeds)))
             (colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (= (dist cell r c) dmin)) seeds)))))
        (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 0)))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (+ (first frame-bb) 1) (third frame-bb))]
                [c (in-range (+ (second frame-bb) 1) (fourth frame-bb))])
      (if (= (at out r c) 0) (set-cell out r c (fill-value r c)) out))))

title: Palette-Recolored Nested Frames
written_solution: The input contains concentric frames all drawn in the same placeholder color plus a palette strip on the bottom row. Crop the nested-frame region and recolor the outer frame with the first palette color, the next frame with the second, and so on inward.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define palette (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (bottom-row g)))
    (define frame-cells
      (for*/list ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))]
                  [c (in-range (cols g))]
                  #:when (not (= (at g r c) 0)))
        (list r c)))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells frame-cells))
    (define (border-filled? depth)
      (let ((r0 (+ (first bb) (* 2 depth)))
            (c0 (+ (second bb) (* 2 depth)))
            (r1 (- (third bb) (* 2 depth)))
            (c1 (- (fourth bb) (* 2 depth))))
        (and (<= r0 r1) (<= c0 c1)
             (all? (lambda (c) (and (not (= (at g r0 c) 0)) (not (= (at g r1 c) 0))))
                   (range c0 (+ c1 1)))
             (all? (lambda (r) (and (not (= (at g r c0) 0)) (not (= (at g r c1) 0))))
                   (range r0 (+ r1 1))))))
    (define depths
      (let loop ([d 0])
        (if (border-filled? d) (loop (+ d 1)) d)))
    (define out-h (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
    (define out-w (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb))))
    (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [d 0])
      (if (= d depths)
          out
          (let* ((r0 (+ (first bb) (* 2 d)))
                 (c0 (+ (second bb) (* 2 d)))
                 (r1 (- (third bb) (* 2 d)))
                 (c1 (- (fourth bb) (* 2 d)))
                 (color (nth palette d))
                 (cells (append
                          (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list (- r0 (first bb)) (- c (second bb))))
                          (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list (- r1 (first bb)) (- c (second bb))))
                          (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list (- r (first bb)) (- c0 (second bb))))
                          (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list (- r (first bb)) (- c1 (second bb)))))))
            (loop (paint-cells out cells color) (+ d 1)))))))

title: Dihedral Match Matrix
written_solution: Compare the two top motifs against the two bottom motifs using shape only, ignoring color. Output a 2×2 matrix where a cell is 8 if the corresponding pair is equivalent under some rotation or reflection, otherwise 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (binary panel)
      (grid-from-fn (rows panel) (cols panel)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at panel r c) 0) 0 1))))
    (define (same-under-dihedral? a b)
      (let* ((aa (crop-to-content (binary a)))
             (bb (crop-to-content (binary b)))
             (variants (list aa (rotate-cw aa) (rotate-180 aa) (rotate-ccw aa)
                             (flip-lr aa) (flip-ud aa)
                             (rotate-cw (flip-lr aa)) (rotate-cw (flip-ud aa)))))
        (not (eq? (find-first (lambda (v) (equal? (crop-to-content v) bb)) variants) #f))))
    (let ((tops (list (subgrid g 0 0 2 2) (subgrid g 0 6 2 8)))
          (bots (list (subgrid g 4 0 6 2) (subgrid g 4 6 6 8))))
      (grid-from-fn 2 2
        (lambda (r c)
          (if (same-under-dihedral? (nth tops r) (nth bots c)) 8 0))))))

title: Transform Analogy
written_solution: The second 3×3 panel is the first panel after one geometric transform from a small fixed family. Infer that transform from panel A to panel B, then apply the same transform to panel C and output the transformed 3×3 grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (letrec ((apply-transform
            (lambda (grid cmd)
              (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
                    [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
                    [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
                    [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
                    [else (flip-ud grid)]))))
    (let* ((a (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 1) 2))
           (b (subgrid g 0 4 (- (rows g) 1) 6))
           (c (subgrid g 0 8 (- (rows g) 1) 10))
           (cmd (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (apply-transform a t) b)) (list 0 1 2 4 5))))
      (apply-transform c (if (eq? cmd #f) 0 cmd)))))

title: Commanded Room Slides
written_solution: The maroon(9)s divide the grid into four independent rooms. In each chamber, the top-left cell is a command: blue(1) → up, red(2) → right, green(3) → down, yellow(4) → left. Remove that command marker, slide the colored object in that chamber as far as possible in the commanded direction, and keep the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (direction cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 1) (list -1 0)]
            [(= cmd 2) (list 0 1)]
            [(= cmd 3) (list 1 0)]
            [else (list 0 -1)]))
    (define (can-move? board cells dir)
      (all? (lambda (p)
              (let ((nr (+ (first p) (first dir))) (nc (+ (second p) (second dir))))
                (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows board) (cols board))
                     (or (= (at board nr nc) 0) (member? (list nr nc) cells)))))
            cells))
    (define (shift cells dir)
      (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) (first dir)) (+ (second p) (second dir)))) cells))
    (define (slide board cells dir)
      (let loop ([cur cells])
        (if (can-move? board cur dir) (loop (shift cur dir)) cur)))
    (define (wall-board)
      (grid-from-fn 13 13
        (lambda (r c) (if (or (= r 0) (= r 6) (= r 12) (= c 0) (= c 6) (= c 12)) 9 0))))
    (define (room-cells r0 c0)
      (for*/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r0 5))]
                  [c (in-range c0 (+ c0 5))]
                  #:when (let ((v (at g r c)))
                           (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9))
                                (not (member? v (list 1 2 3 4))))))
        (list r c)))
    (for/fold ([out (paint-cells (empty-grid 13 13 0) (find-color g 9) 9)])
              ([origin (in-list (list (list 1 1) (list 1 7) (list 7 1) (list 7 7)))])
      (let* ((r0 (first origin))
             (c0 (second origin))
             (cmd (at g r0 c0))
             (cells (room-cells r0 c0)))
        (if (empty? cells)
            out
            (let* ((color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells))))
                   (board (paint-cells (wall-board) cells color))
                   (moved (slide board cells (direction cmd))))
              (paint-cells out moved color)))))))

title: Blocked Geodesic Voronoi
written_solution: The frame and interior 5-cells are walls. For every reachable zero cell, compute the shortest BFS step count to each colored seed while staying out of walls. Color the cell with the unique nearest seed, and leave ties as 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (and (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 5))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (define (shortest-distance r c seed)
      (let ((visited (make-hash)))
        (let bfs ([queue (list (list r c 0))])
          (cond [(empty? queue) 999]
                [else
                 (let* ((cur (first queue))
                        (rr (first cur))
                        (cc (second cur))
                        (dist (third cur))
                        (restq (rest queue)))
                   (cond [(hash-has-key? visited (list rr cc)) (bfs restq)]
                         [(not (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g))) (bfs restq)]
                         [(= (at g rr cc) 5) (bfs restq)]
                         [(and (= rr (first seed)) (= cc (second seed))) dist]
                         [else
                          (hash-set! visited (list rr cc) #t)
                          (bfs (append restq
                                       (map (lambda (d)
                                              (list (+ rr (first d)) (+ cc (second d)) (+ dist 1)))
                                            cardinal-deltas)))]))]))))
    (define (fill-value r c)
      (let* ((distances (map (lambda (seed) (list (shortest-distance r c seed) (third seed))) seeds))
             (dmin (apply min (map first distances)))
             (colors (remove-duplicates (map second (filter (lambda (x) (= (first x) dmin)) distances)))))
        (if (and (< dmin 999) (= (length colors) 1)) (first colors) 0)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0) (not (= (at g r c) 5)))
            (fill-value r c)
            (at g r c))))))

title: Commanded Template Mosaic
written_solution: Two source templates are shown in the input. Each command digit selects one of the templates and one transform: blue(1)..yellow(4) mean template A with identity, 90° clockwise, flip horizontal, or 180°; gray(5)..cyan(8) mean the same four transforms applied to template B. Build the 2×2 output mosaic in row-major order from the four commands.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (decode cmd)
      (list (if (<= cmd 4) 0 1)
            (cond [(or (= cmd 1) (= cmd 5)) 0]
                  [(or (= cmd 2) (= cmd 6)) 1]
                  [(or (= cmd 3) (= cmd 7)) 4]
                  [else 2])))
    (let* ((a (subgrid g 2 1 4 3))
           (b (subgrid g 2 7 4 9))
           (tiles (map (lambda (pos)
                         (let* ((cmd (at g 0 pos))
                                (info (decode cmd))
                                (base (if (= (first info) 0) a b)))
                           (apply-transform base (second info))))
                       (list 1 3 7 9))))
      (vconcat (hconcat (first tiles) (second tiles))
               (hconcat (third tiles) (fourth tiles))))))

title: Overlap After Transform
written_solution: A command digit specifies how to transform the right-hand 3×3 motif: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → flip horizontal, yellow(4) → 180°. After transforming it, output a 3×3 grid with cyan(8) exactly where the transformed right motif overlaps the left motif, and black(0) elsewhere.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; The command cell controls how the right 3x3 occupancy mask is aligned.
  (letrec ((apply-command
            (lambda (grid cmd)
              (cond [(= cmd 1) grid]
                    [(= cmd 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
                    [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr grid)]
                    [else (rotate-180 grid)]))))
    ;; The two motifs occupy columns 0..2 and 4..6 below the command row.
    (let* ((cmd (at g 0 3))
           (left (subgrid g 1 0 3 2))
           (right (apply-command (subgrid g 1 4 3 6) cmd)))
      ;; Colors inside the motifs are irrelevant: cyan marks occupancy overlap.
      (grid-from-fn 3 3
        (lambda (r c)
          (if (and (not (zero? (at left r c)))
                   (not (zero? (at right r c))))
              8
              0))))))

title: Pack by Hole Count
written_solution: Extract every component, count how many enclosed holes it has inside its own bbox, crop the component, sort the cropped components by descending hole count and then descending area, and pack them left-to-right with one zero column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (hole-count obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
             (w (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb))))
             (occ (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb))))
                       (obj-cells obj))))
        (define (free? r c) (not (member? (list r c) occ)))
        (let loop ([remaining (filter (lambda (p) (free? (first p) (second p)))
                                      (positions-in-rect 0 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)))]
                   [holes 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              holes
              (let* ((p (first remaining))
                     (region (connected-region (empty-grid h w 0) (first p) (second p)
                               (lambda (r c v) (free? r c)) 4))
                     (touch? (any? (lambda (q)
                                     (or (= (first q) 0) (= (second q) 0)
                                         (= (first q) (- h 1)) (= (second q) (- w 1))))
                                   region)))
                (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining)
                      (if touch? holes (+ holes 1))))))))
    (define (pack-h grids gap)
      (let* ((h (apply max (map rows grids)))
             (w (+ (apply + (map cols grids)) (* gap (max 0 (- (length grids) 1))))))
        (let loop ([out (empty-grid h w 0)] [remaining grids] [left 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              out
              (let ((block (first remaining)))
                (loop (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                  ([r (in-range (rows block))]
                                   [c (in-range (cols block))]
                                   #:when (not (= (at block r c) 0)))
                        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at block r c)))
                      (rest remaining)
                      (+ left (cols block) gap)))))))
    (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (let ((ha (hole-count a)) (hb (hole-count b)))
                           (cond [(not (= ha hb)) (> ha hb)]
                                 [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                 [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])))))
           (blocks (map (lambda (o) (subgrid g (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o))) objs)))
      (pack-h blocks 1))))

title: Phase Transform Tile Grid
written_solution: The lower-left 3×3 panel is the base motif. Row-guide digits on the left and column-guide digits on the top choose transforms from a small family, and each output tile is formed by composing the row transform with the column transform on the base motif. Assemble the resulting 2×2 tile grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-phase grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 1) grid]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [else (flip-lr grid)]))
    (let* ((row-cmds (list (at g 2 0) (at g 4 0)))
           (col-cmds (list (at g 0 1) (at g 0 3)))
           (motif (subgrid g 2 1 4 3))
           (rows-out
            (map (lambda (rc)
                   (let ((tiles (map (lambda (cc)
                                        (apply-phase (apply-phase motif rc) cc))
                                      col-cmds)))
                     (hconcat (first tiles) (second tiles))))
                 row-cmds)))
      (vconcat (first rows-out) (second rows-out)))))

title: Color-and-Transform Analogy
written_solution: Panel B is panel A after a geometric transform plus a recoloring from the source color to a target color. Infer the transform from the change in shape and infer the target color from panel B, then transform panel C in the same way and recolor all of its occupied cells to the target color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (binary grid)
      (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at grid r c) 0) 0 1))))
    ;; A->B reveals the support transform; B's nonzero color is the target color.
    (let* ((a (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 1) 2))
           (b (subgrid g 0 4 (- (rows g) 1) 6))
           (c (subgrid g 0 8 (- (rows g) 1) 10))
           (a-mask (binary a))
           (b-mask (binary b))
           (target (third (first (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells b)))))
           (cmd (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (apply-transform a-mask t) b-mask)) (list 0 1 2 4 5)))
           ;; Apply the inferred transform to C before recoloring its occupied cells.
           (out-mask (apply-transform (binary c) (if (eq? cmd #f) 0 cmd))))
      (grid-from-fn (rows out-mask) (cols out-mask)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at out-mask r c) 0) 0 target))))))

title: Recolor the Outermost Layer
skills: boundary peeling, same-size recolor, component-wise depth
written_solution: Compute onion layers for every nonzero component. Recolor all cells in depth 1, the outermost peel layer, to cyan(8) while leaving deeper occupied cells unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (keep-cell? v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9)))) (define (shape-mask grid) (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid) (lambda (r c) (if (keep-cell?
