title: Plain : Layer-Colored :: Plain : ?
skills: analogy, palette inference, candidate selection, panel reasoning
written_solution: Infer the depth-to-color mapping from the first two panels, apply that same mapping to the third panel, and mark the candidate that matches the resulting layer-colored shape.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Panels split by maroon(9) columns. Panels 1+2 are a PLAIN/COLORED
 ;; pair teaching an onion palette: peel each shape into boundary
 ;; layers and read the majority color per depth. Recolor panel 3 by
 ;; that palette (the EXPECTED answer) and emit one row marking which
 ;; of the remaining candidate panels equals it (8 = match).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (keep-cell? v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 9))))
     (define (comp-masks grid)  ;; one 0/1 mask per shape, left-to-right
       (map (lambda (obj)
              (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows grid) (cols grid) 0)
                           (obj-cells obj) 1))
            (sort (objects (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid)
                                         (lambda (r c)
                                           (if (keep-cell?
                                                (at grid r c))
                                               1 0)))
                           0)
                  (lambda (a b)
                    (let ((ac (obj-cells a)) (bc (obj-cells b)))
                      (if (= (min-of second ac) (min-of second bc))
                          (< (min-of first ac) (min-of first bc))
                          (< (min-of second ac)
                             (min-of second bc))))))))
     (define (peel layers cur depth)  ;; onion: boundary ring = depth
       (if (empty? cur)
           layers
           (let ((boundary
                  (filter (lambda (p)
                            (any? (lambda (d)
                                    (not (member? (list (+ (first p)
                                                           (first d))
                                                        (+ (second p)
                                                           (second d)))
                                                  cur)))
                                  cardinal-deltas))
                          cur)))
             (peel (paint-cells layers boundary depth)
                   (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p boundary)))
                           cur)
                   (+ depth 1)))))
     (define (onion grid)
       (for/fold ((layers (empty-grid (rows grid) (cols grid) 0)))
                 ((comp (in-list (comp-masks grid))))
         (peel layers
               (filter (lambda (p) (> (at comp (first p) (second p))
                                      0))
                       (grid-positions comp))
               1)))
     (define (panels-of grid)  ;; split at full maroon columns
       (let scan ((c 0) (start 0) (acc (list)))
         (cond ((= c (cols grid))
                (if (> c start)
                    (append acc (list (subgrid grid 0 start
                                               (- (rows grid) 1)
                                               (- c 1))))
                    acc))
               ((all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 9))
                      (range 0 (rows grid)))
                (scan (+ c 1) (+ c 1)
                      (if (> c start)
                          (append acc (list (subgrid grid 0 start
                                                     (- (rows grid) 1)
                                                     (- c 1))))
                          acc)))
               (else (scan (+ c 1) start acc)))))
     (define (majority vals)
       (let ((nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
         (if (empty? nz)
             0
             (first (first (sort (map (lambda (col)
                                        (list col
                                              (count-if (lambda (v)
                                                          (= v col))
                                                        nz)))
                                      (remove-duplicates nz))
                                 (lambda (a b)
                                   (if (= (second a) (second b))
                                       (< (first a) (first b))
                                       (> (second a) (second b))))))))))
     (define (palette-from plain colored)  ;; depth -> majority color
       (let* ((layers (onion plain))
              (depths (filter (lambda (v) (> v 0))
                              (apply append layers))))
         (map (lambda (d)
                (majority (map (lambda (p) (at colored (first p)
                                              (second p)))
                               (filter (lambda (p)
                                         (= (at layers (first p)
                                                (second p))
                                            d))
                                       (grid-positions layers)))))
              (range 1 (+ (if (empty? depths) 0 (apply max depths))
                          1)))))
     (define (recolor panel palette)
       (let ((layers (onion panel)))
         (grid-from-fn (rows panel) (cols panel)
                       (lambda (r c)
                         (let ((d (at layers r c)))
                           (cond ((= d 0) 0)
                                 ((empty? palette) 0)
                                 (else (nth palette
                                            (min (- d 1)
                                                 (- (length palette)
                                                    1))))))))))
     (let* ((panels (panels-of g))
            (expected (recolor (third panels)
                               (palette-from (first panels)
                                             (second panels)))))
       (list (map (lambda (cand) (if (equal? expected cand) 8 0))
                  (rest (rest (rest panels)))))))))

title: In Each Frame, Select by Size Key, Transform, and Pack
written_solution: Handle each frame separately. The top key chooses whether to keep the smaller or larger interior component; the left key chooses the transform (90° clockwise, flip horizontal, or 180°). After selecting and transforming the chosen component, crop it tightly and pack the results into a horizontal strip in frame order.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Each maroon(9) rectangular FRAME holds a few components. The key dot row
 ;; ABOVE the frame picks which one (2 = smallest, else largest); the key dot
 ;; column LEFT of it picks a transform (4 = rotate-cw, 5 = flip-lr,
 ;; 6 = rotate-180, else identity). The chosen, transformed parts line up
 ;; horizontally (vertically centered, 1-col gaps), frames in top-left order.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (crop-nonzero grid)
       (let ((cells (filter (lambda (p) (!= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))
                            (grid-positions grid))))
         (if (empty? cells)
             (list (list 0))
             (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
               (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))
     (define (rect-frame? obj)
       ;; exactly the border of a >=3x3 bbox: every cell on the border AND
       ;; the cell count equals the perimeter
       (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
              (hh (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
              (ww (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb)))))
         (and (>= hh 3) (>= ww 3)
              (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ hh ww)) 4))
              (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (first bb))
                                    (= (first p) (third bb))
                                    (= (second p) (second bb))
                                    (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                    (obj-cells obj)))))
     (define frames
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 9) (rect-frame? o)))
                     (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                 (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                     (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                          (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))
     (define (first-key vals)
       (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (member? v (list 0 9)))) vals)))
     (define (key-above fr)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox fr)))
         (first-key (if (>= (- (first bb) 1) 0)
                        (map (lambda (c) (at g (- (first bb) 1) c))
                             (range (second bb) (+ (fourth bb) 1)))
                        (list)))))
     (define (key-left fr)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox fr)))
         (first-key (if (>= (- (second bb) 1) 0)
                        (map (lambda (r) (at g r (- (second bb) 1)))
                             (range (first bb) (+ (third bb) 1)))
                        (list)))))
     (define (part-of fr)
       (let* ((bb (obj-bbox fr))
              (sub (subgrid g (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                            (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))
              (comps (sort (objects sub 0)
                           (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))
              (chosen (if (= (key-above fr) 2) (first comps) (last comps)))
              (part (crop-nonzero
                     (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows sub) (cols sub) 0)
                                  (obj-cells chosen) (obj-color chosen)))))
         (cond ((= (key-left fr) 4) (rotate-cw part))
               ((= (key-left fr) 5) (flip-lr part))
               ((= (key-left fr) 6) (rotate-180 part))
               (else part))))
     (define (hstack-center pieces)
       (if (empty? pieces)
           (list (list))
           (let* ((hh (apply max (map rows pieces)))
                  (ww (+ (apply + (map cols pieces)) (- (length pieces) 1))))
             (let loop ((xs pieces) (left 0) (out (empty-grid hh ww 0)))
               (if (empty? xs)
                   out
                   (let ((piece (first xs)))
                     (loop (rest xs) (+ left (cols piece) 1)
                           (paste out piece
                                  (quotient (- hh (rows piece)) 2)
                                  left))))))))
     (hstack-center (map part-of frames)))))

title: Build the Typed Shape-and-Color Relation Matrix
written_solution: Compare every left-column framed shape against every top-row framed shape. Write 8 if shape and color both match, 6 if the shapes match up to rotation but the colors differ, 3 if the colors match but the shapes do not, and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Maroon(9) frames form a top header row and a left header column of
 ;; small colored shapes. Output the relation matrix (left headers x
 ;; top headers): cyan(8) = same shape (up to rotation) AND same color,
 ;; magenta(6) = shape only, green(3) = color only, 0 = neither.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (crop-nonzero grid)
       (let ((cells (filter (lambda (p) (> (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))
                            (grid-positions grid))))
         (if (empty? cells)
             (list (list 0))
             (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
               (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb)
                        (third bb) (fourth bb))))))
     (define (shape-of grid)  ;; binary silhouette cropped to content
       (crop-nonzero (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid)
                                   (lambda (r c)
                                     (if (= (at grid r c) 0) 0 1)))))
     (define (same-shape? a b)  ;; equal silhouettes up to 90-degree turns
       (member? (shape-of b)
                (let loop ((cur (shape-of a)) (n 0) (acc (list)))
                  (if (= n 4) acc
                      (loop (rotate-cw cur) (+ n 1) (cons cur acc))))))
     (define (color-of grid)
       (first (filter (lambda (v) (> v 0)) (apply append grid))))
     (define (frame? o)  ;; hollow rectangle outline, at least 3x3
       (and (>= (obj-h o) 3) (>= (obj-w o) 3)
            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define (interior fr)
       (crop-nonzero (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1) (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1)
                              (- (obj-r2 fr) 1) (- (obj-c2 fr) 1))))
     (define frames
       (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 9) (frame? o)))
               (objects g 0)))
     (define top (apply min (map obj-r1 frames)))
     (define tops
       (map interior (sort (filter (lambda (f) (= (obj-r1 f) top)) frames)
                           (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))))))
     (define lefts
       (map interior
            (sort (filter (lambda (f)
                            (and (= (obj-c1 f)
                                    (apply min (map obj-c1 frames)))
                                 (> (obj-r1 f) top)))
                          frames)
                  (lambda (a b) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
     (grid-from-fn (length lefts) (length tops)
                   (lambda (r c)
                     (let* ((a (list-ref lefts r))
                            (b (list-ref tops c))
                            (shape-hit (same-shape? a b))
                            (color-hit (= (color-of a) (color-of b))))
                       (cond ((and shape-hit color-hit) 8)
                             (shape-hit 6)
                             (color-hit 3)
                             (else 0))))))))

title: Make a Local Bounding-Box Overlap Gallery
written_solution: Inside each frame, compute the bounding boxes of the red(2) object and the blue(1) object. Fill their overlapping rectangle with the local key color above that frame, crop the result tightly, and pack all frame results into a horizontal gallery.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Maroon(9) frames each hold a red(2) and a blue(1) shape whose
 ;; bounding boxes overlap, plus a KEY color dot just above the frame.
 ;; Emit one solid key-colored block per frame, sized like that
 ;; red/blue overlap — laid out in a row, vertically centered, with
 ;; 1-column gaps.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (frame? o)  ;; hollow maroon rectangle outline, 3x3+
       (and (= (obj-color o) 9)
            (>= (obj-h o) 3) (>= (obj-w o) 3)
            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define frames
       (sort (filter frame? (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b) (or (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (and (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                    (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))))
     (define (key-of fr)
       (let ((r (- (obj-r1 fr) 1)))
         (first (if (>= r 0)
                    (filter (lambda (v) (not (member? v (list 0 9))))
                            (map (lambda (c) (at g r c))
                                 (range (obj-c1 fr)
                                        (+ (obj-c2 fr) 1))))
                    (list)))))
     (define (part-of fr)  ;; the red/blue bbox overlap as a key block
       (let* ((interior (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1) (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1)
                                 (- (obj-r2 fr) 1) (- (obj-c2 fr) 1)))
              (rb (bbox-of-cells (find-color interior 2)))
              (bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color interior 1))))
         (empty-grid (+ 1 (- (min (third rb) (third bb))
                             (max (first rb) (first bb))))
                     (+ 1 (- (min (fourth rb) (fourth bb))
                             (max (second rb) (second bb))))
                     (key-of fr))))
     (define parts (map part-of frames))
     (let ((gh (apply max (map rows parts)))
           (gw (+ (apply + (map cols parts)) (- (length parts) 1))))
       (let loop ((xs parts) (left 0) (out (empty-grid gh gw 0)))
         (if (empty? xs)
             out
             (let ((piece (first xs)))
               (loop (rest xs) (+ left (cols piece) 1)
                     (for*/fold ((acc out))
                                ((r (range 0 (rows piece)))
                                 (c (range 0 (cols piece))))
                       (let ((v (at piece r c)))
                         (if (> v 0)
                             (set-cell acc
                                       (+ (quotient (- gh (rows piece))
                                                    2)
                                          r)
                                       (+ left c) v)
                             acc)))))))))))

title: Select from the Library and Transform into a Gallery
written_solution: The framed templates at the top form a small library, each named by the key above it. The second-to-last row selects library entries, and the last row supplies transforms (5 → identity, 6 → rotate clockwise, 7 → flip horizontally). For each column of the code strip, take the named template, apply the requested transform, and place the result into a horizontal gallery.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; A LIBRARY of maroon(9)-framed patterns, each keyed by the color dot in
 ;; the row ABOVE its frame. The second-to-last grid row lists the keys to
 ;; SELECT, in order; the last row lists a transform per pick (5 = keep,
 ;; 6 = rotate-cw, 7 = flip-lr). The picked, transformed patterns line up
 ;; horizontally (vertically centered, 1-col gaps).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (crop-nonzero grid)
       (let ((cells (filter (lambda (p) (!= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))
                            (grid-positions grid))))
         (if (empty? cells)
             (list (list 0))
             (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
               (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))
     (define (rect-frame? obj)
       ;; exactly the border of a >=3x3 bbox: every cell on the border AND
       ;; the cell count equals the perimeter
       (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
              (hh (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
              (ww (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb)))))
         (and (>= hh 3) (>= ww 3)
              (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ hh ww)) 4))
              (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (first bb))
                                    (= (first p) (third bb))
                                    (= (second p) (second bb))
                                    (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                    (obj-cells obj)))))
     (define frames
       ;; library frames only — anything reaching the two control rows at
       ;; the bottom is not a library entry
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 9)
                                      (rect-frame? o)
                                      (< (third (obj-bbox o)) (- (rows g) 3))))
                     (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                 (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                     (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                          (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))
     (define (key-above fr)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox fr)))
         (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (member? v (list 0 9))))
                        (map (lambda (c) (at g (- (first bb) 1) c))
                             (range (second bb) (+ (fourth bb) 1)))))))
     (define (pattern-of fr)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox fr)))
         (crop-nonzero (subgrid g (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1)
                               (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))))
     (define library (map (lambda (fr) (list (key-above fr) (pattern-of fr)))
                          frames))
     (define (lookup k)
       (second (first (filter (lambda (kv) (= (first kv) k)) library))))
     (define selectors
       (filter (lambda (v)
                 (not (empty? (filter (lambda (kv) (= (first kv) v))
                                      library))))
               (row g (- (rows g) 2))))
     (define transforms (filter (lambda (v) (member? v (list 5 6 7)))
                                (last g)))
     (define parts
       (let loop ((ks selectors) (ts transforms) (acc (list)))
         (if (or (empty? ks) (empty? ts))
             (reverse acc)
             (loop (rest ks) (rest ts)
                   (cons (cond ((= (first ts) 6) (rotate-cw (lookup (first ks))))
                               ((= (first ts) 7) (flip-lr (lookup (first ks))))
                               (else (lookup (first ks))))
                         acc)))))
     (define (hstack-center pieces)
       (if (empty? pieces)
           (list (list))
           (let* ((hh (apply max (map rows pieces)))
                  (ww (+ (apply + (map cols pieces)) (- (length pieces) 1))))
             (let loop ((xs pieces) (left 0) (out (empty-grid hh ww 0)))
               (if (empty? xs)
                   out
                   (let ((piece (first xs)))
                     (loop (rest xs) (+ left (cols piece) 1)
                           (paste out piece
                                  (quotient (- hh (rows piece)) 2)
                                  left))))))))
     (hstack-center parts))))

title: Build the Boolean Gallery from the Two Templates
written_solution: Take the two framed binary templates and align them on a common canvas. Then read the code row: 4 → union, 5 → intersection, 6 → left-minus-right, 7 → xor. For each code, compute the corresponding boolean combination, color the kept cells with that code color, crop tightly, and place the result in a strip.

(rule!
 ;; TWO maroon(9) rectangular frames hold shapes A (left) and B (right),
 ;; taken shape-only: binarized, cropped, and centered on a common canvas.
 ;; The BOTTOM row lists op codes: 4 = A OR B, 5 = A AND B, 6 = A MINUS B,
 ;; 7 = A XOR B. Each code paints its combination in its own color; the
 ;; results line up horizontally (vertically centered, 1-col gaps).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (crop-nonzero grid)
       (let ((cells (filter (lambda (p) (!= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))
                            (grid-positions grid))))
         (if (empty? cells)
             (list (list 0))
             (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
               (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))
     (define (rect-frame? obj)
       ;; exactly the border of a >=3x3 bbox: every cell on the border AND
       ;; the cell count equals the perimeter
       (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
              (hh (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
              (ww (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb)))))
         (and (>= hh 3) (>= ww 3)
              (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ hh ww)) 4))
              (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (first bb))
                                    (= (first p) (third bb))
                                    (= (second p) (second bb))
                                    (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                    (obj-cells obj)))))
     (define frames
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 9) (rect-frame? o)))
                     (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b) (< (second (obj-bbox a)) (second (obj-bbox b))))))
     (define (shape-in fr)
       ;; the frame interior as a cropped BINARY mask (1 = occupied)
       (let ((bb (obj-bbox fr)))
         (crop-nonzero
          (grid-from-fn (- (third bb) (first bb) 1)
                        (- (fourth bb) (second bb) 1)
                        (lambda (r c)
                          (if (= (at g (+ (first bb) 1 r) (+ (second bb) 1 c)) 0)
                              0 1))))))
     (define (pad-center grid hh ww)
       (paste (empty-grid hh ww 0) grid
              (quotient (- hh (rows grid)) 2)
              (quotient (- ww (cols grid)) 2)))
     (define (hstack-center pieces)
       (if (empty? pieces)
           (list (list))
           (let* ((hh (apply max (map rows pieces)))
                  (ww (+ (apply + (map cols pieces)) (- (length pieces) 1))))
             (let loop ((xs pieces) (left 0) (out (empty-grid hh ww 0)))
               (if (empty? xs)
                   out
                   (let ((piece (first xs)))
                     (loop (rest xs) (+ left (cols piece) 1)
                           (paste out piece
                                  (quotient (- hh (rows piece)) 2)
                                  left))))))))
     (let* ((a0 (shape-in (first frames)))
            (b0 (shape-in (second frames)))
            (hh (max (rows a0) (rows b0)))
            (ww (max (cols a0) (cols b0)))
            (a (pad-center a0 hh ww))
            (b (pad-center b0 hh ww))

             (start (- (cols g) (length vals))))
        (if (< c start) 0 (list-ref vals (- c start)))))))

title: Recolor objects by perimeter rank
written_solution: Measure each object’s perimeter. The largest perimeter becomes red(2), the next becomes green(3), the next yellow(4), and so on by descending rank.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (objects g 0))
         (palette (list 2 3 4 6 8 9 1 5 7)))
    (define (perimeter obj)
      (for*/sum ([p (in-list (obj-cells obj))]
                 [d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (if (member (list (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d))) (obj-cells obj)) 0 1)))
    (define perims (sort (remove-duplicates (map perimeter objs)) >))
    (define (rank-color p)
      (list-ref palette
                (let loop ([xs perims] [i 0])
                  (if (= (first xs) p) i (loop (rest xs) (+ i 1))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list objs)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (rank-color (perimeter obj))))))

title: Replace each object with its bounding-box frame
written_solution: For every connected object, ignore its internal shape and draw only the rectangular frame of its tight bbox in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border obj)
      (append (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
              (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))
              (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
              (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (border obj) (obj-color obj)))))

title: Convert the object into a row-profile chart
written_solution: Crop the object, count how many colored cells appear in each cropped row, and output a left-justified bar chart of those row counts using the object’s color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((obj (first (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
         (counts (for/list ([r (in-range (rows crop))])
                   (count-where (lambda (c) (not (= (at crop r c) 0))) (range 0 (cols crop)))))
         (w (apply max counts)))
    (grid-from-fn (length counts) w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (< c (list-ref counts r)) (obj-color obj) 0)))))

title: Recolor objects by symmetry class
written_solution: Classify each cropped object by its mirror symmetries: both vertical and horizontal → cyan(8), vertical only → red(2), horizontal only → green(3), neither → yellow(4). Preserve the shape positions.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (mask obj)
      (let ((crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
        (grid-from-fn (rows crop) (cols crop)
          (lambda (r c) (if (not (= (at crop r c) 0)) 1 0)))))
    (define (v-sym? m) (equal? m (flip-lr m)))
    (define (h-sym? m) (equal? m (flip-ud m)))
    (define (class-color obj)
      (let* ((m (mask obj))
             (vs (v-sym? m))
             (hs (h-sym? m)))
        (if (and vs hs) 8 (if vs 2 (if hs 3 4)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (class-color obj)))))

title: Stack cropped objects vertically by height
written_solution: Crop every object and stack the cropped shapes from tallest to shortest, with one background row between consecutive shapes. Keep original colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                             (let ((crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                               (list (rows crop) (obj-color obj) crop)))
                           (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (first a) (first b))
                            (< (second a) (second b))
                            (> (first a) (first b))))))
         (shapes (map third items))
         (out-h (+ (apply + (map rows shapes)) (max 0 (- (length shapes) 1))))
         (out-w (apply max (map cols shapes))))
    (let pack ([remaining shapes] [top 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                         (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) c v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ top (rows shape) 1) next))))))

title: Dock each object under its matching top-row marker
written_solution: Each nonzero cell in the top row is a dock marker. Find the object of the same color, crop it, then place it in the output so its left edge starts in that marker’s column and its bottom edge sits on the output floor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((markers (filter (lambda (cell) (and (= (first cell) 0) (not (= (third cell) 0)))) (grid-cells g)))
         (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (objs (objects body 0)))
    (define (crop-for color)
      (let* ((obj (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) objs))))
        (subgrid body (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define crops (map (lambda (m) (list (third m) (second m) (crop-for (third m)))) markers))
    (define out-h (apply max (map (lambda (x) (rows (third x))) crops)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid out-h (cols g) 0)]) ([item (in-list crops)])
      (let* ((left (second item))
             (crop (third item))
             (top (- out-h (rows crop))))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
          (let ((v (at crop r c)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) v) acc)))))))

title: Apply the top-row color legend
written_solution: Read the top row as adjacent old→new color pairs. Apply that recoloring to the body of the grid and drop the legend row from the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((mapping (make-hash)))
    (let loop ([c 0])
      (when (< (+ c 1) (cols g))
        (if (and (not (= (at g 0 c) 0)) (not (= (at g 0 (+ c 1)) 0)))
            (begin (hash-set! mapping (at g 0 c) (at g 0 (+ c 1))) (loop (+ c 2)))
            (loop (+ c 1)))))
    (grid-from-fn (- (rows g) 1) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at g (+ r 1) c)))
          (hash-ref mapping v v))))))

title: Route a waypoint path through the maze
written_solution: Find one shortest path from red(2) to yellow(4) that must pass through the waypoint green(3), moving only orthogonally through black(0) cells and avoiding gray(5) walls. Paint the whole routed path cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define start (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define waypoint (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define goal (first (find-color g 4)))
    (define (bfs src dst)
      (define queue (list src))
      (define prev (make-hash))
      (hash-set! prev (cons (first src) (second src)) #f)
      (define (search)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (define cur (first queue))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (unless (equal? cur dst)
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (define nr (+ (first cur) (first d)))
              (define nc (+ (second cur) (second d)))
              (define key (cons nr nc))
              (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                         (not (hash-has-key? prev key))
                         (or (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)) (and (= nr (first dst)) (= nc (second dst)))))
                (hash-set! prev key cur)
                (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
          (search)))
      (search)
      (let rebuild ([cur dst] [acc (list)])
        (if (not cur)
            acc
            (rebuild (hash-ref prev (cons (first cur) (second cur)) #f) (cons cur acc)))))
    (let* ((p1 (bfs start waypoint))
           (p2 (bfs waypoint goal))
           (path (append (take p1 (- (length p1) 1)) p2)))
      (paint-cells g path 8))))

title: Take the majority overlay of three normalized shapes
written_solution: Crop the three objects, align their top-left corners on a common canvas, and keep exactly the cells occupied in at least two of the three shapes. Paint the consensus shape cyan(8) and crop it.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shapes (map (lambda (obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))) (objects g 0)))
         (h (apply max (map rows shapes)))
         (w (apply max (map cols shapes)))
         (out (grid-from-fn h w
                (lambda (r c)
                  (let ((cnt (count-where (lambda (shape)
                                            (and (< r (rows shape)) (< c (cols shape)) (not (= (at shape r c) 0))))
                                          shapes)))
                    (if (>= cnt 2) 8 0))))))
    (crop-to-content out)))

title: Rotate inserts into matching-color frames
written_solution: Each hollow frame matches the external object of the same color. A key inside the frame says how to rotate that object before placing it into the frame interior: blue(1)=identity, red(2)=90° clockwise, green(3)=180°, yellow(4)=270° clockwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj)) (w (obj-w obj))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                         (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define (transform shape key)
      (if (= key 1) shape (if (= key 2) (rotate-cw shape) (if (= key 3) (rotate-180 shape) (rotate-ccw shape)))))
    (define objs (objects g 0))
    (define frames (filter frame? objs))
    (define inserts (filter (lambda (obj) (and (not (frame? obj)) (> (obj-size obj) 1))) objs))
    (define singles (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-size obj) 1) (member (obj-color obj) (list 1 2 3 4)))) objs))
    (define with-frames
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([fr (in-list frames)])
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells fr) (obj-color fr))))
    (for/fold ([out with-frames]) ([fr (in-list frames)])
      (let* ((key-candidates (filter (lambda (s)
                                       (let ((p (first (obj-cells s))))
                                         (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 fr)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 fr))
                                              (> (second p) (obj-c1 fr)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 fr)))))
                                     singles))
             (key (if (empty? key-candidates) 1 (obj-color (first key-candidates))))
             (insert (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) (obj-color fr))) inserts)))
             (shape (transform (subgrid g (obj-r1 insert) (obj-c1 insert) (obj-r2 insert) (obj-c2 insert)) key)))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
          (let ((v (at shape r c)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1 r) (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1 c) v) acc)))))))

title: Connect object anchors in x-order
written_solution: Take the top-left anchor of each object’s bbox, sort those anchors from left to right, and connect consecutive anchors with orthogonal polylines: first horizontally, then vertically. Draw the connector in cyan(8) on top of the original grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
         (anchors (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj))) objs)))
    (define (step-range a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (reverse (range b (+ a 1)))))
    (let loop ([pts anchors] [out g])
      (if (< (length pts) 2)
          out
          (let* ((a (first pts))
                 (b (second pts))
                 (hpath (map (lambda (c) (list (first a) c)) (step-range (second a) (second b))))
                 (vpath (map (lambda (r) (list r (second b))) (step-range (first a) (first b)))))
            (loop (rest pts) (paint-cells (paint-cells out hpath 8) vpath 8)))))))

title: Use two keys to select and transform an object
written_solution: The top-left key names which colored object to select. The top-right key names the transform to apply to that cropped object: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → flip horizontal, yellow(4) → transpose, gray(5) → 180°.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((sel (at g 0 0))
         (key (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))
         (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (chosen (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) sel)) (objects body 0))))
         (crop (subgrid body (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen)))
         (tf (cond [(= key 2) (rotate-cw crop)]
                   [(= key 3) (flip-lr crop)]
                   [(= key 4) (transpose crop)]
                   [(= key 5) (rotate-180 crop)]
                   [else crop])))
    (crop-to-content tf)))

title: Build a transformation timeline gallery
written_solution: Read the top-row keys from left to right. Starting from the cropped object, apply each transform in sequence and output a horizontal gallery of every stage: the original, then after key 1, then after key 2, and so on, with one background column between stages.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((keys (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
         (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (obj (first (sort (objects body 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (start (crop-to-content (subgrid body (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))))
    (define (apply-key shape key)
      (crop-to-content
        (cond [(= key 2) (rotate-cw shape)]
              [(= key 3) (flip-lr shape)]
              [(= key 4) (transpose shape)]
              [(= key 5) (rotate-180 shape)]
              [else shape])))
    (define stages
      (let loop ([remaining keys] [cur start] [acc (list start)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            (reverse acc)
            (let ((next (apply-key cur (first remaining))))
              (loop (rest remaining) next (cons next acc))))))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows stages)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols stages)) (max 0 (- (length stages) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining stages] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                         (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols shape) 1) next))))))

title: Pack one object from each symmetry class into a 2x2 table
written_solution: Identify one object from each symmetry class and pack them into a 2×2 gallery: top-left = both axes symmetric, top-right = vertical-only, bottom-left = horizontal-only, bottom-right = neither. Use tight crops and separate the gallery cells with one background row and one background column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (mask crop)
      (grid-from-fn (rows crop) (cols crop) (lambda (r c) (if (not (= (at crop r c) 0)) 1 0))))
    (define (shape obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define both #f)
    (define vertical #f)
    (define horizontal #f)
    (define neither #f)
    (for ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (let* ((crop (shape obj))
             (m (mask crop))
             (vs (equal? m (flip-lr m)))
             (hs (equal? m (flip-ud m))))
        (if (and vs hs)
            (set! both crop)
            (if vs
                (set! vertical crop)
                (if hs (set! horizontal crop) (set! neither crop))))))
    (define top-h (max (rows both) (rows vertical)))
    (define bot-h (max (rows horizontal) (rows neither)))
    (define left-w (max (cols both) (cols horizontal)))
    (define right-w (max (cols vertical) (cols neither)))
    (define (paste-shape out shape top left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                  [c (in-range (cols shape))])
        (let ((v (at shape r c)))
          (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) v) acc))))
    (paste-shape
      (paste-shape
        (paste-shape
          (paste-shape (empty-grid (+ top-h 1 bot-h) (+ left-w 1 right-w) 0) both 0 0)
          vertical 0 (+ left-w 1))
        horizontal (+ top-h 1) 0)
      neither (+ top-h 1) (+ left-w 1))))

title: Fill Between Matching Endpoints
written_solution: Scan each row independently. Whenever the same non-background color appears as a left and right endpoint, fill the whole horizontal span between them with that color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((color (in-list (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g r)))))) (let ((cs (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) color)) (range (cols g))))) (if (>= (length cs) 2) (paint-cells acc (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (apply min cs) (+ (apply max cs) 1))) color) acc))))))

title: Complete the Vertical Mirror
written_solution: Reflect every nonzero cell across the vertical midline of the grid. Keep the original cells; add the mirrored copies.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Overlay the LEFT-RIGHT mirror onto the grid: every non-zero cell also
 ;; lands at its horizontally mirrored position.
 (overlay g (flip-lr g)))

title: Draw Rectangle Borders from Corner Pairs
written_solution: Each color marks two opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Take the bbox of each color pair and draw the full rectangle border in that color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-colors-reading grid) (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (map (lambda (p) (at grid (first p) (second p))) (grid-positions grid))))) (define (f14-border-cells r0 c0 r1 c1) (for*/list ((r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))) (c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))) #:when (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))) (list r c))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((color (in-list (e8b-colors-reading g)))) (let ((cells (find-color g color))) (if (>= (length cells) 2) (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))) (paint-cells out (f14-border-cells (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) color)) out)))))

title: Move the Cropped Object to the Top-Left
written_solution: Find the bbox of the whole nonzero object, crop it tightly, and paste that crop into the top-left corner of a background grid of the same original size.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (nonzero-cells grid) (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))) (grid-positions grid))) (define (crop-nonzero grid) (let ((cells (nonzero-cells grid))) (if (empty? cells) (list (list 0)) (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))))) (define (e8b-paste grid pat top left) (for*/fold ((out grid)) ((r (in-range (rows pat))) (c (in-range (cols pat)))) (let ((v (at pat r c)) (rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c))) (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr cc (rows out) (cols out))) (set-cell out rr cc v) out)))) (e8b-paste (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (crop-nonzero g) 0 0)))

title: Read Column Markers as a Row
written_solution: Look left to right across the columns. Whenever a column contains a colored marker, emit that color into a 1-row output, preserving the column order.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; One row of each column's FIRST non-zero value (empty columns dropped).
 (list (filter (lambda (v) (!= v 0))
               (for/list ((c (in-range w)))
                 (let ((hits (filter (lambda (r) (!= (at g r c) 0)) (range h))))
                   (if (empty? hits) 0 (at g (first hits) c)))))))

title: Cast Rightward Rays Until the Wall
written_solution: Every non-gray(5) seed cell extends horizontally to the right through zero cells until it hits a gray(5) wall or the boundary. Keep the original walls in place.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g r c))) (if (or (= v 0) (= v 5)) out (let loop ((cc (+ c 1)) (acc out)) (if (and (< cc (cols g)) (= (at g r cc) 0)) (loop (+ cc 1) (set-cell acc r cc v)) acc)))))))

title: Expand Diagonal Pairs into Xs
written_solution: Each color gives two opposite corners of a 3×3 box. Complete that box into a full X by drawing both diagonals in the same color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-colors-reading grid) (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (map (lambda (p) (at grid (first p) (second p))) (grid-positions grid))))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((color (in-list (e8b-colors-reading g)))) (let ((cells (find-color g color))) (if (= (length cells) 2) (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)) (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb)) (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((i (in-range (+ 1 (- r1 r0))))) (set-cell (set-cell acc (+ r0 i) (+ c0 i) color) (+ r0 i) (- c1 i) color))) out)))))

title: Stack Cropped Components by Area
written_solution: Split the input into connected components, crop each component to its own bbox, sort the crops by component area from smallest to largest, and stack them vertically with one background row between them.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8b-list< a b) (cond ((empty? a) #f) ((< (first a) (first b)) #t) ((> (first a) (first b)) #f) (else (e8b-list< (rest a) (rest b))))) (define (e8b-paste grid pat top left) (for*/fold ((out grid)) ((r (in-range (rows pat))) (c (in-range (cols pat)))) (let ((v (at pat r c)) (rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c))) (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr cc (rows out) (cols out))) (set-cell out rr cc v) out)))) (define (f14b-vstack-center grids (gap 1)) (if (empty? grids) (list (list)) (let* ((w (apply max (map cols grids))) (h (+ (apply + (map rows grids)) (* gap (- (length grids) 1))))) (let loop ((ys grids) (top 0) (out (empty-grid h w 0))) (if (empty? ys) out (let* ((piece (first ys)) (left (quotient (- w (cols piece)) 2))) (loop (rest ys) (+ top (rows piece) gap) (e8b-paste out piece top left)))))))) (define (s17b-object-crop grid obj) (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))) (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (first (obj-bbox obj)) (second (obj-bbox obj)) (s17b-object-crop g obj))) (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (e8b-list< (list (first a) (second a) (third a)) (list (first b) (second b) (third b))))))) (f14b-vstack-center (map fourth items) 1))))

title: Transform the Object by the Key Cell
written_solution: The top-left key cell tells you how to transform the unique object: blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → 180°, yellow(4) → flip horizontal. Remove the key cell, crop the object, and output the transformed crop.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (nonzero-cells grid) (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at grid (first p) (second p)) 0))) (grid-positions grid))) (define (crop-nonzero grid) (let ((cells (nonzero-cells grid))) (if (empty? cells) (list (list 0)) (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))) (subgrid grid (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))))) (define (t10b-transform grid code) (cond ((= code 1) grid) ((= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)) ((= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)) ((= code 4) (flip-lr grid)) ((= code 5) (flip-ud grid)) ((= code 6) (rotate-ccw grid)) (else grid))) (let* ((key (at g 0 0)) (body (set-cell g 0 0 0))) (t10b-transform (crop-nonzero body) key))))

title: Build the Equality Matrix from Headers
written_solution: Use the top row and left column as headers. For each interior position, write the header color if the row header and column header are the same non-background color; otherwise write 0.

written_solution: Find every blue(1) component that touches the outer border of the grid. Recolor that entire component to red(2); keep interior blue(1) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
    (if (any? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- h 1)) (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- w 1)))) (obj-cells obj))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 2)
        out)))

title: Recolor L-shaped green triominoes
written_solution: Look at each green(3) component of size 3. If its cells form an L-shape in a 2×2 box, recolor all three cells to yellow(4). Leave straight 3-cell bars unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))])
    (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 3) (= (obj-h obj) 2) (= (obj-w obj) 2))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 4)
        out)))

title: Reflect the magenta shape across the divider
written_solution: Find the full cyan(8) divider line of 8s. Reflect every magenta(6) cell across that divider and add the reflected copy, keeping the original shape too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((div-row (find-first (lambda (r) (for/and ([c (range 0 w)]) (= (at g r c) 8))) (range 0 h)))
         (div-col (find-first (lambda (c) (for/and ([r (range 0 h)]) (= (at g r c) 8))) (range 0 w))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (find-color g 6)])
      (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
             (nr (if div-col r (- (* 2 div-row) r)))
             (nc (if div-col (- (* 2 div-col) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (set-cell out nr nc 6) out)))))

title: Crop to the bounding box of all non-zero cells
written_solution: Ignore the black(0) background. Take the smallest rectangle that contains every non-zero cell, and output exactly that cropped subgrid with all colors preserved.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))) (grid-positions g)))))
    (if bb (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) (list (list 0)))))

title: Recolor the largest red component
written_solution: Among all red(2) connected components, find the unique largest one by number of cells. Recolor that whole component to cyan(8) and leave the smaller red(2) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((reds (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))
         (largest (argmax obj-size reds)))
    (paint-cells g (obj-cells largest) 8)))

title: Copy the blue object by the marker vector
written_solution: Use the vector from the red(2) marker 2 to the green(3) marker 3. Copy the entire blue(1) object by that vector and draw the translated copy in yellow(4), keeping the original object and the markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first b) (first a)))
         (dc (- (second b) (second a)))
         (moved (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc))) (find-color g 1))))
    (paint-cells g moved 4)))

title: Complete mirror symmetry across the divider
written_solution: Find the full divider line of 8s. The orange(7) pattern should be mirror-symmetric across that line, so add every missing reflected orange(7) cell and keep any orange(7) cells already present.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((div-row (find-first (lambda (r) (for/and ([c (range 0 w)]) (= (at g r c) 8))) (range 0 h)))
         (div-col (find-first (lambda (c) (for/and ([r (range 0 h)]) (= (at g r c) 8))) (range 0 w))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (find-color g 7)])
      (let* ((r (first p)) (c (second p))
             (nr (if div-col r (- (* 2 div-row) r)))
             (nc (if div-col (- (* 2 div-col) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (set-cell out nr nc 7) out)))))

title: Recolor blue components by geometry
written_solution: Examine each blue(1) component. If it is a horizontal straight line, recolor it red(2). If it is a vertical straight line, recolor it green(3). If it is a filled square, recolor it yellow(4). Leave other blue(1) shapes unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
    (cond [(= (obj-h obj) 1) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 2)]
          [(= (obj-w obj) 1) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)]
          [(and (= (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)) (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 4)]
          [else out])))

title: Take the Cartesian product of marked rows and columns
written_solution: Rows marked by red(2) cells on the left border and columns marked by blue(1) cells on the top border define intersection points. Place green(3) at every such row-column intersection and keep the border markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((rs (for/list ([r (range 1 h)] #:when (= (at g r 0) 2)) r))
         (cs (for/list ([c (range 1 w)] #:when (= (at g 0 c) 1)) c)))
    (paint-cells g (for*/list ([r rs] [c cs]) (list r c)) 3)))

title: Fill each blue frame with its internal marker color
written_solution: Each blue(1) hollow rectangle contains one colored marker cell. Fill the entire interior of that frame with the marker’s color, while leaving the blue(1) border intact.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1) (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b)) (all? (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (inside (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1) (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))
             (markers (filter (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 1))))) inside)))
        (if (and (same-cells? (obj-cells obj) (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
                 (not (empty? markers)))
            (paint-cells out inside (at g (first (first markers)) (second (first markers))))
            out)))))

title: Pack objects into a size-sorted strip
written_solution: Extract each non-zero object, crop it to its own bbox, sort the cropped objects by increasing area, and pack them left-to-right with one background column between them. Preserve each object’s color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (sorted-cells cells) (sort cells cell<?))
    (define (entry obj)
      (let* ((n (sorted-cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj))))
             ;; Bounding box enclosing the cells
             (bb (bbox-of-cells n))
             (tl (first (sorted-cells (obj-cells obj)))))
        (list (obj-color obj) n (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb))
              (obj-size obj) (first tl) (second tl))))
    (define (entry<? a b)
      (cond
        [(not (= (list-ref a 4) (list-ref b 4))) (< (list-ref a 4) (list-ref b 4))]
        [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
        [(not (= (list-ref a 5) (list-ref b 5))) (< (list-ref a 5) (list-ref b 5))]
        [else (< (list-ref a 6) (list-ref b 6))]))
    (define entries (sort (map entry (objects g 0)) entry<?))
    (if (empty? entries)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((out-h (apply max (map (lambda (e) (list-ref e 2)) entries)))
               (out-w (+ (foldl + 0 (map (lambda (e) (list-ref e 3)) entries))
                         (max 0 (- (length entries) 1)))))
          (let loop ((remaining entries) (cur-c 0) (out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)))
            (if (empty? remaining)
                out
                (let* ((e (first remaining))
                       (color (first e))
                       (cells (second e))
                       (w (list-ref e 3)))
                  (loop (rest remaining)
                        (+ cur-c w 1)
                        (paint-cells out
                                     (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (+ cur-c (second p)))) cells)
                                     color)))))))))

title: Crop the object nearest to the marker
written_solution: Find the unique red(2) marker 2. Among all other colored objects, choose the one whose cells are closest to that marker in Manhattan distance, then output only that object cropped to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define marker (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define objs (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) 2))) (objects g 0)))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (obj-min-cell o) (first (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?)))
    (define (obj-dist o)
      (apply min (map (lambda (p) (pos-manhattan p marker)) (obj-cells o))))
    (define (obj<? a b)
      (let ((da (obj-dist a)) (db (obj-dist b))
            (ta (obj-min-cell a)) (tb (obj-min-cell b)))
        (cond
          [(not (= da db)) (< da db)]
          [(not (= (first ta) (first tb))) (< (first ta) (first tb))]
          [(not (= (second ta) (second tb))) (< (second ta) (second tb))]
          [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))])))
    (if (empty? objs)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((best (first (sort objs obj<?)))
               (cells (sort (normalize-cells (obj-cells best)) cell<?))
               (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
               (out (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0)))
          (paint-cells out cells (obj-color best))))))

title: Mark cells equidistant from two seeds under wall distance
written_solution: Treat 5s as walls. Compute shortest-path distances through the open cells from the red(2) seed 2 and the green(3) seed 3, then recolor every open cell that is reachable from both seeds at equal distance to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      ;; Mutable lookup table for dist
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue))
                 (r (first p))
                 (c (second p))
                 (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    ;; Position of the first red(2) cell
    (define a (first (find-color g 2)))
    ;; Position of the first green(3) cell
    (define b (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((p (list r c)) (v (at g r c)))
          (if (and (= v 0) (hash-has-key? da p) (hash-has-key? db p)
                   (= (hash-ref da p) (hash-ref db p)))
              8
              v))))))

title: Take the union of shortest paths through a checkpoint
written_solution: Walls are 5. Find all cells that lie on some shortest path from start 2 to checkpoint 3, and also all cells that lie on some shortest path from checkpoint 3 to goal 4. Mark the union of those path cells with cyan(8), preserving the markers and walls.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue))
                 (r (first p))
                 (c (second p))
                 (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define (path-cells a b)
      (let ((da (dist-from a)) (db (dist-from b)))
        (if (not (hash-has-key? da b))
            (list)
            (let ((target (hash-ref da b)))
              (filter (lambda (p)
                        (and (hash-has-key? da p)
                             (hash-has-key? db p)
                             (= (+ (hash-ref da p) (hash-ref db p)) target)))
                      (grid-positions g))))))
    (define s (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define m (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define t (first (find-color g 4)))
    (define cells (remove-duplicates (append (path-cells s m) (path-cells m t))))
    (foldl (lambda (p acc)
             (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
                 (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 8)
                 acc))
           g cells)))

title: Fill the selected band between nested frames
written_solution: Count the red(2) control cells 2. Sort the blue(1) hollow frames from outside to inside. Use the count k to choose the k-th frame and the next inner frame, then fill the zero-valued band between those two frames with yellow(4), leaving the frame borders blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (sorted-cells cells) (sort cells cell<?))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                    (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (hollow-rect? obj)
      (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
        (and (>= (- (third bb) (first bb)) 2)
             (>= (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 2)
             (equal? (sorted-cells (obj-cells obj))
                     (sorted-cells (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))))))
    (define frames
      (sort (map obj-bbox (filter hollow-rect? (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))))
            (lambda (a b)
              (> (* (+ 1 (- (third a) (first a))) (+ 1 (- (fourth a) (second a))))
                 (* (+ 1 (- (third b) (first b))) (+ 1 (- (fourth b) (second b))))))))
    (define idx (- (length (find-color g 2)) 1))
    (if (or (empty? frames) (< idx 0) (>= idx (- (length frames) 1)))
        g
        (let* ((outer (list-ref frames idx))
               (inner (list-ref frames (+ idx 1)))
               (r0 (first outer)) (c0 (second outer)) (r1 (third outer)) (c1 (fourth outer))
               (ir0 (first inner)) (ic0 (second inner)) (ir1 (third inner)) (ic1 (fourth inner)))
          (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
            (lambda (r c)
              (if (and (> r r0) (< r r1) (> c c0) (< c c1)
                       (not (and (>= r ir0) (<= r ir1) (>= c ic0) (<= c ic1)))
                       (= (at g r c) 0))
                  4
                  (at g r c))))))))

title: Apply a legend-controlled boolean operation to normalized shapes
written_solution: Take the blue(1) shape and the red(2) shape, normalize each to its own top-left corner, and combine them according to the control color: 3 → union, 4 → intersection, and 6 → XOR. Output the resulting normalized shape in cyan(8) as a cropped grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm color) (sort (normalize-cells (find-color g color)) cell<?))
    (define (has-cell? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (define a (norm 1))
    (define b (norm 2))
    (define op (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 'union]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 'inter]
                     [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 'xor]
                     [else 'union]))
    (define res0
      (cond
        [(eq? op 'union) (remove-duplicates (append a b))]
        [(eq? op 'inter) (filter (lambda (p) (has-cell? p b)) a)]
        [else (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p b))) a)
                      (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p a))) b))]))
    (define res (sort (normalize-cells res0) cell<?))
    (if (empty? res)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells res))
               (out (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0)))
          (paint-cells out res 8)))))

title: Partition the maze by nearest seed
written_solution: Treat 5s as walls. For each reachable open cell, compare its shortest-path distance to seed 2 and to seed 3. Fill the cell with red(2) if seed 2 is nearer, with green(3) if seed 3 is nearer, and with cyan(8) if the distances tie.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue))
                 (r (first p))
                 (c (second p))
                 (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define a (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define b (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((p (list r c)) (v (at g r c)))
          (if (and (= v 0) (hash-has-key? da p) (hash-has-key? db p))
              (cond [(< (hash-ref da p) (hash-ref db p)) 2]
                    [(< (hash-ref db p) (hash-ref da p)) 3]
                    [else 8])
              v))))))

title: Transform the source shape and stamp it repeatedly along a vector
written_solution: Read the source shape from blue(1). The control color chooses a transform: yellow(4) → identity, magenta(6) → 90° clockwise, orange(7) → flip horizontal. Normalize the transformed shape and stamp it in cyan(8) starting at the red(2) marker, then keep adding the vector from red(2) to green(3) until the next stamp would go out of bounds. Output only the stamped pattern.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define (flip-h cells)
      (let* ((n (norm cells))
             (rmax (apply max (map first n))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (- rmax (first p)) (second p))) n))))
    (define shape0 (norm (find-color g 1)))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 4]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 6]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 7))) 7]
                       [else 4]))
    (define cells (cond [(= ctrl 6) (rot shape0)]
                        [(= ctrl 7) (flip-h shape0)]
                        [else shape0]))
    (define start (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define nxt (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define dr (- (first nxt) (first start)))
    (define dc (- (second nxt) (second start)))
    (let loop ((ar (first start)) (ac (second start)) (out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)))
      (let ((placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ ar (first p)) (+ ac (second p)))) cells)))
        (if (all? (lambda (p) (pos-in-bounds? p (rows g) (cols g))) placed)
            (loop (+ ar dr) (+ ac dc) (paint-cells out placed 8))
            out)))))

title: Fill each chamber by the winning seed color
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls that split the grid into chambers. In each chamber, count the red(2) cells and the green(3) cells already inside it. Fill the background cells of that chamber with red(2) if red(2) is the majority, with green(3) if green(3) is the majority, and with cyan(8) if they tie.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (or (= v 0) (= v 2) (= v 3)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (foldl
      (lambda (comp acc)
        (let* ((cnt2 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) comp))
               (cnt3 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 3)) comp))
               (fill (cond [(> cnt2 cnt3) 2] [(> cnt3 cnt2) 3] [else 8])))
          (foldl (lambda (p acc2)
                   (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                       (set-cell acc2 (first p) (second p) fill)
                       acc2))
                 acc comp)))
      g comps)))

title: Vertical Bar Selector
written_solution: Find every blue(1) object that is exactly a 3-cell vertical line. Recolor those cells red(2). Leave horizontal blue(1) bars unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (objs-of color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((obj (in-list (objs-of 1)))) (if (equal? (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)) (list (list 0 0) (list 1 0) (list 2 0))) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 2) out))))

title: Smallest Green Object
written_solution: Among all green(3) objects, select the smallest component and recolor it magenta(6). Keep the larger green(3) objects unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (objs-of color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))) (let* ((greens (objs-of 3)) (smallest (first (sort greens (lambda (a b) (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) (cell< (first (sort (obj-cells a) cell<)) (first (sort (obj-cells b) cell<))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))) (paint-cells g (obj-cells smallest) 6))))

title: Horizontal Span Fill
written_solution: Whenever a row contains two orange(7) endpoints with only black(0) cells between them, fill the whole horizontal segment between those endpoints with orange(7). Rows without such a pair stay unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (rows g)))) (let ((cols-hit (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 7)) (range 0 (cols g))))) (if (and (= (length cols-hit) 2) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ (first cols-hit) 1) (second cols-hit)))) (paint-cells out (for/list ((c (in-range (first cols-hit) (+ (second cols-hit) 1)))) (list r c)) 7) out)))))

title: Diagonal Echo
written_solution: Each red(2) cell creates a yellow(4) copy one step diagonally down and right, but only if that target location is inside the grid and empty. The original red(2) cells remain.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Paint a yellow(4) diagonally DOWN-RIGHT of every red(2) (empty cells only).
 (for/fold ((out g)) ((cell (in-list (find-color g 2))))
   (let ((r (+ (first cell) 1)) (c (+ (second cell) 1)))
     (if (and (in-bounds? r c h w) (= (at g r c) 0))
         (set-cell out r c 4)
         out))))

title: Missing Cyan Corner
written_solution: Complete every almost-full 2x2 cyan(8) square: when three corners are cyan(8) and the fourth corner is black(0), fill that missing corner with cyan(8).

(let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range 0 (- (rows g) 1))) (c (in-range 0 (- (cols g) 1)))) (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list (+ r 1) c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))) (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))) (if (and (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 8)) vals) 3) (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1)) (let ((p (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)))) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)) out)))))

title: Frame Filled by Inner Dot

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (objs-of color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))) (define (rect-outline? obj) (and (>= (obj-h obj) 3) (>= (obj-w obj) 3) (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4)) (all? (let ((dummy 0)) (define (objs-of color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))) (define (copy-cells out cells color r0 c0) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((p (in-list cells))) (let ((r (+ r0 (first p))) (c (+ c0 (second p)))) (if (in-bounds? r c (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell acc r c color) acc)))) (let* ((template (first (sort (objs-of 2) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))) (offsets (normalize-cells (obj-cells template))) (anchors (find-color g 1))) (for/fold ((out g)) ((anchor (in-list anchors))) (copy-cells out offsets 1 (first anchor) (second anchor))))))

program_solution: (rule! title: Header Pair Recolor Map
written_solution: The top row is a legend made of consecutive non-background color pairs. Each pair defines a recolor rule from the first color to the second. Recolor the body using those mappings, but do not change the header row.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((nonzero (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0))) (pairs (let loop ((xs nonzero)) (if (empty? xs) (list) (cons (list (first xs) (second xs)) (loop (rest (rest xs)))))))) (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= r 0) (at g r c) (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (pair) (= (first pair) (at g r c))) pairs))) (if (eq? hit #f) (at g r c) (second hit)))))))))

title: Equality Matrix from Headers
written_solution: The top row and left column act as headers. Each interior cell becomes colored only when its row-header color matches its column-header color, and then it takes that shared color.

 ;; its ROW header equals its COLUMN header, else clears.
 (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
   (if (or (= r 0) (= c 0)) (at g r c)
       (if (= (at g 0 c) (at g r 0)) (at g 0 c) 0)))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (objs-of color) (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))) (define (shape-key cells) (format "~a" (normalize-cells cells))) (let* ((greens (objs-of 3)) (keys (map (lambda (obj) (shape-key (obj-cells obj))) greens)) (target (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (count-where (lambda (k) (equal? k (shape-key (obj-cells obj)))) keys) 1)) greens))) (r1 (- (obj-r1 target) 1)) (c1 (- (obj-c1 target) 1)) (r2 (+ (obj-r2 target) 1)) (c2 (+ (obj-c2 target) 1))) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range r1 (+ r2 1))) (c (in-range c1 (+ c2 1)))) (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (or (= r r1) (= r r2) (= c c1) (= c c2))) (set-cell out r c 4) out)))))

title: Column legend painter
written_solution: Treat the top row as a legend. In every column whose top cell is nonzero, replace each body cell equal to cyan(8) with that column's legend color. Leave all other cells alone.

 (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c)
   (let ((key (at g 0 c)) (v (at g r c)))
     (if (and (> r 0) (= v 8) (!= key 0)) key v)))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (- (rows g) 2))) (c (in-range (- (cols g) 2)))) (let ((a (at g r c)) (b (at g r (+ c 2))) (mid (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1))) (d (at g (+ r 2) c)) (e (at g (+ r 2) (+ c 2)))) (cond ((and (not (= a 0)) (= a e) (= mid 0)) (set-cell out (+ r 1) (+ c 1) a)) ((and (not (= b 0)) (= b d) (= mid 0)) (set-cell out (+ r 1) (+ c 1) b)) (else out))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))) (c (in-range (- (cols g) 1)))) (let ((a (at g r c)) (b (at g r (+ c 1))) (d (at g (+ r 1) c)) (e (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))) (cond ((and (not (= a 0)) (= a e) (= b 0) (= d 0)) (set-cell (set-cell out r (+ c 1) a) (+ r 1) c a)) ((and (not (= b 0)) (= b d) (= a 0) (= e 0)) (set-cell (set-cell out r c b) (+ r 1) (+ c 1) b)) (else out))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8-cell<? a b) (or (< (first a) (first b)) (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b))))) (define (e8-norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) e8-cell<?)) (let* ((anchors (find-color g 1)) (proto (first (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (not (= (obj-color obj) 1))) (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))) (shape (e8-norm (obj-cells proto))) (color (obj-color proto))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((anchor (in-list anchors))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((rel (in-list shape))) (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (first rel))) (c (+ (second anchor) (second rel)))) (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell acc r c color) acc)))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((obj (in-list (objects g 0)))) (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj)) (r1 (first bb)) (c1 (second bb)) (r2 (third bb)) (c2 (fourth bb)) (border (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2) (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2))) (positions-in-rect r1 c1 r2 c2)))) (paint-cells out border (obj-color obj))))))

written_solution: Find the component that encloses at least one real hole: an empty cell region inside its bbox that cannot reach the box boundary through background cells. Keep only that component and delete all others.
