(let ((dummy 0)) (define dirs4 (list (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1))) (define (e8-component-has-hole? obj) (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj)) (bb (obj-bbox obj)) (r1 (first bb)) (c1 (second bb)) (r2 (third bb)) (c2 (fourth bb)) (open (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p cells))) (positions-in-rect r1 c1 r2 c2)))) (if (empty? open) #f (let* ((border-open (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2) (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2))) open))) (let bfs ((queue border-open) (seen border-open)) (if (empty? queue) (< (length seen) (length open)) (let* ((cur (first queue)) (nbrs (filter (lambda (p) (and (member? p open) (not (member? p seen)))) (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (first cur) (first d)) (+ (second cur) (second d)))) dirs4)))) (bfs (append (rest queue) nbrs) (append seen nbrs))))))))) (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((obj (in-list (objects g 0)))) (if (e8-component-has-hole? obj) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj)) out))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((anchor (first (find-color g 1))) (ar (first anchor)) (ac (second anchor))) (for*/fold ((out (set-cell (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) ar ac 1))) ((r (in-range (rows g))) (c (in-range (cols g)))) (let ((v (at g r c))) (if (member? v (list 0 1)) out (let ((mr (- (* 2 ar) r)) (mc (- (* 2 ac) c))) (let ((out2 (set-cell out r c v))) (if (in-bounds? mr mc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out2 mr mc v) out2)))))))))

(let ((dummy 0)) (define (e8-cell<? a b) (or (< (first a) (first b)) (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b))))) (define (e8-norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) e8-cell<?))         (pr (first pivot))

written_solution: Use the neutral blue(1) template as a shape exemplar. Inside every gray(5) frame, replace the unique interior marker with a copy of the template recolored to that marker's color.

(rule! (lambda (g)
  ;; each hollow 5-rectangle FRAME holds one colored marker in its interior: erase the marker
  ;; and stamp the color-1 TEMPLATE shape into the frame interior, in the marker's color.
  (define (objs-color color) (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) (objects g 0)))
  (define (rect-outline? o)                       ;; >=3x3 and every cell ON its bbox ring, ring full
    (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 o)) (c1 (obj-c1 o)) (r2 (obj-r2 o)) (c2 (obj-c2 o))
           (ring-n (- (* 2 (+ (- r2 r1) (- c2 c1) 2)) 4)))
      (and (>= (- r2 r1) 2) (>= (- c2 c1) 2)
           (= (obj-size o) ring-n)
           (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                                 (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                 (obj-cells o)))))
  (define (bbox< a b)                             ;; deterministic template pick: topmost-leftmost
    (cond ((!= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
          ((!= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))
          ((!= (obj-r2 a) (obj-r2 b)) (< (obj-r2 a) (obj-r2 b)))
          (else (< (obj-c2 a) (obj-c2 b)))))
  (define (frame-marker f)                        ;; LAST interior cell that is neither bg nor frame
    (let* ((hits (for*/list ((r (range (+ (obj-r1 f) 1) (obj-r2 f)))
                             (c (range (+ (obj-c1 f) 1) (obj-c2 f)))
                             #:when (not (member? (at g r c) (list 0 5))))
                   (list r c (at g r c)))))
      (if (empty? hits) #f (last hits))))
  (let* ((template (first (sort (objs-color 1) bbox<)))
         (shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells template))))
    (for/fold ((out g)) ((f (filter rect-outline? (objs-color 5))))
      (let* ((m (frame-marker f)))
        (if (not m) out
            (recolor-cells (set-cell out (first m) (second m) 0)
                           (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (obj-r1 f) 1 (first p))
                                                  (+ (obj-c1 f) 1 (second p))))
                                shape)
                           (third m))))))))

title: Three-Panel Transform Transfer
written_solution: Read the three 3×3 panels as A, B, and C. Infer the dihedral transform that maps A to B, then apply that same transform to C and return only the transformed third panel.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ()
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                          (range 0 (cols grid)))))
        (let loop ([remaining (append seps (list (cols grid)))] [start 0] [panels (list)])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              (reverse panels)
              (let ((stop (first remaining)))
                (loop (rest remaining) (+ stop 1)
                      (if (> stop start) (cons (subgrid grid 0 start (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels) panels)))))))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels g))
           (a (first panels))
           (b (second panels))
           (c (third panels))
           (code (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code a t) b))
                                        (list 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8))))
                   (if hit hit 1))))
      (transform-code c code))))

title: Rectangle from Three Corners
written_solution: The three nonzero cells are three corners of one axis-aligned rectangle. Take their bbox and draw the full border in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))))
    (if (empty? cells)
        g
        (let* ((color (at g (first (first cells)) (second (first cells))))
               (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
               (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb)) (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb))
               (outline
                 (append
                   (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r0 c))
                   (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r1 c))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c0))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c1)))))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) outline color)))))

title: Extract the Densest Row
written_solution: Scan the rows and count nonzero cells. Select the row with the highest count, breaking ties by the earliest row, and output that row alone.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((rows-ranked
           (sort (range 0 (rows g))
                 (lambda (a b)
                   (let ((ca (count-where (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g a)))
                         (cb (count-where (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g b))))
                     (if (= ca cb) (< a b) (> ca cb)))))))
    (list (row-at g (first rows-ranked)))))

title: Crop the Unique-Color Object
written_solution: Count connected components separately for each color. Exactly one color occurs only once; crop to that lone object’s bbox and output it.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (objects g 0))
    (define colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define chosen
      (let ((hit
              (find-first
                (lambda (color) (= (length (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) objs)) 1))
                colors)))
        (if hit
            (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) hit)) objs))
            (first (sort objs
                         (lambda (a b)
                           (if (= (obj-color a) (obj-color b))
                               (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                               (> (obj-color a) (obj-color b)))))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Reflect Across the Guide Bar
written_solution: The solid column of 5s is a mirror guide. Reflect the existing pattern across it, preserving the original cells and the guide itself.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((div (find-first (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                         (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (if (eq? div #f)
        g
        (for*/fold ([out g])
                   ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                    [c (in-range (cols g))]
                    #:when (let ((v (at g r c))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)) (not (= c div)))))
          (let ((mc (- (* 2 div) c)))
            (if (and (in-bounds? r mc (rows out) (cols out)) (= (at out r mc) 0))
                (set-cell out r mc (at g r c))
                out))))))

title: Finish the 2×2 Squares
written_solution: Each target pattern is an almost-complete 2×2 monochrome block. Fill the missing cell wherever a 2×2 window has three equal nonzero cells and one zero.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (step grid)
      (for*/fold ([state (list grid #f)])
                 ([r (in-range (- (rows grid) 1))]
                  [c (in-range (- (cols grid) 1))])
        (let* ((out (first state))
               (changed (second state))
               (vals (list (at grid r c) (at grid r (+ c 1))
                           (at grid (+ r 1) c) (at grid (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
               (nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
          (if (and (= (length nz) 3)
                   (= (length (remove-duplicates nz)) 1)
                   (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1))
              (let* ((idx (let loop ([xs vals] [i 0])
                            (if (= (first xs) 0) i (loop (rest xs) (+ i 1)))))
                     (rr (+ r (quotient idx 2)))
                     (cc (+ c (modulo idx 2))))
                (list (set-cell out rr cc (first nz)) #t))
              (list out changed)))))
    (let loop ([grid g] [fuel (* (rows g) (cols g))])
      (if (= fuel 0)
          grid
          (let ((result (step grid)))
            (if (second result)
                (loop (first result) (- fuel 1))
                (first result)))))))

title: Row-Major Compaction
written_solution: Traverse the input in row-major order, collect all nonzero values, and output them as a single compact row in that same order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((vals (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (if (empty? vals) (list (list 0)) (list vals))))

title: Framed Transform Transfer
written_solution: Each large panel is only a frame around a smaller motif. Remove the frames, infer the dihedral transform from the first interior to the second, and apply it to the third interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-blank-cols grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (define (inside-frame panel)
      (let ((h (rows panel)) (w (cols panel)))
        (if (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
                 (all? (lambda (c) (= (at panel 0 c) 5)) (range 0 w))
                 (all? (lambda (c) (= (at panel (- h 1) c) 5)) (range 0 w))
                 (all? (lambda (r) (= (at panel r 0) 5)) (range 0 h))
                 (all? (lambda (r) (= (at panel r (- w 1)) 5)) (range 0 h)))
            (subgrid panel 1 1 (- h 2) (- w 2))
            (crop-to-content panel))))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((panels (split-blank-cols g))
           (A (inside-frame (first panels)))
           (B (inside-frame (second panels)))
           (C (inside-frame (third panels)))
           (code (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code A t) B))
                                        (list 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8))))
                   (if hit hit 1))))
      (transform-code C code))))

title: Area-Sorted Component Packing
written_solution: Find every component, crop each to its own bbox, sort by component area from largest to smallest, and concatenate the crops in that order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-object obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define (paste out pat left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                  [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                  #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at pat r c))))
    (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                               [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                               [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                               [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
           (crops (map crop-object objs))
           (out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
           (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1)))))
      (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining crops] [left 0])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            out
            (loop (paste out (first remaining) left)
                  (rest remaining)
                  (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1)))))))

title: Seeded Frame Fill
written_solution: Each gray(5) rectangle is a frame containing one seed. Preserve the border and flood the interior with that seed color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g (obj-r1 obj) c) 5)) (range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g (obj-r2 obj) c) 5)) (range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r (obj-c1 obj)) 5)) (range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r (obj-c2 obj)) 5)) (range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1)))))
    (define (seed-color obj)
      (let ((vals
              (remove-duplicates
                (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                  (for*/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]
                              [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (obj-c2 obj))])
                    (at g r c))))))
        (if (= (length vals) 1) (first vals) #f)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((color (seed-color frame)))
        (if (eq? color #f)
            out
            (paint-cells out
              (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)
                                 (- (obj-r2 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1))
              color))))))

title: Token-Selected Object Rotation
written_solution: The top-left token selects one of the basic rotations. Remove the token from consideration, crop the object, and rotate the crop as commanded.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
           (clean (set-cell g 0 0 0)))
      (transform-code (crop-to-content clean) cmd))))

title: Crop the Most-Holed Object
written_solution: Among the components, one has the most enclosed voids. Count holes per component and crop to the maximal one.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (hole-count obj)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm))
             (h (+ (third bb) 3))
             (w (+ (fourth bb) 3))
             (occ (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) 1) (+ (second p) 1))) norm)))
        (define (free? r c) (not (member? (list r c) occ)))
        (let loop ([remaining (filter (lambda (p) (free? (first p) (second p)))
                                      (positions-in-rect 0 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)))]
                   [holes 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              holes
              (let* ((p (first remaining))
                     (region (connected-region (empty-grid h w 0) (first p) (second p)
                                (lambda (r c v) (free? r c)) 4))
                     (touch? (any? (lambda (q) (or (= (first q) 0) (= (second q) 0)
                                                    (= (first q) (- h 1)) (= (second q) (- w 1))))
                                   region)))
                (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining)
                      (if touch? holes (+ holes 1))))))))
    (define entries (map (lambda (obj) (list (hole-count obj) (obj-size obj) obj)) (objects g 0)))
    (define chosen
      (third
        (first
          (sort entries
            (lambda (a b)
              (let ((oa (third a)) (ob (third b)))
                (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (> (first a) (first b))]
                      [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (> (second a) (second b))]
                      [(not (= (obj-r1 oa) (obj-r1 ob))) (< (obj-r1 oa) (obj-r1 ob))]
                      [else (< (obj-c1 oa) (obj-c1 ob))])))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Dihedral Shape-Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: Treat each object as a binary shape. After ordering them by location, fill a 3×3 matrix with cyan(8) wherever two shapes are equivalent under a dihedral transform, otherwise 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (define (binary-crop obj)
      (let ((crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
        (grid-from-fn (rows crop) (cols crop)
          (lambda (r c) (if (= (at crop r c) 0) 0 1)))))
    (define (dihedral-match? a b)
      (not (eq? (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code a t) b)) (list 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8)) #f)))
    (define objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                             (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                             (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define shapes (map binary-crop objs))
    (define n (length shapes))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (dihedral-match? (list-ref shapes r) (list-ref shapes c)) 8 0)))))

title: Chamber Flood Fill
written_solution: The wall color partitions the grid. For each connected non-wall chamber, if all nonzero cells inside share one color, fill the background cells of that chamber with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (region start)
      (connected-region g (first start) (second start)
        (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5))) 4))
    (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5))))] [out g])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((cells (region (first remaining)))
                 (colors (remove-duplicates
                           (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                                   (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells)))))
            (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p cells))) remaining)
                  (if (= (length colors) 1)
                      (paint-cells out
                        (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)
                        (first colors))
                      out)))))))

title: Two-Axis Analogy Mosaic
written_solution: The four panels form an analogy grid: top-left maps to top-right by one transform, and top-left maps to bottom-left by another. Apply the row transform to the bottom-left panel to produce the missing result.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (define div-row
      (find-first (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (cols g))))
                  (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define div-col
      (find-first (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 9)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                  (range 0 (cols g))))
    (define tl (subgrid g 0 0 (- div-row 1) (- div-col 1)))
    (define tr (subgrid g 0 (+ div-col 1) (- div-row 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define bl (subgrid g (+ div-row 1) 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- div-col 1)))
    (define code
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code tl t) tr)) (list 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8))))
        (if hit hit 1)))
    (transform-code bl code)))

title: Manhattan Voronoi Frame
written_solution: Inside the border, color each empty cell by the nearest seed under Manhattan distance. When two or more seeds are tied for nearest, leave that cell 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (let ((v (third cell))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
                       (grid-cells g))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (at g r c)))
          (cond [(= v 5) 5]
                [(not (= v 0)) v]
                [else
                 (let* ((distances
                          (map (lambda (seed)
                                 (list (+ (abs (- r (first seed))) (abs (- c (second seed))))
                                       (third seed)))
                               seeds))
                        (best (apply min (map first distances)))
                        (colors (remove-duplicates
                                  (map second (filter (lambda (d) (= (first d) best)) distances)))))
                   (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 0))]))))))

title: Nested Depth Recoloring
written_solution: The top row is a depth legend. Detect the nested 5-colored rectangles below, order them from largest to smallest, and recolor each border by its depth using the legend colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define legend (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))) (first g)))
    (define body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (all? (lambda (c) (= (at body (obj-r1 obj) c) 5)) (range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (c) (= (at body (obj-r2 obj) c) 5)) (range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (r) (= (at body r (obj-c1 obj)) 5)) (range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1)))
           (all? (lambda (r) (= (at body r (obj-c2 obj)) 5)) (range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1)))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects body 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define (frame-cells obj)
      (append
        (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (+ 1 (obj-r1 obj)) c))
        (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (+ 1 (obj-r2 obj)) c))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list (+ 1 r) (obj-c1 obj)))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list (+ 1 r) (obj-c2 obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list frames)] [idx (in-naturals)])
      (paint-cells out (frame-cells frame)
                   (if (< idx (length legend)) (list-ref legend idx) (last legend))))))

title: Overlap After Guided Transform
written_solution: The token selects a dihedral transform for the right 3×3 motif. Transform that motif, intersect it with the left motif, and paint the overlapping nonzero cells with orange(7).

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
           (left (subgrid g 1 0 3 2))
           (right (subgrid g 1 4 3 6))
           (tr (transform-code right cmd)))
      (grid-from-fn 3 3

title: Elbow-Guided Terminal Route
written_solution: The green(3) marker fixes the bend of the path. Connect the two terminal cells with an orthogonal polyline that passes through that elbow, painting the route in red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((pts (find-color g 2))
        (elbows (find-color g 3)))
    (define (draw-seg out p1 p2 color)
      (let ((r1 (first p1)) (c1 (second p1)) (r2 (first p2)) (c2 (second p2)))
        (cond [(= r1 r2)
               (for/fold ([acc out]) ([c (in-range (min c1 c2) (+ (max c1 c2) 1))])
                 (if (= (at acc r1 c) 5) acc (set-cell acc r1 c color)))]
              [(= c1 c2)
               (for/fold ([acc out]) ([r (in-range (min r1 r2) (+ (max r1 r2) 1))])
                 (if (= (at acc r c1) 5) acc (set-cell acc r c1 color)))]
              [else out])))
    (if (or (not (= (length pts) 2)) (not (= (length elbows) 1)))
        g
        (let* ((a (first pts))
               (b (second pts))
               (e (first elbows))
               (p1 (list (first a) (second e)))
               (p2 (list (first b) (second e))))
          (set-cell
            (draw-seg (draw-seg (draw-seg (draw-seg g a p1 2) p1 e 2) e p2 2) p2 b 2)
            (first e) (second e) 2)))))

title: Legend-Ordered Canonical Gallery
written_solution: The top row specifies the order of colors to output. For each color, find its object, normalize that object to its lexicographically minimal dihedral orientation, and concatenate the canonical crops in legend order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
    (define body (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= r 0) 0 (at g r c)))))
    (define (transforms grid)
      (list grid (rotate-cw grid) (rotate-180 grid) (transpose grid)
            (flip-lr grid) (flip-ud grid)))
    (define (row<? xs ys)
      (cond [(and (empty? xs) (empty? ys)) #f]
            [(empty? xs) #t]
            [(empty? ys) #f]
            [(not (= (first xs) (first ys))) (< (first xs) (first ys))]
            [else (row<? (rest xs) (rest ys))]))
    (define (grid<? a b)
      (let loop ([xs a] [ys b])
        (cond [(and (empty? xs) (empty? ys)) #f]
              [(empty? xs) #t]
              [(empty? ys) #f]
              [(not (equal? (first xs) (first ys))) (row<? (first xs) (first ys))]
              [else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys))])))
    (define (best-grid grids)
      (first (sort grids grid<?)))
    (define (canonical obj)
      (best-grid (map crop-to-content
                      (transforms (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))))
    (define entries (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-color obj) (canonical obj))) (objects body 0)))
    (define (crop-for color)
      (second (first (filter (lambda (entry) (= (first entry) color)) entries))))
    (define crops (map crop-for legend))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (define (paste out pat left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                  [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                  #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at pat r c))))
    (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining crops] [left 0])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (loop (paste out (first remaining) left)
                (rest remaining)
                (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1))))))

title: Row/Column Command Mosaic
written_solution: The input encodes a tiny transform table. Apply each row command and each column command to the source motif, compose them, and place the four resulting motifs into a 2×2 mosaic.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (anti-transpose grid) (rotate-180 (transpose grid)))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= code 7) (transpose grid)]
            [else (anti-transpose grid)]))
    (define (hcat grids)
      (let* ((out-h (apply max (map rows grids)))
             (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols grids)) (max 0 (- (length grids) 1)))))
        (define (paste out pat left)
          (for*/fold ([acc out])
                     ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                      [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                      #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
            (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at pat r c))))
        (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining grids] [left 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              out
              (loop (paste out (first remaining) left)
                    (rest remaining)
                    (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1))))))
    (define (vcat grids)
      (let* ((out-h (+ (apply + (map rows grids)) (max 0 (- (length grids) 1))))
             (out-w (apply max (map cols grids))))
        (define (paste out pat top)
          (for*/fold ([acc out])
                     ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                      [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                      #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
            (set-cell acc (+ top r) c (at pat r c))))
        (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining grids] [top 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              out
              (loop (paste out (first remaining) top)
                    (rest remaining)
                    (+ top (rows (first remaining)) 1))))))
    (let* ((row-cmds (list (at g 3 0) (at g 5 0)))
           (col-cmds (list (at g 0 3) (at g 0 5)))
           (src (subgrid g 3 3 5 5))
           (rows-out
             (map (lambda (rcmd)
                    (hcat (map (lambda (ccmd) (transform-code (transform-code src rcmd) ccmd)) col-cmds)))
                  row-cmds)))
      (vcat rows-out))))

              ([obj (in-list (objects (remove-color g 8 0) 0))])

        (paint-cells out (map (lambda (p) (rotate-around p pivot)) (obj-cells obj)) (obj-color obj))))))

title: Sort Crops by Area
written_solution: Extract each connected colored component as a tight crop, sort the crops by area ascending, and place them in one top-aligned row separated by a single background column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
        (lambda (a b)
          (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
    (define crops (map (lambda (o) (subgrid g (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o))) objs))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining crops] [left 0])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let ((crop (first remaining)))
            (loop (for*/fold ([acc out])
                              ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                               [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                    (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at crop r c)))
                  (rest remaining)
                  (+ left (cols crop) 1)))))))

title: Checker Frames
written_solution: For every rectangular border, use its border color and the unique interior marker color to fill the interior with a checkerboard whose top-left interior cell takes the marker color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define (marker-color frame)
      (let ((vals
              (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v (obj-color frame)))))
                      (for*/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                                  [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
                        (at g r c)))))
        (if (empty? vals) 1 (first vals))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((marker (marker-color frame)) (border (obj-color frame)))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
          (set-cell acc r c
                    (if (= (modulo (+ (- r (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1))
                                      (- c (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1))) 2) 0)
                        marker
                        border)))))))

title: Commanded Crop Transform
written_solution: Read the command in the top-left cell, crop the rest of the nonzero motif, and transform the crop: 1 → rotate90, 2 → rotate180, 3 → flip horizontally, 4 → transpose.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-command grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (apply-command (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0)) (at g 0 0))))

title: Chamber Ownership Fill
written_solution: Partition the grid into non-8 chambers. Any chamber containing exactly one non-background color is filled entirely with that color while walls remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 8))))] [out g])
    (if (empty? remaining)
        out
        (let* ((start (first remaining))
               (region (connected-region g (first start) (second start)
                         (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 8))) 4))
               (colors (remove-duplicates
                         (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8))))
                                 (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) region))))
               (next-remaining (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining)))
          (if (= (length colors) 1)
              (loop next-remaining (paint-cells out region (first colors)))
              (loop next-remaining out))))))

title: Shape Equality Matrix
written_solution: Separate the three panels, crop each object to a translation-invariant binary mask, and output a 3x3 matrix with blue(1) where two masks are equal and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (define (mask panel)
      (crop-to-content
        (grid-from-fn (rows panel) (cols panel)
          (lambda (r c) (if (= (at panel r c) 0) 0 1)))))
    (let* ((masks (map mask (split-panels g)))
           (n (length masks)))
      (grid-from-fn n n
        (lambda (r c) (if (equal? (nth masks r) (nth masks c)) 1 0))))))

title: Select Panel by Border
written_solution: Find the outside selector color, choose the framed panel with the same border color, and output the interior of that panel without its border.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define frames (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (define (inside-any-frame? r c)
      (not (eq? (find-first (lambda (fr)
                              (and (>= r (obj-r1 fr)) (<= r (obj-r2 fr))
                                   (>= c (obj-c1 fr)) (<= c (obj-c2 fr))))
                            frames)
                #f)))
    (define selector
      (third (first (filter (lambda (cell)
                              (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                                   (not (inside-any-frame? (first cell) (second cell)))))
                            (grid-cells g)))))
    (define chosen (first (filter (lambda (fr) (= (obj-color fr) selector)) frames)))
    (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 chosen) 1) (+ (obj-c1 chosen) 1)
             (- (obj-r2 chosen) 1) (- (obj-c2 chosen) 1))))

title: Commanded Pivot Rotations
written_solution: Each anchor has a command cell just to its left. Match each colored component to its nearest anchor and rotate it clockwise by the command value in quarter-turns, keeping only pivots and rotated components.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((pivots (find-color g 8)))
    (define (dist p q) (+ (abs (- (first p) (first q))) (abs (- (second p) (second q)))))
    (define (nearest-pivot obj)
      (first (sort pivots
                   (lambda (a b)
                     (< (apply min (map (lambda (cell) (dist a cell)) (obj-cells obj)))
                        (apply min (map (lambda (cell) (dist b cell)) (obj-cells obj))))))))
    (define (rotate-around p pivot turns)
      (let loop ([cur p] [k (modulo turns 4)])
        (if (= k 0)
            cur
            (let ((dr (- (first cur) (first pivot)))
                  (dc (- (second cur) (second pivot))))
              (loop (list (+ (first pivot) dc) (- (second pivot) dr)) (- k 1))))))
    (define comps (objects (remove-color (remove-color g 8 0) 1 0) 0))
    (for/fold ([out (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) pivots 8)])
              ([obj (in-list comps)])
      (let* ((pivot (nearest-pivot obj))
             (cmd-c (- (second pivot) 1))
             (turns (if (and (>= cmd-c 0) (member? (at g (first pivot) cmd-c) (list 1 2 3)))
                        (at g (first pivot) cmd-c)
                        0)))
        (paint-cells out (map (lambda (p) (rotate-around p pivot turns)) (obj-cells obj)) (obj-color obj))))))

title: Transform Analogy
written_solution: Split the three panels, identify which allowed transform maps panel A to panel B, then apply that same transform to panel C and output the result.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (define (apply-transform grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 0) grid]
            [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-ud grid)]
            [(= cmd 5) (transpose grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((panels (map crop-to-content (split-panels g)))
           (a (first panels))
           (b (second panels))
           (c (third panels))
           (cmd (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (apply-transform a t) b)) (list 0 1 2 3 4 5 6))))
      (apply-transform c (if (eq? cmd #f) 0 cmd)))))

title: Nested Palette Fill
written_solution: The left palette lists fill colors from outermost chamber inward. For each zero cell inside the nested 8 rectangles, count how many frames contain it and fill it with the corresponding palette color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define palette
      (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                 #:when (and (not (= (at g r 0) 0)) (not (= (at g r 0) 8))))
        (at g r 0)))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 8)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                  (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                  (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (if (= (at g r c) 0)
          (let ((depth (count-where (lambda (fr)
                                      (and (> r (obj-r1 fr)) (< r (obj-r2 fr))
                                           (> c (obj-c1 fr)) (< c (obj-c2 fr))))
                                    frames)))
            (if (and (> depth 0) (<= depth (length palette)))
                (set-cell out r c (nth palette (- depth 1)))
                out))
          out))))

title: Voronoi Inside the Frame
written_solution: Inside the 8 frame, fill every cell with the color of the nearest seed using Manhattan distance. If two or more seed colors tie for nearest, leave the cell 0. Keep the border and seeds.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g 8)))
         (seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                          (and (> (first cell) (first bb)) (< (first cell) (third bb))
                               (> (second cell) (second bb)) (< (second cell) (fourth bb))
                               (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 8))))
                        (grid-cells g))))
    (define (dist cell r c)
      (+ (abs (- r (first cell))) (abs (- c (second cell)))))
    (define (fill-value r c)
      (let* ((dmin (apply min (map (lambda (cell) (dist cell r c)) seeds)))
             (colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (= (dist cell r c) dmin)) seeds)))))
        (if (= (length colors) 1) (first colors) 0)))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]
                [c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
      (if (= (at g r c) 8) out (set-cell out r c (fill-value r c))))))

title: Compose Two Commands
written_solution: Read the two command cells, crop the remaining motif, and compose the transforms in order: first command 1 then command 2.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-command grid cmd)
      (cond [(= cmd 1) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= cmd 2) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= cmd 3) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= cmd 4) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (let* ((cmd1 (at g 0 0))
           (cmd2 (at g 0 1))
           (motif (crop-to-content (set-cell (set-cell g 0 0 0) 0 1 0))))
      (apply-command (apply-command motif cmd1) cmd2))))

title: Area Comparison Matrix
written_solution: Split the three panels, measure each object’s area, and output a 3x3 matrix: 1 for equal area, 2 when the row panel is larger, and 3 when it is smaller.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid)))
               (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid))
                         (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r stop) 8)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (let* ((areas (map (lambda (p)
                         (count-where (lambda (cell) (and (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 8))))
                                      (grid-cells p)))

           (n (length areas)))
      (grid-from-fn n n
        (lambda (r c)

            (cond [(= a b) 1]

title: Select and Transform the Panel
written_solution: Use the first top-row cell to select the framed panel by border color, crop that panel’s interior motif, then transform it according to the second top-row command.

(rule!
  (let ((selector (at g 0 0))
        (cmd (at g 0 1)))

title: Guide Mirror Copy
written_solution: Locate the full 5-colored guide line. Keep every original nonzero cell, and add its mirror image across that guide.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define guide-rows (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define guide-cols (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))
    (define cells (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member (third cell) (list 0 5)))) (grid-cells g)))
    (define (mirror out cell axis p)
      (let* ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell))
             (nr (if (= axis 0) r (- (* 2 p) r)))
             (nc (if (= axis 0) (- (* 2 p) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out nr nc v) out)))
    (cond [(not (empty? guide-cols))
           (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list cells)]) (mirror out cell 0 (first guide-cols)))]
          [(not (empty? guide-rows))
           (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list cells)]) (mirror out cell 1 (first guide-rows)))]
          [else g])))

title: Straight Segment Completion
written_solution: For each color, find its two endpoints. If they are aligned horizontally or vertically, fill every cell between them with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (remove-duplicates (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))))
    (define (seg a b color)
      (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
             (for/list ([c (in-range (min (second a) (second b)) (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1))])
               (list (first a) c color))]
            [(= (second a) (second b))
             (for/list ([r (in-range (min (first a) (first b)) (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1))])
               (list r (second a) color))]
            [else (list)]))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (paint-cells out (seg (first pts) (second pts) color))
            out)))))

title: Left Header Row Flood
written_solution: Whenever the first cell of a row is nonzero, flood that whole row with the same color. Leave rows with a zero header empty.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((color (at g r 0)))
        (if (not (= color 0)) color 0)))))

title: Row Pack Left
written_solution: For each row, read the nonzero cells from left to right and rewrite them flush against the left edge, padding the rest with zeros.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g r))))
        (if (< c (length vals)) (list-ref vals c) 0)))))

title: Diagonal-Corner Rectangle Fill
written_solution: Group cells by color. Each color gives two diagonal corners of a rectangle. Fill the whole rectangle with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; alt: the same fold can inline bbox painting directly in the exactly-two branch.
  (let ((paint-bbox
         (lambda (out color pts)
           (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells pts))
                  (r0 (first bb)) (c0 (second bb))
                  (r1 (third bb)) (c1 (fourth bb)))
             (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1) color)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid h w 0)])
              ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (paint-bbox out color pts)
            out)))))

title: Tight Bounding Crop
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (crop-to-content g))

title: Singleton Multiset Strip
written_solution: Count how many times each non-background color appears. Output a single row where colors are listed in ascending order, repeated by their counts.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (row (apply append
                     (map (lambda (color) (make-list (length (find-color g color)) color)) colors))))
    (if (empty? row) (list (list 0)) (list row))))

title: Mirror Target Color Across Guide
written_solution: Read the target color from the top-left cell. Keep the whole grid, and reflect only cells of that color across the gray(5) guide line.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((target (at g 0 0)))
    (define guide-rows (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define guide-cols (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))
    (define cells (filter (lambda (cell)
                            (and (= (third cell) target)
                                 (not (and (= (first cell) 0) (= (second cell) 0)))))
                          (grid-cells g)))
    (define (mirror out cell axis p)
      (let* ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell))
             (nr (if (= axis 0) r (- (* 2 p) r)))
             (nc (if (= axis 0) (- (* 2 p) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out nr nc v) out)))
    (cond [(not (empty? guide-cols))
           (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list cells)]) (mirror out cell 0 (first guide-cols)))]
          [(not (empty? guide-rows))
           (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list cells)]) (mirror out cell 1 (first guide-rows)))]
          [else g])))

title: Column Packing Inside Frame
written_solution: Keep the rectangular frame. Inside it, compress each column up so the nonzero cells stack from the top of the interior while preserving top-to-bottom order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (let* ((frames (filter rect-border? (objects g 0))))
      (if (empty? frames)
          g
          (let* ((frame (first frames))
                 (bb (obj-bbox frame))
                 (with-border (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells frame) (obj-color frame))))
            (for/fold ([out with-border]) ([c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
              (let ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0)))
                                  (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]) (at g r c)))))
                (for/fold ([acc out]) ([v (in-list vals)] [i (in-naturals)])
                  (set-cell acc (+ (first bb) 1 i) c v)))))))))

title: Periodic Tile Fill
written_solution: Crop the nonzero motif in the corner and tile that exact pattern periodically across the entire output grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((motif (crop-to-content g))
         (mh (rows motif))
         (mw (cols motif)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c) (at motif (modulo r mh) (modulo c mw))))))

title: Command Rotate Crop
written_solution: Ignore the command cell at the top-left, crop the remaining nonzero object, and rotate it according to the command: 1 → id, 2=90° clockwise, 3=180°, 4=270° clockwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (obj (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0))))
    (cond [(= cmd 1) obj]
          [(= cmd 2) (rotate-cw obj)]
          [(= cmd 3) (rotate-180 obj)]
          [else (rotate-ccw obj)])))

title: Masked Submatrix Extraction
written_solution: Take the interior matrix. Keep only the rows marked by cyan(8) in the first column and only the columns marked by cyan(8) in the top row, preserving their original order.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((rs (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r 0) 8)) (range 1 (rows g))))
         (cs (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 8)) (range 1 (cols g)))))
    (if (or (empty? rs) (empty? cs))
        (list (list 0))
        (for/list ([r (in-list rs)])
          (for/list ([c (in-list cs)])
            (at g r c))))))

title: Area-Sorted Rectangle Strip
written_solution: Extract the disconnected solid rectangles, crop each one tightly, sort them by area ascending, and place the crops left to right with one zero column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                   (list (obj-size obj)
                         (obj-color obj)
                         (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (first a) (first b))
                  (< (second a) (second b))
                  (< (first a) (first b))))))
    (define crops (map third items))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((crop (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                         (let ((v (at crop r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols crop) 1) next))))))

title: Colorized Template Transfer
written_solution: One component is a solid rectangle that supplies the target color; the other is the template shape. Crop the template and recolor every nonzero cell with the rectangle’s color.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((comps (objects g 0)) (rects (filter solid-rect? comps)) (shapes (filter (lambda (obj) (not (solid-rect? obj))) comps))) (if (or (empty? rects) (empty? shapes)) (list (list 0)) (let* ((rect (last rects)) (shape (last shapes)) (crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 shape) (obj-c1 shape) (obj-r2 shape) (obj-c2 shape)))) (grid-from-fn (rows crop) (cols crop) (lambda (r c) (if (not (= (at crop r c) 0)) (obj-color rect) 0))))))))

title: Quadrant Mirror From Dual Guides
written_solution: Detect the full vertical 5-guide and the full horizontal 6-guide. Keep the original object and reflect it across the vertical guide, the horizontal guide, and both guides so it appears in all symmetric quadrants.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define guide-row
      (first (filter (lambda (r)
                       (let ((vals (row-at g r)))
                         (and (all? (lambda (v) (member v (list 5 6))) vals)
                              (>= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 6)) vals) (- (cols g) 1)))))
                     (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (define guide-col
      (first (filter (lambda (c)
                       (let ((vals (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))]) (at g r c))))
                         (and (all? (lambda (v) (member v (list 5 6))) vals)
                              (>= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 5)) vals) (- (rows g) 1)))))
                     (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (define (interesting grid)
      (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member (third cell) (list 0 5 6)))) (grid-cells grid)))
    (define (mirror out cell axis p)
      (let* ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell))
             (nr (if (= axis 0) r (- (* 2 p) r)))
             (nc (if (= axis 0) (- (* 2 p) c) c)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (set-cell out nr nc v) out)))
    (let* ((vpass (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (interesting g))]) (mirror out cell 0 guide-col))))
      (for/fold ([out vpass]) ([cell (in-list (interesting vpass))]) (mirror out cell 1 guide-row)))))

title: Bounding-Box Projection Matrix
written_solution: Extract the solid rectangles in row-major order. Build an n×n matrix where each entry is 3 if the two rectangles’ bounding boxes overlap in both rows and columns, 1 if only row ranges overlap, 2 if only column ranges overlap, and 0 if neither overlaps.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                    (lambda (a b)
                      (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                        (if (= (first ba) (first bb))
                            (< (second ba) (second bb))
                            (< (first ba) (first bb))))))))
    (define (row-overlap? a b)
      (not (or (< (third a) (first b)) (< (third b) (first a)))))
    (define (col-overlap? a b)
      (not (or (< (fourth a) (second b)) (< (fourth b) (second a)))))
    (grid-from-fn (length objs) (length objs)
      (lambda (i j)
        (let* ((b1 (obj-bbox (list-ref objs i)))
               (b2 (obj-bbox (list-ref objs j)))
               (ro (row-overlap? b1 b2))
               (co (col-overlap? b1 b2)))
          (if (and ro co) 3 (if ro 1 (if co 2 0))))))))

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define (floor-half x)
      (if (>= x 0) (quotient x 2) (- 0 (quotient (+ (- 0 x) 1) 2))))
    (define (center frame-grid obj-grid)

             (ow (cols obj-grid))

             (sc (+ (second bb) 1 (floor-half (- (- (fourth bb) (second bb) 1) ow)))))
        (for*/fold ([out frame-grid])
                   ([r (in-range oh)]

            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out (+ sr r) (+ sc c) v) out)))))

           (tf-cmd (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))

                      (objects work 0))

                    (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))
                    (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

(let ((dummy 0)) (let* ((k (length (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))) (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))) (anchor (first (find-color body 9))) (objs (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? (at body (first p) (second p)) (list 0 9)))) (grid-positions body)))) (for/fold ((out (set-cell (empty-grid (rows body) (cols body) 0) (first anchor) (second anchor) 9))) ((p (in-list objs))) (let* ((dr (- (first p) (first anchor))) (dc (- (second p) (second anchor))) (positions (list (list dr dc) (list dc (- dr)) (list (- dr) (- dc)) (list (- dc) dr)))) (for/fold ((acc out)) ((rel (in-list (take positions (min k 4))))) (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (first rel))) (c (+ (second anchor) (second rel)))) (if (in-bounds? r c (rows body) (cols body)) (set-cell acc r c (at body (first p) (second p))) acc))))))))
