title: Seed expands to a 3x3 square
written_solution: Each nonzero seed becomes a solid 3x3 block of the same color, clipped by the grid border.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (x) (not (= (third x) 0))) (grid-cells g)))])
    (paint-cells out
      (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
              (for*/list ([dr (in-list (list -1 0 1))]
                           [dc (in-list (list -1 0 1))])
                (list (+ (first cell) dr) (+ (second cell) dc))))
      (third cell))))

title: Keep only the bottommost cell in each column
written_solution: In every column, erase all nonzero cells except the lowest one. Keep that cell's color and position.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((hits (filter (lambda (r) (not (= (at g r c) 0))) (reverse (range 0 (rows g))))))
      (if (empty? hits)
          out
          (set-cell out (first hits) c (at g (first hits) c))))))

title: Right-pack every row
written_solution: Within each row, keep the nonzero cells in their left-to-right order but slide them all the way to the right.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let* ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g r)))
             (start (- (cols g) (length vals))))
        (if (< c start) 0 (list-ref vals (- c start)))))))

title: Complete 2x2 blocks from L-shapes
written_solution: Whenever a 2x2 window has exactly three cells of the same non-background color and one 0, fill the missing corner with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
           (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
           (nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
      (if (and (= (length nz) 3)
               (= (length (remove-duplicates nz)) 1))
          (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list cells)])
            (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) (first nz))
                acc))
          out))))

title: Seed paints its whole row and column
written_solution: Each nonzero seed fills its entire row and its entire column with the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
            ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (x) (not (= (third x) 0))) (grid-cells g)))])
    (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
      (paint-cells
        (paint-cells out (for/list ([rr (in-range (rows g))]) (list rr c)) v)
        (for/list ([cc (in-range (cols g))]) (list r cc))
        v))))

title: Fill vertical segments between matching endpoints
written_solution: If a column has two endpoints of the same non-background color with only 0s between them, fill the vertical segment between the endpoints.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; alt: transpose, reuse the horizontal bridge rule, then transpose back.
  (let ((clear-span?
         (lambda (c r0 r1)
           (all? (lambda (r) (zero? (at g r c)))
                 (range (+ r0 1) r1)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([c (in-range w)])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
        (let ((rs (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) color)) (range h))))
          (if (and (= (length rs) 2) (clear-span? c (first rs) (second rs)))
              (paint-cells acc
                           (for/list ([r (in-range (first rs) (+ (second rs) 1))])
                             (list r c))
                           color)
              acc))))))

title: Rotate the square grid by 180 degrees
written_solution: Turn the whole square grid upside down: the output is the 180-degree rotation of the input.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (rotate-180 g))

title: Recolor each object by aspect ratio
written_solution: Treat each component as an object. Recolor tall objects to red(2), wide objects to green(3), and square-bbox objects to yellow(4), preserving each shape and position.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let ((color (if (> (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)) 2 (if (> (obj-w obj) (obj-h obj)) 3 4))))
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color))))

title: Keep only frame objects
written_solution: Preserve only objects that are hollow rectangular frames. Erase all filled or irregular objects.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj)) (w (obj-w obj))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                         (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (filter frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj)))))

title: Output the object and its horizontal mirror
written_solution: Crop the unique object tightly. Output the crop, then a background separator column, then its left-right mirror.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((obj (crop-to-content g))
         (mir (flip-lr obj))
         (h (max (rows obj) (rows mir)))
         (w (+ (cols obj) 1 (cols mir))))
    (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid h w 0)])
               ([r (in-range h)]
                [c (in-range w)])
      (let ((v (if (and (< r (rows obj)) (< c (cols obj)))
                   (at obj r c)
                   (if (and (< r (rows mir)) (>= c (+ (cols obj) 1)))
                       (at mir r (- c (+ (cols obj) 1)))
                       0))))
        (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out r c v) out)))))

title: Keep only even-area objects
written_solution: Treat each component as an object and keep only those with an even number of cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (if (= (modulo (obj-size obj) 2) 0)
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (obj-color obj))
        out)))

title: Keep the largest object of each color
written_solution: For each color independently, keep only the largest component of that color and erase the smaller ones.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let* ((objs (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) color)) (objects g 0))
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                             (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                 (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                                 (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                             (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
           (best (first objs)))
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells best) color))))

title: Column-majority color row
written_solution: Build a 1-row output. In each column, write the non-background color that appears most often in that input column; write black(0) if the column is empty.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (list
    (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let* ((colors (grid-colors (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))]) (list (at g r c))) 0))
             (ranked (sort (map (lambda (color)
                                  (list color (count-where (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) color)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
                                colors)
                           (lambda (a b)
                             (if (= (second a) (second b))
                                 (< (first a) (first b))
                                 (> (second a) (second b)))))))
        (if (empty? ranked) 0 (first (first ranked)))))))

title: Rotate each object inside its own square box
written_solution: Each object occupies a square bbox. Rotate each object 90° clockwise within its own box, keeping the boxes in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let ((rot (rotate-cw (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))))
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows rot))]
                  [c (in-range (cols rot))])
        (let ((v (at rot r c)))
          (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ (obj-r1 obj) r) (+ (obj-c1 obj) c) v) acc))))))

title: Stamp rotated copies of a template at marker cells
written_solution: The non-marker pattern is a template. For each singleton marker: blue(1) stamps the template as-is, 2 stamps a 90-degree clockwise rotation, 3 stamps 180°, and 4 stamps 270 degrees. Place each copy with its top-left corner at the marker cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define markers
      (filter (lambda (cell)
                (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
                  (and (member v (list 1 2 3 4))
                       (empty? (filter (lambda (d)
                                         (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                                           (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                                                (= (at g nr nc) v))))
                                       cardinal-deltas)))))
              (grid-cells g)))
    (define cleaned
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([m (in-list markers)])
        (set-cell out (first m) (second m) 0)))
    (define template (crop-to-content cleaned))
    (define (rot v)
      (if (= v 1) template
          (if (= v 2) (rotate-cw template)
              (if (= v 3) (rotate-180 template) (rotate-ccw template)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([m (in-list markers)])
      (let ((stamp (rot (third m))))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (rows stamp))]
                    [c (in-range (cols stamp))])
          (let ((v (at stamp r c)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ (first m) r) (+ (second m) c) v) acc)))))))

title: Concatenate frame interiors from left to right
written_solution: Find all rectangular frames. Take the full interior rectangle of each frame (without the border) and concatenate those interior grids from left to right, separated by one background column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames (sort (filter (lambda (obj)
                                  (let* ((h (obj-h obj)) (w (obj-w obj))
                                         (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
                                    (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
                                         (all? (lambda (p)
                                                 (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                                                     (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                                               (obj-cells obj)))))
                                (objects g 0))
                         (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
         (interiors (map (lambda (obj) (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1))) frames)))
    (if (empty? interiors)
        (list (list 0))
        (let ((out-h (apply max (map rows interiors)))
              (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols interiors)) (max 0 (- (length interiors) 1)))))
          (let pack ([remaining interiors] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
            (if (empty? remaining)
                out
                (let* ((sub (first remaining))
                       (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                         ([r (in-range (rows sub))]
                                          [c (in-range (cols sub))])
                               (let ((v (at sub r c)))
                                 (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
                  (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols sub) 1) next))))))))

title: Recolor objects by marker order after sorting by area
written_solution: Read the top-row marker colors from left to right. Sort the non-marker objects by area from smallest to largest. Recolor the smallest object to the first marker color, the next object to the second marker color, and so on.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((markers (sort (filter (lambda (cell) (and (= (first cell) 0) (not (= (third cell) 0)))) (grid-cells g))
                        (lambda (a b) (< (second a) (second b)))))
         (body (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))])
                 (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))])
                   (if (= r 0) 0 (at g r c)))))
         (objs (sort (objects body 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                           (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                               (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                           (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)] [marker (in-list markers)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (third marker)))))

title: Make a quadrant mosaic of normalized objects
written_solution: Assign each object to top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right based on the quadrant of its center in the original grid. Crop each object tightly, then build a 2×2 mosaic with one background row and one background column separating the quadrants.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define mid-r (- (rows g) 1))
    (define mid-c (- (cols g) 1))
    (define (top? obj) (< (* 2 (apply + (obj-rs obj))) (* (obj-size obj) mid-r)))
    (define (left? obj) (< (* 2 (apply + (obj-cs obj))) (* (obj-size obj) mid-c)))
    (define (shape obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define objs (objects g 0))
    (define tl (map shape (filter (lambda (obj) (and (top? obj) (left? obj))) objs)))
    (define tr (map shape (filter (lambda (obj) (and (top? obj) (not (left? obj)))) objs)))
    (define bl (map shape (filter (lambda (obj) (and (not (top? obj)) (left? obj))) objs)))
    (define br (map shape (filter (lambda (obj) (and (not (top? obj)) (not (left? obj)))) objs)))
    (define s-tl (if (empty? tl) #f (first tl)))
    (define s-tr (if (empty? tr) #f (first tr)))
    (define s-bl (if (empty? bl) #f (first bl)))
    (define s-br (if (empty? br) #f (first br)))
    (define top-h (max (if s-tl (rows s-tl) 1) (if s-tr (rows s-tr) 1)))
    (define bot-h (max (if s-bl (rows s-bl) 1) (if s-br (rows s-br) 1)))
    (define left-w (max (if s-tl (cols s-tl) 1) (if s-bl (cols s-bl) 1)))
    (define right-w (max (if s-tr (cols s-tr) 1) (if s-br (cols s-br) 1)))
    (define (paste-shape out shape top left)
      (if (not shape)
          out
          (for*/fold ([acc out])
                     ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                      [c (in-range (cols shape))])
            (let ((v (at shape r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) (+ left c) v) acc)))))
    (paste-shape
      (paste-shape
        (paste-shape
          (paste-shape (empty-grid (+ top-h 1 bot-h) (+ left-w 1 right-w) 0) s-tl 0 0)
          s-tr 0 (+ left-w 1))
        s-bl (+ top-h 1) 0)
      s-br (+ top-h 1) (+ left-w 1))))

title: Flip each frame's contents according to the frame color
written_solution: Inside every rectangular frame, transform the entire interior rectangle. If the frame color is odd, flip the interior left-right; if the frame color is even, flip it top-bottom. Keep the frames themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj)) (w (obj-w obj))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                         (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (let* ((interior (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (- (obj-r2 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1)))
             (trans (if (= (modulo (obj-color frame) 2) 1) (flip-lr interior) (flip-ud interior)))
             (cleared (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                  ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                                   [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
                        (set-cell acc r c 0))))
        (for*/fold ([acc cleared])
                   ([r (in-range (rows trans))]
                    [c (in-range (cols trans))])
          (let ((v (at trans r c)))
            (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1 r) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1 c) v) acc)))))))

title: Sort objects by bounding-box perimeter and stack them
written_solution: Crop each object tightly. If an object's box is taller than it is wide, rotate it 90° clockwise so its longer side becomes horizontal. Then sort the objects by bounding-box perimeter from largest to smallest; if perimeters tie, keep row-major order. Stack them top-to-bottom with one background row between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                             (let* ((sub0 (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
                                    (sub (if (> (rows sub0) (cols sub0)) (rotate-cw sub0) sub0))
                                    (per (* 2 (+ (rows sub) (cols sub)))))
                               (list per (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) sub)))
                           (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (first a) (first b))
                            (if (= (second a) (second b))
                                (< (third a) (third b))
                                (< (second a) (second b)))
                            (> (first a) (first b))))))
         (shapes (map fourth items))
         (out-h (+ (apply + (map rows shapes)) (max 0 (- (length shapes) 1))))
         (out-w (apply max (map cols shapes))))
    (let pack ([remaining shapes] [top 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                         (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) c v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ top (rows shape) 1) next))))))

title: Select the nth-largest object using marker count
written_solution: Count the maroon(9) markers in the top row. Sort the non-marker objects by area from largest to smallest and output a tight crop of the nth-largest object, where n is the number of markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((n (count-where (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 9)) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (body (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))])
                 (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))])
                   (if (and (= r 0) (= (at g r c) 9)) 0 (at g r c)))))
         (objs (sort (objects body 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                           (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (> (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                               (> (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                           (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (define chosen (list-ref objs (- n 1)))
    (subgrid body (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Broadcast Motif to Marker Anchors
written_solution: Locate the unique source anchor colored gray(5). Collect every nonzero cell except the gray(5) and the destination magenta(6) markers, convert them to offsets from the gray(5), and copy that sparse motif to every magenta(6) anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((src (first (find-color g 5)))
         (anchors (find-color g 6))
         (motif (filter (lambda (cell) (not (member? (third cell) (list 0 5 6)))) (grid-cells g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
      (for/fold ([cur out]) ([cell (in-list motif)])
        (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (- (first cell) (first src))))
              (c (+ (second anchor) (- (second cell) (second src)))))
          (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
              (set-cell cur r c (third cell))
              cur))))))

title: Complete Straight Segments
written_solution: For each color, find its two endpoints. If they share a row, fill all cells between them horizontally; if they share a column, fill vertically.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (let ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts)))
              (cond [(= (first a) (first b))
                     (paint-cells out
                                  (map (lambda (c) (list (first a) c))
                                       (range (min (second a) (second b)) (+ (max (second a) (second b)) 1)))
                                  color)]
                    [(= (second a) (second b))
                     (paint-cells out
                                  (map (lambda (r) (list r (second a)))
                                       (range (min (first a) (first b)) (+ (max (first a) (first b)) 1)))
                                  color)]
                    [else out]))
            out)))))

title: Finish Monochrome 2×2 Blocks
written_solution: Whenever a 2×2 window contains exactly three cells of the same non-background color and one empty cell, fill the missing corner with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range 0 (- (rows g) 1))] [c (in-range 0 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c (at g r c)) (list r (+ c 1) (at g r (+ c 1)))
                        (list (+ r 1) c (at g (+ r 1) c)) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1) (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))))
           (vals (map third cells))
           (nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) vals)))
      (if (and (= (length nz) 3) (= (length (remove-duplicates nz)) 1) (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1))
          (let ((missing (first (filter (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) 0)) cells))))
            (set-cell out (first missing) (second missing) (first nz)))
          out))))

title: Fill Rectangles from Diagonal Corners
written_solution: For each color, take its two points as the diagonal corners of an axis-aligned rectangle and fill the full rectangle with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))
                   (r0 (min (first a) (first b))) (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
                   (c0 (min (second a) (second b))) (c1 (max (second a) (second b))))
              (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1) color))
            out)))))

title: Remove Isolated Noise
written_solution: Keep a nonzero cell if at least one of its four orthogonal neighbors has the same color. Delete isolated singletons.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (at g r c)))
        (if (and (not (= v 0))
                 (any? (lambda (d)
                         (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                           (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g nr nc) v))))
                       cardinal-deltas))
            v
            0)))))

title: Crop the Selector-Colored Object
written_solution: Use the top-left cell as the target color. Find the unique component of that color in the rest of the grid and return its tight crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (at g 0 0))
         (choices (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) target)
                                           (not (member? (list 0 0) (obj-cells o)))))
                          (objects g 0))))
    (if (empty? choices)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (obj-cells (first choices)))))
          (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))

title: Mirror Across the Full Guide Column
written_solution: Find the column filled with 5s. Mirror every non-guide colored cell on the left side across that axis, keeping the original cells and the guide.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((guides (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (if (empty? guides)
        g
        (let ((gc (first guides)))
          (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range gc)])
            (let ((v (at g r c))
                  (mc (- (* 2 gc) c)))
              (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)) (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g)))
                  (set-cell out r mc v)
                  out)))))))

title: Selector Broadcast of One Motif Color
written_solution: Read the selector color from the top-left cell. Around the unique gray(5) anchor, keep only motif cells of that selected color and broadcast those offsets to every magenta(6) anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (at g 0 0))
         ;; Position of the first color 5 cell
         (src (first (find-color g 5)))
         ;; Positions of every color 6 cell
         (anchors (find-color g 6))
         (motif (filter (lambda (cell) (and (= (third cell) target)
                                            (not (and (= (first cell) 0) (= (second cell) 0)))))
                        (grid-cells g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
      (for/fold ([cur out]) ([cell (in-list motif)])
        (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (- (first cell) (first src))))
              (c (+ (second anchor) (- (second cell) (second src)))))
          (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
              (set-cell cur r c (third cell))
              cur))))))

title: Row-Wise Right Shifts from Header Codes
written_solution: For each row, read the translate amount from the first column and move every other nonzero cell in that row to the right by that many columns.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (= c 0)
          (at g r 0)
          (let* ((shift (at g r 0))
                 (src-c (- c shift)))
            (if (and (>= src-c 1) (< src-c (cols g)) (not (= (at g r src-c) 0)))
                (at g r src-c)
                0))))))

title: Convert Components to Area Bars
written_solution: Find the connected components in top-left order. For each component, output one row containing a horizontal bar of that component’s color whose length equals the component area.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((comps (sort (objects g 0)
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                            (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                            (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
         (w (apply max (map obj-size comps))))
    (grid-from-fn (length comps) w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((obj (list-ref comps r)))
          (if (< c (obj-size obj)) (obj-color obj) 0))))))

title: Fill Only the Selected Frames
written_solution: Use the top-left selector color to choose which rectangular frame borders matter. Fill the interiors of all frames with that border color and leave other frames hollow.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((target (at g 0 0)))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) target)
                                                                (not (member? (list 0 0) (obj-cells o)))))
                                               (objects g 0)))])
      (if (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))
          (paint-cells out
                       (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                                          (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1))
                       target)
          out))))

title: Recolor Components by Area Rank
written_solution: Read the legend colors from the top row. Sort the components below by area descending, breaking ties by top-left position, and recolor the largest with the first legend color, the next with the second, and so on.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
         (seen (make-hash))
         (comps (list)))
    (for* ([r (in-range 1 (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (= (at g r c) 0))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define cells (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (>= nr 1)
                             (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (set! comps (cons cells comps))))
    (define sorted-comps
      (sort comps
            (lambda (a b)
              (let ((ba (bbox-of-cells a)) (bb (bbox-of-cells b)))
                (if (= (length a) (length b))
                    (if (= (first ba) (first bb))
                        (< (second ba) (second bb))
                        (< (first ba) (first bb)))
                    (> (length a) (length b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= r 0) (at g r c) 0)))])
              ([cells (in-list sorted-comps)] [idx (in-naturals)])
      (paint-cells out cells (list-ref legend idx)))))

title: Crop the Median-Area Component
written_solution: Find all components and sort them by area ascending. Take the median component, crop it to its bbox, and rotate it clockwise once if the crop is taller than it is wide.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                           (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                               (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                               (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                           (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (obj (list-ref objs (quotient (length objs) 2)))
         (h (obj-h obj))
         (w (obj-w obj))
         (crop (grid-from-fn h w
                 (lambda (r c)
                   (let ((rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) r)) (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) c)))
                     (if (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj)) (at g rr cc) 0))))))
    (if (> h w) (rotate-cw crop) crop)))

title: Bounding-Box Width Comparison Matrix
written_solution: Order the components by top-left position. Build an N×N matrix where 1 → equal bbox width, 2 → the row component is wider, and 3 → it is narrower.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                           (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                           (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
         (widths (map obj-w objs))
         (n (length widths)))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((a (list-ref widths r)) (b (list-ref widths c)))
          (cond [(= a b) 1] [(> a b) 2] [else 3]))))))

title: Legend-Recolored Broadcast Copies
written_solution: Read the legend colors from the top row and sort the destination 6 anchors in row-major order. Copy the sparse motif around the unique 5 anchor to each destination anchor, recoloring every copied cell with that anchor’s legend color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
         (src (first (find-color g 5)))
         (anchors (sort (find-color g 6)
                        (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))))
         (motif (filter (lambda (cell) (and (not (= (first cell) 0))
                                            (not (member? (third cell) (list 0 5 6)))))
                        (grid-cells g))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)] [idx (in-naturals)])
      (for/fold ([cur out]) ([cell (in-list motif)])
        (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (- (first cell) (first src))))
              (c (+ (second anchor) (- (second cell) (second src)))))
          (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
              (set-cell cur r c (list-ref legend idx))
              cur))))))

title: Infer a Whole-Panel Transform
written_solution: Split the input into three panels using the separator columns. Determine which whole-panel transform maps panel A to panel B, then apply the same transform to panel C and return the transformed third panel.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (define (panel start end) (subgrid g 0 start (- (rows g) 1) (- end 1)))
    (define A (panel 0 (first seps)))
    (define B (panel (+ (first seps) 1) (second seps)))
    (define C (panel (+ (second seps) 1) (cols g)))
    (define (xform grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (flip-lr grid)]))
    (define code (first (filter (lambda (k) (equal? (xform A k) B)) (list 1 2 3 4 5))))
    (xform C code)))

title: Rotational Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: Crop every component to its bbox and convert it to a binary shape. Order components by top-left position and build an N×N matrix with red(2) when two shapes are equal up to rotation, 1 on the diagonal, and 3 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (sort (objects g 0)
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                             (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                             (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define (shape-key cells)
      (format "~a" (sort (normalize-cells cells)
                         (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define keys (map (lambda (o) (map (lambda (k) (shape-key (rotate (obj-cells o) k))) (list 0 1 2 3))) objs))
    (define n (length objs))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (cond [(= r c) 1]
              [(member? (first (list-ref keys c)) (list-ref keys r)) 2]
              [else 3])))))

title: Frame-Local 2×2 Tiling
written_solution: For every cyan(8) bordered frame, read the 2×2 sample block immediately above its left edge and tile that sample periodically across the frame interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define frames
      (filter (lambda (obj)
                (and (= (obj-color obj) 8)
                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?) (sort (border-cells obj) cell<?))))
              (objects g 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list frames)])
      (for*/fold ([cur out]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                              [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
        (set-cell cur r c
                  (at g
                      (+ (- (obj-r1 frame) 2) (modulo (- r (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1)) 2))
                      (+ (obj-c1 frame) (modulo (- c (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)) 2))))))))

title: Normalized XOR of Two Panels
written_solution: Split the input into two panels, crop the nonzero object in each panel, align the two cropped binary masks at the top-left of a common canvas, and output orange(7) wherever exactly one mask is occupied.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((sep (first (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
         (A (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- sep 1)))
         (B (subgrid g 0 (+ sep 1) (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))))
    (define (norm-binary panel)
      (let* ((cells (filter-cells panel (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (if bb
            (let ((sub (subgrid panel (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))
              (grid-from-fn (rows sub) (cols sub) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at sub r c) 0) 0 1))))
            (empty-grid 1 1 0))))
    (define a (norm-binary A))
    (define b (norm-binary B))
    (define h (max (rows a) (rows b)))
    (define w (max (cols a) (cols b)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((av (if (and (< r (rows a)) (< c (cols a))) (at a r c) 0))
              (bv (if (and (< r (rows b)) (< c (cols b))) (at b r c) 0)))
          (if (not (= av bv)) 7 0))))))

title: Find the Transform-Matching Candidate
written_solution: Use the first panel as a template shape. Among the candidate panels, find the one whose cropped binary object matches the template up to rotation or reflection, and return that full candidate panel.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g)))))
    (define starts (cons 0 (map add1 seps)))
    (define ends (append seps (list (cols g))))
    (define panels (map (lambda (s e) (subgrid g 0 s (- (rows g) 1) (- e 1))) starts ends))
    (define (norm-cells panel)
      (normalize-cells (filter-cells panel (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))))
    (define (shape-key cells)
      (format "~a" (sort cells (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-lr cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) norm))))
    (define template (norm-cells (first panels)))
    (define keys (remove-duplicates (append* (map (lambda (k)
                                                    (let ((rot (rotate template k)))
                                                      (list (shape-key rot) (shape-key (rotate (reflect-lr template) k)))))
                                                  (list 0 1 2 3)))))
    (first (filter (lambda (p) (member? (shape-key (norm-cells p)) keys)) (rest panels)))))

title: Pack Crops by Hole Count
written_solution: Crop every component, count how many enclosed zero holes it has, sort components by hole count descending and then area descending, and pack the crops from left to right with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-object obj)
      (grid-from-fn (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((rr (+ (obj-r1 obj) r)) (cc (+ (obj-c1 obj) c)))
            (if (member? (list rr cc) (obj-cells obj)) (at g rr cc) 0)))))
    (define (hole-count crop)
      (define seen (make-hash))
      (define holes 0)
      (for* ([r (in-range (rows crop))] [c (in-range (cols crop))])
        (when (and (= (at crop r c) 0) (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c))))
          (define queue (list (cons r c)))
          (define touches #f)
          (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
          (let bfs ([fuel 0])
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (let ((cur (first queue)))
                (set! queue (rest queue))
                (when (or (= (car cur) 0) (= (cdr cur) 0) (= (car cur) (- (rows crop) 1)) (= (cdr cur) (- (cols crop) 1)))
                  (set! touches #t))
                (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                  (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                    (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows crop) (cols crop))
                               (= (at crop nr nc) 0)
                               (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                      (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                      (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
              (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
          (unless touches (set! holes (+ holes 1)))))
      holes)
    (define enriched
      (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                   (let ((crop (crop-object obj)))
                     (list (hole-count crop) (- 0 (obj-size obj)) (obj-color obj) crop)))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (> (first a) (first b))]
                    [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                    [else (< (third a) (third b))]))))
    (define crops (map fourth enriched))
    (define H (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define W (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (- (length crops) 1)))
    (grid-from-fn H W
      (lambda (r c)
        (let loop ([remaining crops] [offset 0])
          (cond [(empty? remaining) 0]
                [(and (>= c offset) (< c (+ offset (cols (first remaining)))))
                 (if (< r (rows (first remaining))) (at (first remaining) r (- c offset)) 0)]
                [else (loop (rest remaining) (+ offset (cols (first remaining)) 1))]))))))

title: Mark the centers of vertical length-5 blue segments
written_solution: Find every blue(1) component that is a straight vertical line of length 5. Recolor exactly its middle cell red(2) and leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 1) (= (obj-c1 o) (obj-c2 o)) (= (obj-size o) 5))) (objects g 0))])
    (set-cell out (quotient (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) 2) (obj-c1 obj) 2)))

title: Fill one-cell horizontal gaps in orange rows
written_solution: Whenever an empty cell has orange(7) immediately to its left and right in the same row, fill that gap with green(3). All other cells stay as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
               (= (at g r c) 0)
               (= (at g r (- c 1)) 7)
               (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 7))
          3
          (at g r c)))))

title: Complete yellow L-triominoes with an orientation-coded corner
written_solution: Each yellow(4) L-triomino occupies three cells of a 2x2 square. Fill its missing corner with a color determined by which corner is absent: top-left→cyan(8), top-right→green(3), bottom-left→red(2), bottom-right→blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define corners (list (list 0 0) (list 0 1) (list 1 0) (list 1 1)))
    (define (missing-color mr mc)
      (cond [(and (= mr 1) (= mc 1)) 1]
            [(and (= mr 1) (= mc 0)) 2]
            [(and (= mr 0) (= mc 1)) 3]
            [else 8]))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))])
      (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 3) (= (- (obj-r2 obj) (obj-r1 obj)) 1) (= (- (obj-c2 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) 1))
          (let* ((local (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj)))) (obj-cells obj)))
                 (miss (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p local))) corners)))
            (if (= (length miss) 1)
                (let* ((m (first miss))
                       (r (+ (obj-r1 obj) (first m)))
                       (c (+ (obj-c1 obj) (second m))))
                  (set-cell out r c (missing-color (first m) (second m))))
                out))
          out))))

title: Mirror the magenta shape across the gray divider
written_solution: A full gray(5) column marks the mirror axis. Copy every magenta(6) cell to its reflected position on the other side of the divider and paint the mirrored copy cyan(8), keeping the original grid intact.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((axis (first (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g)))) (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((mc (- (* 2 axis) (second p))))
               (if (and (in-bounds? (first p) mc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out (first p) mc) 0))
                   (set-cell out (first p) mc 8)
                   out)))
           g (find-color g 6))))

title: Crop the smallest object
written_solution: Identify the smallest connected nonzero object in the grid and output only its bounding-box crop, preserving its original color pattern.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define objs
      (apply append
             (map (lambda (color) (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) (objects g 0)))
                  (range 1 10))))
    (if (empty? objs)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((best (first (sort objs
                                   (lambda (a b)
                                     (let ((ta (first (sort (obj-cells a) cell<?)))
                                           (tb (first (sort (obj-cells b) cell<?))))
                                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                             [(not (= (obj-color a) (obj-color b))) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]
                                             [(not (= (first ta) (first tb))) (< (first ta) (first tb))]
                                             [else (< (second ta) (second tb))]))))))
               (bb (obj-bbox best)))
          (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))

title: Recolor green components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Look at each green(3) component and count how many outer borders of the grid it touches. Recolor only the components that touch exactly one border to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define h (rows g))
    (define w (cols g))
    (define (side-count obj)
      (+ (if (= (obj-r1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-r2 obj) (- h 1)) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c1 obj) 0) 1 0)
         (if (= (obj-c2 obj) (- w 1)) 1 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 3) (= (side-count o) 1))) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8))))

title: Fill the interiors of side-4 hollow squares
written_solution: Among the blue(1) hollow rectangles, select only those that are 4x4 outer squares. Fill each selected square’s interior with red(2) and leave all other shapes unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                    (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (hollow-rect? obj)
      (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))

    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 1) (hollow-rect? o) (= (obj-h o) 4) (= (obj-w o) 4))) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (bbox-interior-cells obj) 2))))

title: Copy the blue object by the marker vector
written_solution: Colors 2 and 3 define a displacement vector from the 2-cell to the 3-cell. Copy the blue(1) object by exactly that vector and paint the translated copy cyan(8), while keeping the original object and markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
         (p3 (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first p3) (first p2)))
         (dc (- (second p3) (second p2))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr)) (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 8)
                   out)))
           g (find-color g 1))))

title: Complete same-color rectangles from corner pairs
written_solution: For each color among red(2), green(3), and yellow(4), the two cells of that color are opposite corners of a rectangle. Draw the full rectangle border in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (list 2 3 4))])
    (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length pts) 2)
          (let* ((a (first pts)) (b (second pts))
                 (r0 (min (first a) (first b)))
                 (c0 (min (second a) (second b)))
                 (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
                 (c1 (max (second a) (second b))))
            (if (and (not (= r0 r1)) (not (= c0 c1)))
                (paint-cells out
                             (filter (lambda (p)
                                       (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                                           (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
                                     (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))
                             color)
                out))
          out))))

title: Output a component-count histogram row
written_solution: Count the connected components of red(2), green(3), and yellow(4). Output a single row made of that many 2s, then 0, then that many 3s, then 0, then that many 4s.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((n2 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))
         (n3 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))))
         (n4 (length (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))))

title: Fill the chamber with the most red seeds
written_solution: Gray(5) walls divide the grid into chambers. Count the red(2) seeds in each chamber and fill the background cells of the chamber with the largest seed count using cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (not (= v 5)))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (define best
      (if (empty? comps)
          #f
          (first (sort comps (lambda (a b)
                               (> (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) a)
                                  (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) b)))))))
    (if best
        (foldl (lambda (p out)
                 (if (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)
                     (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                     out))
               g best)
        g)))

title: Rotate the template according to the control and stamp it at the anchor
written_solution: Treat the blue(1) shape as a template. The control marker chooses a rotation; the orange(7) cell gives the placement anchor. Output a background grid containing the rotated template anchored at the orange(7) cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 2))) 2]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 3]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 4]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 6]
                       [else 2]))
    (define times (cond [(= ctrl 2) 0] [(= ctrl 3) 1] [(= ctrl 4) 2] [else 3]))
    (define shape
      (let loop ((k times) (cells (norm (find-color g 1))))
        (if (= k 0) cells (loop (- k 1) (rot cells)))))
    ;; Position of the first color 7 cell
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 7)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
                 (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)
                 8)))

title: Mark the cells that lie on every shortest path
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls, red(2) is the start, and green(3) is the goal. Recolor every empty cell that belongs to every shortest path between start and goal with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue)) (r (first p)) (c (second p)) (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define (ways-from start dist)
      (define ways (make-hash))
      (hash-set! ways start 1)
      (for ([p (in-list (sort (hash-keys dist) (lambda (a b) (< (hash-ref dist a) (hash-ref dist b)))))])
        (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
          (let ((n (list (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d)))))
            (when (and (hash-has-key? dist n) (= (hash-ref dist n) (+ (hash-ref dist p) 1)))
              (hash-set! ways n (+ (hash-ref ways n 0) (hash-ref ways p 0)))))))
      ways)
    (define s (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define t (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define ds (dist-from s))
    (if (not (hash-has-key? ds t))
        g
        (let* ((dg (dist-from t))
               (ws (ways-from s ds))
               (wg (ways-from t dg))
               (best (hash-ref ds t))
               (total (hash-ref ws t)))
          (foldl (lambda (p out)
                   (if (and (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                            (hash-has-key? ds p)
                            (hash-has-key? dg p)
                            (= (+ (hash-ref ds p) (hash-ref dg p)) best)
                            (= (* (hash-ref ws p 0) (hash-ref wg p 0)) total))
                       (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                       out))
                 g (grid-positions g))))))

title: Recolor shapes by hole count
written_solution: Every yellow(4) object is either solid or has one enclosed hole. Recolor solid objects red(2) and one-hole objects cyan(8), keeping everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((out0 (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 4) 0 (at g r c))))))
    (for/fold ([out out0]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (if (= (topo-count-holes g obj) 1) 8 2)))))

title: Apply the control-selected boolean operation to the two templates
written_solution: Normalize the red(2) and green(3) templates to the same origin. The control chooses union, intersection, or XOR. Output the resulting shape as a cropped maroon(9) grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm color) (sort (normalize-cells (find-color g color)) cell<?))
    (define a (norm 2))
    (define b (norm 3))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 0]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 1]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 8))) 2]
                       [else 0]))
    (define (has? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (define res0
      (cond [(= ctrl 0) (remove-duplicates (append a b))]
            [(= ctrl 1) (filter (lambda (p) (has? p b)) a)]
            [else (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p b))) a)
                          (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p a))) b))]))
    (define res (sort (normalize-cells res0) cell<?))
    (if (empty? res)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells res))
               (out (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0)))
          (paint-cells out res 9)))))

title: Fill the wall-constrained three-seed Voronoi diagram
written_solution: Using wall-aware shortest-path distance, assign each empty cell to the nearest seed among colors 2, 3, and 4. Paint nearest-to-2 cells magenta(6), nearest-to-3 cells orange(7), nearest-to-4 cells cyan(8), and ties maroon(9).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list start))
      (hash-set! dist start 0)
      (define (bfs)
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let* ((p (first queue)) (r (first p)) (c (second p)) (d0 (hash-ref dist p)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (list nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (list nr nc) (+ d0 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc)))))))
            (bfs))))
      (bfs)
      dist)
    (define colors (list 2 3 4))
    (define dists (map (lambda (color) (list color (dist-from (first (find-color g color))))) colors))
    (define (out-color color) (cond [(= color 2) 6] [(= color 3) 7] [else 8]))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let* ((p (list r c))
                   (vals (filter (lambda (cd) (hash-has-key? (second cd) p)) dists)))
              (if (empty? vals)
                  0
                  (let* ((mind (apply min (map (lambda (cd) (hash-ref (second cd) p)) vals)))
                         (winners (filter (lambda (cd) (= (hash-ref (second cd) p) mind)) vals)))
                    (if (> (length winners) 1) 9 (out-color (first (first winners))))))))))))

title: Select the nested band indicated by the control
written_solution: There are three concentric blue(1) frames. The control selects one of three regions: the band between outer and middle, the band between middle and inner, or the inner cavity. Output only the selected region in cyan(8) on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1)
                    (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (hollow-rect? obj)
      (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
        (and (>= (- (third bb) (first bb)) 2)
             (>= (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 2)
             (equal? (sort (obj-cells obj) cell<?)
                     (sort (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)) cell<?)))))
    (define frames
      (sort (map obj-bbox (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 1) (hollow-rect? o))) (objects g 0)))
            (lambda (a b)
              (> (* (+ 1 (- (third a) (first a))) (+ 1 (- (fourth a) (second a))))
                 (* (+ 1 (- (third b) (first b))) (+ 1 (- (fourth b) (second b))))))))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 2))) 2]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 3]
                       [else 4]))
    (define (interior bb) (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1) (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))
    (define (has? p cells) (member? p cells))
    (if (< (length frames) 3)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (let* ((outer (first frames)) (middle (second frames)) (inner (third frames))
               (cells (cond [(= ctrl 2) (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p (interior middle)))) (interior outer))]
                            [(= ctrl 3) (filter (lambda (p) (not (has? p (interior inner)))) (interior middle))]
                            [else (interior inner)])))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) cells 8)))))

title: Repeat the transformed template along the marker vector until blocked
written_solution: Rotate the blue(1) template according to the control marker. Use the vector from orange(7) to cyan(8) as the repeat step, start the first placement at the cyan(8) cell, and repeatedly stamp the transformed template in maroon(9) until the next placement would hit a wall or leave the grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (rot cells) (norm (rotate-cells-cw cells)))
    (define ctrl (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 2))) 2]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) 3]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) 4]
                       [(not (empty? (find-color g 6))) 6]
                       [else 2]))
    (define times (cond [(= ctrl 2) 0] [(= ctrl 3) 1] [(= ctrl 4) 2] [else 3]))
    (define shape
      (let loop ((k times) (cells (norm (find-color g 1))))
        (if (= k 0) cells (loop (- k 1) (rot cells)))))
    (define p7 (first (find-color g 7)))
    (define p8 (first (find-color g 8)))
    (define dr (- (first p8) (first p7)))
    (define dc (- (second p8) (second p7)))
    (let loop ((top (first p8)) (left (second p8)) (out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)))
      (let ((placed (map (lambda (p) (list (+ top (first p)) (+ left (second p)))) shape)))
        (if (all? (lambda (p) (and (pos-in-bounds? p (rows g) (cols g)) (not (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 5)))) placed)
            (loop (+ top dr) (+ left dc) (paint-cells out placed 9))
            out)))))

title: Fill each chamber by the plurality seed color
written_solution: Gray(5) walls divide the grid into chambers. In each chamber, look at the seed colors 2, 3, and 4 already present; fill that chamber’s background cells with magenta(6), orange(7), or cyan(8) according to the plurality seed color, and use maroon(9) for ties.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (passable? r c v) (not (= v 5)))
    ;; Mutable lookup table for seen
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define comps (list))
    (for ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
      (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
        (when (and (not (hash-has-key? seen p)) (passable? r c (at g r c)))
          (let ((comp (connected-region g r c passable?)))
            (for ([q (in-list comp)]) (hash-set! seen q #t))
            (set! comps (cons comp comps))))))
    (define (mapped color) (cond [(= color 2) 6] [(= color 3) 7] [else 8]))
    (define (winner comp)
      (let* ((counts (map (lambda (color)
                            (list color (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) color)) comp)))
                          (list 2 3 4)))
