                    (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj))
                    (obj-color obj)))
     (define (stamp out sub tr tc)  ;; nonzero cells only, clipped
       (foldl (lambda (cell acc)
                (let ((r (+ tr (first cell))) (c (+ tc (second cell))))
                  (if (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                           (in-bounds? r c (rows acc) (cols acc)))
                      (set-cell acc r c (third cell))
                      acc)))
              out (grid-cells sub)))
     (define (rect-frame? obj)
       (and (>= (obj-h obj) 3) (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
            (= (obj-size obj)
               (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (c) (and (= (at g (obj-r1 obj) c)
                                      (obj-color obj))
                                   (= (at g (obj-r2 obj) c)
                                      (obj-color obj))))
                  (range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))
            (all? (lambda (r) (and (= (at g r (obj-c1 obj))
                                      (obj-color obj))
                                   (= (at g r (obj-c2 obj))
                                      (obj-color obj))))
                  (range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1)))))
     (define (fit-of entry og)
       ;; (leftover frame-r1 frame-c1 idx frame oriented-shape) or #f
       (let* ((frame (second entry))
              (ih (- (obj-h frame) 2))
              (iw (- (obj-w frame) 2))
              (rot (rotate-cw og))
              (fit (cond ((and (<= (rows og) ih) (<= (cols og) iw)) og)
                         ((and (<= (rows rot) ih) (<= (cols rot) iw))
                          rot)
                         (else #f))))
         (and fit
              (list (- (* ih iw) (* (rows fit) (cols fit)))
                    (obj-r1 frame) (obj-c1 frame)
                    (first entry) frame fit))))
     (define all-objs (objects g 0))
     (define frames (sort (filter rect-frame? all-objs) obj<))
     (define indexed (enumerate-list frames))
     (define solids
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (not (rect-frame? o))) all-objs) obj<))
     (define (best-fit og used)  ;; tightest, then topmost/leftmost
       (let ((cands (filter (lambda (x) x)
                            (map (lambda (e)
                                   (and (not (member (first e) used))
                                        (fit-of e og)))
                                 indexed))))
         (and (not (empty? cands))
              (first (sort cands
                           (lambda (a b)
                             (cond ((not (= (first a) (first b)))
                                    (< (first a) (first b)))
                                   ((not (= (second a) (second b)))
                                    (< (second a) (second b)))
                                   (else (< (third a) (third b))))))))))
     (let assign ((remaining solids) (used (list))
                  (out (for/fold ((o (empty-grid h w 0)))
                                 ((f (in-list frames)))
                         (paint-cells o (obj-cells f) (obj-color f)))))
       (if (empty? remaining)
           out
           (let ((hit (best-fit (object-grid (first remaining)) used)))
             (if hit
                 (let* ((frame (fifth hit))
                        (sub (sixth hit))
                        (tr (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1
                               (quotient (- (- (obj-h frame) 2)
                                            (rows sub))
                                         2)))
                        (tc (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1
                               (quotient (- (- (obj-w frame) 2)
                                            (cols sub))
                                         2))))
                   (assign (rest remaining) (cons (fourth hit) used)
                           (stamp out sub tr tc)))
                 (assign (rest remaining) used out))))))))

title: Find the shortest ordered checkpoint path
written_solution: In the maze, find the shortest orthogonal path that starts at 2, then visits 3, then 4, then ends at 6. Keep walls and markers, and color the traversed background cells with cyan(8).
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (points-of grid color) (sort (find-color grid color) cell<)) (define (path-between grid start goal) (define deltas cardinal-deltas) (define parent (make-hash)) (define seen (make-hash)) (define found #f) (hash-set! seen start #t) (let bfs ((queue (list start))) (cond ((or found (empty? queue)) #f) (else (let* ((cur (first queue)) (restq (rest queue))) (if (equal? cur goal) (set! found #t) (let ((newq (let add-neighbors ((ds deltas) (acc restq)) (if (empty? ds) acc (let* ((d (first ds)) (np (list (+ (first cur) (first d)) (+ (second cur) (second d))))) (if (and (in-bounds? (first np) (second np) (rows grid) (cols grid)) (not (= (at grid (first np) (second np)) 5)) (not (hash-has-key? seen np))) (begin (hash-set! seen np #t) (hash-set! parent np cur) (add-neighbors (rest ds) (append acc (list np)))) (add-neighbors (rest ds) acc))))))) (bfs newq))))))) (if (not found) (list start) (let reconstruct ((cur goal) (acc (list goal))) (if (equal? cur start) acc (let ((prev (hash-ref parent cur))) (reconstruct prev (cons prev acc))))))) (define p2 (first (points-of g 2))) (define p3 (first (points-of g 3))) (define p4 (first (points-of g 4))) (define p6 (first (points-of g 6))) (define path (append (path-between g p2 p3) (path-between g p3 p4) (path-between g p4 p6))) (foldl (lambda (p acc) (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0) (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 8) acc)) g path)))

title: Rectangle or Not
written_solution: Every non-background object is recolored by shape: yellow(4) if its cells solidly fill its bbox, otherwise blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule! (lambda (grid)
  ;; 4-connected components (excluding background)
  (let ((objects-list (objects grid 0)))
    (reduce (lambda (acc obj)
      (recolor-cells acc (obj-cells obj)
        (if (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4 1)))
      grid objects-list))))

title: Mirror Repair with Highlighted Fixes
written_solution: The blue(1) pattern should be left-right symmetric around the vertical midline. Existing blue(1) cells stay blue(1); any missing mirrored cells are added in yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule! (lambda (grid)
  (let ((height (rows grid)) (width (cols grid)))
    (grid-from-fn height width (lambda (row col)
      (let ((mirror-col (- (- width 1) col))
            (value (cell-at grid row col)))
        (if (!= value 0) value
          (if (= (cell-at grid row mirror-col) 1) 4 0))))))))

title: Find the Candidate Matching the Template
written_solution: A gray(5) template object appears once, and several red(2) candidate objects appear elsewhere. Recolor the candidate with the same cropped shape as the template to yellow(4), and recolor the non-matching candidates to blue(1).
program_solution:
(rule! (lambda (grid)
  (define (shape-grid obj)
    (recolor
      (crop-to-content
        (subgrid (keep-only grid (obj-color obj))
                 (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
      (obj-color obj) 1))
  (let* ((objects-list (objects grid 0))
         (template (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 5)) objects-list)))
         (template-shape (shape-grid template)))
    (reduce (lambda (acc obj)
      (if (= (obj-color obj) 2)
          (recolor-cells acc (obj-cells obj)
            (if (= (shape-grid obj) template-shape) 4 1))
          acc))
      grid objects-list))))

title: Recolor singleton red components
written_solution: Find every red(2) component. If a component has exactly one cell, recolor that cell to green(3). Leave larger red(2) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 2) (= (obj-size o) 1))) (objects g 0)))])
    (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)))

title: Fill straight gaps between blue endpoints
written_solution: Look for rows or columns that contain exactly two blue(1) endpoints with only background cells between them. Fill the cells strictly between the endpoints with green(3), while keeping the blue(1) endpoints unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((after-rows
         (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
           (let ((cols1 (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 1)) (range 0 (cols g)))))
             (if (and (= (length cols1) 2)
                      (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ (first cols1) 1) (second cols1))))
                 (paint-cells out (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range (+ (first cols1) 1) (second cols1))) 3)
                 out)))))
    (for/fold ([out after-rows]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((rows1 (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 1)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
        (if (and (= (length rows1) 2)
                 (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ (first rows1) 1) (second rows1))))
            (paint-cells out (map (lambda (r) (list r c)) (range (+ (first rows1) 1) (second rows1))) 3)
            out)))))

title: Recolor the L-triominoes
written_solution: Inspect each orange(7) component. Recolor only those components that have size 3 and fit inside a 2×2 bbox, which makes them exact L-triominoes. Change those cells to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 7) (= (obj-size o) 3) (= (obj-h o) 2) (= (obj-w o) 2))) (objects g 0)))])
    (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 8)))

title: Extend exact length-3 bars
written_solution: Find every yellow(4) component that is a straight horizontal or vertical bar of length 3. Paint one extra cell just beyond each end of the bar in cyan(8), provided those cells are inside the grid and currently background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 4) (= (obj-size o) 3))) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((rs (remove-duplicates (map first (obj-cells obj))))
           (cs (remove-duplicates (map second (obj-cells obj)))))
      (cond [(= (length rs) 1)
             (let* ((r (first rs))
                    (lo (apply min cs))
                    (hi (apply max cs)))
               (if (and (= (- hi lo) 2) (= (length cs) 3))
                   (foldl (lambda (c acc)
                            (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g r c) 0))
                                (set-cell acc r c 8)
                                acc))
                          out
                          (list (- lo 1) (+ hi 1)))
                   out))]
            [(= (length cs) 1)
             (let* ((c (first cs))
                    (lo (apply min rs))
                    (hi (apply max rs)))
               (if (and (= (- hi lo) 2) (= (length rs) 3))
                   (foldl (lambda (r acc)
                            (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g r c) 0))
                                (set-cell acc r c 8)
                                acc))
                          out
                          (list (- lo 1) (+ hi 1)))
                   out))]
            [else out]))))

title: Crop to the nonzero bounding box
written_solution: Ignore the outer black(0) padding. Find the smallest axis-aligned rectangle that contains every nonzero cell in the input, and output exactly that crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0)))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Recolor corner-touching components
written_solution: Inspect each red(2) component and check whether it touches one of the four grid corners. If it does, recolor the whole component to green(3). Leave red(2) components that do not touch a corner unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g))
         (corners (list (list 0 0) (list 0 (- w 1)) (list (- h 1) 0) (list (- h 1) (- w 1)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))])
      (if (any? (lambda (p) (member? p corners)) (obj-cells obj))
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 3)
          out))))

title: Reflect the object across the divider row
written_solution: The row of gray(5) cells is a mirror line. Reflect the object above the divider across that row, and draw the reflected copy below in cyan(8), leaving the original object and divider unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((divs (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (if (empty? divs)
        g
        (let ((d (first divs)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([cell (in-list (grid-cells g))])
            (let* ((r (first cell))
                   (c (second cell))
                   (v (third cell))
                   (rr (- (* 2 d) r)))
              (if (and (< r d) (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))
                       (in-bounds? rr c (rows g) (cols g))
                       (= (at g rr c) 0))
                  (set-cell out rr c 8)
                  out)))))))

title: Copy the object by the marker vector
written_solution: Use the red(2) marker as the source and the blue(1) marker as the target. Compute the translation vector from the red(2) marker to the blue(1) marker, then copy the yellow(4) object by exactly that vector and draw the copied object in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
         (p1 (first (find-color g 1)))
         (dr (- (first p1) (first p2)))
         (dc (- (second p1) (second p2)))
         (obj (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))
                           (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (foldl (lambda (p out)
             (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr))
                   (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
               (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (set-cell out nr nc 8)
                   out)))
           g
           (obj-cells obj))))

title: Extract the second-largest purple component
written_solution: Rank the purple(6) connected components by area from largest to smallest. Take the second-largest one, crop to its bbox, and output that crop with the selected component recolored to red(2) on a black(0) background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((comps (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                            (let ((ba (obj-bbox a)) (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                              (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                                  (and (= (first ba) (first bb)) (< (second ba) (second bb)))))
                            (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (obj (second comps))
         (cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj) 0) cells 2)))

title: Draw rectangle borders from opposite-corner markers
written_solution: The two red(2) cells are opposite corners of one axis-aligned rectangle, and the two blue(1) cells are opposite corners of another. Draw the red(2)-defined rectangle border in green(3) and the blue(1)-defined rectangle border in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border a b)
      (let* ((r1 (min (first a) (first b)))
             (r2 (max (first a) (first b)))
             (c1 (min (second a) (second b)))
             (c2 (max (second a) (second b))))
        (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                                (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                (positions-in-rect r1 c1 r2 c2))))
    (define out1
      (let ((pts (find-color g 2)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2) (paint-cells g (rect-border (first pts) (second pts)) 3) g)))
    (let ((pts (find-color g 1)))
      (if (= (length pts) 2) (paint-cells out1 (rect-border (first pts) (second pts)) 8) out1))))

title: Fill the walled chamber containing the seed
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. Starting from the red(2) seed, flood through background cells without crossing walls, and fill the reachable chamber interior with cyan(8). Leave the walls and the seed itself unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((seed (first (find-color g 2)))
         (seen (make-hash)))
    (define queue (list (cons (first seed) (second seed))))
    (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
    (let bfs ([step 0])
      (unless (empty? queue)
        (let ((cur (first queue)))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
            (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                  (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
              (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                         (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                         (or (= (at g nr nc) 0) (= (at g nr nc) 2)))
                (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
        (bfs (+ step 1))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([key (in-list (hash-keys seen))])
      (if (= (at g (car key) (cdr key)) 0)
          (set-cell out (car key) (cdr key) 8)
          out))))

title: Color-matched row/column product
written_solution: Rows are marked on the left border and columns are marked on the top border. Fill intersections of red(2)-marked rows and red(2)-marked columns with green(3), and intersections of blue(1)-marked rows and blue(1)-marked columns with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((top-red (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 2)) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (left-red (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r 0) 2)) (range 0 (rows g))))
         (top-blue (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 1)) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (left-blue (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r 0) 1)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (define out-red
      (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-list left-red)] [c (in-list top-red)])
        (if (and (> r 0) (> c 0) (= (at g r c) 0)) (set-cell out r c 3) out)))
    (for*/fold ([out out-red]) ([r (in-list left-blue)] [c (in-list top-blue)])
      (if (and (> r 0) (> c 0) (= (at g r c) 0)) (set-cell out r c 8) out))))

title: Recolor objects by hole count
written_solution: For each yellow(4) component, count how many holes it encloses. Recolor components with 0 holes to red(2), components with 1 hole to green(3), and components with 2 holes to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let* ((n (topo-count-holes g obj 0))
           (hit (cond [(= n 0) 2] [(= n 1) 3] [(= n 2) 8] [else #f])))
      (if hit (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) hit) out))))

title: Stamp a transformed template from the control count
written_solution: The green(3) object is the template. Count the blue(1) control cells: 1 → identity, 2 → 90° clockwise, 3 → 180°, 4 → flip horizontal. Stamp the resulting transformed template at the orange(7) anchor in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define template (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))
                                  (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rot180 cells) (rot90 (rot90 cells)))
    (define (flip-h cells)
      (let ((w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells))))
    (define shape0 (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)))
    (define k (length (find-color g 1)))
    (define shape (cond [(= k 1) shape0] [(= k 2) (rot90 shape0)] [(= k 3) (rot180 shape0)] [else (flip-h shape0)]))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 7)))
    (paint-cells g (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape) 8)))

title: Trace the shortest corridor path
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are blocked walls. Find a shortest 4-neighbor path from the red(2) start to the green(3) goal through the open corridor cells, and color the interior cells of that path cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define parent (make-hash))
    (define seen (make-hash))
    (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
    (define goal-key (cons (first goal) (second goal)))
    (define found #f)
    (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
    (let bfs ([step 0])
      (unless (or found (empty? queue))
        (let ((cur (first queue)))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (when (equal? cur goal-key) (set! found #t))
          (unless found
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc)))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                  (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                  (hash-set! parent (cons nr nc) cur)
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc)))))))))
        (bfs (+ step 1))))
    (if (not found)
        g
        (let trace ([cur goal-key] [path (list)])
          (if (equal? cur (cons (first start) (second start)))
              (foldl (lambda (p out)
                       (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                           (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                           out))
                     g
                     path)
              (trace (hash-ref parent cur) (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) path)))))))

title: Recolor the k-th concentric frame
written_solution: The yellow(4) rectangles are concentric frames. The number of blue(1) control cells tells you which frame to select, counting from the outside inward. Recolor exactly that frame to green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((k (length (find-color g 1)))
         (comps (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))))))
    (if (and (>= k 1) (<= k (length comps)))
        (paint-cells g (obj-cells (list-ref comps (- k 1))) 3)
        g)))

title: XOR the two normalized shapes
written_solution: Take the red(2) object and the blue(1) object, normalize each one to its own top-left corner, and compute their symmetric difference (cells present in exactly one of the two normalized shapes). Output the minimal crop of that XOR shape in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape2 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))
                                                         (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))))
         (shape1 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))
                                                         (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))))
         (x (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (member? p shape2) (member? p shape1)))) (append shape2 shape1))))
    (if (empty? x)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells x))
               (norm (normalize-cells x)))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb)) 0) norm 8)))))

title: Shell the diagonally symmetric object
written_solution: Among the orange(7) objects, find the one whose normalized shape is symmetric under main-diagonal transpose. Around that object, draw the Manhattan-distance-1 shell in cyan(8), without overwriting the original orange(7) cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define (diag-sym? cells)
      (let* ((s (norm cells))
             (t (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (first p))) s))))
        (equal? s t)))
    (define targets (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 7) (diag-sym? (obj-cells o)))) (objects g 0)))
    (if (empty? targets)
        g
        (let ((cells (obj-cells (first targets))))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (grid-positions g))])
            (let ((d (apply min (map (lambda (q) (+ (abs (- (first p) (first q))) (abs (- (second p) (second q))))) cells))))
              (if (and (= d 1) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))
                  (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)
                  out)))))))

title: Compose rotation and reflection controls
written_solution: The magenta(6) object is the template. The blue(1) control count chooses a rotation (1→0°, 2→90°, 3→180°, 4→270°), and the red(2) control count chooses whether to reflect horizontally afterward (1 → no, 2 → yes). Stamp the final transformed template at the orange(7) anchor in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define template (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0))
                                  (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur cells])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (flip-h cells)
      (let ((w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) cells))))
    (define base (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)))
    (define rot (- (length (find-color g 1)) 1))
    (define ref (length (find-color g 2)))
    (define shape (if (= ref 2) (flip-h (rotate base rot)) (rotate base rot)))
    (define anchor (first (find-color g 7)))
    (paint-cells g (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape) 8)))

title: Voronoi fill under wall constraints
written_solution: Treat the red(2) and green(3) seeds as competing sources, but measure distance through the open cells only: gray(5) walls block movement. Fill each background cell with the color of the seed that reaches it by a strictly shorter path. Leave tie cells black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (multi-dist starts)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (map (lambda (p) (cons (first p) (second p))) starts))
      (for ([p (in-list queue)]) (hash-set! dist p 0))
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                    (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc)))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5)))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      dist)
    (define d2 (multi-dist (find-color g 2)))
    (define d3 (multi-dist (find-color g 3)))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
            (at g r c)
            (let ((a (hash-ref d2 (cons r c) 999999))
                  (b (hash-ref d3 (cons r c) 999999)))
              (cond [(< a b) 2] [(< b a) 3] [else 0])))))))

title: Recolor scene objects by matching the rotated legend shapes
written_solution: Above the gray(5) divider is a legend: each colored glyph (red(2), green(3), yellow(4)) defines a reference shape. Below the divider are orange(7) scene objects. Recolor each orange(7) object to the color of the legend glyph whose shape it matches up to rotation.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (norm cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) cell<?))
    (define div (first (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (cols g)))) (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (define top (subgrid g 0 0 (- div 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define scene (subgrid g (+ div 1) 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (norm (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotations cells)
      (let* ((a (norm cells))
             (b (rot90 a))
             (c (rot90 b))
             (d (rot90 c)))
        (list a b c d)))
    (define (matches? shape legend-shape)
      (any? (lambda (s) (equal? shape s)) (rotations legend-shape)))
    (define legend
      (map (lambda (color)
             (list color (norm (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) color)) (objects top 0)))))))
           (list 2 3 4)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 7)) (objects scene 0)))])
      (let* ((shape (norm (obj-cells obj)))
             (hits (filter (lambda (item) (matches? shape (second item))) legend)))
        (if (empty? hits)
            out
            (paint-cells out (map (lambda (p) (list (+ div 1 (first p)) (second p))) (obj-cells obj)) (first (first hits))))))))

title: Mirror singleton seeds across the vertical axis
written_solution: Copy every nonzero cell to its mirror position across the vertical center line, keeping the original cells too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g g
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (= v 0)
          out
          (set-cell out r (- (- (cols g) 1) c) v)))))

title: Grow full crosshairs from seeds
written_solution: Each nonzero seed paints its entire row and entire column with the seed color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (= v 0)
          out
          (let* ((row-cells (for/list ([cc (in-range (cols g))]) (list r cc)))
                 (col-cells (for/list ([rr (in-range (rows g))]) (list rr c))))
            (paint-cells (paint-cells out row-cells v) col-cells v))))))

title: Turn solid rectangles into hollow frames
written_solution: Every solid monochrome rectangle is hollowed out so that only its border remains.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let ((border (append
                   (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
                   (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (obj-r2 obj))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj))))))
      (paint-cells out border (obj-color obj)))))

title: Reflect cells across the main diagonal
written_solution: Copy every nonzero cell to its transposed position across the main diagonal, keeping the original cells too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g g
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (= v 0) out (set-cell out c r v)))))

title: Cast downward rays from seeds
written_solution: Every nonzero seed extends straight down to the bottom border in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (= v 0)
          out
          (paint-cells out
                       (for/list ([rr (in-range r (rows g))]) (list rr c))
                       v)))))

title: Keep only the main diagonal of each 2×2 block
written_solution: Each solid monochrome 2×2 block is reduced to its top-left and bottom-right diagonal cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
             ([r (in-range 0 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 0 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((vals (list (at g r c) (at g (+ r 1) c) (at g r (+ c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))))
      (if (and (not (= (first vals) 0))
               (all? (lambda (v) (= v (first vals))) vals))
          (set-cell (set-cell out r c (first vals)) (+ r 1) (+ c 1) (first vals))
          out))))

title: Fill the border-marker intersections
written_solution: Top-row markers choose columns and left-column markers choose rows; fill every matching-color row/column intersection.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
            ([color (in-list (sort (filter (lambda (v)
                                             (and (member v (row g 0))
                                                  (member v (col g 0))))
                                           (grid-colors g 0))
                                      <))])
    (let ((rs (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r 0) color)) (range 0 (rows g))))
          (cs (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) color)) (range 0 (cols g)))))
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([r (in-list rs)])
        (for/fold ([acc2 acc]) ([c (in-list cs)])
          (set-cell acc2 r c color))))))

title: Crop the corner-selected object
written_solution: A single colored corner marker chooses the object of the same color; output that object cropped to its tight bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g))
         (corner-cells (list (list 0 0 (at g 0 0))
                             (list 0 (- w 1) (at g 0 (- w 1)))
                             (list (- h 1) 0 (at g (- h 1) 0))
                             (list (- h 1) (- w 1) (at g (- h 1) (- w 1)))))
         (marker (first (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) corner-cells)))
         (color (third marker))
         (clean (foldl (lambda (p acc) (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 0))
                       g
                       (map (lambda (cell) (list (first cell) (second cell))) corner-cells)))
         (cells (find-color clean color))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid clean (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Rotate the object by marker count
written_solution: Count the top-row key markers: 1 → rotate the object 90° clockwise, 2 → 180°, and 3 → 270° clockwise. Output the rotated object tightly cropped.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((count9 (count-where (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 9)) (range 0 (cols g))))
         (clean (for/fold ([out g]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
                  (if (= (at g 0 c) 9) (set-cell out 0 c 0) out)))
         (obj (crop-to-content clean 0)))
    (cond [(= count9 1) (rotate-cw obj)]
          [(= count9 2) (rotate-180 obj)]
          [else (transpose obj)])))

title: Pack objects left-to-right by area
written_solution: Crop each connected object to its bbox and pack the crops left-to-right in ascending order of object area, bottom-aligned with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-obj obj)
      (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define (min-nonzero crop)
      (apply min (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (apply append crop))))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                   (let ((crop (crop-obj obj)))
                     (list (obj-size obj) (rows crop) (cols crop) (min-nonzero crop) crop)))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                    [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                    [(not (= (third a) (third b))) (< (third a) (third b))]
                    [else (< (fourth a) (fourth b))]))))
    (define crops (map fifth items))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [c0 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((crop (first remaining))
                 (r0 (- out-h (rows crop)))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                         (let ((v (at crop r c)))
                           (if (= v 0) acc (set-cell acc (+ r0 r) (+ c0 c) v))))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ c0 (cols crop) 1) next))))))

title: Convert columns into bottom-aligned histograms
written_solution: For each column, count its nonzero cells and replace them with a bottom-aligned vertical bar of the same height and color in that same column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (col g c))))
      (if (empty? vals)
          out
          (paint-cells out
                       (for/list ([r (in-range (- (rows g) (length vals)) (rows g))]) (list r c))
                       (first vals))))))

title: Transfer a motif by marker offset
written_solution: Treat the blue(1) cell as a source marker and the red(2) cell as a target marker. Copy the entire motif using the same relative offsets from the target marker, then crop tightly around the copied motif.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((src (first (find-color g 1)))
         (tgt (first (find-color g 2)))
         (motif (filter (lambda (cell)
                          (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                               (not (and (= (first cell) (first src)) (= (second cell) (second src))))
                               (not (and (= (first cell) (first tgt)) (= (second cell) (second tgt))))))
                        (grid-cells g)))
         (painted
          (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([cell (in-list motif)])
            (let ((rr (+ (first tgt) (- (first cell) (first src))))
                  (cc (+ (second tgt) (- (second cell) (second src)))))
              (if (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g))
                  (set-cell out rr cc (third cell))
                  out)))))
    (crop-to-content painted 0)))

title: Project row shadows to a wall
written_solution: A vertical wall of gray(5) stops the projection. Every colored cell to the left of the wall fills the background cells to its right until the wall.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((wall-col (first (filter (lambda (c)
                                   (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                                 (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range wall-col)])
      (let ((v (at g r c)))
        (if (or (= v 0) (= v 5))
            out
            (for/fold ([acc out]) ([cc (in-range (+ c 1) wall-col)])
              (if (= (at acc r cc) 0) (set-cell acc r cc v) acc)))))))

title: Recolor objects by aspect ratio
written_solution: Recolor each object according to its bounding-box aspect: tall objects become red(2), wide objects become green(3), and square objects become yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let* ((h (obj-h obj))
           (w (obj-w obj))
           (color (cond [(> h w) 2] [(> w h) 3] [else 4])))
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color))))

title: Fit solid inserts into matching frames
written_solution: Loose solid rectangles match frames by interior size. Place each insert into the frame whose empty interior has the same height and width.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 obj)) (c1 (obj-c1 obj))
             (r2 (obj-r2 obj)) (c2 (obj-c2 obj))
             (h (+ 1 (- r2 r1))) (w (+ 1 (- c2 c1)))
             (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2)))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
             (= (obj-size obj) perim)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2)
                         (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2)))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define frames (filter frame? (objects (keep-only g 8) 0)))
    (define inserts
      (filter (lambda (obj) (and (not (= (obj-color obj) 8)) (filled? obj))) (objects g 0)))
    (define seeded (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([fr (in-list frames)])
                     (paint-cells out (obj-cells fr) 8)))
    (for/fold ([out seeded]) ([ins (in-list inserts)])
      (let* ((target (find-first (lambda (fr)
                                   (and (= (obj-h ins) (- (obj-h fr) 2))
                                        (= (obj-w ins) (- (obj-w fr) 2))))
                                 frames)))
        (if (eq? target #f)
            out
            (paint-cells out
                         (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 target) 1) (+ (obj-c1 target) 1)
                                            (- (obj-r2 target) 1) (- (obj-c2 target) 1))
                         (obj-color ins)))))))

title: Color-code the normalized overlap of two objects
written_solution: Normalize the red(2) object and the green(3) object to their own top-left corners, overlay them, and output a crop where cells only in the first object stay red(2), only in the second stay green(3), and shared cells become cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pt< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb)))
        (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) r0) (- (second p) c0))) cells) pt<)))
    (define a (normalize (find-color g 2)))
    (define b (normalize (find-color g 3)))
    (define allc (remove-duplicates (append a b)))
    (define out-h (+ 1 (apply max (map first allc))))
    (define out-w (+ 1 (apply max (map second allc))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)]) ([p (in-list allc)])
      (cond [(and (member p a) (member p b)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 8)]
            [(member p a) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 2)]
            [else (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 3)]))))

title: Find the key-and-door shortest path
written_solution: Find the shortest orthogonal route from start red(2) to goal green(3), but door cells 5 can only be crossed after the key cell 4 has been visited. Mark the traversed background cells with orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define start (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define goal (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define keys (find-color g 4))
    (define doors (find-color g 5))
    (define walls (find-color g 8))
    (define queue (list (list (first start) (second start) #f)))
    (define prev (make-hash))
    (define goal-state #f)
    (hash-set! prev (first queue) #f)
    (define (search)
      (unless (or (empty? queue) goal-state)
        (let* ((cur (first queue))
               (r (first cur))
               (c (second cur))
               (has-key (third cur)))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (if (and (= r (first goal)) (= c (second goal)))
              (set! goal-state cur)
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let* ((nr (+ r (first d)))
                       (nc (+ c (second d)))
                       (new-key (or has-key (member (list nr nc) keys)))
                       (st (list nr nc new-key)))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (member (list nr nc) walls))
                             (or new-key (not (member (list nr nc) doors)))
                             (not (hash-has-key? prev st)))
                    (hash-set! prev st cur)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list st)))))))
          (search))))
    (search)
    (define path
      (if goal-state
          (let rebuild ([cur goal-state] [acc (list)])
            (if (eq? cur #f)
                acc
                (rebuild (hash-ref prev cur #f) (cons (list (first cur) (second cur)) acc))))
          (list)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list path)])
      (let ((v (at out (first p) (second p))))
        (if (member v (list 2 3 4 5 8))
            out
            (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 7))))))

title: Pack objects by hole count
written_solution: Crop each connected object and pack the crops left-to-right in ascending order of the number of holes inside the object, bottom-aligned with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-obj obj)
      (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                   (let ((crop (crop-obj obj)))
                     (list (topo-count-holes g obj 0) (rows crop) (cols crop) (obj-color obj) crop)))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                    [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                    [(not (= (third a) (third b))) (< (third a) (third b))]
                    [else (< (fourth a) (fourth b))]))))
    (define crops (map fifth items))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [c0 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((crop (first remaining))
                 (r0 (- out-h (rows crop)))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                         (let ((v (at crop r c)))
                           (if (= v 0) acc (set-cell acc (+ r0 r) (+ c0 c) v))))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ c0 (cols crop) 1) next))))))

title: Transfer a framed pattern through a keyed portal
written_solution: Two same-sized frames form a portal pair. Move the source frame’s interior pattern into the empty target frame using the key marker: blue(1) → flip horizontal, red(2) → flip vertical, green(3) → 180°.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (frame? obj) (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 obj)) (c1 (obj-c1 obj)) (r2 (obj-r2 obj)) (c2 (obj-c2 obj)) (h (+ 1 (- r2 r1))) (w (+ 1 (- c2 c1))) (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2))))) (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3) (= (obj-size obj) perim) (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r1) (= (first p) r2) (= (second p) c1) (= (second p) c2))) (obj-cells obj))))) (define frames (filter frame? (filter (lambda (obj) (member (obj-color obj) (list 6 7))) (objects g 0)))) (define key-cells (filter (lambda (cell) (member (third cell) (list 1 2 3))) (grid-cells g))) (define key (if (empty? key-cells) 0 (third (first key-cells)))) (define (interior-cells fr) (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1) (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1) (- (obj-r2 fr) 1) (- (obj-c2 fr) 1))) (define (has-pattern? fr) (any? (lambda (p) (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p)))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v (obj-color fr)))))) (interior-cells fr))) (define src (first (filter has-pattern? frames))) (define tgt (first (filter (lambda (fr) (not (has-pattern? fr))) frames))) (define src-grid (grid-from-fn (- (obj-h src) 2) (- (obj-w src) 2) (lambda (r c) (let ((v (at g (+ (obj-r1 src) 1 r) (+ (obj-c1 src) 1 c)))) (if (member v (list 6 7)) 0 v))))) (define transformed (cond ((= key 1) (flip-lr src-grid)) ((= key 2) (flip-ud src-grid)) ((= key 3) (rotate-180 src-grid)) (else src-grid))) (define seeded (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0))) ((fr (in-list frames))) (paint-cells out (obj-cells fr) (obj-color fr)))) (for*/fold ((out seeded)) ((r (in-range (rows transformed))) (c (in-range (cols transformed)))) (let ((v (at transformed r c))) (if (= v 0) out (set-cell out (+ (obj-r1 tgt) 1 r) (+ (obj-c1 tgt) 1 c) v))))))

title: Connect component centers in color order
written_solution: Order the components by color value and connect their centers in that order using L-shaped polylines: horizontal first, then vertical. Each segment uses the color of its starting component.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (step-range a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (range a (- b 1) -1)))
    (define pts
      (sort (map (lambda (obj)
                   (list (obj-color obj)
                         (quotient (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) 2)
                         (quotient (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) 2)))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (< (first a) (first b)))))
    (define connected
      (let loop ([remaining pts] [out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
        (if (or (empty? remaining) (empty? (rest remaining)))
            out
            (let* ((a (first remaining))
                   (b (second remaining))
                   (color (first a))
                   (r1 (second a)) (c1 (third a))
                   (r2 (second b)) (c2 (third b))
                   (hpath (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c)) (step-range c1 c2)))
                   (vpath (map (lambda (r) (list r c2)) (step-range r1 r2))))
              (loop (rest remaining) (paint-cells (paint-cells out hpath color) vpath color))))))
    (for/fold ([out connected]) ([p (in-list pts)])
      (set-cell out (second p) (third p) (first p)))))

title: Place objects into topology-matching sockets
written_solution: Frame color encodes the required topology: blue(1) wants a zero-hole object, red(2) wants a one-hole object, and green(3) wants a two-hole object. Center each object inside the matching frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((r1 (obj-r1 obj)) (c1 (obj-c1 obj))
             (r2 (obj-r2 obj)) (c2 (obj-c2 obj))
             (h (+ 1 (- r2 r1))) (w (+ 1 (- c2 c1)))

written_solution: Each frame key encodes a target hole count: key blue(1) wants a 0-hole object, key red(2) wants a 1-hole object, and key green(3) wants a 2-hole object. Move each matching object into the corresponding frame, centered inside it.

(rule!
  (let ()
    (define (frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5) (hollow-frame? obj)))
    (define (frame< a b)
      (cell< (list (obj-r1 a) (obj-c1 a))
             (list (obj-r1 b) (obj-c1 b))))
    (define (key-pos frame)
      (list (- (obj-r1 frame) 1)
            (quotient (+ (obj-c1 frame) (obj-c2 frame)) 2)))
    (define (erase-frame+key grid frame)
      (let* ((without-frame (erase-cells grid (obj-cells frame) 0))
             (key (key-pos frame)))
        (if (in-bounds? (first key) (second key) (rows grid) (cols grid))
            (set-cell without-frame (first key) (second key) 0)
            without-frame)))
    (define (floor-half n)
      (if (< n 0)
          (- (quotient (+ (- n) 1) 2))
          (quotient n 2)))
    (define (paste-transparent grid piece top left)
      (for*/fold ((out grid))
                 ((r (in-range (rows piece)))
                  (c (in-range (cols piece))))
        (let ((v (at piece r c)) (rr (+ top r)) (cc (+ left c)))
          (if (and (!= v 0)
                   (in-bounds? rr cc (rows out) (cols out)))
              (set-cell out rr cc v)

                     (floor-half (- (- (obj-h frame) 2) (rows piece)))))
             (left (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1
                      (floor-half (- (- (obj-w frame) 2) (cols piece))))))

    (let* ((frames (sort (filter frame? (objects g 0)) frame<))
           (source (for/fold ((out g)) ((frame (in-list frames)))
                     (erase-frame+key out frame)))
           (loose (objects source 0))
           (base (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)))
                           ((frame (in-list frames)))
                   (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) 5))))
      (for/fold ((out base)) ((frame (in-list frames)))
        (let* ((key (key-pos frame))
               (value (if (in-bounds? (first key) (second key)
                                      (rows g) (cols g))
                          (at g (first key) (second key))
                          0))

                        loose))

title: Chamber Seed Fill
written_solution: The wall cells split the grid into chambers. Each chamber contains exactly one colored seed; fill every non-wall cell in that chamber with that seed color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (chamber-cells start)
      (connected-region g (first start) (second start)
        (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5)))
        4))
    (define (marker-color cells)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (p)
                               (let ((v (at g (first p) (second p))))
                                 (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
                             cells)))
        (if hit (at g (first hit) (second hit)) 0)))
    (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5))))] [out (keep-only g 5)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((region (chamber-cells (first remaining)))
                 (color (marker-color region)))
            (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining)
                  (paint-cells out region color)))))))

title: Diagonal Midpoint Completion

    (lambda (r c)
      (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
          (at g r c)

                   (remove-duplicates
                     (append
                       (if (and (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
                                (not (= (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) 0))
                                (= (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
                           (list (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)))
                           (list))
                       (if (and (> r 0) (< r (- (rows g) 1)) (> c 0) (< c (- (cols g) 1))
                                (not (= (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) 0))
                                (= (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) (- c 1))))
                           (list (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)))

            (if (= (length hits) 1) (first hits) 0))))))

title: Row Span Paint
written_solution: Each active row contains two endpoints of the same color. Fill every cell between those endpoints, inclusive, with that color.

(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let* ((vals (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g r)))
             (colors (remove-duplicates vals)))
        (if (and (= (length colors) 1) (= (length vals) 2))
            (let* ((color (first colors))
                   (cols (map second (filter (lambda (cell) (= (third cell) color))
                                             (for/list ([cc (in-range (cols g))])
                                               (list r cc (at g r cc)))))))
              (if (and (>= c (apply min cols)) (<= c (apply max cols))) color (at g r c)))
            (at g r c))))))

                  (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))))

title: One-Step Shift by Code
written_solution: The top-left cell encodes a one-cell direction: 1 up, 2 right, 3 down, 4 left. translate the whole object one step that way and remove the code.

(rule!
  (let* ((code (at g 0 0))
         (delta (cond [(= code 1) (list -1 0)]
                      [(= code 2) (list 0 1)]
                      [(= code 3) (list 1 0)]
                      [else (list 0 -1)]))
         (dr (first delta))
         (dc (second delta)))
    (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))]
                #:when (and (not (and (= r 0) (= c 0))) (not (= (at g r c) 0))))
      (let ((nr (+ r dr)) (nc (+ c dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows out) (cols out))
            (set-cell out nr nc (at g r c))
            out)))))

title: Chamber Max Selector
written_solution: The wall cells define chambers. In each chamber, inspect the colored markers already present and repaint the entire chamber with the largest color number found there.

  (let ((dummy 0))

title: Commanded Crop Rotation
written_solution: Ignore the top-left command cell when finding the object. Crop the object's bbox, then rotate it according to the code: 1 identity, 2 90°, 3 180°, 4 270°.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (let* ((code (at g 0 0))
           (clean (set-cell g 0 0 0)))
      (transform-code (crop-to-content clean) code))))

title: Area-Sorted Color Strip
written_solution: Find each connected colored object, measure its area, sort objects from largest to smallest (breaking ties by color), and output a single row where each object's color is repeated by its area.

(rule!
  (let* ((items
           (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (obj-color obj))) (objects g 0))
                 (lambda (a b)
                   (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (> (first a) (first b))]
                         [else (< (second a) (second b))]))))
         (row (apply append (map (lambda (item) (make-list (first item) (second item))) items))))
    (if (empty? row) (list (list 0)) (list row))))

title: Normalized Overlap Overlay
written_solution: Take the two colored shapes, normalize each to its own top-left bounding-box origin, and overlay them on one canvas. Cells belonging to both become maroon(9); otherwise keep the unique shape's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors g 0)))
         (c1 (first colors))
         (c2 (second colors))
         (n1 (normalize-cells (find-color g c1)))
         (n2 (normalize-cells (find-color g c2)))
         (both (append n1 n2)))
    (let ((max-r (apply max (map first both)))
          (max-c (apply max (map second both))))
      (grid-from-fn (+ max-r 1) (+ max-c 1)
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((p (list r c)))
            (cond [(and (member? p n1) (member? p n2)) 9]
                  [(member? p n1) c1]
                  [(member? p n2) c2]
                  [else 0])))))))

title: Shape Equality Matrix
written_solution: List the disconnected objects from left to right and compare their shapes after normalizing away position and color. Output an N×N matrix with cyan(8) wherever two normalized shapes are equal, else 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (nonzero-components grid)
      (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells grid (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))] [out (list)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            (reverse out)
            (let ((region (connected-region grid (first (first remaining)) (second (first remaining))
                            (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))) 4)))
              (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining) (cons region out))))))
    (define (pos< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (canon cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) pos<))
    (define comps
      (sort (nonzero-components g)
            (lambda (a b) (< (second (bbox-of-cells a)) (second (bbox-of-cells b))))))
    (define shapes (map canon comps))
    (define n (length shapes))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (equal? (list-ref shapes r) (list-ref shapes c)) 8 0)))))

title: Ranked Object Extraction
written_solution: The top-left cell gives a rank: 1 largest, 2 second largest, 3 third largest. Rank the disconnected objects by area and crop out the object at that rank.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((rank (at g 0 0))
         (clean (set-cell g 0 0 0))
         (objs (sort (objects clean 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                             [(not (= (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]
                             [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
         (obj (list-ref objs (- rank 1))))
    (subgrid clean (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
