  (let* ((commands (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (last g)))
         (base (subgrid g 0 0 (- (rows g) 2) (- (cols g) 1)))
         (motif (crop-to-content base))
         (mh (rows motif))
         (mw (cols motif))
         (out-w (+ (* (length commands) mw) (max 0 (- (length commands) 1)))))
    (grid-from-fn mh out-w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((tile (quotient c (+ mw 1)))
               (offset (modulo c (+ mw 1))))
          (if (or (>= tile (length commands)) (>= offset mw) (= (at motif r offset) 0))
              0
              (list-ref commands tile)))))))

title: Chamber Checker Weave
written_solution: The wall cells define chambers. In each chamber, take the smallest and largest marker colors present there and fill the chamber with a checkerboard anchored at that chamber's top-left cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (chamber-cells start)
      (connected-region g (first start) (second start)
        (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5)))
        4))
    (define (paint-chamber out region)
      (let ((colors (sort (remove-duplicates
                            (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                                    (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) region)))
                          <))
            (bb (bbox-of-cells region)))
        (cond [(empty? colors) (paint-cells out region 0)]
              [(= (length colors) 1) (paint-cells out region (first colors))]
              [else
               (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list region)])
                 (set-cell acc (first p) (second p)
                           (if (= (modulo (+ (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb))) 2) 0)
                               (first colors)
                               (last colors))))])))
    (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 5))))] [out (keep-only g 5)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let ((region (chamber-cells (first remaining))))
            (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining)
                  (paint-chamber out region)))))))

title: Panel Transform Analogy
written_solution: The input contains three panels separated by full separator columns. Infer the geometric transform that maps panel A's cropped object to panel B's, then apply that same transform to panel C's cropped object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    ;; Full-height 5-columns delimit A, B, and C; panel padding is irrelevant.
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 5))
                                                   (range 0 (rows grid))))
                          (range 0 (cols grid)))))
        (let loop ([remaining (append seps (list (cols grid)))]
                   [start 0]
                   [panels (list)])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              (reverse panels)
              (let ((stop (first remaining)))
                (loop (rest remaining)
                      (+ stop 1)
                      (if (> stop start)
                          (cons (subgrid grid 0 start
                                         (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1))
                                panels)
                          panels)))))))
    ;; Code order is semantic: the first exact colored A->B match wins.
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels g))
           (a (crop-to-content (first panels)))
           (b (crop-to-content (second panels)))
           (c (crop-to-content (third panels)))
           (code (let ((hit (find-first
                              (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code a t) b))
                              (list 1 2 3 4 5 6))))
                   ;; No exact match is an intentional identity fallback.
                   (if hit hit 1))))
      (transform-code c code))))

title: Sequential Transform Mosaic
written_solution: The top row is a sequence of transform codes and the lower part contains one source motif. Crop the motif and emit transformed copies in command order, separated by one background column.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (transform-code grid code) (cond ((= code 1) grid) ((= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)) ((= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)) ((= code 4) (transpose grid)) ((= code 5) (flip-lr grid)) (else (flip-ud grid)))) (define commands (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g))) (define motif (crop-to-content (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))) (define pieces (map (lambda (cmd) (transform-code motif cmd)) commands)) (define out-h (apply max (map rows pieces))) (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols pieces)) (max 0 (- (length pieces) 1)))) (let loop ((out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)) (remaining pieces) (left 0)) (if (empty? remaining) out (loop (paste out (first remaining) 0 left) (rest remaining) (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1))))))

title: Hole-Count Packing
written_solution: Crop each disconnected object, count how many enclosed holes it contains, then pack the cropped objects left to right in increasing hole count order, breaking ties by larger area first.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-object obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
    (define (hole-count obj)
      ;; Same shape, translated so its bbox starts at (0,0)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
             ;; Bounding box enclosing the cells
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm))
             (h (+ (third bb) 3))
             (w (+ (fourth bb) 3))
             (occ (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) 1) (+ (second p) 1))) norm)))
        (define (free? r c) (not (member? (list r c) occ)))
        (let loop ([remaining (filter (lambda (p) (free? (first p) (second p)))
                                      (positions-in-rect 0 0 (- h 1) (- w 1)))]
                   [holes 0])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              holes
              (let* ((p (first remaining))
                     (region (connected-region (empty-grid h w 0) (first p) (second p)
                                (lambda (r c v) (free? r c)) 4))
                     (touch? (any? (lambda (q) (or (= (first q) 0) (= (second q) 0)
                                                    (= (first q) (- h 1)) (= (second q) (- w 1))))
                                   region)))
                (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining)
                      (if touch? holes (+ holes 1))))))))
    (define (paste out pat left)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (rows pat))]
                  [c (in-range (cols pat))]
                  #:when (not (= (at pat r c) 0)))
        (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at pat r c))))
    (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (hole-count obj) (- (obj-size obj)) (obj-color obj) (crop-object obj)))
                             (objects g 0))
                        (lambda (a b)
                          (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                                [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                                [else (< (third a) (third b))]))))
           (crops (map fourth items))
           (out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
           (out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1)))))
      (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining crops] [left 0])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            out
            (loop (paste out (first remaining) left)
                  (rest remaining)
                  (+ left (cols (first remaining)) 1)))))))

title: Rotation-Equivalence Matrix
written_solution: List the disconnected objects from left to right. Output an N×N matrix with orange(7) when two objects have the same shape up to rotation, and 0 otherwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (nonzero-components grid)
      (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells grid (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))] [out (list)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            (reverse out)
            (let ((region (connected-region grid (first (first remaining)) (second (first remaining))
                            (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))) 4)))
              (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining) (cons region out))))))
    (define (pos< a b)
      (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b))))
    (define (canon cells) (sort (normalize-cells cells) pos<))
    (define (rot-match? a b)
      (let loop ([cur (canon a)] [k 0])
        (cond [(>= k 4) #f]
              [(equal? cur (canon b)) #t]
              [else (loop (canon (rotate-cells-cw cur)) (+ k 1))])))
    (define comps (sort (nonzero-components g)
                        (lambda (a b) (< (second (bbox-of-cells a)) (second (bbox-of-cells b))))))
    (define n (length comps))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c) (if (rot-match? (list-ref comps r) (list-ref comps c)) 7 0)))))

title: Anchor-Aligned Overlap
written_solution: Treat each connected object as having a single anchor cell colored 9. Translate both objects so their anchors coincide, then overlay them; cells claimed by both become cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (nonzero-components grid)
      (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells grid (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))] [out (list)])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            (reverse out)
            (let ((region (connected-region grid (first (first remaining)) (second (first remaining))
                            (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))) 4)))
              (loop (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p region))) remaining) (cons region out))))))
    (define comps (nonzero-components g))
    (define rels
      (map (lambda (cells)
             (let ((anchor (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 9)) cells))))
               (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first anchor))
                                      (- (second p) (second anchor))
                                      (at g (first p) (second p))))
                    cells)))
           comps))
    (define all-rel (apply append rels))
    (define min-r (apply min (map first all-rel)))
    (define min-c (apply min (map second all-rel)))
    (define max-r (apply max (map first all-rel)))
    (define max-c (apply max (map second all-rel)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (+ 1 (- max-r min-r)) (+ 1 (- max-c min-c)) 0)])
              ([rel (in-list rels)])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list rel)])
        (let* ((rr (- (first p) min-r))
               (cc (- (second p) min-c))
               (v (third p))
               (old (at acc rr cc)))
          (set-cell acc rr cc (if (= old 0) v 8)))))))

title: Color+Transform Analogy
written_solution: Split the three panels. Infer the geometric transform from panel A to panel B and also the uniform recolor from A's non-background color to B's; then apply both to panel C's cropped object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let ((seps (filter (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
                          (range 0 (cols grid)))))
        (let loop ([remaining (append seps (list (cols grid)))] [start 0] [panels (list)])
          (if (empty? remaining)
              (reverse panels)
              (let ((stop (first remaining)))
                (loop (rest remaining) (+ stop 1)
                      (if (> stop start) (cons (subgrid grid 0 start (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels) panels)))))))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define (binary grid)
      (grid-from-fn (rows grid) (cols grid) (lambda (r c) (if (= (at grid r c) 0) 0 1))))
    (let* ((panels (split-panels g))
           (a (crop-to-content (first panels)))
           (b (crop-to-content (second panels)))
           (c (crop-to-content (third panels)))
           (code (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code (binary a) t) (binary b)))
                                        (list 1 2 3 4 5 6))))
                   (if hit hit 1)))
           (dst (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (grid-colors b 0))))
           (tc (transform-code c code)))
      (grid-from-fn (rows tc) (cols tc)
        (lambda (r c) (if (= (at tc r c) 0) 0 dst))))))

title: Recolor the corners of filled blue rectangles
written_solution: Find every blue(1) component that forms a solid solid rectangle. Recolor exactly its four corner cells to red(2) and leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (filled-rect? obj)
      (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))])
      (if (and (filled-rect? obj) (>= (obj-h obj) 2) (>= (obj-w obj) 2))
          (paint-cells out (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))) 2)
          out))))

title: Mark one-cell horizontal gaps between blue markers
written_solution: Whenever a zero cell has blue(1) immediately on its left and right, change that middle cell to red(2). Everything else stays the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fold-cells g g
    (lambda (out r c v)
      (if (and (= v 0) (> c 0) (< c (- w 1)) (= (at g r (- c 1)) 1) (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 1))
          (set-cell out r c 2)
          out))))

title: Recolor magenta components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Look at each magenta(6) component and count how many different grid borders it touches. If it touches exactly one border, recolor the whole component to yellow(4). Leave all other magenta(6) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0))])
    (let ((touches (+ (if (= (obj-r1 obj) 0) 1 0)
                      (if (= (obj-r2 obj) (- h 1)) 1 0)
                      (if (= (obj-c1 obj) 0) 1 0)
                      (if (= (obj-c2 obj) (- w 1)) 1 0))))
      (if (= touches 1) (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 4) out))))

title: Complete red L-triominoes into 2×2 squares
written_solution: Each red(2) L-triomino occupies three cells of a 2×2 block. Add the missing fourth corner as green(3), keeping the original red(2) cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))])
    (if (and (= (obj-size obj) 3) (= (obj-h obj) 2) (= (obj-w obj) 2))
        (let* ((box (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
               (missing (find-first (lambda (p) (not (member? p (obj-cells obj)))) box)))
          (if missing (set-cell out (first missing) (second missing) 3) out))
        out)))

title: Extract the smallest orange component
written_solution: Among all orange(7) connected components, choose the one with the fewest cells. Crop tightly around that component, normalize it to the top-left, and recolor it cyan(8) in the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-cells cells color)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm)))
        (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb))
          (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) color 0)))))
    (let* ((objs (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 7)) (objects g 0)))
           (best (argmin (lambda (o) (+ (* 10000 (obj-size o))
                                        (* 100 (obj-r1 o))
                                        (obj-c1 o)))
                         objs)))
      (crop-cells (obj-cells best) 8))))

title: Recolor endpoints of exact-length cyan lines
written_solution: Find every cyan(8) component that is a straight horizontal or vertical segment of exactly length 4. Recolor just its two endpoints to red(2) and leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 8) (= (obj-size o) 4))) (objects g 0))])
    (if (or (and (= (obj-h obj) 1) (= (obj-w obj) 4))
            (and (= (obj-h obj) 4) (= (obj-w obj) 1)))
        (paint-cells out
          (if (= (obj-h obj) 1)
              (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
              (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj))))
          2)
        out)))

title: Fill the center of each 3×3 yellow frame
written_solution: Each hollow yellow(4) frame of size 3×3 has a single center cell. Fill that center with blue(1). Ignore larger yellow(4) frames or other shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 4)) (objects g 0))])
    (if (and (= (obj-h obj) 3) (= (obj-w obj) 3) (= (obj-size obj) 8))
        (paint-cells out (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1) (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)) 1)
        out)))

title: Translate a green shape by the marker vector
written_solution: Take the green(3) shape and compute the vector from the red(2) marker 2 to the blue(1) marker 1. Move the whole green(3) shape by that vector. Output only the moved copy, recolored cyan(8), on a background grid of the same size.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape (argmax obj-size (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))))
         (a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 1)))
         (dr (- (first b) (first a)))
         (dc (- (second b) (second a)))
         (moved (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc))) (obj-cells shape))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0) moved 8)))

title: Reflect the blue object across the divider line
written_solution: A vertical gray(5) divider splits the grid. Mirror each blue(1) object across that divider and output only the reflected copy in cyan(8) on a background grid of the same size.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((div-col (find-first (lambda (c) (for/and ([r (range 0 h)]) (= (at g r c) 5))) (range 0 w))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid h w 0)]) ([p (find-color g 1)])
      (let ((nr (first p)) (nc (- (* 2 div-col) (second p))))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (set-cell out nr nc 8) out)))))

title: Take the Cartesian product of marked rows and columns
written_solution: Collect all rows that contain a red(2) marker and all columns that contain a green(3) marker. In the output, color every intersection of those selected rows and columns cyan(8) on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((rs (unique (map first (find-color g 2))))
         (cs (unique (map second (find-color g 3)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0)
                 (for*/list ([r rs] [c cs]) (list r c))
                 8)))

title: Extract the second-largest red component
written_solution: Consider all red(2) connected components. Rank them by size from largest to smallest, choose the second-largest one, crop tightly around it, normalize it to the top-left, and recolor it cyan(8) in the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-cells cells color)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (bb (bbox-of-cells norm)))
        (grid-from-fn (+ 1 (third bb)) (+ 1 (fourth bb))
          (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) color 0)))))
    (let* ((reds (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))
           (sorted (sort reds (lambda (a b)
                                (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                      [else (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]))))
           (target (second sorted)))
      (crop-cells (obj-cells target) 8))))

title: Trace the unique shortest path through the maze
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. Find the unique shortest path from the red(2) start 2 to the green(3) goal 3 through the open cells, and output that path in cyan(8) on a background grid of the same size.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3)))
         (painted (shortest-path-fill g (first a) (second a) (first b) (second b) 8 0)))
    (map-grid painted (lambda (r c v) (if (= v 8) 8 0)))))

title: Intersect two shapes after normalizing them
written_solution: Take the red(2) shape and the green(3) shape, crop each to its own bbox, align both normalized shapes to the top-left, and keep only the cells occupied in both. Output that normalized intersection in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (crop-cells cells color)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (list (list 0))
          (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
                 (hh (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb))))
                 (ww (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb)))))
            (grid-from-fn hh ww
              (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list (+ r (first bb)) (+ c (second bb))) cells) color 0))))))
    (let* ((a (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
           (b (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 3)) (objects g 0))))))
           (inter (filter (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)))
      (crop-cells inter 8))))

title: Fill each gray frame with its interior marker color
written_solution: Each hollow gray(5) rectangle contains exactly one colored clue cell in its interior. Fill the rest of that frame’s interior with the clue’s color, keeping the gray(5) border and the original clue cell unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1) (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (define (same-cells? a b)
      (and (= (length a) (length b)) (all? (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0))])
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (inside (positions-in-rect (+ (first bb) 1) (+ (second bb) 1) (- (third bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) 1)))
             (colors (unique (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))))
                                     (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) inside)))))
        (if (and (same-cells? (obj-cells obj) (rect-border (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
                 (= (length colors) 1))
            (paint-cells out (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) inside) (first colors))
            out)))))

title: Keep cells occupied in exactly two of three normalized shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1), red(2), and green(3) shapes to their own top-left corners. Output the cells that appear in exactly two of those three normalized shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((s1 (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (s2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (s3 (normalize-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (union (remove-duplicates (append s1 s2 s3)))
         (exact2 (filter (lambda (p)
                           (= (+ (if (member? p s1) 1 0)
                                 (if (member? p s2) 1 0)
                                 (if (member? p s3) 1 0))
                              2))
                         union)))
    (if (empty? exact2)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells exact2))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Take the union of all shortest maze paths
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls. Between the red(2) start 2 and the green(3) goal 3, consider all shortest paths through the open cells. Output the union of every cell that lies on at least one shortest path, colored cyan(8), on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
         (goal (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define ds (dist-from start))
    (define dg (dist-from goal))
    (define D (hash-ref ds (cons (first goal) (second goal)) 999999))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (< D 999999)
                 (hash-has-key? ds (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? dg (cons r c))
                 (= (+ (hash-ref ds (cons r c)) (hash-ref dg (cons r c))) D))
            8
            0)))))

title: Fill the chamber containing the most seeds
written_solution: Gray(5) walls divide the grid into chambers. Count how many red(2) seed cells 2 lie inside each chamber, choose the chamber with the largest count, and fill that entire chamber with cyan(8) in the output.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seen (make-hash))
        (best-score #f)
        (best-cells (list)))
    (define (better? score old)
      (or (not old)
          (> (first score) (first old))
          (and (= (first score) (first old))
               (or (> (second score) (second old))
                   (and (= (second score) (second old))
                        (string<? (third score) (third old)))))))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (unless (or (hash-has-key? seen (cons r c)) (not (member? (at g r c) (list 0 2))))
        (define queue (list (cons r c)))
        (define cells (list))
        (hash-set! seen (first queue) #t)
        (let bfs ([fuel 0])
          (unless (empty? queue)
            (let ((cur (first queue)))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (member? (at g nr nc) (list 0 2))
                             (not (hash-has-key? seen (cons nr nc))))
                    (hash-set! seen (cons nr nc) #t)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
            (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
        (let* ((sorted-cells (sort cells cell<?))
               (seeds (count-where (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2)) sorted-cells))
               (score (list seeds (length sorted-cells) (format "~a" (first sorted-cells)))))
          (when (better? score best-score)
            (set! best-score score)
            (set! best-cells sorted-cells)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) best-cells 8)))

title: Apply a dihedral transform chosen by the controls
written_solution: The corner marker 1 selects a rotation: top-left=0°, top-right=90°, bottom-right=180°, bottom-left=270°. If a control cell 3 is present, first flip the shape horizontally, then apply the chosen rotation. Transform the red(2) shape, crop it tightly, normalize it to the top-left, and output it in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define shape (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))))
    (define rot (cond [(= (at g 0 0) 1) 0]
                      [(= (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)) 1) 1]
                      [(= (at g (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)) 1) 2]
                      [(= (at g (- (rows g) 1) 0) 1) 3]
                      [else 0]))
    (define base (if (empty? (find-color g 3)) (normalize-cells shape) (reflect-h shape)))
    (define cells (rotate base rot))
    (let* ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells))))
           (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
      (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) cells) 8 0))))))

title: Partition the maze by graph distance to two seeds
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. For every reachable open cell, compare its shortest-path distance to the red(2) seed 2 and the green(3) seed 3. Color cells closer to red(2) as cyan(8), closer to green(3) as magenta(6), and equal-distance tie cells as yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (hash-has-key? da (cons r c)) (hash-has-key? db (cons r c)))
            (cond [(< (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c))) 8]
                  [(< (hash-ref db (cons r c)) (hash-ref da (cons r c))) 6]
                  [else 4])
            0)))))

title: Stamp a shape repeatedly along a marker vector
written_solution: Compute the vector from marker 3 to marker 4. Starting from the red(2) shape’s current position, place three copies of that shape: at offsets 0·v, 1·v, and 2·v. Output the union of those copies in cyan(8) on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((shape (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0)))))
         (a (first (find-color g 3)))
         (b (first (find-color g 4)))
         (dr (- (first b) (first a)))
         (dc (- (second b) (second a))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([k (in-range 0 3)])
      (paint-cells out
                   (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) (* k dr)) (+ (second p) (* k dc)))) shape)
                   8))))

title: Apply the legend-selected boolean operation to two normalized shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1) and red(2) shapes to the top-left. Then apply the operation chosen by the unique legend marker: 3 → intersection, 4 → union, and 6 → xor. Output the normalized result as a cyan(8) crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 1)) (objects g 0))))))
         (b (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
         (cells (cond [(not (empty? (find-color g 3))) (filter (lambda (p) (member? p b)) a)]
                      [(not (empty? (find-color g 4))) (remove-duplicates (append a b))]
                      [else (append (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p b))) a)
                                    (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? p a))) b))])))
    (if (empty? cells)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Orthogonal Halo
written_solution: Each red(2) behaves like a beacon. Keep the red(2) itself, and paint each orthogonal neighbor with magenta(6) when that neighbor lies inside the grid. Leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 2))])
    (for/fold ([acc out]) ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
      (let ((rr (+ (first p) (first d)))
            (cc (+ (second p) (second d))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at acc rr cc) 0))
            (set-cell acc rr cc 6)
            acc)))))

title: Horizontal Span Fill
written_solution: Look at each row separately. If a row has exactly two 5s, fill every 0 strictly between those two 5s with green(3). Keep the endpoint 5s as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (let ((cols-hit (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))] #:when (= (at g r c) 5)) c)))
      (if (= (length cols-hit) 2)
          (let ((c1 (first cols-hit)) (c2 (second cols-hit)))
            (if (and (> c2 (+ c1 1))
                     (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ c1 1) c2)))
                (for/fold ([acc out]) ([c (in-range (+ c1 1) c2)])
                  (set-cell acc r c 3))
                out))
          out))))

title: Missing L Corner
written_solution: Inspect every 2×2 block. Whenever three cells are yellow(4) and the fourth cell is black(0), turn the missing corner into maroon(9). The original yellow(4)s stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
          (vals (list (at g r c) (at g r (+ c 1)) (at g (+ r 1) c) (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))))
      (if (and (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 4)) vals) 3)
               (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 0)) vals) 1))
          (let ((p (nth cells (let loop ([xs vals] [i 0])
                                (if (= (first xs) 0) i (loop (rest xs) (+ i 1)))))))
            (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 9))
          out))))

title: Plus Center Insert
written_solution: Any black(0) cell whose four orthogonal neighbors are all blue(1) becomes cyan(8). The surrounding blue(1) cells remain blue(1), and every other cell stays the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
             (= (at g (- r 1) c) 1)
             (= (at g (+ r 1) c) 1)
             (= (at g r (- c 1)) 1)
             (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 1))
        (set-cell out r c 8)
        out)))

title: Directed Pair Extension
written_solution: Scan each row for the pattern `2,3,0` in consecutive cells. When that exact left-to-right pattern appears, replace the trailing 0 with cyan(8). Other arrangements, including `3,2`, do not change.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 2))])
    (if (and (= (at g r c) 2) (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 3) (= (at g r (+ c 2)) 0))
        (set-cell out r (+ c 2) 8)
        out)))

title: Vertical Span Fill
written_solution: Look at each column separately. If a column has exactly two orange(7)s, fill every black(0) strictly between those two orange(7)s with yellow(4). Keep the orange(7)s themselves unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((rows-hit (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))] #:when (= (at g r c) 7)) r)))
      (if (= (length rows-hit) 2)
          (let ((r1 (first rows-hit)) (r2 (second rows-hit)))
            (if (and (> r2 (+ r1 1))
                     (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ r1 1) r2)))
                (for/fold ([acc out]) ([r (in-range (+ r1 1) r2)])
                  (set-cell acc r c 4))
                out))
          out))))

title: Midpoint Marker
written_solution: For each row with exactly two 8s, find the midpoint between them when it lands on a single cell. If that midpoint cell is 0, change it to red(2). The two 8 endpoints remain 8.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (let ((cols-hit (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))] #:when (= (at g r c) 8)) c)))
      (if (= (length cols-hit) 2)
          (let ((c1 (first cols-hit)) (c2 (second cols-hit)))
            (if (= (modulo (+ c1 c2) 2) 0)
                (let ((mid (quotient (+ c1 c2) 2)))
                  (if (= (at g r mid) 0) (set-cell out r mid 2) out))
                out))
          out))))

title: Crop the Smallest Object
written_solution: Find all connected nonzero objects. Choose the one with the fewest cells, then output only its tight bounding-box crop, preserving its original color pattern.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((chosen
          (first
            (sort (objects g 0)
              (lambda (a b)
                (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                      [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                      [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Seeded Frame Interior Fill
written_solution: Locate every hollow rectangular frame made of 1s. If a frame contains at least one 2 inside it, fill its interior 0-cells with green(3) while leaving the border 1s and any 2 seeds unchanged. Frames without a seed stay untouched.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define (has-seed? obj)
      (any? (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 2))
            (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                               (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (if (has-seed? frame)
          (for*/fold ([acc out])
                     ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                      [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
            (if (= (at acc r c) 0) (set-cell acc r c 3) acc))
          out))))

title: Mirror Inside the Frame
written_solution: Inside each blue(1) frame, take every yellow(4) cell and reflect it across the frame’s vertical axis. Put an orange(7) at the mirrored location when that location is empty. Keep the original yellow(4)s and the frame itself.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                  [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
        (if (= (at g r c) 4)
            (let ((mc (- (+ (obj-c1 frame) (obj-c2 frame)) c)))
              (if (and (> mc (obj-c1 frame)) (< mc (obj-c2 frame)) (= (at acc r mc) 0))
                  (set-cell acc r mc 7)
                  acc))
            acc)))))

title: Marker-Selected Object Crop
written_solution: the unique nonzero marker in the top row tells you the target color. Among the larger objects in the main field, select the object of that same color and output its tight bounding-box crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((marker (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (top-row g))))
         (chosen (first
                  (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) marker) (> (obj-size obj) 1)))
                                (objects g 0))
                        (lambda (a b)
                          (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                              (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                              (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Bounding Box Outline
written_solution: For each connected object of magenta(6), compute its tight bbox and draw that box’s border in red(2). Everything else remains unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)))])
    (let ((cells (append
                   (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
                   (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
                   (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj))))))
      (paint-cells out cells 2))))

title: Recolor Only the Enclosed Cells
written_solution: Any cell of red(2) that lies strictly inside a rectangular 1-frame becomes yellow(4). Cells of red(2) outside all frames do not change.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define frames (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (define (inside-frame? r c frame)
      (and (> r (obj-r1 frame)) (< r (obj-r2 frame))
           (> c (obj-c1 frame)) (< c (obj-c2 frame))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 2)
               (not (eq? (find-first (lambda (frame) (inside-frame? r c frame)) frames) #f)))
          (set-cell out r c 4)
          out))))

title: Crop the Vertically Symmetric Object
written_solution: Find all connected nonzero objects and take each one’s tight crop. Choose the object whose crop is vertically symmetric, then output that crop by itself.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (symmetric-crop? obj)
      (let ((crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
        (all? (lambda (r)
                (all? (lambda (c) (= (at crop r c) (at crop r (- (cols crop) 1 c))))
                      (range 0 (cols crop))))
              (range 0 (rows crop)))))
    (let ((chosen (first (sort (filter symmetric-crop? (objects g 0))
                               (lambda (a b)
                                 (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                     (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                                     (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))))
      (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen)))))

title: Pack Components by Area
written_solution: Extract every connected nonzero object and crop it tightly. Sort the crops by decreasing cell count, then place them left-to-right in a new grid, top-aligned, with a single zero column separating neighboring crops.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define sorted-objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
        (lambda (a b)
          (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
    (define crops (map (lambda (o) (subgrid g (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o))) sorted-objs))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let loop ([out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)] [remaining crops] [left 0])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let ((crop (first remaining)))
            (loop (for*/fold ([acc out])
                              ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                               [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                    (set-cell acc r (+ left c) (at crop r c)))
                  (rest remaining)
                  (+ left (cols crop) 1)))))))

title: Two-Row Legend Recolor
written_solution: Use the first two rows as a legend: each non-background color in row 0 maps to the color directly beneath it in row 1. Remove those two legend rows, and recolor the remaining grid according to that mapping.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    ;; Read each aligned nonzero cell pair in the first two rows as source -> destination.
    (define mapping
      (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))]
                 #:when (and (not (= (at g 0 c) 0))
                             (not (= (at g 1 c) 0))))
        (list (at g 0 c) (at g 1 c))))
    ;; Apply one lookup only; any body color absent from the source row stays unchanged.
    (define (mapped v)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (p) (= (first p) v)) mapping)))
        (if (eq? hit #f) v (second hit))))
    ;; Drop the two legend rows and recolor the remaining cells.
    (grid-from-fn (- (rows g) 2) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c) (mapped (at g (+ r 2) c))))))

title: Quadrant Pack by Color
written_solution: Crop the four colored objects tightly and order them by increasing color value. Place the first two crops in the top row of a new 2×2 arrangement and the next two in the bottom row, using a single zero row and a single zero column as separators.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b)))))
    (define crops (map (lambda (o) (subgrid g (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o))) objs))
    (define tl (first crops))
    (define tr (second crops))
    (define bl (third crops))
    (define br (fourth crops))
    (define row0 (max (rows tl) (rows tr)))
    (define row1 (max (rows bl) (rows br)))
    (define col0 (max (cols tl) (cols bl)))
    (define col1 (max (cols tr) (cols br)))
    (define out (empty-grid (+ row0 1 row1) (+ col0 1 col1) 0))
    (define (paste-all grid crop r0 c0)
      (for*/fold ([acc grid])
                 ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                  [c (in-range (cols crop))])
        (set-cell acc (+ r0 r) (+ c0 c) (at crop r c))))
    (paste-all
      (paste-all
        (paste-all
          (paste-all out tl 0 0)
          tr 0 (+ col0 1))
        bl (+ row0 1) 0)
      br (+ row0 1) (+ col0 1))))

title: Stencil Transfer to the Solid Canvas
written_solution: Take the tight crop of the green(3) exemplar as a binary mask. Find the solid cyan(8) rectangle with the same dimensions, and keep only those 8-cells whose positions match nonzero cells in the exemplar mask. Everything else in that canvas becomes 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define proto (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 3)) (objects g 0))))
    (define proto-crop (subgrid g (obj-r1 proto) (obj-c1 proto) (obj-r2 proto) (obj-c2 proto)))
    (define canvas
      (find-first
        (lambda (obj)
          (and (= (obj-color obj) 8)
               (= (obj-h obj) (rows proto-crop))
               (= (obj-w obj) (cols proto-crop))
               (= (obj-size obj) (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))))
        (objects g 0)))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows proto-crop))]
                [c (in-range (cols proto-crop))])
      (set-cell out (+ (obj-r1 canvas) r) (+ (obj-c1 canvas) c)
                (if (= (at proto-crop r c) 3) 8 0)))))

title: Vector Overlap Highlight
written_solution: The vector from the unique 8 to the unique 9 is the movement rule. translate every 3-cell by that vector, and whenever a shifted 3 lands on a 4-cell, mark that landing cell with orange(7) in an otherwise empty output grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((p8 (first (find-color g 8)))
         (p9 (first (find-color g 9)))
         (dr (- (first p9) (first p8)))
         (dc (- (second p9) (second p8))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 3))])
      (let ((rr (+ (first p) dr))
            (cc (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (and (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at g rr cc) 4))
            (set-cell out rr cc 7)

title: Select the Seed-Rich Frame

written_solution: Count the orange(7)s on the top row to choose the 1st, 2nd, or 3rd object by area rank. Use the corner maroon(9) to choose the rotation (same convention as medium_n06). Then place the transformed chosen object centered inside the cyan(8) frame and clear everything else.

(rule!
 ;; A maroon(9) corner picks a rotation (TL none, TR cw, BR 180, BL ccw)
 ;; and the count of orange(7) marks on the top row picks a rank (1-3).
 ;; Strip those marks, find the largest hollow cyan(8) frame, rank the
 ;; other objects by size (ties: bbox order), and place the rank-th
 ;; smallest — rotated — centered inside the frame on a blank canvas.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define code
       (cond ((= (at g 0 0) 9) 0)
             ((= (at g 0 (- w 1)) 9) 1)
             ((= (at g (- h 1) (- w 1)) 9) 2)
             ((= (at g (- h 1) 0) 9) 3)
             (else 0)))
     (define rank
       (max 1 (min 3 (count-if (lambda (c) (= (at g 0 c) 7))
                               (range 0 w)))))
     (define clean  ;; drop the corner 9s and the top-row 7s
       (for/fold ((out g))
                 ((p (in-list (cons (list 0 0)
                                    (cons (list 0 (- w 1))
                                          (cons (list (- h 1) 0)
                                                (cons (list (- h 1) (- w 1))
                                                      (for/list ((c (in-range w)))
                                                        (list 0 c)))))))))
         (let ((v (at out (first p) (second p))))
           (if (or (and (= v 9) (or (= (first p) 0) (= (first p) (- h 1)))
                        (or (= (second p) 0) (= (second p) (- w 1))))

            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define frame
       (pick-max (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 8) (frame? o)))
                         (objects clean 0))
                 (lambda (o) (* (- (obj-h o) 2) (- (obj-w o) 2)))))
     (define scene (erase-cells clean (obj-cells frame) 0))
     (define comps
       (sort (filter (lambda (o)
                       (not (member? (obj-color o) (list 7 8 9))))
                     (objects scene 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                   (let loop ((xs (list (obj-r1 a) (obj-c1 a)
                                        (obj-r2 a) (obj-c2 a)))
                              (ys (list (obj-r1 b) (obj-c1 b)
                                        (obj-r2 b) (obj-c2 b))))
                     (cond ((empty? xs) #f)
                           ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
                           ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
                           (else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys)))))
                   (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
     (define chosen (list-ref comps (- rank 1)))
     (define sub
       (let ((raw (subgrid scene (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen)
                           (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))
         (cond ((= code 1) (rotate-cw raw))
               ((= code 2) (rotate-180 raw))
               ((= code 3) (rotate-ccw raw))
               (else raw))))
     (let ((sr (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1
                  (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-h frame) 2 (rows sub)) 2))))
           (sc (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1
                  (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-w frame) 2 (cols sub)) 2)))))
       (for*/fold ((acc (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0)
                                     (obj-cells frame) 8)))
                  ((r (in-range (rows sub))) (c (in-range (cols sub))))
         (let ((v (at sub r c)))
           (if (and (> v 0)
                    (< (+ sr r) (obj-r2 frame))
                    (< (+ sc c) (obj-c2 frame)))
               (set-cell acc (+ sr r) (+ sc c) v)
               acc)))))))
