title: Decode a Ferrers shape from row and column headers
written_solution: The bottom-left quadrant contains green(3) bars indicating row lengths. Output a quarter-size grid where each row begins with that many cyan(8) cells, padded with background.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Quadrant histogram: for each bottom-left-quadrant row, count its
 ;; green(3)s and draw a left-aligned cyan(8) bar of that length.
 (let ((h2 (quotient h 2)) (w2 (quotient w 2)))
   (grid-from-fn h2 w2 (lambda (r c)
     (let ((len (count-where (lambda (cc) (= (at g (+ h2 r) cc) 3))
                             (range 0 w2))))
       (if (< c len) 8 0))))))

title: Assign each object to the frame with matching area
written_solution: Each non-frame object must move into the cyan(8) frame whose interior area matches that object’s area. Center the object inside its matched frame and clear the originals.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Hollow cyan(8) frames and loose objects share the canvas. Each
 ;; object belongs in the frame whose interior AREA equals the object's
 ;; cell count. Redraw the frames on a blank canvas and paste each
 ;; object centered inside its matching frame (frames claim objects in
 ;; ascending area order; ties by position).
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (frame? o)  ;; hollow rectangle outline, at least 3x3
       (and (>= (obj-h o) 3) (>= (obj-w o) 3)
            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define (area-of fr) (* (- (obj-h fr) 2) (- (obj-w fr) 2)))
     (define (bbox< a b)
       (let loop ((xs (list (obj-r1 a) (obj-c1 a) (obj-r2 a) (obj-c2 a)))
                  (ys (list (obj-r1 b) (obj-c1 b) (obj-r2 b) (obj-c2 b))))
         (cond ((empty? xs) #f)
               ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
               ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
               (else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys))))))
     (define frames
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 8) (frame? o)))
                     (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (if (= (area-of a) (area-of b))
                   (bbox< a b)
                   (< (area-of a) (area-of b))))))
     (define scene (erase-cells g (flatmap obj-cells frames) 0))
     (define objs
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) 8)))
                     (objects scene 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                   (bbox< a b)
                   (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
     (define (paste-centered out o fr)
       (let* ((sub (subgrid scene (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o)
                            (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o)))
              (sr (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1
                     (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-h fr) 2 (rows sub)) 2))))
              (sc (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1
                     (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-w fr) 2 (cols sub)) 2)))))
         (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((r (in-range (rows sub)))
                                 (c (in-range (cols sub))))
           (let ((v (at sub r c)))
             (if (and (> v 0)
                      (< (+ sr r) (obj-r2 fr))
                      (< (+ sc c) (obj-c2 fr)))
                 (set-cell acc (+ sr r) (+ sc c) v)
                 acc)))))
     (let loop ((frs frames) (avail objs)
                (out (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0)
                                  (flatmap obj-cells frames) 8)))
       (if (empty? frs)
           out
           (let* ((fr (first frs))
                  (cand (find-first (lambda (o)
                                      (= (obj-size o) (area-of fr)))
                                    avail)))
             (if cand
                 (loop (rest frs)
                       (filter (lambda (o) (not (equal? o cand))) avail)
                       (paste-centered out cand fr))
                 (loop (rest frs) avail out))))))))

title: Complete red L-triominoes into green 2x2 squares
written_solution: Find every red(2) component that is an L-triomino: exactly 3 cells whose bbox is 2x2. Replace that whole 2x2 box with green(3). Leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      (lambda (obj)
        (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
               (height (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
               (width (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)))
          (if (and (= (obj-color obj) 2)
                   (= (obj-size obj) 3)
                   (= height 2)
                   (= width 2))
              (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))
              (list))))
      (objects g 0))
    3))

title: Turn diagonal blue pairs into cyan 2x2 blocks
written_solution: Look at every 2x2 window. If it contains blue(1) on one diagonal and black(0) on the other diagonal, recolor all four cells of that 2x2 block to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (any?
            (lambda (p)
              (let ((r0 (fst p))
                    (c0 (snd p)))
                (and (>= r0 0) (< r0 (- h 1))
                     (>= c0 0) (< c0 (- w 1))
                     (or
                       (and (= (cell-at g r0 c0) 1)
                            (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1)) 1)
                            (= (cell-at g r0 (+ c0 1)) 0)
                            (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) c0) 0))
                       (and (= (cell-at g r0 (+ c0 1)) 1)
                            (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) c0) 1)
                            (= (cell-at g r0 c0) 0)
                            (= (cell-at g (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1)) 0))))))
            (list (list r c)
                  (list (- r 1) c)
                  (list r (- c 1))
                  (list (- r 1) (- c 1))))
          8
          (cell-at g r c)))))

title: Extend exact horizontal yellow length-3 lines
written_solution: Find every maximal horizontal yellow(4) run of length exactly 3. Paint the background cell immediately to its left and the background cell immediately to its right magenta(6). Do not change any other yellow(4) segments.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 0)
                 (or
                   (and (< (+ c 3) w)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 2)) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 3)) 4)
                        (or (= (+ c 4) w)
                            (not (= (cell-at g r (+ c 4)) 4))))
                   (and (>= (- c 3) 0)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 1)) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 2)) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 3)) 4)
                        (or (< (- c 4) 0)
                            (not (= (cell-at g r (- c 4)) 4))))))
            6
            v)))))

title: Recolor blue components touching only the top border
written_solution: Inspect each blue(1) component. If it touches the top border and touches no other border, recolor the whole component green(3). Leave all other blue(1) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      (lambda (obj)
        (let ((cells (obj-cells obj)))
          (if (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
                   (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) cells)
                   (not (any?
                          (lambda (p)
                            (or (= (fst p) (- h 1))
                                (= (snd p) 0)
                                (= (snd p) (- w 1))))
                          cells)))
              cells
              (list))))
      (objects g 0))
    3))

title: Mirror the orange object across the magenta divider
written_solution: Find the full-height magenta(6) divider column. Mirror the orange(7) object across that column and draw the reflected copy in cyan(8) on the other side. Keep the original object and divider.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((axis
          (find-first
            (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 6)) (range h)))
            (range w))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
               (src-c (if axis (- (* 2 axis) c) c))
               (src-v (if (and axis (in-bounds? r src-c h w)) (cell-at g r src-c) 0)))
          (cond
            [(not axis) v]
            [(not (= v 0)) v]
            [(and (> c axis) (< src-c axis) (= src-v 7)) 8]
            [else 0]))))))

title: Extract the smallest connected object
written_solution: Among all non-black(0) connected components, find the one with the fewest cells. Output just that object cropped to its bbox, preserving its shape and color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (objects g 0))
         (smallest
           (first
             (sort objs
               (lambda (a b)
                 (let ((sa (obj-size a))
                       (sb (obj-size b))
                       (ba (obj-bbox a))
                       (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                   (or (< sa sb)
                       (and (= sa sb)
                            (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                                (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                                     (or (< (second ba) (second bb))
                                         (and (= (second ba) (second bb))
                                              (or (< (third ba) (third bb))
                                                  (and (= (third ba) (third bb))
                                                       (< (fourth ba) (fourth bb)))))))))))))))
         (bb (obj-bbox smallest)))
    (crop g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Expand singleton red markers into yellow crosses
written_solution: Find every red(2) component of size 1. Replace that lone cell and its four cardinal neighbors with yellow(4), forming a plus sign. Leave larger red(2) components unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      (lambda (obj)
        (if (and (= (obj-color obj) 2) (= (obj-size obj) 1))
            (let* ((p (first (obj-cells obj)))
                   (r (fst p))
                   (c (snd p)))
              (list (list r c)
                    (list (- r 1) c)
                    (list (+ r 1) c)
                    (list r (- c 1))
                    (list r (+ c 1))))
            (list)))
      (objects g 0))
    4))

title: Draw rectangle perimeters from same-colored corner pairs
written_solution: For every color that appears exactly twice, treat those two cells as opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Draw the full perimeter of that rectangle in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-color? color colors)
      (any? (lambda (v) (= v color)) colors))
    (define (color-order remaining acc)
      (if (empty? remaining)
          (reverse acc)
          (let ((v (third (first remaining))))
            (if (or (= v 0) (has-color? v acc))
                (color-order (cdr remaining) acc)
                (color-order (cdr remaining) (cons v acc))))))
    (paint-cells
      g
      (flatmap
        (lambda (color)
          (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
            (if (= (length cells) 2)
                (let* ((a (first cells))
                       (b (second cells))
                       (r1 (fst a))
                       (c1 (snd a))
                       (r2 (fst b))
                       (c2 (snd b))
                       (rmin (min r1 r2))
                       (rmax (max r1 r2))
                       (cmin (min c1 c2))
                       (cmax (max c1 c2)))
                  (if (and (not (= r1 r2)) (not (= c1 c2)))
                      (append
                        (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c color)) (range cmin (+ cmax 1)))
                        (map (lambda (c) (list r2 c color)) (range cmin (+ cmax 1)))
                        (map (lambda (r) (list r c1 color)) (range rmin (+ rmax 1)))
                        (map (lambda (r) (list r c2 color)) (range rmin (+ rmax 1))))
                      (list)))
                (list))))
        (color-order (grid-cells g) (list))))))

title: Rotate the smallest green object onto the target anchor
written_solution: Find the smallest green(3) connected object. The control color in the upper-left corner tells how much to rotate it: 2→0°, 4→90°, 5→180°, 6→270°. Stamp the rotated copy in cyan(8) with its top-left aligned to the maroon(9) anchor cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((control-cell
           (find-first
             (lambda (p)
               (let ((v (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))))
                 (or (= v 2) (= v 4) (= v 5) (= v 6))))
             (grid-positions g)))
         (control (cell-at g (fst control-cell) (snd control-cell)))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
         (greens
           (sort
             (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 3)) (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (let ((sa (obj-size a))
                     (sb (obj-size b))
                     (ba (obj-bbox a))
                     (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                 (or (< sa sb)
                     (and (= sa sb)
                          (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                              (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                                   (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))))
         (base (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first greens))))
         (rot1 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw base)))
         (rot2 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw rot1)))
         (rot3 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw rot2)))
         (shape
           (cond
             [(= control 2) base]
             [(= control 4) rot1]
             [(= control 5) rot2]
             [else rot3])))
    (stamp-normalized-cells g shape (fst anchor) (snd anchor) 8)))

title: Fill chambers containing exactly two red seeds
written_solution: Treat gray(5) cells as walls. In each enclosed chamber, count the red(2) seed cells. If a chamber contains exactly two seeds, fill all its remaining black(0) cells with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (= v 0)
            (let* ((region
                     (connected-region
                       g r c
                       (lambda (rr cc val) (not (= val 5)))
                       4))
                   (seed-count
                     (count-where
                       (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 2))
                       region)))
              (if (= seed-count 2) 8 0))
            v)))))

title: Rank blue objects by size
written_solution: There are exactly three blue(1) objects of different sizes. Recolor the smallest one red(2), the middle one green(3), and the largest one cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((blues
           (sort
             (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (let ((sa (obj-size a))
                     (sb (obj-size b))
                     (ba (obj-bbox a))
                     (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                 (or (< sa sb)
                     (and (= sa sb)
                          (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                              (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                                   (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))))
         (small (first blues))
         (mid (second blues))
         (large (third blues)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (cond
            [(any? (lambda (p) (and (= r (fst p)) (= c (snd p)))) (obj-cells small)) 2]
            [(any? (lambda (p) (and (= r (fst p)) (= c (snd p)))) (obj-cells mid)) 3]
            [(any? (lambda (p) (and (= r (fst p)) (= c (snd p)))) (obj-cells large)) 8]
            [else v]))))))

title: Cross selected rows and columns inside a frame
written_solution: Find the rectangular frame. Red(2) marks on its left edge select interior rows; blue(1) marks on its top edge select interior columns. Fill every selected row/column intersection inside the frame with green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((marker-cells
           (filter
             (lambda (p)
               (let ((v (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))))
                 (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 4))))
             (grid-positions g)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells marker-cells))
         (r0 (first bb))
         (c0 (second bb))
         (r1 (third bb))
         (c1 (fourth bb))
         (rows
           (filter
             (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c0) 2))
             (range (+ r0 1) r1)))
         (cols
           (filter
             (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r0 c) 1))
             (range (+ c0 1) c1))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (member? r rows) (member? c cols))
            3
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Output the normalized XOR of two shapes
written_solution: Take the normalized shape of the blue(1) object and the normalized shape of the red(2) object. Compute their symmetric difference (cells in exactly one of the two shapes) and output that result alone in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-cell? cell cells)
      (any?
        (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (fst cell)) (= (snd p) (snd cell))))
        cells))
    (define (render cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (list (list 0))
          (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
                 (out-h (+ (max-list (map fst norm)) 1))
                 (out-w (+ (max-list (map snd norm)) 1)))
            (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
              (lambda (r c)
                (if (has-cell? (list r c) norm) 8 0))))))
    (let* ((s1 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))))
           (s2 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
           (xor-cells
             (append
               (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p s2))) s1)
               (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p s1))) s2))))
      (render xor-cells))))

title: Draw the shortest path from start to goal
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls. Find the shortest orthogonal path from the red(2) start cell 2 to the green(3) goal cell 3 and draw the interior of that path in cyan(8). Keep the endpoints unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (parent-of p parents)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (entry) (same-pos? p (first entry))) parents)))
        (if hit (second hit) #f)))
    (define (reconstruct goal parents)
      (let loop ((cur goal) (acc (list)))
        (let ((prev (parent-of cur parents)))
          (if prev
              (loop prev (cons cur acc))
              (cons cur acc)))))
    (define (shortest-path start goal)
      (let loop ((visited (list))
                 (queue (list start))
                 (parents (list (list start #f))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            (list)
            (let ((cur (first queue))
                  (restq (cdr queue)))
              (cond
                [(pos-in? cur visited) (loop visited restq parents)]
                [(same-pos? cur goal) (reconstruct goal parents)]
                [else
                 (let* ((new-visited (cons cur visited))
                        (r (fst cur))
                        (c (snd cur))
                        (neighbors
                          (filter
                            (lambda (n)
                              (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
                                (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                     (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                     (not (pos-in? n new-visited))
                                     (not (pos-in? n restq)))))
                            (map
                              (lambda (d) (list (+ r (fst d)) (+ c (snd d))))
                              cardinal-deltas))))
                   (loop new-visited
                         (append restq neighbors)
                         (append parents (map (lambda (n) (list n cur)) neighbors))))])))))
    (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
           (goal (first (find-color g 3)))
           (path (shortest-path start goal))
           (interior
             (filter
               (lambda (p) (not (or (same-pos? p start) (same-pos? p goal))))
               path)))
      (paint-cells g interior 8))))

title: Apply a control-selected dihedral transform to the template
written_solution: Read the two control cells in the upper-left corner. The first control chooses reflection: 2→none, 3→horizontal mirror. The second chooses rotation: 4→0°, 5→90°, 6→180°, 7→270°. Apply that combined transform to the blue(1) template and stamp the result in cyan(8) at the maroon(9) anchor.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((reflect-cell
           (find-first
             (lambda (p)
               (let ((v (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))))
                 (or (= v 2) (= v 3))))
             (grid-positions g)))
         (rotate-cell
           (find-first
             (lambda (p)
               (let ((v (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))))
                 (or (= v 4) (= v 5) (= v 6) (= v 7))))
             (grid-positions g)))
         (anchor (first (find-color g 9)))
         (template (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))
         (reflect-code (cell-at g (fst reflect-cell) (snd reflect-cell)))
         (rotate-code (cell-at g (fst rotate-cell) (snd rotate-cell)))
         (base (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)))
         (reflected (if (= reflect-code 3) (normalize-cells (flip-cells-lr base)) base))
         (rot1 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw reflected)))
         (rot2 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw rot1)))
         (rot3 (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw rot2)))
         (shape
           (cond
             [(= rotate-code 4) reflected]
             [(= rotate-code 5) rot1]
             [(= rotate-code 6) rot2]
             [else rot3])))
    (stamp-normalized-cells g shape (fst anchor) (snd anchor) 8)))

title: Route a path through ordered checkpoints
written_solution: Treat gray(5) as walls. Find a shortest path from red(2) to green(3), then from green(3) to yellow(4), then from yellow(4) to orange(7). Draw the interior cells of all three path segments in cyan(8), preserving the checkpoint markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (parent-of p parents)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (entry) (same-pos? p (first entry))) parents)))
        (if hit (second hit) #f)))
    (define (reconstruct goal parents)
      (let loop ((cur goal) (acc (list)))
        (let ((prev (parent-of cur parents)))
          (if prev
              (loop prev (cons cur acc))
              (cons cur acc)))))
    (define (shortest-path start goal)
      (let loop ((visited (list))
                 (queue (list start))
                 (parents (list (list start #f))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            (list)
            (let ((cur (first queue))
                  (restq (cdr queue)))
              (cond
                [(pos-in? cur visited) (loop visited restq parents)]
                [(same-pos? cur goal) (reconstruct goal parents)]
                [else
                 (let* ((new-visited (cons cur visited))
                        (r (fst cur))
                        (c (snd cur))
                        (neighbors
                          (filter
                            (lambda (n)
                              (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
                                (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                     (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                     (not (pos-in? n new-visited))
                                     (not (pos-in? n restq)))))
                            (map
                              (lambda (d) (list (+ r (fst d)) (+ c (snd d))))
                              cardinal-deltas))))
                   (loop new-visited
                         (append restq neighbors)
                         (append parents (map (lambda (n) (list n cur)) neighbors))))])))))
    (define (interior path start goal)
      (filter
        (lambda (p) (not (or (same-pos? p start) (same-pos? p goal))))
        path))
    (let* ((p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
           (p3 (first (find-color g 3)))
           (p4 (first (find-color g 4)))
           (p7 (first (find-color g 7)))
           (segments (list (list p2 p3) (list p3 p4) (list p4 p7)))
           (path-cells
             (flatmap
               (lambda (seg)
                 (let* ((start (first seg))
                        (goal (second seg))
                        (path (shortest-path start goal)))
                   (if (empty? path) (list) (interior path start goal))))
               segments)))
      (paint-cells g path-cells 8))))

title: Voronoi-fill open cells by nearest seed through walls
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. For every open cell, compare its shortest-path distance to the nearest red(2) seed 2 and the nearest green(3) seed 3. Fill the cell with whichever seed color is strictly closer; leave ties and seedless chambers black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (distance-to sr sc target-color)
      (let loop ((visited (list))
                 (queue (list (list sr sc 0))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            999
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (r (first cur))
                   (c (second cur))
                   (d (third cur))
                   (pos (list r c)))
              (cond
                [(pos-in? pos visited) (loop visited restq)]
                [(= (cell-at g r c) target-color) d]
                [else
                 (let* ((new-visited (cons pos visited))
                        (neighbors
                          (filter
                            (lambda (n)
                              (let ((nr (first n)) (nc (second n)))
                                (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                     (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                     (not (pos-in? (list nr nc) new-visited)))))
                            (map
                              (lambda (delta)
                                (list (+ r (fst delta)) (+ c (snd delta)) (+ d 1)))
                              cardinal-deltas))))
                   (loop new-visited (append restq neighbors)))])))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (= v 0)
              (let ((d2 (distance-to r c 2))
                    (d3 (distance-to r c 3)))
                (cond
                  [(< d2 d3) 2]
                  [(< d3 d2) 3]
                  [else 0]))
              v))))))

title: Fill the band selected by nested-frame depth
written_solution: Count the red(2) markers in the top row; that count is k. Find the k-th rectangular frame from the outside. Fill the region inside that frame but outside the next inner frame with cyan(8). If k points to the innermost frame, fill its central interior instead.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames
           (sort
             (filter
               (lambda (obj)
                 ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of obj
                 (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                        ;; Top edge (row r1)
                        (r0 (first bb))
                        ;; Left edge (col c1)
                        (c0 (second bb))
                        ;; Bottom edge (row r2)
                        (r1 (third bb))
                        ;; Right edge (col c2)
                        (c1 (fourth bb))
                        ;; Bbox height (rows)
                        (height (+ (- r1 r0) 1))
                        ;; Bbox width (cols)
                        (width (+ (- c1 c0) 1))
                        (perimeter (- (+ (* 2 height) (* 2 width)) 4)))
                   (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)
                        (= (obj-size obj) perimeter)
                        (all?
                          (lambda (p)
                            (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                              (= (cell-at g pr pc) 4)))
                          (filter
                            (lambda (p)
                              (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                                (or (= pr r0) (= pr r1) (= pc c0) (= pc c1))))
                            (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))))))
               (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of a
               (let* ((ba (obj-bbox a))
                      ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of b
                      (bb (obj-bbox b))
                      (aa (* (+ (- (third ba) (first ba)) 1)
                             (+ (- (fourth ba) (second ba)) 1)))
                      (ab (* (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                             (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))))
                 (> aa ab)))))
         (raw-k (count-where (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g 0 c) 2)) (range w)))
         (k (max 1 (min raw-k (length frames))))
         (target (nth frames (- k 1)))
         (inner (if (< k (length frames)) (nth frames k) #f))
         ;; Bounding box (r1 c1 r2 c2) of target
         (tb (obj-bbox target))
         (ib (if inner (obj-bbox inner) (list -1 -1 -1 -1))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (= v 0)
                   (> r (first tb)) (< r (third tb))
                   (> c (second tb)) (< c (fourth tb))
                   (not (and inner
                             (> r (first ib)) (< r (third ib))
                             (> c (second ib)) (< c (fourth ib)))))
              8
              v))))))

title: Scale the unique shape class
written_solution: Look only at the blue(1) objects. Several share the same normalized shape, but one normalized shape appears exactly once. Take that unique shape, scale it by a factor of 2, and output it alone in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-cell? cell cells)
      (any?
        (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (fst cell)) (= (snd p) (snd cell))))
        cells))
    (let* ((objs (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0)))
           (target
             (find-first
               (lambda (obj)
                 (= (count-where (lambda (other) (same-shape? obj other)) objs) 1))
               objs)))
      (if target
          (let* ((cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells target)))
                 (scaled
                   (flatmap
                     (lambda (p)
                       (let ((r (* 2 (fst p)))
                             (c (* 2 (snd p))))
                         (list (list r c)
                               (list (+ r 1) c)
                               (list r (+ c 1))
                               (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))))
                     cells))
                 (out-h (+ (max-list (map fst scaled)) 1))
                 (out-w (+ (max-list (map snd scaled)) 1)))
            (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
              (lambda (r c)
                (if (has-cell? (list r c) scaled) 8 0))))
          (list (list 0))))))

title: Apply a control-selected boolean operation to two shapes
written_solution: The control cell chooses a boolean operation on the normalized blue(1) and red(2) shapes: 3→union, 4→intersection, 6→XOR, 7→shape1 minus shape2. Compute that set operation and output the result alone in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-cell? cell cells)
      (any?
        (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (fst cell)) (= (snd p) (snd cell))))
        cells))
    (define (render cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (list (list 0))
          (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
                 (out-h (+ (max-list (map fst norm)) 1))
                 (out-w (+ (max-list (map snd norm)) 1)))
            (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
              (lambda (r c)
                (if (has-cell? (list r c) norm) 8 0))))))
    (let* ((control-cell
             (find-first
               (lambda (p)
                 (let ((v (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p))))
                   (or (= v 3) (= v 4) (= v 6) (= v 7))))
               (grid-positions g)))
           (control (cell-at g (fst control-cell) (snd control-cell)))
           (s1 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))))
           (s2 (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))))
           (result
             (cond
               [(= control 3) (append s1 s2)]
               [(= control 4) (filter (lambda (p) (has-cell? p s2)) s1)]
               [(= control 6)
                (append
                  (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p s2))) s1)
                  (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p s1))) s2))]
               [else (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p s2))) s1)])))
      (render result))))

title: Fill each chamber with the legend color of its majority seed
written_solution: Read the legend in the top two rows: each seed blue(1), 2, or 3 maps to a fill color directly below it. Then examine each chamber below the legend. If one seed color is the strict majority in that chamber, fill the chamber’s black(0) cells with the mapped legend color for that majority seed. Leave tied chambers unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (legend-color seed)
      (let ((hit
              (find-first
                (lambda (c)
                  (and (= (cell-at g 0 c) seed)
                       (not (= (cell-at g 1 c) 0))))
                (range w))))
        (if hit (cell-at g 1 hit) 8)))
    (define (strict-majority c1 c2 c3)
      (cond
        [(and (> c1 c2) (> c1 c3)) 1]
        [(and (> c2 c1) (> c2 c3)) 2]
        [(and (> c3 c1) (> c3 c2)) 3]
        [else 0]))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (>= r 2) (= v 0))
              (let* ((region
                       (connected-region
                         g r c
                         (lambda (rr cc val) (and (>= rr 2) (not (= val 5))))
                         4))
                     (c1 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 1)) region))
                     (c2 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 2)) region))
                     (c3 (count-where (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 3)) region))
                     (maj (strict-majority c1 c2 c3)))
                (if (= maj 0) 0 (legend-color maj)))
              v))))))

title: Diagonal Corner Completion
written_solution: Look at every 2×2 window. If it has green(3) in one diagonal and black(0) in the other diagonal, turn the two empty corner cells into orange(7). Leave the original green(3)s alone.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 0)
                 (or
                   (and (> c 0) (< r (- h 1))
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 1)) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) c) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) (- c 1)) 0))
                   (and (> r 0) (< c (- w 1))
                        (= (cell-at g (- r 1) c) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) 0))
                   (and (< r (- h 1)) (< c (- w 1))
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) c) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)) 0))
                   (and (> r 0) (> c 0)
                        (= (cell-at g (- r 1) c) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 1)) 3)
                        (= (cell-at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) 0))))
            7
            v)))))

title: Diagonal Halo
written_solution: Each green(3) cell acts like a beacon. Keep the green(3) itself, and paint every diagonal neighbor of that green(3) with orange(7) if it is inside the grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 0)
                 (any?
                   (lambda (d)
                     (let ((nr (+ r (fst d)))
                           (nc (+ c (snd d))))
                       (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                            (= (cell-at g nr nc) 3))))
                   diagonal-deltas))
            7
            v)))))

title: One-Gap Completion
written_solution: Fill a black(0) cell with yellow(4) whenever it sits exactly between two 4s in a straight line, either horizontally or vertically. Nothing else changes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 0)
                 (or
                   (and (> c 0) (< c (- w 1))
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 1)) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 4))
                   (and (> r 0) (< r (- h 1))
                        (= (cell-at g (- r 1) c) 4)
                        (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) c) 4))))
            4
            v)))))

title: Bar Caps
written_solution: Every horizontal bar of 6s gets capped by 8s at its open ends. Add one 8 immediately to the left and/or right of the bar if that cell exists and is black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 0)
                 (or
                   (and (< (+ c 2) w)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 1)) 6)
                        (= (cell-at g r (+ c 2)) 6))
                   (and (>= (- c 2) 0)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 1)) 6)
                        (= (cell-at g r (- c 2)) 6))))
            8
            v)))))

title: Solid Square Recolor
written_solution: Whenever a 2×2 area is completely filled with gray(5), recolor those four cells to blue(1). All other cells stay as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ()
    (define (solid-2x2-at? r0 c0)
      (and (>= r0 0) (< r0 (- h 1))
           (>= c0 0) (< c0 (- w 1))
           (= (at g r0 c0) 5)
           (= (at g (+ r0 1) c0) 5)
           (= (at g r0 (+ c0 1)) 5)
           (= (at g (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1)) 5)))
    (define (inside-solid-square? r c)
      (any? (lambda (p) (solid-2x2-at? (first p) (second p)))
            (list (list r c)
                  (list (- r 1) c)
                  (list r (- c 1))
                  (list (- r 1) (- c 1)))))
    (cellmap g (r c v)
      (if (and (= v 5) (inside-solid-square? r c)) 1 v))))

title: Down-Right Shadow
written_solution: Each red(2) casts a one-cell shadow down and to the right. Copy a gray(5) into that down-right cell when it is inside the grid; keep the original red(2)s too.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (cond
          [(not (= v 0)) v]
          [(and (> r 0) (> c 0) (= (cell-at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) 2)) 5]
          [else 0])))))

title: Vertical Middle Highlight
written_solution: Whenever three yellow(4)s form a vertical triplet, change only the middle yellow(4) into maroon(9). The top and bottom yellow(4) remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn h w
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
        (if (and (= v 4)
                 (> r 0) (< r (- h 1))
                 (= (cell-at g (- r 1) c) 4)
                 (= (cell-at g (+ r 1) c) 4))
            9
            v)))))

title: Seeded Frame Fill
written_solution: Find every hollow rectangular frame made of 1. If a frame contains at least one 2 in its interior, fill the entire interior of that frame with yellow(4). Frames without a 2 stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
                      (all?
                        (lambda (p)
                          (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                            (= (cell-at g pr pc) 1)))
                        (filter
                          (lambda (p)
                            (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                              (or (= pr r0) (= pr r1) (= pc c0) (= pc c1))))
                          (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))))))
             (objects g 0)))
         (seeded
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (any?
                   (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 2))
                   (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1)))))
             frames)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (any?
              (lambda (obj)
                (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
                  (and (> r (first bb)) (< r (third bb))
                       (> c (second bb)) (< c (fourth bb)))))
              seeded)
            4
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Largest 3-Component
written_solution: Among all connected components of green(3), identify the largest one. Recolor that one component to cyan(8) and leave every other component untouched.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((comps (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 3)) (objects g 0))))
    (if (empty? comps)
        g
        (let ((largest (first (sort comps (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
          (paint-cells g (obj-cells largest) 8)))))

title: Straight Bridge
written_solution: For any color that appears exactly twice in the grid, if the two cells are aligned in the same row or the same column with only black(0) cells between them, fill the straight path between them with that same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((paths
          (flatmap
            (lambda (color)
              (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
                (if (= (length cells) 2)
                    (let* ((a (first cells))
                           (b (second cells))
                           (r1 (fst a))
                           (c1 (snd a))
                           (r2 (fst b))
                           (c2 (snd b)))
                      (cond
                        [(= r1 r2)
                         (let ((cmin (min c1 c2))
                               (cmax (max c1 c2)))
                           (if (all?
                                 (lambda (c)
                                   (or (= (cell-at g r1 c) 0)
                                       (= c c1)
                                       (= c c2)))
                                 (range cmin (+ cmax 1)))
                               (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c color)) (range cmin (+ cmax 1)))
                               (list)))]
                        [(= c1 c2)
                         (let ((rmin (min r1 r2))
                               (rmax (max r1 r2)))
                           (if (all?
                                 (lambda (r)
                                   (or (= (cell-at g r c1) 0)
                                       (= r r1)
                                       (= r r2)))
                                 (range rmin (+ rmax 1)))
                               (map (lambda (r) (list r c1 color)) (range rmin (+ rmax 1)))
                               (list)))]
                        [else (list)]))
                    (list))))
            (grid-colors g 0))))
    (paint-cells g paths)))

title: Frame Stripe from External Marker
written_solution: Each hollow gray(5) frame may have an orange(7) sitting just outside one side. If the orange(7) is above or below the frame, fill the interior column underneath that marker with green(3). If the orange(7) is left or right of the frame, fill the interior row aligned to that marker with green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((frames
          (filter
            (lambda (obj)
              (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                     (r0 (first bb))
                     (c0 (second bb))
                     (r1 (third bb))
                     (c1 (fourth bb)))
                (and (= (obj-color obj) 5)
                     (all?
                       (lambda (p)
                         (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                           (= (cell-at g pr pc) 5)))
                       (filter
                         (lambda (p)
                           (let ((pr (fst p)) (pc (snd p)))
                             (or (= pr r0) (= pr r1) (= pc c0) (= pc c1))))
                         (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))))))
            (objects g 0))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (any?
                (lambda (obj)
                  (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                         (r0 (first bb))
                         (c0 (second bb))
                         (r1 (third bb))
                         (c1 (fourth bb)))
                    (and (> r r0) (< r r1) (> c c0) (< c c1)
                         (or
                           (and (> r0 0) (= (cell-at g (- r0 1) c) 7))
                           (and (< r1 (- h 1)) (= (cell-at g (+ r1 1) c) 7))
                           (and (> c0 0) (= (cell-at g r (- c0 1)) 7))
                           (and (< c1 (- w 1)) (= (cell-at g r (+ c1 1)) 7))))))
                frames)
              3
              v))))))

title: Vertical Mirror Divider
written_solution: A full column of 9s is a mirror axis. Copy every nonzero, non-9 cell on the left side to its reflected position on the right side, keeping the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((axis
          (find-first
            (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 9)) (range h)))
            (range w))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
               (src-c (if axis (- (* 2 axis) c) c))
               (src-v (if (and axis (in-bounds? r src-c h w)) (cell-at g r src-c) 0)))
          (cond
            [(not axis) v]
            [(not (= v 0)) v]
            [(and (> c axis) (< src-c axis) (not (= src-v 0)) (not (= src-v 9))) src-v]
            [else 0]))))))

title: L-Triomino Filter
written_solution: Look at each component of magenta(6) with exactly three cells. If its bbox is 2×2, then it is an L-shaped triomino, so recolor that whole component to blue(1). Straight triominoes stay magenta(6).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      (lambda (obj)
        (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
               (height (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
               (width (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)))
          (if (and (= (obj-color obj) 6)
                   (= (obj-size obj) 3)
                   (= height 2)
                   (= width 2))
              (obj-cells obj)
              (list))))
      (objects g 0))
    1))

title: Crop the Largest Object
written_solution: Treat each connected nonzero object as a single object even if it uses multiple colors. Select the largest object, then output only its bbox, preserving the colors inside that box.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((regions
           (map
             (lambda (p)
               (connected-region
                 g
                 (fst p)
                 (snd p)
                 (lambda (rr cc v) (not (= v 0)))
                 4))
             (filter
               (lambda (p) (not (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 0)))
               (grid-positions g))))
         (largest
           (if (empty? regions)
               (list)
               (first (sort regions (lambda (a b) (> (length a) (length b))))))))
    (if (empty? largest)
        (list)
        (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells largest)))
          (crop g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))))

title: Translate by Anchor Vector
written_solution: There is one blue(1) marker and one red(2) marker. Compute the displacement vector from blue(1) to red(2). Copy the entire green(3) object by that same displacement, and draw the translated copy in cyan(8) while keeping the original object and both markers.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((p1 (first (find-color g 1)))
         (p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
         (dr (- (fst p2) (fst p1)))
         (dc (- (snd p2) (snd p1))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((sr (- r dr))
               (sc (- c dc))
               (src-v (if (in-bounds? sr sc h w) (cell-at g sr sc) 0))
               (v (cell-at g r c)))
          (cond
            [(or (= v 1) (= v 2)) v]
            [(= src-v 3) 8]
            [(not (= v 0)) v]
            [else 0]))))))

title: Prototype Stamp from Framed Template
written_solution: A blue(1) frame contains the exemplar made of yellow(4)s. Read that interior pattern, then for each orange(7) seed elsewhere in the grid, stamp a copy of the pattern starting at the seed's position. The copied pattern is recolored from yellow(4) to cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
                      (all?
                        (lambda (p)
                          (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                            (= (cell-at g r c) 1)))
                        (filter
                          (lambda (p)
                            (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                              (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))))
                          (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
                      (any?
                        (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 4))
                        (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1))))))
             (objects g 0)))
         (frame (first frames))
         (bb (obj-bbox frame))
         (r0 (first bb))
         (c0 (second bb))
         (r1 (third bb))
         (c1 (fourth bb))
         (pattern
           (map
             (lambda (p) (list (- (fst p) (+ r0 1)) (- (snd p) (+ c0 1))))
             (filter
               (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 4))
               (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1)))))
         (targets
           (flatmap
             (lambda (seed)
               (map
                 (lambda (p) (list (+ (fst seed) (fst p)) (+ (snd seed) (snd p))))
                 pattern))
             (find-color g 7))))
    (paint-cells g targets 8)))

title: Axis-Chooser Reflection
written_solution: A complete line of 9s is the reflection axis. Sometimes it is vertical and sometimes horizontal. Reflect every nonzero, non-9 cell across that axis, keeping the original object and using the same colors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((axis-row
           (find-first
             (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r c) 9)) (range w)))
             (range h)))
         (axis-col
           (find-first
             (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c) 9)) (range h)))
             (range w))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
               (mr (if axis-row (- (* 2 axis-row) r) r))
               (mc (if axis-col (- (* 2 axis-col) c) c))
               (mv (if (in-bounds? mr mc h w) (cell-at g mr mc) 0)))
          (cond
            [(not (= v 0)) v]
            [(and (not (= mv 0)) (not (= mv 9))) mv]
            [else 0]))))))

title: Component Count Bar
written_solution: Count how many connected components of magenta(6) appear in the grid. Starting immediately to the right of the unique 2 marker, draw that many 3s as a horizontal bar. Everything else stays unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((n (count-where (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 6)) (objects g 0)))
         (marker (first (find-color g 2)))
         (mr (fst marker))
         (mc (snd marker)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (= r mr) (> c mc) (<= c (+ mc n)) (= v 0))
              3
              v))))))

title: Smallest and Largest Frame Fill
written_solution: Among all hollow rectangular frames made of 4, compare their interior areas. Fill the smallest frame's interior with red(2) and the largest frame's interior with cyan(8). Any middle-sized frames stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)
                      (all?
                        (lambda (p)
                          (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                            (= (cell-at g r c) 4)))
                        (filter
                          (lambda (p)
                            (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                              (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))))
                          (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))))))
             (objects g 0)))
         (sorted
           (sort frames
             (lambda (a b)
               (let* ((ba (obj-bbox a))
                      (bb (obj-bbox b))
                      (aa (* (- (third ba) (first ba) 1) (- (fourth ba) (second ba) 1)))
                      (ab (* (- (third bb) (first bb) 1) (- (fourth bb) (second bb) 1))))
                 (< aa ab)))))
         (small (first sorted))
         (large (first (reverse sorted)))
         (sb (obj-bbox small))
         (lb (obj-bbox large)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (cond
          [(and (> r (first sb)) (< r (third sb)) (> c (second sb)) (< c (fourth sb))) 2]
          [(and (> r (first lb)) (< r (third lb)) (> c (second lb)) (< c (fourth lb))) 8]
          [else (cell-at g r c)])))))

title: Deepest Seeded Frame
written_solution: Frames are made of 1s. Some may be nested inside others. Fill the interior of a seeded frame with green(3) only if it is the deepest seeded frame in its nesting chain. An outer seeded frame stays unchanged when it contains a smaller seeded frame that is also seeded.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frames
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
                      (all?
                        (lambda (p)
                          (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                            (= (cell-at g r c) 1)))
                        (filter
                          (lambda (p)
                            (let ((r (fst p)) (c (snd p)))
                              (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1))))
                          (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1))))))
             (objects g 0)))
         (seeded
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (any?
                   (lambda (p) (= (cell-at g (fst p) (snd p)) 2))
                   (positions-in-rect (+ r0 1) (+ c0 1) (- r1 1) (- c1 1)))))
             frames))
         (deepest
           (filter
             (lambda (obj)
               (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
                      (r0 (first bb))
                      (c0 (second bb))
                      (r1 (third bb))
                      (c1 (fourth bb)))
                 (not
                   (any?
                     (lambda (other)
                       (let* ((ob (obj-bbox other))
                              (or0 (first ob))
                              (oc0 (second ob))
                              (or1 (third ob))
                              (oc1 (fourth ob)))
                         (and (not (and (= r0 or0) (= c0 oc0) (= r1 or1) (= c1 oc1)))
                              (> or0 r0) (< or1 r1)
                              (> oc0 c0) (< oc1 c1))))
                     seeded))))
             seeded)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (any?
              (lambda (obj)
                (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
                  (and (> r (first bb)) (< r (third bb))
                       (> c (second bb)) (< c (fourth bb)))))
              deepest)
            3
            (cell-at g r c))))))

title: Sorted Component-Size Bars
written_solution: Measure the size of every component of magenta(6) and sort those sizes from largest to smallest. Starting immediately to the right of the unique 2 marker, draw one bar of 3s for each component size, with one black(0) cell separating consecutive bars.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((sizes
           (sort
             (map obj-size (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 6)) (objects g 0)))
             >))
         (bar
           (cdr
             (flatmap
               (lambda (size)
                 (cons 0 (for/list ([i (range size)]) 3)))
               sizes)))
         (marker (first (find-color g 2)))
         (mr (fst marker))
         (mc (snd marker)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((idx (- c mc 1))
              (v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (= r mr) (>= idx 0) (< idx (length bar)) (= (nth bar idx) 3))
              3
              v))))))

title: Slide every red singleton downward
written_solution: Remove the red(2) singletons from the grid, then let each one fall straight down until the next step would hit the border, a blocker, or another settled red(2) cell. Put the red(2) cells back at their landing spots; everything else stays the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define reds
      (sort (find-color g 2)
            (lambda (a b)
              (or (> (first a) (first b))
                  (and (= (first a) (first b)) (> (second a) (second b)))))))
    (define cleared (erase-cells g reds 0))
    (define occupied
      (for/set ([cell (in-list (grid-cells cleared))] #:when (not (= (third cell) 0)))
        (cons (first cell) (second cell))))
    (define (slide-one p occ)
      (let loop ([r (first p)] [c (second p)])
        (let ((nr (+ r 1)))
          (if (or (not (in-bounds? nr c (rows g) (cols g)))
                  (set-member? occ (cons nr c)))
              (list r c)
              (loop nr c)))))
    (let-values ([(out final-occ)
                  (for/fold ([out cleared] [occ occupied]) ([p (in-list reds)])
                    (let ((landed (slide-one p occ)))
                      (values (set-cell out (first landed) (second landed) 2)
                              (set-add occ (cons (first landed) (second landed))))))])
      out)))

title: Recolor the corners of hollow rectangles
written_solution: Find each green(3) hollow rectangle. Leave its border alone except for the four corner cells, which become yellow(4).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (rect-border r0 c0 r1 c1)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) r0) (= (first p) r1) (= (second p) c0) (= (second p) c1)))
              (positions-in-rect r0 c0 r1 c1)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (filter (lambda (o)
                                        (and (= (obj-color o) 3)
                                             (>= (- (obj-r2 o) (obj-r1 o)) 2)
                                             (>= (- (obj-c2 o) (obj-c1 o)) 2)
                                             (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?)
                                                     (sort (rect-border (obj-r1 o) (obj-c1 o) (obj-r2 o) (obj-c2 o)) cell<?))))
                                      (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                             (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj))
                             (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                             (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))) 4))))

title: Fill the span between aligned endpoints
written_solution: Whenever two blue(1) endpoints lie in the same row or column with only background between them, fill the whole straight segment from one endpoint to the other with red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define after-rows
      (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
        (let ((cols1 (filter (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 1)) (range 0 (cols g)))))
          (foldl (lambda (pair acc)
                   (let ((c1 (first pair)) (c2 (second pair)))
                     (if (and (> (- c2 c1) 1)
                              (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ c1 1) c2)))
                         (paint-cells acc (map (lambda (c) (list r c)) (range c1 (+ c2 1))) 2)
                         acc)))
                 out (pairs cols1)))))
    (for/fold ([out after-rows]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((rows1 (filter (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 1)) (range 0 (rows g)))))
        (foldl (lambda (pair acc)
                 (let ((r1 (first pair)) (r2 (second pair)))
                   (if (and (> (- r2 r1) 1)
                            (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 0)) (range (+ r1 1) r2)))
                       (paint-cells acc (map (lambda (r) (list r c)) (range r1 (+ r2 1))) 2)
                       acc)))
               out (pairs rows1))))))

title: Complete orange L-trominoes to 2x2 blocks
written_solution: Look at every 2x2 window. If it has exactly three orange(7) cells and one empty cell, fill the missing cell with orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))] [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let* ((cells (list (list r c) (list r (+ c 1)) (list (+ r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
           (vals (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) cells))
           (zeros (filter (lambda (p) (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)) cells)))
      (if (and (= (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 7)) vals) 3) (= (length zeros) 1))
          (set-cell out (first (first zeros)) (second (first zeros)) 7)
          out))))

title: Recolor elbow joints in green paths
written_solution: In each green(3) path, recolor the turning cells — the cells with exactly one horizontal green(3) neighbor and exactly one vertical green(3) neighbor — to magenta(6). Straight cells stay green(3).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((up (= (safe-at g (- r 1) c 0) 3))
            (down (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) c 0) 3))
            (left (= (safe-at g r (- c 1) 0) 3))
            (right (= (safe-at g r (+ c 1) 0) 3)))
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 3)
                 (= (count-where identity (list up down left right)) 2)
                 (or up down)
                 (or left right))
            6
            (at g r c))))))

title: Mark the intersections of blue lines
written_solution: Recolor a blue(1) cell to red(2) exactly when it is the crossing point of a horizontal and a vertical blue(1) line, so it has blue(1) on all four cardinal sides.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 1)
               (= (safe-at g (- r 1) c 0) 1)
               (= (safe-at g (+ r 1) c 0) 1)
               (= (safe-at g r (- c 1) 0) 1)
               (= (safe-at g r (+ c 1) 0) 1))
          2
          (at g r c)))))

title: Reflect singletons across the main diagonal
written_solution: Copy every nonzero cell to its transposed position across the main diagonal. The original cell remains, diagonal cells stay where they are, and colors are preserved.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
    (if (not (= (at g r c) 0))
        (set-cell out c r (at g r c))
        out)))

title: Slide the object in the marker's direction
written_solution: There is one colored object and one directional marker. The marker color chooses a direction (1 → up, 2 → right, 3 → down, 4 → left). Slide the whole object rigidly in that direction until the next step would hit a blocker, the marker, or the border.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define marker (first (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4))))))
    (define mv (at g (first marker) (second marker)))
    (define dr (cond [(= mv 1) -1] [(= mv 3) 1] [else 0]))
    (define dc (cond [(= mv 2) 1] [(= mv 4) -1] [else 0]))
    (define moving (filter (lambda (cell)
                             (let ((v (third cell)))
                               (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)) (not (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4))))))
                           (grid-cells g)))
    (define cleared (erase-cells g (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (second p))) moving) 0))
    (define occupied
      (for/set ([cell (in-list (grid-cells cleared))]
                #:when (or (= (third cell) 5) (and (= (first cell) (first marker)) (= (second cell) (second marker)))))
        (cons (first cell) (second cell))))
    (define cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (second p))) moving))
    (define (blocked? cells occ)
      (any? (lambda (p)
              (or (not (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
                  (set-member? occ (cons (first p) (second p)))))
            cells))
    (define (shift cells) (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc))) cells))
    (define landed
      (let loop ([cur cells])
        (let ((nxt (shift cur)))
          (if (blocked? nxt occupied) cur (loop nxt)))))
    (paint-cells cleared landed 7)))

title: Extract the holes of hollow objects
written_solution: Ignore the object borders themselves. For each hollow object, output only the enclosed interior hole cells, colored with the same color as the surrounding object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((regions (find-0-regions g 0)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (let ((holes (filter (lambda (reg)
                             (all? (lambda (p)
                                     (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                                          (> (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                                   reg))
                           regions)))
        (paint-cells out (append* holes) (obj-color obj))))))

title: Recolor each object by the nearest marker
written_solution: Each gray(5) object should take on the color of the nearest colored marker. Distance is the smallest Manhattan distance from any object cell to the marker.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define markers (filter (lambda (cell) (and (>= (third cell) 1) (<= (third cell) 4))) (grid-cells g)))
    (define (dist m obj)
      (apply min
             (map (lambda (p)
                    (+ (abs (- (first p) (first m))) (abs (- (second p) (second m)))))
                  (obj-cells obj))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((best (first (sort markers (lambda (a b) (< (dist a obj) (dist b obj)))))))
        (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (third best))))))

title: Normalize and pack objects in encounter order
written_solution: Take every object in top-to-bottom then left-to-right order. Crop each one to its tight bbox, keep its colors and shape, and pack the normalized crops side by side with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (or (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                           (and (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))))
         (height (apply max (map obj-h objs)))
         (width (+ (apply + (map obj-w objs)) (max 0 (- (length objs) 1)))))
    (let-values ([(out final-col)
                  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid height width 0)] [col0 0]) ([obj (in-list objs)])
                    (let ((placed (map (lambda (p)
                                         (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                                               (+ col0 (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj)))))
                                       (obj-cells obj))))
                      (values (paint-cells out placed (obj-color obj))
                              (+ col0 (obj-w obj) 1))))])
      out)))

title: Fill the row-column closure of each object
written_solution: For each object, look at which rows and which columns within its bbox contain object cells. Fill every intersection of those occupied rows and occupied columns with the object's color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let* ((rs (remove-duplicates (map first (obj-cells obj))))
           (cs (remove-duplicates (map second (obj-cells obj))))
           (cells (for*/list ([r (in-list rs)] [c (in-list cs)]) (list r c))))
      (paint-cells out cells (obj-color obj)))))

title: Stamp the template at the anchors
written_solution: The gray(5) component is a template. Copy its shape to every anchor singleton, recoloring each copy to the anchor's color. The output contains only the colored copies, not the original template.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((template (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0))
                                (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (shape (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)))
         (anchors (filter (lambda (cell) (and (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 5)))) (grid-cells g))))
    (foldl (lambda (anchor out)
             (let ((cells (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p)) (+ (second anchor) (second p)))) shape)))
               (paint-cells out cells (third anchor))))
           (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
           anchors)))

title: Transpose each object inside its own box
written_solution: Treat each object separately inside its own tight bbox. Reflect its cells across that box's main diagonal, preserving color and keeping the box anchored in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let ((cells (map (lambda (p)
                        (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) (- (second p) (obj-c1 obj)))
                              (+ (obj-c1 obj) (- (first p) (obj-r1 obj)))))
                      (obj-cells obj))))
      (paint-cells out cells (obj-color obj)))))

title: Slide all objects and let them stack
written_solution: A control marker picks a global direction (1 → up, 2 → right, 3 → down, 4 → left). Every object slides rigidly as far as possible in that direction. The objects then stack against the wall and against each other, as if they all moved together.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define marker (first (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (>= v 1) (<= v 4))))))
    (define mv (at g (first marker) (second marker)))
    (define dr (cond [(= mv 1) -1] [(= mv 3) 1] [else 0]))
    (define dc (cond [(= mv 2) 1] [(= mv 4) -1] [else 0]))
    (define comps
      (filter (lambda (o) (not (and (>= (obj-color o) 1) (<= (obj-color o) 4)))) (objects g 0)))
    (define (comp<? a b)
      (cond [(= dr 1) (> (obj-r2 a) (obj-r2 b))]
            [(= dr -1) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
            [(= dc 1) (> (obj-c2 a) (obj-c2 b))]
            [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))
    (define ordered (sort comps comp<?))
    (define (blocked? cells occ)
      (any? (lambda (p)
              (or (not (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
                  (set-member? occ (cons (first p) (second p)))))
            cells))
    (define (shift cells) (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc))) cells))
    (define (slide-cells cells occ)
      (let loop ([cur cells])
        (let ((nxt (shift cur)))
          (if (blocked? nxt occ) cur (loop nxt)))))
    (let-values ([(out final-occ)
                  (for/fold ([out (set-cell (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (first marker) (second marker) mv)]
                             [occ (set (cons (first marker) (second marker)))])
                            ([obj (in-list ordered)])
                    (let* ((landed (slide-cells (obj-cells obj) occ))
                           (new-out (paint-cells out landed (obj-color obj)))
                           (new-occ (for/fold ([o occ]) ([p (in-list landed)])
                                      (set-add o (cons (first p) (second p))))))
                      (values new-out new-occ)))])
      out)))

title: Trace the perimeter of the marked object
written_solution: A red(2) marker touches exactly one object. Select that object and output only its outer outline, recolored red(2). Everything else disappears.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define marker (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define (touches-marker? obj)
      (any? (lambda (p)
              (any? (lambda (d) (and (= (+ (first marker) (first d)) (first p))
                                      (= (+ (second marker) (second d)) (second p))))
                    cardinal-deltas))
            (obj-cells obj)))
    (define target (first (filter (lambda (o) (and (not (= (obj-color o) 2)) (touches-marker? o))) (objects g 0))))
    (define target-set (for/set ([p (in-list (obj-cells target))]) (cons (first p) (second p))))
    (define perim
      (filter (lambda (p)
                (any? (lambda (d)
                        (not (set-member? target-set (cons (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d))))))
                      cardinal-deltas))
              (obj-cells target)))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) perim 2)))

title: Recolor the template with the legend and stamp it
written_solution: The bottom two rows form a legend: the upper legend row lists source colors and the lower row lists their replacements. Apply that color mapping to the multicolor template, then stamp recolored copies of the template at each anchor cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((h (rows g))
         (w (cols g))
         (cols-used (take (sort (filter (lambda (c) (or (not (= (at g (- h 2) c) 0))
                                                        (not (= (at g (- h 1) c) 0))))
                                      (range 0 w))
                                <)
                          3))
         (pairs (map (lambda (c) (list (at g (- h 2) c) (at g (- h 1) c))) cols-used))
         (anchors (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (< r (- h 2)) (= v 9)))))
         (temp (filter (lambda (cell) (and (< (first cell) (- h 2)) (not (= (third cell) 0)) (not (= (third cell) 9)))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (mapped v) (second (first (filter (lambda (p) (= (first p) v)) pairs))))
    (define r0 (apply min (map first temp)))
    (define c0 (apply min (map second temp)))
    (define template
      (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) r0) (- (second p) c0) (mapped (third p)))) temp))
    (foldl (lambda (anchor out)
             (paint-cells out
                          (map (lambda (p) (list (+ (first anchor) (first p))
                                                 (+ (second anchor) (second p))
                                                 (third p)))
                               template)
                          #f))
           (empty-grid h w 0)
           anchors)))

title: Paint the cells seen by exactly two seeds
written_solution: Each seed sends sight-lines horizontally and vertically until a wall or the border stops it. Count how many seeds see each empty cell, then paint exactly the cells seen by two seeds.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((cov (make-hash)))
    (for ([seed (in-list (find-color g 1))])
      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
        (let loop ([r (+ (first seed) (first d))] [c (+ (second seed) (second d))])
          (when (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (not (= (at g r c) 8)))
            (when (= (at g r c) 0)
              (hash-update! cov (cons r c) add1 0))
            (loop (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c) (if (= (hash-ref cov (cons r c) 0) 2) 2 0)))))

title: Fill the chamber by BFS parity
written_solution: Starting from the seed, perform a shortest-path flood through the non-wall cells. Color even-distance cells green(3) and odd-distance cells yellow(4), while keeping the walls.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((seed (first (find-color g 2)))

  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define colors (sort (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)))) (grid-colors g)) <))
    (define (path-cells start goal)
      (define parent (make-hash))
      (define visited (mutable-set))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (define goal-key (cons (first goal) (second goal)))
      (define found #f)
      (set-add! visited (first queue))
      (let bfs ([step 0])
        (unless (or found (empty? queue))
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (when (equal? cur goal-key) (set! found #t))
            (unless found
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d)))
                      (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                  (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                             (not (set-member? visited (cons nr nc)))
                             (or (= (at g nr nc) 0) (equal? (cons nr nc) goal-key)))

                    (hash-set! parent (cons nr nc) cur)
                    (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc)))))))))
          (bfs (+ step 1))))
      (if (not found)
          (list)
          (let trace ([cur goal-key] [acc (list)])
            (let ((next-acc (cons (list (car cur) (cdr cur)) acc)))
              (if (equal? cur (cons (first start) (second start)))
                  next-acc
                  (trace (hash-ref parent cur) next-acc))))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((pts (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length pts) 2)
            (paint-cells out (path-cells (first pts) (second pts)) color)
            out)))))

      (append* (filter (lambda (reg)

        (if (empty? holes) out (paint-layers out holes))))))
