title: Area-Rank Frame Assignment
written_solution: Ignore the hollow gray(5) frames and sort the free objects by area from smallest to largest. Sort the frames by their interior area from smallest to largest, then center each cropped object inside the correspondingly ranked frame.

(rule!

 ;; the smallest object goes centered into the smallest-interior frame,
 ;; the next into the next, and so on — all drawn on a blank canvas.

   (let ()
     (define (frame? o)  ;; hollow gray rectangle outline, 3x3+
       (and (= (obj-color o) 5)
            (>= (obj-h o) 3) (>= (obj-w o) 3)
            (= (obj-size o) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h o) (obj-w o))) 4))
            (all? (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 o))
                                  (= (first p) (obj-r2 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c1 o))
                                  (= (second p) (obj-c2 o))))
                  (obj-cells o))))
     (define (bb< a b)
       (let loop ((xs (list (obj-r1 a) (obj-r2 a) (obj-c1 a)
                            (obj-c2 a)))
                  (ys (list (obj-r1 b) (obj-r2 b) (obj-c1 b)
                            (obj-c2 b))))
         (cond ((null? xs) #f)
               ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
               ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
               (else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys))))))
     (define frames  ;; smallest interior first
       (sort (filter frame? (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b)
               (let ((ia (* (- (obj-h a) 2) (- (obj-w a) 2)))
                     (ib (* (- (obj-h b) 2) (- (obj-w b) 2))))
                 (if (= ia ib) (bb< a b) (< ia ib))))))
     (define movers  ;; smallest object first
       (sort (filter (lambda (o) (not (= (obj-color o) 5)))
                     (objects g 0))
             (lambda (a b) (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))
                               (bb< a b)
                               (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
     (define (stamp out obj fr)  ;; object centered in the frame
       (let* ((cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells obj)))
              (ch (+ 1 (max-of first cells)))
              (cw (+ 1 (max-of second cells)))
              (sr (+ (obj-r1 fr) 1
                     (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-h fr) 2 ch) 2))))
              (sc (+ (obj-c1 fr) 1
                     (max 0 (quotient (- (obj-w fr) 2 cw) 2)))))
         (paint-cells out
                      (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p)
                                                      (second p) h w))
                              (map (lambda (p)
                                     (list (+ sr (first p))
                                           (+ sc (second p))))
                                   cells))
                      (obj-color obj))))
     (let loop ((objs movers) (frs frames)
                (out (for/fold ((o (empty-grid h w 0)))
                               ((f (in-list frames)))
                       (paint-cells o (obj-cells f) 5))))
       (if (or (empty? objs) (empty? frs))
           out
           (loop (rest objs) (rest frs)
                 (stamp out (first objs) (first frs))))))))

    (define (frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 5) (hollow-frame? obj)))
    (define (frame< a b)
      (cell< (list (obj-r1 a) (obj-c1 a))
             (list (obj-r1 b) (obj-c1 b))))
    (define (key-of frame)
      (let* ((top (obj-r1 frame))
             (bottom (obj-r2 frame))
             (left (obj-c1 frame))
             (right (obj-c2 frame))
             (positions
              (list (list (- top 1) left) (list (- top 1) right)
                    (list (+ bottom 1) left) (list (+ bottom 1) right)
                    (list top (- left 1)) (list top (+ right 1))
                    (list bottom (- left 1)) (list bottom (+ right 1))))
             (values
              (filter (lambda (value) (and (>= value 1) (<= value 4)))
                      (map (lambda (position)
                             (if (in-bounds? (first position) (second position)
                                             (rows g) (cols g))
                                 (at g (first position) (second position))
                                 0))

        (if (empty? values) 1 (first (sort values <)))))

      (cond ((= key 2) (rotate-cw piece))
            ((= key 3) (flip-lr piece))
            ((= key 4) (flip-ud piece))
            (else piece)))

             (interior-h (- (obj-h frame) 2))
             (interior-w (- (obj-w frame) 2))
             (top (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1
                     (max 0 (quotient (- interior-h (rows piece)) 2))))
             (left (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1
                      (max 0 (quotient (- interior-w (cols piece)) 2)))))
        (paste-crop out piece top left)))
    (let* ((frames (sort (filter frame? (objects g 0)) frame<))
           (template-cells
            (filter (lambda (position)
                      (> (at g (first position) (second position)) 5))
                    (grid-positions g))))
      (if (empty? template-cells)
          g
          (let* ((template (crop-cells g template-cells))
                 (base
                  (for/fold ((out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)))
                            ((frame (in-list frames)))
                    (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) 5))))
            (for/fold ((out base)) ((frame (in-list frames)))

  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (covers? seed r c)
      (= (+ (abs (- r (first seed))) (abs (- c (second seed)))) 1))
    (define (same? seed r c)
      (and (= r (first seed)) (= c (second seed))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (seed) (or (same? seed r c) (covers? seed r c))) seeds)))
          (if hit (third hit) 0))))))

title: Bridge Matching Endpoints
written_solution: Each color forms exactly one aligned pair. Fill the full horizontal or vertical segment between the two endpoints, inclusive.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (paint-color out color)
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (not (= (length cells) 2))
            (paint-cells out cells color)
            (let* ((a (first cells))
                   (b (second cells))
                   (r1 (first a)) (c1 (second a))
                   (r2 (first b)) (c2 (second b)))
              (cond [(= r1 r2)
                     (paint-cells out (for/list ([c (in-range (min c1 c2) (+ (max c1 c2) 1))]) (list r1 c)) color)]
                    [(= c1 c2)
                     (paint-cells out (for/list ([r (in-range (min r1 r2) (+ (max r1 r2) 1))]) (list r c1)) color)]
                    [else (paint-cells out cells color)])))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (paint-color out color))))

title: Diagonal Corners to Outline
written_solution: For each color, interpret the two cells as opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle and draw that rectangle’s outline.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-outline a b)
      (let* ((r0 (min (first a) (first b)))
             (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
             (c0 (min (second a) (second b)))
             (c1 (max (second a) (second b))))
        (append
          (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r0 c))
          (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r1 c))
          (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c0))
          (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c1)))))
    (define (paint-color out color)
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (paint-cells out (rect-outline (first cells) (second cells)) color)
            (paint-cells out cells color))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (paint-color out color))))

title: Mirror Across the Guide
written_solution: The all-8 row or column is a mirror. Keep the original shape and add its reflected copy across the guide.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define guide-row
      (find-first
        (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (c) (= (at g r c) 8)) (range 0 (cols g))))
        (range 0 (rows g))))
    (define guide-col
      (find-first
        (lambda (c) (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 8)) (range 0 (rows g))))
        (range 0 (cols g))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))]
                #:when (let ((v (at g r c))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)))))
      (let ((v (at g r c)))
        (cond [(not (eq? guide-row #f))
               (let ((rr (- (* 2 guide-row) r)))
                 (if (in-bounds? rr c (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out rr c v) out))]
              [(not (eq? guide-col #f))
               (let ((cc (- (* 2 guide-col) c)))
                 (if (in-bounds? r cc (rows out) (cols out)) (set-cell out r cc v) out))]
              [else out])))))

title: Count and Sort Colors
written_solution: Count every non-background color, then output one row containing each color repeated by its count, sorted from smallest color number to largest.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((vals (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
         (colors (sort (remove-duplicates vals) <))
         (row (apply append
                (map (lambda (color)
                       (make-list (count-where (lambda (v) (= v color)) vals) color))
                     colors))))
    (if (empty? row) (list (list 0)) (list row))))

title: Seed to 3x3 Frame
written_solution: Every seed becomes the outline of a 3×3 square centered on that seed, using the seed’s color and clipping at the edges.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g))))
    (define (frame-cells seed)
      (let ((sr (first seed)) (sc (second seed)))
        (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
          (for*/list ([dr (in-range -1 2)]
                      [dc (in-range -1 2)]
                      #:when (and (not (and (= dr 0) (= dc 0)))
                                  (or (= (abs dr) 1) (= (abs dc) 1))))
            (list (+ sr dr) (+ sc dc))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([seed (in-list seeds)])
      (paint-cells out (frame-cells seed) (third seed)))))

title: One-Step Shift
written_solution: Ignore the arrow in the output and translate the entire colored component by one cell in the arrow’s direction.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (dir-for token)
      (cond [(= token 1) (list -1 0)]
            [(= token 2) (list 0 1)]
            [(= token 3) (list 1 0)]
            [else (list 0 -1)]))
    (define arrow
      (let ((hits (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4))) (grid-cells g))))
        (if (empty? hits) #f (last hits))))
    (if (not arrow)
        g
        (let* ((d (dir-for (third arrow)))
               (dr (first d))
               (dc (second d))
               (cells (filter (lambda (cell)
                                 (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                                      (not (member? (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4)))))
                               (grid-cells g))))
          (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
                    ([cell (in-list cells)])
            (let ((nr (+ (first cell) dr)) (nc (+ (second cell) dc)))
              (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows out) (cols out))
                  (set-cell out nr nc (third cell))
                  out)))))))

title: Token-Specific Kernels in Frames
written_solution: Each border-1 frame contains one seed and one token. The token chooses a kernel shape—plus, X, or full 3×3—and that kernel is painted in the seed color, clipped to the frame interior.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define (kernel token)
      (cond [(= token 2) (list (list 0 0) (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1))]
            [(= token 3) (list (list 0 0) (list -1 -1) (list -1 1) (list 1 -1) (list 1 1))]
            [else (for*/list ([dr (in-range -1 2)] [dc (in-range -1 2)]) (list dr dc))]))
    (define (paint-frame out frame)
      (let* ((interior (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)
                                          (- (obj-r2 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1)))
             (interior-cells
               (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0))) interior))
             (token-cells
               (filter (lambda (p) (member? (at g (first p) (second p)) (list 2 3 4))) interior-cells))
             (seed-cells
               (filter (lambda (p) (not (member? (at g (first p) (second p)) (list 2 3 4)))) interior-cells)))
        (if (or (empty? token-cells) (empty? seed-cells))
            out
            (let* ((token (at g (first (last token-cells)) (second (last token-cells))))
                   (seed (last seed-cells))
                   (sr (first seed))
                   (sc (second seed))
                   (color (at g sr sc))
                   (cells
                     (filter (lambda (p)
                               (and (> (first p) (obj-r1 frame)) (< (first p) (obj-r2 frame))
                                    (> (second p) (obj-c1 frame)) (< (second p) (obj-c2 frame))))
                             (map (lambda (d) (list (+ sr (first d)) (+ sc (second d)))) (kernel token)))))
              (paint-cells out cells color)))))
    (let ((frames (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
                        (lambda (a b)
                          (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                              (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                              (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))))))
      (for/fold ([out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                         (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 1) 1 0)))])
                ([frame (in-list frames)])
        (paint-frame out frame)))))

title: Corner-Marker Stripe Fill
written_solution: For each border-1 frame, the two cells just inside the top corners specify two colors. Fill the frame interior with alternating vertical stripes starting with the left marker color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define (paint-frame out frame)
      (let ((a (at g (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)))
            (b (at g (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (- (obj-c2 frame) 1))))
        (for*/fold ([acc out])
                   ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
          (set-cell acc r c (if (= (modulo (- c (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1)) 2) 0) a b)))))

      (for/fold ([out (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)

title: Crop and Rotate by Token
written_solution: Ignore the token cell when finding the motif. Crop the motif to its bbox and rotate it: 1 → none, 2 → 90°, 3 → 180°, and 4 → 270°.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (let* ((token-hits (filter (lambda (cell) (member? (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4))) (grid-cells g)))
           (token (if (empty? token-hits) 1 (third (last token-hits))))
           (cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (member? v (list 1 2 3 4)))))))
           (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
           (crop (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))
      (transform-code crop token))))

title: Area-Rank Recoloring
written_solution: Find the separate components, sort them by area from smallest to largest, and recolor them with red(2), 3, 4 in that order while keeping the shapes in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs
           (sort (objects g 0)
                 (lambda (a b)
                   (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                         [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))) (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                         [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))])))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)] [rank (in-naturals 2)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) rank))))

title: Fill Chambers from Seeds
written_solution: The walls split the grid into chambers. Any chamber that contains one seed gets filled completely with that seed’s color, while the walls remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (paint-region out region)
      (let* ((colors (remove-duplicates
                       (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0)))
                               (map (lambda (p) (at g (first p) (second p))) region)))))
        (if (= (length colors) 1)
            (paint-cells out region (first colors))
            out)))
    (let loop ([remaining (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (= v 0)))] [out g])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((p (first remaining))
                 (region (connected-region g (first p) (second p)
                            (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 1)))
                            4)))
            (loop (filter (lambda (q) (not (member? q region))) remaining)
                  (paint-region out region)))))))

title: Stamp the Mask at Anchors
written_solution: Extract the pattern made by the 5-cells, normalize it, remove it, and stamp that same pattern at each nonzero anchor using the anchor’s color and position as the top-left origin.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mask-cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (= v 5))))
         (norm (normalize-cells mask-cells)))
    (if (empty? mask-cells)
        (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)
        (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
                   ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                    [c (in-range (cols g))]
                    #:when (let ((v (at g r c))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
          (paint-cells out
            (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)))
                    (map (lambda (d) (list (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))) norm))
            (at g r c))))))

title: Priority Sprouts
written_solution: The top row gives a priority ordering of colors. In the body, each seed grows a plus of radius 1, and whenever two sprouts compete for the same cell, the higher-priority color wins. The output drops the priority row.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define priority-colors (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
    (define (priority color)
      (let loop ([remaining priority-colors] [idx 0])
        (cond [(empty? remaining) 1000000]
              [(= color (first remaining)) idx]
              [else (loop (rest remaining) (+ idx 1))])))
    (define seeds
      (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0)))
        (for*/list ([r (in-range 1 (rows g))]
                    [c (in-range (cols g))])
          (list (- r 1) c (at g r c)))))
    (define (covers? seed r c)
      (<= (+ (abs (- r (first seed))) (abs (- c (second seed)))) 1))
    (define (best-seed r c)
      (let loop ([remaining seeds] [best #f] [best-priority 1000001])
        (if (empty? remaining)
            best
            (let* ((seed (first remaining))
                   (rank (priority (third seed))))
              (if (and (covers? seed r c) (< rank best-priority))
                  (loop (rest remaining) seed rank)
                  (loop (rest remaining) best best-priority))))))
    (grid-from-fn (- (rows g) 1) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((hit (best-seed r c)))
          (if hit (third hit) 0))))))

title: A:B::C Transform Analogy
written_solution: The top pair demonstrates a transformation such as rotation or reflection. Infer that transform from A→B, crop C tightly, and output the transformed version of C.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                  (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                  (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))
    (define (inner-crop obj)
      (crop-to-content
        (subgrid g (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                 (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1))))
    (if (< (length frames) 3)
        (list (list 0))
        (let* ((A (inner-crop (first frames)))
               (B (inner-crop (second frames)))
               (C (inner-crop (third frames)))
               (code (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (t) (equal? (transform-code A t) B))
                                            (list 1 2 3 4 5 6))))
                       (if hit hit 1))))
          (transform-code C code)))))

title: Palette-Depth Nested Frames
written_solution: The top strip lists colors in depth order. Recolor the nested border-1 frames from outermost to innermost using that palette, and output only the body.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define palette (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)))
    (define body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))
                                (* (- (obj-h obj) 2) (- (obj-w obj) 2))))
           (all? (lambda (p)
                   (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj))
                       (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj))
                       (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-cells obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter rect-frame? (objects body 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define (frame-cells obj)
      (append
        (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r1 obj) c))
        (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list (obj-r2 obj) c))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c1 obj)))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r (obj-c2 obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows body) (cols body) 0)])
              ([frame (in-list frames)] [idx (in-naturals)])
      (paint-cells out (frame-cells frame)
                   (if (< idx (length palette)) (list-ref palette idx) (last palette))))))

written_solution: The three framed motifs must be classified by symmetry. Output a 3×3 matrix with red(2) wherever two motifs share the same symmetry class and 0 otherwise.

           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)

title: Route Pairs Around the Wall
written_solution: The matching colored terminals must be connected through background cells while avoiding the cyan(8) wall. Draw the shortest path for each pair, preserving walls and terminals.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define dirs (list (list 0 1) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list -1 0)))
    (define (blocked-cells out color)
      (filter-cells out
        (lambda (r c v)
          (or (= v 8) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)) (not (= v color)))))))
    (define (shortest-path blocked start goal)
      ;; Mutable lookup table for predecessor links during BFS.
      (define prev (make-hash))
      (hash-set! prev start #f)
      (define (blocked? p) (member? p blocked))
      (define (neighbors p)
        (filter (lambda (q)
                  (and (in-bounds? (first q) (second q) (rows g) (cols g))
                       (not (blocked? q))
                       (not (hash-has-key? prev q))))
                (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (first p) (first d)) (+ (second p) (second d)))) dirs)))
      (define (reconstruct cur acc)
        (let ((p (hash-ref prev cur)))
          (if p
              (reconstruct p (cons cur acc))
              (cons cur acc))))
      (let bfs ([queue (list start)])
        (cond [(empty? queue) (list start goal)]
              [else
               (let ((cur (first queue)))
                 (if (equal? cur goal)
                     (reconstruct cur (list))
                     (let ((new-neighbors (neighbors cur)))
                       (for ([n (in-list new-neighbors)]) (hash-set! prev n cur))
                       (bfs (append (rest queue) new-neighbors)))))])))
    (define colors
      (sort (filter (lambda (v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 8)))) (grid-colors g 0)) <))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list colors)])
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (paint-cells out (shortest-path (blocked-cells out color) (first cells) (second cells)) color)
            out)))))

title: Legend-Driven Transform Stamping
written_solution: The top two rows map anchor colors to transforms. Extract the gray(5) motif, normalize it, then for each anchor stamp the appropriately transformed motif in the anchor’s color. The output excludes the legend and the source.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (token-map raw)
      (cond [(= raw 9) 1]
            [(= raw 2) 2]
            [(= raw 3) 3]
            [(= raw 4) 4]
            [else 1]))
    (define (transform-code grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (transpose grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [else (flip-ud grid)]))
    (define mapping
      (filter identity
        (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))])
          (let ((color (at g 1 c)) (raw (at g 0 c)))
            (if (and (not (= color 0)) (member? raw (list 9 2 3 4)))
                (list color (token-map raw))
                #f)))))
    (define (code-for color)
      (second (first (filter (lambda (entry) (= (first entry) color)) mapping))))
    (define source-cells
      (for*/list ([r (in-range 2 (rows g))]
                  [c (in-range (cols g))]
                  #:when (= (at g r c) 5))
        (list (- r 2) c)))
    (define norm (normalize-cells source-cells))
    (define (cells->grid cells)
      (let* ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells))))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second cells)))))
        (grid-from-fn h w
          (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) cells) 1 0)))))
    (define (transform-coords cells code)
      (let ((tg (transform-code (cells->grid cells) code)))
        (filter-cells tg (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))))
    (if (empty? source-cells)
        (empty-grid (- (rows g) 2) (cols g) 0)
        (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (- (rows g) 2) (cols g) 0)])
                   ([r (in-range 2 (rows g))]
                    [c (in-range (cols g))]
                    #:when (let ((v (at g r c))) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)))))
          (paint-cells out
            (filter (lambda (p) (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows out) (cols out)))
                    (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (- r 2) (first d)) (+ c (second d))))
                         (transform-coords norm (code-for (at g r c)))))
            (at g r c))))))

title: Fill the Source Bounding Box at the Target
skills: local bounding boxes, abstraction, frame-relative rendering
written_solution: Take the source motif's local bbox and draw that whole filled local rectangle in the target frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Corner triads define local coordinate FRAMES: a 2 with orthogonal
 ;; 3/4 neighbors is the SOURCE, a 5 with 6/7 the TARGET. Read the
 ;; source's motif of 8s in local coordinates and FILL its whole
 ;; bounding box with 8s through the target frame.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (point< a b)
       (cond ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b)))
             ((not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b)))
             (else (< (third a) (third b)))))
     (define (gpos f u v)
       (list (+ (first (first f)) (* u (first (second f)))
                (* v (first (third f))))
             (+ (second (first f)) (* u (second (second f)))
                (* v (second (third f))))))
     (define (lpos f p)
       (let ((dr (- (first p) (first (first f))))
             (dc (- (second p) (second (first f)))))
         (list (+ (* dr (first (second f))) (* dc (second (second f))))
               (+ (* dr (first (third f))) (* dc (second (third f)))))))
     (define (frame< a b)
       (let loop ((xs (append (first a) (second a) (third a)))
                  (ys (append (first b) (second b) (third b))))
         (cond ((null? xs) #f)
               ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
               ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
               (else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys))))))
     (define (find-frames a b c)
       (sort (remove-duplicates
              (filter (lambda (x) x)
                      (for*/list ((r (in-range h)) (col (in-range w))
                                  (dx (in-list cardinal-deltas))
                                  (dy (in-list cardinal-deltas)))
                        (and (= (at g r col) a)
                             (in-bounds? (+ r (first dx))
                                         (+ col (second dx)) h w)
                             (in-bounds? (+ r (first dy))
                                         (+ col (second dy)) h w)
                             (= (at g (+ r (first dx))
                                    (+ col (second dx)))
                                b)
                             (= (at g (+ r (first dy))
                                    (+ col (second dy)))
                                c)
                             (zero? (+ (* (first dx) (first dy))
                                       (* (second dx) (second dy))))
                             (list (list r col) dx dy)))))
             frame<))
     (define (motif-uvs f)  ;; the 8-cells in local coords, radius 3
       (sort (filter (lambda (x) x)
                     (for*/list ((r (in-range h)) (c (in-range w)))
                       (and (= (at g r c) 8)
                            (let ((uv (lpos f (list r c))))
                              (and (<= (max (abs (first uv))
                                            (abs (second uv)))
                                       3)
                                   (list (first uv) (second uv) 8))))))
             point<))
     (define sf (first (find-frames 2 3 4)))
     (define tf (first (find-frames 5 6 7)))
     (define uvs (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (second p)))
                      (motif-uvs sf)))
     (define u0 (min-of first uvs))
     (define v0 (min-of second uvs))
     (define u1 (max-of first uvs))
     (define v1 (max-of second uvs))
     (for*/fold ((out g)) ((u (in-range u0 (+ u1 1)))
                           (v (in-range v0 (+ v1 1))))
       (let ((rc (gpos tf u v)))
         (set-cell out (first rc) (second rc) 8))))))

title: Copy the Farthest Local Points
skills: distance ranking, local metrics, frame-relative copy
written_solution: Find the source motif cells with largest local Manhattan distance from the origin and reproduce only those farthest cells in the target frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Two orthogonal color tripods act as coordinate frames. The SOURCE frame
 ;; is a 2-cell whose 3-neighbor gives the x axis and 4-neighbor the y axis;
 ;; the TARGET frame is a 5-cell with 6 and 7 likewise. Of the 8-marker
 ;; cells within Chebyshev radius 3 of the source origin (in source-local
 ;; coordinates), only those at MAXIMUM Manhattan distance are copied to
 ;; the same local positions in the target frame. Rest of grid unchanged.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (lex< a b)  ;; lexicographic over equal-length number lists
       (cond ((null? a) #f)
             ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b)))
             (else (lex< (rest a) (rest b)))))
     (define (find-frame a b c)  ;; -> (origin vx vy), lex-first candidate
       (first
        (sort (remove-duplicates
               (filter values
                       (for*/list ((r (range h)) (col (range w))
                                   (dx cardinal-deltas) (dy cardinal-deltas))
                         (and (= (at g r col) a)
                              (in-bounds? (+ r (first dx)) (+ col (second dx)) h w)
                              (in-bounds? (+ r (first dy)) (+ col (second dy)) h w)
                              (= (at g (+ r (first dx)) (+ col (second dx))) b)
                              (= (at g (+ r (first dy)) (+ col (second dy))) c)
                              (zero? (+ (* (first dx) (first dy))
                                        (* (second dx) (second dy))))
                              (list (list r col) dx dy)))))
              (lambda (fa fb)
                (lex< (append (first fa) (second fa) (third fa))
                      (append (first fb) (second fb) (third fb)))))))
     (define (lpos f r c)  ;; grid position -> frame-local (u v)
       (let ((dr (- r (first (first f))))
             (dc (- c (second (first f)))))
         (list (+ (* dr (first (second f))) (* dc (second (second f))))
               (+ (* dr (first (third f))) (* dc (second (third f)))))))
     (define (gpos f u v)  ;; frame-local (u v) -> grid position
       (list (+ (first (first f))
                (* u (first (second f))) (* v (first (third f))))
             (+ (second (first f))
                (* u (second (second f))) (* v (second (third f))))))
     (define src (find-frame 2 3 4))
     (define tgt (find-frame 5 6 7))
     (define pts  ;; (u v color) 8-markers near the source origin, sorted
       (sort (filter values
                     (for*/list ((r (range h)) (c (range w)))
                       (and (= (at g r c) 8)
                            (let ((uv (lpos src r c)))
                              (and (<= (max (abs (first uv)) (abs (second uv))) 3)
                                   (list (first uv) (second uv) 8))))))
             lex<))
     (define far  ;; the markers at maximum Manhattan distance from origin
       (let ((maxrad (max-of (lambda (p) (+ (abs (first p)) (abs (second p))))
                             pts)))
         (filter (lambda (p) (= (+ (abs (first p)) (abs (second p))) maxrad))
                 pts)))
     (for/fold ((out g)) ((p far))
       (let ((rc (gpos tgt (first p) (second p))))
         (set-cell out (first rc) (second rc) (third p)))))))

title: Diagonal Reflection Then Copy
skills: coordinate transforms, local reflection, orientation-aware rendering
written_solution: Read the motif relative to the source frame, swap each point's local x and y coordinates, and then place the transformed points in the target frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Two orthogonal color tripods act as coordinate frames. The SOURCE frame
 ;; is a 2-cell whose 3-neighbor gives the x axis and 4-neighbor the y axis;
 ;; the TARGET frame is a 5-cell with 6 and 7 likewise. The 8-marker cells
 ;; within Chebyshev radius 3 of the source origin (in source-local
 ;; coordinates) are reflected across the local diagonal -- (u v) becomes
 ;; (v u) -- and painted into the target frame. Rest of grid unchanged.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (lex< a b)  ;; lexicographic over equal-length number lists
       (cond ((null? a) #f)
             ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b)))
             (else (lex< (rest a) (rest b)))))
     (define (find-frame a b c)  ;; -> (origin vx vy), lex-first candidate
       (first
        (sort (remove-duplicates
               (filter values
                       (for*/list ((r (range h)) (col (range w))
                                   (dx cardinal-deltas) (dy cardinal-deltas))
                         (and (= (at g r col) a)
                              (in-bounds? (+ r (first dx)) (+ col (second dx)) h w)
                              (in-bounds? (+ r (first dy)) (+ col (second dy)) h w)
                              (= (at g (+ r (first dx)) (+ col (second dx))) b)
                              (= (at g (+ r (first dy)) (+ col (second dy))) c)
                              (zero? (+ (* (first dx) (first dy))
                                        (* (second dx) (second dy))))
                              (list (list r col) dx dy)))))
              (lambda (fa fb)
                (lex< (append (first fa) (second fa) (third fa))
                      (append (first fb) (second fb) (third fb)))))))
     (define (lpos f r c)  ;; grid position -> frame-local (u v)
       (let ((dr (- r (first (first f))))
             (dc (- c (second (first f)))))
         (list (+ (* dr (first (second f))) (* dc (second (second f))))
               (+ (* dr (first (third f))) (* dc (second (third f)))))))
     (define (gpos f u v)  ;; frame-local (u v) -> grid position
       (list (+ (first (first f))
                (* u (first (second f))) (* v (first (third f))))
             (+ (second (first f))
                (* u (second (second f))) (* v (second (third f))))))
     (define src (find-frame 2 3 4))
     (define tgt (find-frame 5 6 7))
     (define pts  ;; (u v color) 8-markers near the source origin, sorted
       (sort (filter values
                     (for*/list ((r (range h)) (c (range w)))
                       (and (= (at g r c) 8)
                            (let ((uv (lpos src r c)))
                              (and (<= (max (abs (first uv)) (abs (second uv))) 3)
                                   (list (first uv) (second uv) 8))))))
             lex<))
     (for/fold ((out g)) ((p pts))  ;; reflect (u v) -> (v u), paint at target
       (let ((rc (gpos tgt (second p) (first p))))
         (set-cell out (first rc) (second rc) (third p)))))))

                (* u (first (second f))) (* v (first (third f))))

title: Frame-Library Lookup
skills: analogy, local motif keys, keyed value retrieval, multi-frame parsing
written_solution: Build a small lookup table from the example rows: local source-key motif to local target-value motif. Then match the query key motif and replay the corresponding value motif in the background query target.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; Corner triads define local coordinate FRAMES: a 2 with orthogonal
 ;; 3/4 neighbors is a SOURCE frame, a 5 with 6/7 a TARGET frame. Each
 ;; source frame carries a motif of 8s in its local coordinates; the
 ;; first two source/target pairs teach motif -> decoration (8s and
 ;; 9s), and the third target gets the decoration its motif maps to,
 ;; painted through its own frame.
 (lambda (g)
   (let ()
     (define (uv< a b)
       (if (= (first a) (first b))
           (< (second a) (second b))
           (< (first a) (first b))))
     (define (point< a b)
       (cond ((not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b)))
             ((not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b)))
             (else (< (third a) (third b)))))
     ;; frame = (origin vx vy): local (u v) -> origin + u*vx + v*vy
     (define (gpos f u v)
       (list (+ (first (first f)) (* u (first (second f)))
                (* v (first (third f))))
             (+ (second (first f)) (* u (second (second f)))
                (* v (second (third f))))))
     (define (lpos f p)
       (let ((dr (- (first p) (first (first f))))
             (dc (- (second p) (second (first f)))))
         (list (+ (* dr (first (second f))) (* dc (second (second f))))
               (+ (* dr (first (third f))) (* dc (second (third f)))))))
     (define (frame< a b)
       (let loop ((xs (append (first a) (second a) (third a)))
                  (ys (append (first b) (second b) (third b))))
         (cond ((null? xs) #f)
               ((< (first xs) (first ys)) #t)
               ((> (first xs) (first ys)) #f)
               (else (loop (rest xs) (rest ys))))))
     (define (find-frames a b c)
       (sort (remove-duplicates
              (filter (lambda (x) x)
                      (for*/list ((r (in-range h)) (col (in-range w))
                                  (dx (in-list cardinal-deltas))
                                  (dy (in-list cardinal-deltas)))
                        (and (= (at g r col) a)
                             (in-bounds? (+ r (first dx))
                                         (+ col (second dx)) h w)
                             (in-bounds? (+ r (first dy))
                                         (+ col (second dy)) h w)
                             (= (at g (+ r (first dx))
                                    (+ col (second dx)))
                                b)
                             (= (at g (+ r (first dy))
                                    (+ col (second dy)))
                                c)
                             (zero? (+ (* (first dx) (first dy))
                                       (* (second dx) (second dy))))
                             (list (list r col) dx dy)))))
             frame<))
     (define (local-points f colors)  ;; (u v color) within radius 3
       (sort (filter (lambda (x) x)
                     (for*/list ((r (in-range h)) (c (in-range w)))
                       (and (member? (at g r c) colors)
                            (let ((uv (lpos f (list r c))))
                              (and (<= (max (abs (first uv))
                                            (abs (second uv)))
                                       3)
                                   (list (first uv) (second uv)
                                         (at g r c)))))))
             point<))
     (define (motif f)  ;; the 8-cells' local footprint
       (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (second p)))
                  (local-points f (list 8)))
             uv<))
     (define sfs (find-frames 2 3 4))
     (define tfs (find-frames 5 6 7))
     (define mapping
       (list (list (motif (first sfs)) (local-points (first tfs)
                                                     (list 8 9)))
             (list (motif (second sfs)) (local-points (second tfs)
                                                      (list 8 9)))))
     (for/fold ((out g))
               ((p (in-list (second (find (lambda (e)
                                            (equal? (first e)
                                                    (motif (third sfs))))
                                          mapping)))))
       (let ((rc (gpos (third tfs) (first p) (second p))))
         (set-cell out (first rc) (second rc) (third p)))))))

title: Diagonal Halo
written_solution: Each red(2) acts like a diagonal beacon. Keep the red(2) itself, and paint each in-bounds diagonal neighbor with magenta(6). Leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((diags (list (list -1 -1) (list -1 1) (list 1 -1) (list 1 1))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([p (in-list (find-color g 2))]
                [d (in-list diags)])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) (first d)))
            (c (+ (second p) (second d))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r c) 0))
            (set-cell out r c 6)
            out)))))

title: X-Center Fill
written_solution: Whenever a 0 cell has 1s on all four diagonal neighbors, change that center cell to cyan(8). Everything else stays as it was.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
             (= (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) 1)
             (= (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) 1)
             (= (at g (+ r 1) (- c 1)) 1)
             (= (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)) 1))
        (set-cell out r c 8)
        out)))

title: Horizontal Sandwich
written_solution: If a cell is 0 and its immediate left and right neighbors are both 5, recolor that middle cell to green(3). Keep the two 5s and everything else unchanged.

  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
             (= (at g r (- c 1)) 5)
             (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 5))
        (set-cell out r c 3)
        out)))
