             (= (at g (- r 1) c) 7)
             (= (at g (+ r 1) c) 7))
        (set-cell out r c 4)
        out)))

title: Diagonal Square Completion
written_solution: In any 2x2 block where the two cyan(8)s occupy one diagonal and the other diagonal is empty, fill the two background cells with blue(1). Leave the cyan(8)s as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((a (at g r c))
          (b (at g r (+ c 1)))
          (d (at g (+ r 1) c))
          (e (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1))))
      (cond [(and (= a 8) (= e 8) (= b 0) (= d 0))
             (set-cell (set-cell out r (+ c 1) 1) (+ r 1) c 1)]
            [(and (= b 8) (= d 8) (= a 0) (= e 0))
             (set-cell (set-cell out r c 1) (+ r 1) (+ c 1) 1)]
            [else out]))))

title: Horizontal Bar Caps
written_solution: Each horizontal 4-4 bar gets capped with maroon(9) on its immediate left and right whenever those cells exist and are 0. The original 4s stay in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (- (cols g) 1))])
    (if (and (= (at g r c) 4) (= (at g r (+ c 1)) 4))
        (let* ((left-out (if (and (>= (- c 1) 0) (= (at g r (- c 1)) 0))
                             (set-cell out r (- c 1) 9)
                             out))
               (right-c (+ c 2)))
          (if (and (< right-c (cols g)) (= (at g r right-c) 0))
              (set-cell left-out r right-c 9)
              left-out))
        out)))

title: Marker Takes the Row Color
written_solution: If a row contains exactly one distinct non-background color besides maroon(9), replace every maroon(9) in that row with that color. Rows that do not meet that condition stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (let ((colors (remove-duplicates (filter (lambda (v) (not (member v (list 0 9)))) (row g r)))))
      (if (and (= (length colors) 1) (member 9 (row g r)))
          (for/fold ([acc out]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
            (if (= (at g r c) 9) (set-cell acc r c (first colors)) acc))
          out))))

title: Crop the Marked Component
written_solution: Among all green(3) components, choose the one that is 4-connected to the red(2) marker. Output the bounding-box crop of that component alone.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((markers (find-color g 2)))
    (define (touches-marker? obj)
      (not (empty?
        (filter (lambda (p)
                  (not (empty?
                    (filter (lambda (d)
                              (member (list (+ (first p) (first d))
                                            (+ (second p) (second d)))
                                      markers))
                            cardinal-deltas))))
                (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define chosen
      (first (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) 3) (touches-marker? obj)))
                     (objects g 0))))
    (grid-from-fn (obj-h chosen) (obj-w chosen)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((p (list (+ (obj-r1 chosen) r) (+ (obj-c1 chosen) c))))
          (if (member p (obj-cells chosen)) 3 0))))))

title: Frame Border Recolor from Seed
written_solution: Every blue(1) rectangular frame contains one nonzero seed color in its interior. Recolor the entire border of that frame to the seed color, while leaving the interior seed and zeros unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (let ((colors (remove-duplicates
                      (filter (lambda (v) (not (member v (list 0 1))))
                        (for*/list ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                                    [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
                          (at g r c))))))
        (if (= (length colors) 1)
            (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) (first colors))
            out)))))

title: Horizontal Mirror Inside the Frame
written_solution: Inside each rectangular blue(1) frame, every yellow(4) cell gets a mirrored partner across the frame's horizontal axis. Add that partner as orange(7) if the mirrored spot is empty; keep the original yellow(4)s and the frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([frame (in-list (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1) (obj-r2 frame))]
                  [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1) (obj-c2 frame))])
        (let ((mr (- (+ (obj-r1 frame) (obj-r2 frame)) r)))
          (if (and (= (at g r c) 4) (= (at acc mr c) 0))
              (set-cell acc mr c 7)
              acc))))))

title: Outer Corner Markers
written_solution: For every solid rectangular magenta(6) object, place a red(2) one cell outside each of its four bounding-box corners whenever that outside cell lies inside the grid. Keep the rectangles themselves unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((corners (lambda (obj) (list (list (- (obj-r1 obj) 1) (- (obj-c1 obj) 1)) (list (- (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)) (list (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c1 obj) 1)) (list (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1)))))) (for*/fold ((out g)) ((obj (in-list (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 6) (solid-rect? o))) (objects g 0)))) (p (in-list (corners obj)))) (if (and (in-bounds? (first p) (second p) (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out (first p) (second p)) 0)) (set-cell out (first p) (second p) 2) out))))

title: Recolor by Size Rank
written_solution: There are exactly three 8-colored components. Recolor the smallest one to red(2), the middle-sized one to green(3), and the largest one to yellow(4), preserving every component's shape and position.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 8)) (objects g 0))
                     (lambda (a b) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))
         (colors (list 2 3 4)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)]
               [color (in-list colors)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color))))

title: Legend-Selected Crop
written_solution: The top row contains one nonzero legend color. Among the components below, select the component of that color and output its bounding-box crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (first (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0))))
         (candidates
          (filter (lambda (obj)
                    (and (= (obj-color obj) target)
                         (all? (lambda (p) (> (first p) 0)) (obj-cells obj))))
                  (objects g 0)))
         (chosen (first (sort candidates
                              (lambda (a b)
                                (if (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))
                                    (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))
                                    (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 chosen) (obj-c1 chosen) (obj-r2 chosen) (obj-c2 chosen))))

title: Translate the Component to the Marker
written_solution: Take the unique 5-colored component and translate it so that the top-left corner of its bbox lands exactly on the 2 marker. Output only the translated component on a background grid of the same size.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((obj (first (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 5)) (objects g 0))))
         ;; Position of the first red(2) cell
         ;; It marks the destination bbox origin, which need not be occupied.
         (marker (first (find-color g 2)))
         (dr (- (first marker) (obj-r1 obj)))
         (dc (- (second marker) (obj-c1 obj))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list (obj-cells obj))])
      (set-cell out (+ (first p) dr) (+ (second p) dc) 5))))

title: Axis-Chosen Reflection
written_solution: If the 2 marker is in the top row, its column is a vertical mirror axis. If the 2 marker is in the left column, its row is a horizontal mirror axis. Keep the original 5-object, and add its reflected copy in orange(7) across that axis.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((top-markers (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))] #:when (= (at g 0 c) 2)) c))
        (left-markers (for/list ([r (in-range (rows g))] #:when (= (at g r 0) 2)) r)))
    (if (not (empty? top-markers))
        (let ((axis (first top-markers)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 5))])
            (let ((mc (- (* 2 axis) (second p))))
              (if (and (in-bounds? (first p) mc (rows g) (cols g))
                       (= (at out (first p) mc) 0))
                  (set-cell out (first p) mc 7)
                  out))))
        (let ((axis (first left-markers)))
          (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list (find-color g 5))])
            (let ((mr (- (* 2 axis) (first p))))
              (if (and (in-bounds? mr (second p) (rows g) (cols g))
                       (= (at out mr (second p)) 0))
                  (set-cell out mr (second p) 7)
                  out)))))))

title: Nested Frame Depth Fill
written_solution: Every empty cell inside at least one rectangular blue(1) frame is recolored by its nesting depth: cells inside one frame become red(2), cells inside two nested frames become green(3), inside three become yellow(4), and so on. The blue(1) borders remain unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (and (= (obj-color obj) 1)
           (>= (obj-h obj) 3)
           (>= (obj-w obj) 3)
           (= (obj-size obj) (- (* 2 (+ (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj))) 4))))
    (define frames (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0)))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (if (= (at g r c) 0)
          (let ((depth (count-where (lambda (fr)
                                      (and (> r (obj-r1 fr)) (< r (obj-r2 fr))
                                           (> c (obj-c1 fr)) (< c (obj-c2 fr))))
                                    frames)))
            (if (> depth 0) (set-cell out r c (+ depth 1)) out))
          out))))

title: Template Stamping from Markers
written_solution: The non-singleton 6-object is a template. Ignore its absolute position, keep only its shape relative to its bbox, and stamp that shape in magenta(6) with its top-left corner aligned to every 2 marker. Output only the stamped copies on a background grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 6)) (objects g 0)))
         (template (first (sort objs (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (rel (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 template))
                                     (- (second p) (obj-c1 template))))
                   (obj-cells template))))
    (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
               ([marker (in-list (find-color g 2))]
                [p (in-list rel)])
      (let ((r (+ (first marker) (first p)))
            (c (+ (second marker) (second p))))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 6)
            out)))))

title: Vector Copy by Marker Pair
written_solution: The vector from the red(2) marker to the green(3) marker tells you how far to copy the yellow(4) object. Keep the original yellow(4) object, remove the markers, and add a translated copy in cyan(8) at that offset.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((src (first (find-color g 2)))
         (dst (first (find-color g 3)))
         (dr (- (first dst) (first src)))
         (dc (- (second dst) (second src))))
    (for/fold ([out (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (find-color g 4) 4)])
              ([p (in-list (find-color g 4))])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) dr))
            (c (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Component Size Bars
written_solution: Measure every nonzero component, sort the components from largest to smallest, and output a single row of solid bars whose lengths equal those sizes. Preserve each component's color and separate consecutive bars by one 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Sort nonzero components by occupied-cell count, largest first.  The color
  ;; tie-break is deterministic but unreachable in the generator curriculum.
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                             [else (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))
         (total (+ (apply + (map obj-size objs)) (max 0 (- (length objs) 1)))))
    ;; Pack one same-color bar per component, separated by a single zero cell.
    (let pack ([remaining objs] [left 0] [out (empty-grid 1 total 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((obj (first remaining))
                 (next (for/fold ([acc out]) ([c (in-range left (+ left (obj-size obj)))])
                         (set-cell acc 0 c (obj-color obj)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (obj-size obj) 1) next))))))

title: Legend-Order Assembly
written_solution: The nonzero cells in the top row define an order of colors. For each listed color, find the matching component below, crop it to its bbox, and assemble those crops left-to-right in legend order, separated by one background column.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((legend (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0))))
    (define (piece color)
      (let ((obj (first (filter (lambda (o)
                                  (and (= (obj-color o) color)
                                       (all? (lambda (p) (> (first p) 0)) (obj-cells o))))
                                (objects g 0)))))
        (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define parts (map piece legend))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows parts)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols parts)) (max 0 (- (length parts) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining parts] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((p (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows p))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols p))])
                         (let ((v (at p r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols p) 1) next))))))

title: Mask Transfer to the Rectangle
written_solution: Take the magenta(6) component's occupied cells relative to its bbox as a mask. Find the solid green(3) rectangle with the same bbox size, clear that rectangle, and redraw the mask there using cyan(8). Keep the original magenta(6) template unchanged.
program_solution: (rule! (let* ((template (first (sort (filter (lambda (o) (= (obj-color o) 6)) (objects g 0)) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))) (rel (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (obj-r1 template)) (- (second p) (obj-c1 template)))) (obj-cells template)))) (define target (first (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) 3) (solid-rect? obj) (= (obj-h obj) (obj-h template)) (= (obj-w obj) (obj-w template)))) (objects g 0)))) (let ((cleared (paint-cells g (obj-cells target) 0))) (for/fold ((out cleared)) ((p (in-list rel))) (set-cell out (+ (obj-r1 target) (first p)) (+ (obj-c1 target) (second p)) 8)))))

title: Diagonal Halo Stamp
written_solution: Each red(2) anchor keeps its value and stamps orange(7) onto its four diagonal neighbors, clipped by the grid boundary.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((diags (list (list -1 -1) (list -1 1) (list 1 -1) (list 1 1))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([p (in-list (find-color g 2))]
                [d (in-list diags)])
      (let ((r (+ (first p) (first d)))
            (c (+ (second p) (second d))))
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out r c 7)
            out)))))

title: Corner-To-Rectangle Border
written_solution: For each non-background color, the two input cells are opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Draw the full border of that rectangle in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (border-cells bb)
      (append
        (for/list ([c (in-range (second bb) (+ (fourth bb) 1))]) (list (first bb) c))
        (for/list ([c (in-range (second bb) (+ (fourth bb) 1))]) (list (third bb) c))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]) (list r (second bb)))
        (for/list ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]) (list r (fourth bb)))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (paint-cells out (border-cells (bbox-of-cells cells)) color)
            out)))))

title: Vertical Mirror Add
written_solution: Mirror every nonzero cell across the vertical center line of the grid, keeping the originals. The result is the union of the input and its left-right reflection.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((v (at g r c)))
      (if (not (= v 0))
          (set-cell out r (- (- (cols g) 1) c) v)
          out))))

title: Count-To-Bar
written_solution: Count how many red(2) cells appear anywhere in the input. Output a single row whose length equals that count, filled entirely with red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (list (make-list (length (find-color g 2)) 2)))

title: Top-Row Column Fill
written_solution: Every nonzero cell in the top row controls its whole column. Copy that color straight down through the entire column, leaving unmarked columns black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
             ([c (in-range (cols g))]
              [r (in-range (rows g))])
    (let ((v (at g 0 c)))
      (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out r c v) out))))

title: Center Completion
written_solution: If a black(0) cell has the same non-background color on all four orthogonal neighbors, fill the center with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((vals (list (at g (- r 1) c) (at g (+ r 1) c) (at g r (- c 1)) (at g r (+ c 1)))))
      (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
               (not (= (first vals) 0))
               (all? (lambda (v) (= v (first vals))) vals))
          (set-cell out r c (first vals))
          out))))

title: Crop The Nonzero Object
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (crop-to-content g))

title: Largest Component Crop
written_solution: Find the largest connected nonzero component in the grid and crop the output to that component's bbox. Smaller components are discarded.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 0 1))))
         (obj (first (sort (objects mask 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))

title: Marker-Framed Crop
written_solution: Use the top-left marker color as the border color. Crop the rest of the nonzero object to its bbox, then surround that crop with a one-cell frame of the marker color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((frame-color (at g 0 0))
         (cells (filter-cells g (lambda (r c v) (and (not (= v 0)) (not (and (= r 0) (= c 0)))))))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
         (core (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))
    (grid-from-fn (+ (rows core) 2) (+ (cols core) 2)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (or (= r 0) (= c 0) (= r (+ (rows core) 1)) (= c (+ (cols core) 1)))
            frame-color
            (at core (- r 1) (- c 1)))))))

title: Fill Enclosed Holes
written_solution: Any black(0) region that is completely enclosed and does not touch the outer border is filled with orange(7). Border-connected zero regions remain black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((zero-mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                      (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 1 0))))
         (zero-objs (objects zero-mask 0)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list zero-objs)])
      (if (empty? (filter (lambda (p)
                            (or (= (first p) 0) (= (second p) 0)
                                (= (first p) (- (rows g) 1))
                                (= (second p) (- (cols g) 1))))
                          (obj-cells obj)))
          (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) 7)
          out))))

title: Area-Sorted Color Row
written_solution: Measure the area of each connected colored component. Output a single row containing their colors sorted from smallest component to largest component.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (obj-color obj))) (objects g 0))
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (first a) (first b))
                            (< (second a) (second b))
                            (< (first a) (first b)))))))
    (list (map second items))))

title: Axis Command Mirror
written_solution: Read the top-left command cell. If it is blue(1), mirror the non-command pattern across the vertical axis; if it is red(2), mirror it across the horizontal axis. Keep the command cell.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (work (set-cell g 0 0 0)))
    (define mirrored
      (if (= cmd 1)
          (for*/fold ([out work])
                     ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                      [c (in-range (cols g))])
            (let ((v (at work r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out r (- (- (cols g) 1) c) v) out)))
          (for*/fold ([out work])
                     ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                      [c (in-range (cols g))])
            (let ((v (at work r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out (- (- (rows g) 1) r) c v) out)))))
    (set-cell mirrored 0 0 cmd)))

title: Template Broadcast
written_solution: Treat the top-left 3×3 motif as a template whose center is the digit 2. Stamp that exact 3×3 motif, centered, at every other red(2) anchor in the grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((template (subgrid g 0 0 2 2))
         (anchors (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (< (first p) 3) (< (second p) 3))))
                          (find-color g 2))))
    (define (stamp out anchor)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([tr (in-range 3)]
                  [tc (in-range 3)])
        (let* ((v (at template tr tc))
               (r (+ (first anchor) (- tr 1)))
               (c (+ (second anchor) (- tc 1))))
          (if (and (not (= v 0))
                   (not (and (= r (first anchor)) (= c (second anchor))))
                   (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
                   (= (at g r c) 0))
              (set-cell acc r c v)
              acc))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
      (set-cell (stamp out anchor) (first anchor) (second anchor) 2))))

title: Midpoint Dots
written_solution: For each color, the two input cells define a horizontal or vertical segment of odd length. Mark the exact midpoint of that segment with maroon(9), keeping the endpoints unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 2)
          (let ((a (first cells)) (b (second cells)))
            (cond [(and (= (first a) (first b)) (= (modulo (abs (- (second a) (second b))) 2) 0))
                   (set-cell out (first a) (quotient (+ (second a) (second b)) 2) 9)]
                  [(and (= (second a) (second b)) (= (modulo (abs (- (first a) (first b))) 2) 0))
                   (set-cell out (quotient (+ (first a) (first b)) 2) (second a) 9)]
                  [else out]))
          out))))

title: Depth-Colored Nested Frames
written_solution: The input consists of nested rectangular frames. Recolor the outermost frame to red(2), the next nested frame to green(3), the next to yellow(4), and so on in depth order, preserving the frame shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((mask (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c) (if (= (at g r c) 0) 0 1))))
         (objs (sort (objects mask 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)]
               [i (in-naturals 2)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) i))))

title: Guide-Selected Mirror
written_solution: Find the two gray(5) guide cells. If they share a row, mirror the non-guide pattern across the horizontal axis; if they share a column, mirror it across the vertical axis. Keep the guides.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((guides (find-color g 5))
         (work (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
                 (lambda (r c)
                   (let ((v (at g r c)))
                     (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5))) v 0))))))
    (define mirrored
      (if (and (= (length guides) 2) (= (first (first guides)) (first (second guides))))
          (for*/fold ([out work])
                     ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                      [c (in-range (cols g))])
            (let ((v (at work r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out (- (- (rows g) 1) r) c v) out)))
          (for*/fold ([out work])
                     ([r (in-range (rows g))]
                      [c (in-range (cols g))])
            (let ((v (at work r c)))
              (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell out r (- (- (cols g) 1) c) v) out)))))
    (paint-cells mirrored guides 5)))

title: Color-Frequency Ranking
written_solution: Count the total number of cells of each non-background color across the whole grid, combining all components of that color. Output one row of colors ordered from highest total count to lowest.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((colors (grid-colors g 0))
         (items (sort (map (lambda (color) (list color (length (find-color g color)))) colors)
                      (lambda (a b)
                        (if (= (second a) (second b))
                            (< (first a) (first b))
                            (> (second a) (second b)))))))
    (list (map first items))))

title: Normalized Shape XOR
written_solution: Crop the blue(1) shape and the red(2) shape to their own bounding boxes, align both cropped binaries to the top-left corner of a common canvas, and output their XOR silhouette in orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (mask color)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells (find-color g color))))
        (grid-from-fn (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1)
                      (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1)
          (lambda (r c)
            (if (= (at g (+ (first bb) r) (+ (second bb) c)) color) 1 0)))))
    (let* ((a (mask 1))
           (b (mask 2))
           (h (max (rows a) (rows b)))
           (w (max (cols a) (cols b))))
      (grid-from-fn h w
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((av (and (< r (rows a)) (< c (cols a)) (= (at a r c) 1)))
                (bv (and (< r (rows b)) (< c (cols b)) (= (at b r c) 1))))
            (if (or (and av (not bv)) (and bv (not av))) 7 0)))))))

title: Perimeter-Sorted Shape Stack
written_solution: Compute the perimeter of each connected colored component. Crop each component to its own bbox, sort the cropped shapes from largest perimeter to smallest, and stack them top-to-bottom with one background row between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (perimeter obj)
      (apply +
        (map (lambda (p)
               (count-where (lambda (d)
                              (not (member (list (+ (first p) (first d))
                                                 (+ (second p) (second d)))
                                           (obj-cells obj))))
                            cardinal-deltas))
             (obj-cells obj))))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (perimeter obj)
                                     (obj-color obj)
                                     (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (if (= (first a) (first b))
                  (< (second a) (second b))
                  (> (first a) (first b))))))
    (define shapes (map third items))
    (define out-h (+ (apply + (map rows shapes)) (max 0 (- (length shapes) 1))))
    (define out-w (apply max (map cols shapes)))
    (let pack ([remaining shapes] [top 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                         (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc (+ top r) c v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ top (rows shape) 1) next))))))

title: Anchor Motif Substitution
written_solution: Use the top-left 3×3 motif as a template. Wherever the template contains 9, substitute the color of the current anchor cell; all other template colors stay literal. Stamp that substituted motif around every anchor outside the template block.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((template (subgrid g 0 0 2 2))
         (anchors (filter (lambda (cell) (not (and (< (first cell) 3) (< (second cell) 3))))
                          (filter (lambda (cell) (not (= (third cell) 0))) (grid-cells g)))))
    (define (stamp out anchor)
      (for*/fold ([acc out])
                 ([tr (in-range 3)]
                  [tc (in-range 3)])
        (let* ((tv (at template tr tc))
               (paint (if (= tv 9) (third anchor) tv))
               (r (+ (first anchor) (- tr 1)))
               (c (+ (second anchor) (- tc 1))))
          (if (and (not (= tv 0))
                   (not (and (= r (first anchor)) (= c (second anchor))))
                   (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
                   (= (at g r c) 0))
              (set-cell acc r c paint)
              acc))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([anchor (in-list anchors)])
      (set-cell (stamp out anchor) (first anchor) (second anchor) (third anchor)))))

title: Ray Intersections With Blockers
written_solution: Red(2) sources project horizontally through zeros until blocked by any nonzero cell, and green(3) sources project vertically the same way. Output cyan(8) only at cells reached by both a red(2) horizontal ray and a blue(1) vertical ray.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((twos (find-color g 2))
        (threes (find-color g 3)))
    (define (horizontal-hit? r c)
      (not (empty?
        (filter (lambda (p)
                  (and (= (first p) r)
                       (all? (lambda (cc) (= (at g r cc) 0))
                             (range (+ (min (second p) c) 1) (max (second p) c)))))
                twos))))
    (define (vertical-hit? r c)
      (not (empty?
        (filter (lambda (p)
                  (and (= (second p) c)
                       (all? (lambda (rr) (= (at g rr c) 0))
                             (range (+ (min (first p) r) 1) (max (first p) r)))))
                threes))))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0) (horizontal-hit? r c) (vertical-hit? r c)) 8 0)))))

title: Distance-2 Cross Echo
written_solution: Keep every seed. For each nonzero cell, also paint the cells exactly two steps up, down, right, and left with the same color, when those positions stay inside the grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([cell (in-list (filter (lambda (x) (not (= (third x) 0))) (grid-cells g)))]
              [d (in-list (list (list -2 0) (list 2 0) (list 0 -2) (list 0 2)))])
    (let ((r (+ (first cell) (first d)))
          (c (+ (second cell) (second d))))
      (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
          (set-cell out r c (third cell))
          out))))

title: Diagonal Midpoint Fill
written_solution: Whenever two identical colors appear with row and column differences of 2 on a diagonal, fill the midpoint between them with that same color. Keep all existing cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out g])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (cols g))]
              [d (in-list (list (list 2 2) (list 2 -2)))])
    (let* ((v (at g r c))
           (nr (+ r (first d)))
           (nc (+ c (second d)))
           (mr (+ r (quotient (first d) 2)))
           (mc (+ c (quotient (second d) 2))))
      (if (and (not (= v 0))
               (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
               (= (at g nr nc) v)
               (= (at out mr mc) 0))
          (set-cell out mr mc v)
          out))))

title: Header Column Flood
written_solution: Copy each nonzero cell in the top row straight down through the entire column. All other columns stay zero.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (at g 0 c)))
        (if (not (= v 0)) v 0)))))

title: Solid Rectangle From Corners
written_solution: Each color marks the four corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Fill the full rectangle, including its interior, with that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
 ;; A color whose four cells sit EXACTLY at its bbox corners gets the whole
 ;; bbox FILLED with that color; every other color's cells are dropped.
 ;; (Colors iterate in first-appearance order — overlap paint order matters.)
 (let ((colors (remove-duplicates
                (map third (filter (lambda (cell) (!= (third cell) 0))
                                   (grid-cells g))))))
   (for/fold ((out (empty-grid h w 0))) ((color (in-list colors)))
     (let* ((cells (find-color g color))
            (bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
            (corners (list (list (first bb) (second bb))
                           (list (first bb) (fourth bb))
                           (list (third bb) (second bb))
                           (list (third bb) (fourth bb)))))
       (if (and (= (length cells) 4)
                (all? (lambda (p) (member? p corners)) cells))
           (paint-cells out
                        (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb)
                                           (third bb) (fourth bb))
                        color)
           out)))))

title: Remove Isolated Cells
written_solution: Keep a nonzero cell only if at least one 4-connected cell has the same color. Delete isolated singletons.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
             ([r (in-range (rows g))]
              [c (in-range (cols g))])
    (let ((v (at g r c)))
      (if (and (not (= v 0))
               (any? (lambda (d)
                       (let ((nr (+ r (first d))) (nc (+ c (second d))))
                         (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                              (= (at g nr nc) v))))
                     cardinal-deltas))
          (set-cell out r c v)
          out))))

title: Anti-Diagonal Mirror Add
written_solution: Reflect every nonzero cell across the anti-diagonal and add the reflected copy. If a reflected position is already filled, leave it as it is.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
    (lambda (r c)
      (let ((v (at g r c))
            (ref (at g (- (rows g) 1 c) (- (cols g) 1 r))))
        (if (and (= v 0) (not (= ref 0))) ref v)))))

title: Ordered Marker Polyline
written_solution: For each color separately, sort its markers in row-major order and connect consecutive markers with horizontal-then-vertical Manhattan segments in the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (step-range a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (reverse (range b (+ a 1)))))
    (define (trace points)
      (if (empty? points)
          (list)
          (let loop ([remaining (rest points)] [prev (first points)] [out (list (first points))])
            (if (empty? remaining)
                (reverse (foldl (lambda (p acc) (if (member p acc) acc (cons p acc))) (list) (reverse out)))
                (let* ((next (first remaining))
                       (r1 (first prev)) (c1 (second prev))
                       (r2 (first next)) (c2 (second next))
                       (hpart (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c)) (rest (step-range c1 c2))))
                       (vpart (map (lambda (r) (list r c2)) (rest (step-range r1 r2)))))
                  (loop (rest remaining) next (append out hpart vpart)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (trace (find-color g color)))])
        (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) color)
            acc)))))

title: Selector Crop By Color
written_solution: The top-left cell selects a target color. Keep only cells of that color and crop the result to its tight bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((selector (at g 0 0))
         (cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (and (= (first p) 0) (= (second p) 0))))
                        (find-color g selector)))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
    (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb))))

title: Checkerboard Interior Fill
written_solution: Find the hollow rectangular frame. Read the two seed colors inside it and fill the entire interior as a checkerboard anchored so the top-left interior cell matches the left seed.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= (obj-size obj) 8)
             (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (let* ((frame (first (filter rect-border? (objects g 0))))
           (bb (obj-bbox frame))
           (interior (filter (lambda (cell)
                               (let ((v (third cell)))
                                 (and (not (= v 0))
                                      (> (first cell) (first bb))
                                      (< (first cell) (third bb))
                                      (> (second cell) (second bb))
                                      (< (second cell) (fourth bb)))))
                             (grid-cells g)))
           (a (third (first interior)))
           (b (third (second interior)))
           (with-border (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells frame) (obj-color frame))))
      (for*/fold ([out with-border])
                 ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]
                  [c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
        (set-cell out r c
                  (if (= (modulo (+ (- r (+ (first bb) 1)) (- c (+ (second bb) 1))) 2) 0) a b))))))

title: Command Rotate Crop
written_solution: Ignore the command cell in the top-left. Crop the remaining nonzero object tightly, then rotate it according to the command: 1 → id, 2=90° clockwise, 3=180°, 4=270° clockwise.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd (at g 0 0))
         (base (set-cell g 0 0 0))
         (cropped (crop-to-content base)))
    (cond [(= cmd 1) cropped]
          [(= cmd 2) (rotate-cw cropped)]
          [(= cmd 3) (rotate-180 cropped)]
          [else (rotate-ccw cropped)])))

title: Border Equality Matrix
written_solution: Build an output matrix from the first column and first row. At each interior position, write the row label if it equals the column label; otherwise write 0.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((out-h (- (rows g) 1))
        (out-w (- (cols g) 1)))
    (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((rv (at g (+ r 1) 0))
              (cv (at g 0 (+ c 1))))
          (if (= rv cv) rv 0))))))

title: Rectangle Strip By Area
written_solution: Extract all solid monochrome rectangles, sort them by area ascending (breaking ties by color), and place their cropped rectangles left to right with a one-column gap between consecutive pieces.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define items (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (obj-size obj) (obj-color obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))) (filter solid-rect? (objects g 0))) (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))) (define crops (map third items)) (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops))) (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1)))) (let pack ((remaining crops) (left 0) (out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0))) (if (empty? remaining) out (let* ((crop (first remaining)) (next (for*/fold ((acc out)) ((r (in-range (rows crop))) (c (in-range (cols crop)))) (let ((v (at crop r c))) (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc))))) (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols crop) 1) next))))))

written_solution: For each color separately, sort its markers in row-major order and connect consecutive markers with horizontal-then-vertical Manhattan segments in the same color.

                (let* ((next (first remaining))

title: Center Template In Frames
written_solution: Extract the non-frame shape made of 2s, normalize it to its own bbox, then place a centered copy inside each hollow frame. Recolor the copied template to the frame’s color and keep the frames.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= (obj-size obj) 8)
             (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)))
    (define (floor-half x)
      (if (>= x 0) (quotient x 2) (- 0 (quotient (+ (- 0 x) 1) 2))))
    (define (center-stamp out templ frame)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox frame))
             (tbb (bbox-of-cells templ))
             (th (+ (- (third tbb) (first tbb)) 1))
             (tw (+ (- (fourth tbb) (second tbb)) 1))
             (ih (- (obj-h frame) 2))
             (iw (- (obj-w frame) 2))
             (sr (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1 (floor-half (- ih th))))
             (sc (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1 (floor-half (- iw tw)))))
        (paint-cells out
                     (map (lambda (p) (list (+ sr (first p)) (+ sc (second p)))) templ)
                     (obj-color frame))))
    (let* ((source (first (filter (lambda (obj) (not (rect-border? obj))) (objects (keep-only g 2) 0))))
           (templ (normalize (obj-cells source)))
           (frames (filter rect-border?
                           (flatmap (lambda (color) (objects (keep-only g color) 0))
                                    (filter (lambda (color) (not (= color 2))) (grid-colors g 0))))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([frame (in-list frames)])
        (center-stamp (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) (obj-color frame)) templ frame)))))

title: Select Rotate And Stamp
written_solution: Use the top-left cell to choose which source component color to keep. Use the top-right command to rotate that selected component. Normalize the rotated component and center a recolored copy inside every hollow frame, using each frame’s color for the copy.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (>= (obj-size obj) 8)
             (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)))
    (define (transform cells cmd)
      (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (raw (map (lambda (p)
                         (let ((r (first p)) (c (second p)))
                           (cond [(= cmd 2) (list c (- h 1 r))]
                                 [(= cmd 3) (list (- h 1 r) (- w 1 c))]
                                 [(= cmd 4) (list (- w 1 c) r)]
                                 [else (list r c)])))
                       cells))
             (rbb (bbox-of-cells raw)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first rbb)) (- (second p) (second rbb)))) raw)))
    (define (floor-half x)
      (if (>= x 0) (quotient x 2) (- 0 (quotient (+ (- 0 x) 1) 2))))
    (define (center-stamp out templ frame)
      (let* ((tbb (bbox-of-cells templ))
             (th (+ (- (third tbb) (first tbb)) 1))
             (tw (+ (- (fourth tbb) (second tbb)) 1))
             (ih (- (obj-h frame) 2))
             (iw (- (obj-w frame) 2))
             (sr (+ (obj-r1 frame) 1 (floor-half (- ih th))))
             (sc (+ (obj-c1 frame) 1 (floor-half (- iw tw)))))
        (paint-cells out
                     (map (lambda (p) (list (+ sr (first p)) (+ sc (second p)))) templ)
                     (obj-color frame))))
    (let* ((sel (at g 0 0))
           (cmd (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))
           (source (first (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (not (member (list 0 0) (obj-cells obj))))
                                        (objects (keep-only g sel) 0))
                                (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
           (templ (transform (normalize (obj-cells source)) cmd))
           (colors (filter (lambda (color) (and (not (= color sel)) (not (= color cmd)))) (grid-colors g 0)))
           (frames (filter rect-border? (flatmap (lambda (color) (objects (keep-only g color) 0)) colors))))
      (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([frame (in-list frames)])
        (center-stamp (paint-cells out (obj-cells frame) (obj-color frame)) templ frame)))))

title: Normalized Shape Intersection
written_solution: Crop the red(2) shape and the green(3) shape to their own bounding boxes and align both at the top-left. Output only the cells occupied in both normalized shapes, colored cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (normalize cells)
      (let ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
        (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells)))
    (let* ((comp2 (first (sort (objects (keep-only g 2) 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
           (comp3 (first (sort (objects (keep-only g 3) 0) (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
           (n2 (normalize (obj-cells comp2)))
           (n3 (normalize (obj-cells comp3)))
           (pts (sort (filter (lambda (p) (member p n3)) n2)
                      (lambda (a b) (if (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)) (< (first a) (first b)))))))
      (if (empty? pts)
          (list (list 0))
          (paint-cells (empty-grid (+ (apply max (map first pts)) 1)
                                   (+ (apply max (map second pts)) 1)
                                   0)
                         pts
                         8)))))

title: Hole-Count Legend Recolor
written_solution: The first three nonzero cells in the top row give the output colors for components with 0, 1, and 2 holes. Recolor every component below the legend according to its hole count.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (components-lower)
      (define visited (make-hash))
      (define comps (list))
      (for* ([r (in-range 1 (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
        (when (and (not (= (at g r c) 0))
                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
          (define queue (list (list r c)))
          (define cells (list))
          (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
          (define (bfs)
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (define p (first queue))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons p cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                (when (and (>= nr 1)
                           (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                           (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
              (bfs)))
          (bfs)
          (set! comps (cons (reverse cells) comps))))
      (reverse comps))
    (define (hole-count cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          0
          (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
                 (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
                 (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
                 (solid (make-hash))
                 (visited (make-hash))
                 (holes 0))
            (for ([p (in-list cells)])
              (hash-set! solid (cons (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb))) #t))
            (for* ([r (in-range h)] [c (in-range w)])
              (when (and (not (hash-has-key? solid (cons r c)))
                         (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
                (let ((queue (list (list r c)))
                      (touch (or (= r 0) (= c 0) (= r (- h 1)) (= c (- w 1)))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
                  (define (bfs0)
                    (unless (empty? queue)
                      (define p (first queue))
                      (set! queue (rest queue))
                      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                        (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                        (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                        (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                   (not (hash-has-key? solid (cons nr nc)))
                                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                          (when (or (= nr 0) (= nc 0) (= nr (- h 1)) (= nc (- w 1)))
                            (set! touch #t))
                          (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                          (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
                      (bfs0)))
                  (bfs0)
                  (when (not touch) (set! holes (+ holes 1))))))
            holes)))
    (let* ((legend (take (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (first g)) 3))
           (base (set-cell (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) 0 0 (at g 0 0)))
           (with-legend (foldl (lambda (c acc) (set-cell acc 0 c (at g 0 c))) base (range 1 (cols g)))))
      (for/fold ([out with-legend]) ([cells (in-list (components-lower))])
        (let* ((holes (hole-count cells))
               (color (list-ref legend (min holes 2))))
          (paint-cells out cells color))))))

title: Manhattan Tie Cells In Frame
written_solution: Keep the frame and the two seeds. Inside the frame, color every cell whose Manhattan distance to the first seed equals its Manhattan distance to the second seed with maroon(9).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rect-border? obj)
      (let* ((bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
             (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
             (border-size (- (* h w) (* (max 0 (- h 2)) (max 0 (- w 2))))))
        (and (= (obj-size obj) border-size)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (first bb)) (= (first p) (third bb))
                         (= (second p) (second bb)) (= (second p) (fourth bb))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (let* ((frame (first (filter rect-border? (objects g 0))))
           (bb (obj-bbox frame))
           (fcolor (obj-color frame))
           (seeds (filter (lambda (cell)
                            (let ((r (first cell)) (c (second cell)) (v (third cell)))
                              (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v fcolor))
                                   (not (= r 0)) (not (= c 0))
                                   (not (= r (- (rows g) 1))) (not (= c (- (cols g) 1))))))
                          (grid-cells g)))
           (a (first seeds))
           (b (second seeds))
           (with-seeds (paint-cells (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells frame) fcolor)
                                    (list a b))))
      (for*/fold ([out with-seeds])
                 ([r (in-range (+ (first bb) 1) (third bb))]
                  [c (in-range (+ (second bb) 1) (fourth bb))])
        (if (or (and (= r (first a)) (= c (second a)))
                (and (= r (first b)) (= c (second b))))
            out
            (if (= (+ (abs (- r (first a))) (abs (- c (second a))))
                   (+ (abs (- r (first b))) (abs (- c (second b)))))
                (set-cell out r c 9)
                out))))))

title: Rotate Then Flip
written_solution: Ignore the two command cells in the top corners. Crop the remaining object, rotate it according to the left command (1 → id, 2=90° clockwise, 3=180°, 4=270° clockwise), then flip it according to the right command (1 → flip vertical across a horizontal axis, 2 → flip horizontal across a vertical axis).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd-rot (at g 0 0))
         (cmd-flip (at g 0 (- (cols g) 1)))
         (base (set-cell (set-cell g 0 0 0) 0 (- (cols g) 1) 0))
         (cropped (crop-to-content base))
         (rotated (cond [(= cmd-rot 1) cropped]
                        [(= cmd-rot 2) (rotate-cw cropped)]
                        [(= cmd-rot 3) (rotate-180 cropped)]
                        [else (rotate-ccw cropped)])))
    (if (= cmd-flip 1) (flip-ud rotated) (flip-lr rotated))))

title: Hole-Sorted Component Strip
written_solution: Extract the disconnected nonzero components, sort them by hole count ascending and then by area ascending, crop each one tightly, and place the cropped components left to right with one zero column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (components-all)
      (define visited (make-hash))
      (define comps (list))
      (for* ([r (in-range (rows g))] [c (in-range (cols g))])
        (when (and (not (= (at g r c) 0))
                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
          (define color (at g r c))
          (define queue (list (list r c)))
          (define cells (list))
          (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
          (define (bfs)
            (unless (empty? queue)
              (define p (first queue))
              (set! queue (rest queue))
              (set! cells (cons p cells))
              (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 0))
                           (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
              (bfs)))
          (bfs)
          (set! comps (cons (list color (reverse cells)) comps))))
      (reverse comps))
    (define (hole-count cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          0
          (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
                 (h (+ (- (third bb) (first bb)) 1))
                 (w (+ (- (fourth bb) (second bb)) 1))
                 (solid (make-hash))
                 (visited (make-hash))
                 (holes 0))
            (for ([p (in-list cells)])
              (hash-set! solid (cons (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb))) #t))
            (for* ([r (in-range h)] [c (in-range w)])
              (when (and (not (hash-has-key? solid (cons r c)))
                         (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons r c))))
                (let ((queue (list (list r c)))
                      (touch (or (= r 0) (= c 0) (= r (- h 1)) (= c (- w 1)))))
                  (hash-set! visited (cons r c) #t)
                  (define (bfs0)
                    (unless (empty? queue)
                      (define p (first queue))
                      (set! queue (rest queue))
                      (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
                        (define nr (+ (first p) (first d)))
                        (define nc (+ (second p) (second d)))
                        (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                   (not (hash-has-key? solid (cons nr nc)))
                                   (not (hash-has-key? visited (cons nr nc))))
                          (when (or (= nr 0) (= nc 0) (= nr (- h 1)) (= nc (- w 1)))
                            (set! touch #t))
                          (hash-set! visited (cons nr nc) #t)
                          (set! queue (append queue (list (list nr nc))))))
                      (bfs0)))
                  (bfs0)
                  (when (not touch) (set! holes (+ holes 1))))))
            holes)))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (item)
                   (let* ((color (first item))
                          (cells (second item))
                          (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)))
                     (list (hole-count cells)
                           (length cells)
                           color
                           (subgrid g (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))))
                 (components-all))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                    [(not (= (second a) (second b))) (< (second a) (second b))]
                    [else (< (third a) (third b))]))))
    (define crops (map fourth items))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [left 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((crop (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                         (let ((v (at crop r c)))
                           (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols crop) 1) next))))))

title: Polyline Intersections Highlighted
written_solution: Sort each color’s markers in row-major order and trace a horizontal-then-vertical Manhattan polyline through them. Color normal path cells with their path color, but recolor any cell used by two or more different paths to maroon(9).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (step-range a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (reverse (range b (+ a 1)))))
    (define (trace points)
      (if (empty? points)
          (list)
          (let loop ([remaining (rest points)] [prev (first points)] [out (list (first points))])
            (if (empty? remaining)
                (reverse (foldl (lambda (p acc) (if (member p acc) acc (cons p acc))) (list) (reverse out)))
                (let* ((next (first remaining))
                       (r1 (first prev)) (c1 (second prev))
                       (r2 (first next)) (c2 (second next))
                       (hpart (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c)) (rest (step-range c1 c2))))
                       (vpart (map (lambda (r) (list r c2)) (rest (step-range r1 r2)))))
                  (loop (rest remaining) next (append out hpart vpart)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
      (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (trace (find-color g color)))])
        (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) color)
            (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 9))))))

title: Keep only the endcaps of each vertical run
written_solution: For each contiguous vertical run of a non-background color, keep only its topmost and bottommost cells; erase the interior of the run.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (paint-col c out)
      (let loop ([r 0] [acc out])
        (cond [(>= r (rows g)) acc]
              [(= (at g r c) 0) (loop (+ r 1) acc)]
              [else
               (let* ((color (at g r c))
                      (r2 (let find-end ([rr r])
                            (if (and (< (+ rr 1) (rows g)) (= (at g (+ rr 1) c) color))
                                (find-end (+ rr 1))
                                rr)))
                      (next (set-cell (set-cell acc r c color) r2 c color)))
                 (loop (+ r2 1) next))])))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([c (in-range (cols g))])
      (paint-col c out))))

title: Erase globally unique colors
written_solution: Count each non-background color across the whole grid. Any color that appears exactly once disappears; colors that appear two or more times stay where they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((counts (color-frequency g)))
    (map-grid g
      (lambda (r c v)
        (if (and (not (= v 0)) (> (hash-ref counts v 0) 1)) v 0)))))

title: Turn solid rectangles into checkerboards
written_solution: Every solid monochrome rectangle becomes a checkerboard on its own bbox, keeping the rectangle color on alternating cells and turning the other cells black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
            ([obj (in-list (filter filled? (objects g 0)))])
    (for*/fold ([acc out])
               ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]
                [c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))])
      (if (= (modulo (+ (- r (obj-r1 obj)) (- c (obj-c1 obj))) 2) 0)
          (set-cell acc r c (obj-color obj))
          acc))))

title: Turn odd rectangles into pluses
written_solution: Each solid odd-by-odd rectangle is replaced by the plus made from its center row and center column, using the same color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
            ([obj (in-list (filter filled? (objects g 0)))])
    (if (and (= (modulo (- (obj-r2 obj) (obj-r1 obj)) 2) 0)
             (= (modulo (- (obj-c2 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) 2) 0))
        (let ((rm (quotient (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) 2))
              (cm (quotient (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) 2)))
          (paint-cells
           (paint-cells out
                        (for/list ([c (in-range (obj-c1 obj) (+ (obj-c2 obj) 1))]) (list rm c))
                        (obj-color obj))
           (for/list ([r (in-range (obj-r1 obj) (+ (obj-r2 obj) 1))]) (list r cm))
           (obj-color obj)))
        out)))

title: Fill the center of each hollow odd frame
written_solution: Keep every hollow odd-by-odd frame and add a single cell of the same color at its exact center.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj))
             (w (obj-w obj))
             (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2)))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
             (= (obj-size obj) perim)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                         (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (filter frame? (objects g 0)))])
      (if (and (= (modulo (- (obj-r2 obj) (obj-r1 obj)) 2) 0)
               (= (modulo (- (obj-c2 obj) (obj-c1 obj)) 2) 0))
          (set-cell out
                    (quotient (+ (obj-r1 obj) (obj-r2 obj)) 2)
                    (quotient (+ (obj-c1 obj) (obj-c2 obj)) 2)
                    (obj-color obj))
          out))))

title: Each plus becomes an X
written_solution: Every 5-cell plus shape is replaced by the 5-cell X shape centered at the same cell and colored the same way.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
             ([r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((v (at g r c)))
      (if (and (not (= v 0))
               (= (at g (- r 1) c) v)
               (= (at g (+ r 1) c) v)
               (= (at g r (- c 1)) v)
               (= (at g r (+ c 1)) v))
          (paint-cells out
                       (list (list r c) (list (- r 1) (- c 1)) (list (- r 1) (+ c 1))
                             (list (+ r 1) (- c 1)) (list (+ r 1) (+ c 1)))
                       v)
          out))))

title: Each X becomes a plus
written_solution: Every 5-cell X shape is replaced by the 5-cell plus shape centered at the same cell and colored the same way.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
             ([r (in-range 1 (- (rows g) 1))]
              [c (in-range 1 (- (cols g) 1))])
    (let ((v (at g r c)))
      (if (and (not (= v 0))
               (= (at g (- r 1) (- c 1)) v)
               (= (at g (- r 1) (+ c 1)) v)
               (= (at g (+ r 1) (- c 1)) v)
               (= (at g (+ r 1) (+ c 1)) v))
          (paint-cells out
                       (list (list r c) (list (- r 1) c) (list (+ r 1) c)
                             (list r (- c 1)) (list r (+ c 1)))
                       v)
          out))))

title: Fill the room that contains each seed
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. In each enclosed chamber, a colored seed expands to fill every black(0) cell in that chamber, while the walls stay gray(5).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (room-cells sr sc)
      (let ((visited (make-hash)))
        (let bfs ([queue (list (list sr sc))] [acc (list)])
          (if (empty? queue)
              (reverse acc)
              (let* ((p (first queue))
                     (r (first p))
                     (c (second p))
                     (restq (rest queue)))
                (cond [(hash-has-key? visited p) (bfs restq acc)]
                      [(not (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))) (bfs restq acc)]
                      [(and (not (and (= r sr) (= c sc))) (not (= (at g r c) 0))) (bfs restq acc)]
                      [else
                       (hash-set! visited p #t)
                       (bfs (append restq
                                    (map (lambda (d) (list (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)))) cardinal-deltas))
                            (cons p acc))]))))))
    (fold-cells g g
      (lambda (out r c v)
        (if (or (= v 0) (= v 5))
            out
            (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list (room-cells r c))])
              (if (= (at g (first p) (second p)) 0)
                  (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) v)
                  acc)))))))

title: Keep only the median-area object
written_solution: Find all connected objects and compare their areas. Keep only the object whose area is the median one; erase the smaller and larger objects.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((indexed (map (lambda (pair)
                         (let ((i (first pair)) (obj (second pair)))
                           (list (obj-size obj) i obj)))
                       (enumerate-list (objects g 0))))
         (ranked (sort indexed
                       (lambda (a b)
                         (if (= (first a) (first b))
                             (< (second a) (second b))
                             (< (first a) (first b))))))
         (keep (third (list-ref ranked (quotient (length ranked) 2)))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells keep) (obj-color keep))))

title: Crop the object with exactly one hole
written_solution: Among all connected objects, select the one that encloses exactly one hole and output just that object cropped to its tight bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((obj (find-first (lambda (o) (= (topo-count-holes g o 0) 1)) (objects g 0))))
    (if (eq? obj #f) (grid (list 0)) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))))

title: Pack objects left-to-right by color
written_solution: Crop every object to its own bbox, sort the cropped objects by color value from smallest to largest, then pack them left-to-right with one background column between neighbors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define crops
      (map (lambda (obj) (subgrid g (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj)))
           (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b))))))
    (define out-h (apply max (map rows crops)))
    (define out-w (+ (apply + (map cols crops)) (max 0 (- (length crops) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining crops] [c0 0] [out (empty-grid out-h out-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((crop (first remaining))
                 (next (for*/fold ([acc out])
                                   ([r (in-range (rows crop))]
                                    [c (in-range (cols crop))])
                         (let ((v (at crop r c)))
                           (if (= v 0) acc (set-cell acc r (+ c0 c) v))))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ c0 (cols crop) 1) next))))))

title: Recolor objects by prime vs composite area
written_solution: For each connected object, compute its area. Prime-area objects become red(2); composite-area objects become cyan(8). The shapes stay the same.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (prime? n)
      (and (>= n 2)
           (let loop ([i 2])
             (cond [(> (* i i) n) #t]
                   [(= (modulo n i) 0) #f]
                   [else (loop (+ i 1))]))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (if (prime? (obj-size obj)) 2 8)))))

title: Draw rectangle borders from matching corner markers
written_solution: Each color appears exactly twice, and the two cells of a color are opposite corners of a rectangle. Draw only that rectangle’s border in that color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 2)
          (let* ((a (first cells))
                 (b (second cells))
                 (r0 (min (first a) (first b)))
                 (r1 (max (first a) (first b)))
                 (c0 (min (second a) (second b)))
                 (c1 (max (second a) (second b))))
            (paint-cells out
                         (remove-duplicates
                          (append (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c0))
                                  (for/list ([r (in-range r0 (+ r1 1))]) (list r c1))
                                  (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r0 c))
                                  (for/list ([c (in-range c0 (+ c1 1))]) (list r1 c))))
                         color))
          out))))

title: Stamp transformed templates at the markers
written_solution: The small template above the gray(5) separator row is copied below. Marker blue(1) → identity, red(2) → 90° clockwise, green(3) → 180°, yellow(4) → 90° counter-clockwise; stamp the chosen transform centered on each marker.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define sep (first (filter (lambda (r) (all? (lambda (v) (= v 5)) (row g r))) (range 0 (rows g)))))
    (define top (subgrid g 0 0 (- sep 1) (- (cols g) 1)))
    (define cells (filter (lambda (p) (not (= (at top (first p) (second p)) 0))) (grid-positions top)))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
    (define template (subgrid top (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
    (define out-h (- (rows g) sep 1))
    (define (transform marker)
      (cond [(= marker 1) template]
            [(= marker 2) (rotate-cw template)]
            [(= marker 3) (rotate-180 template)]
            [(= marker 4) (transpose template)]
            [else template]))
    (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid out-h (cols g) 0)])
               ([r (in-range (+ sep 1) (rows g))]
                [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((marker (at g r c)))
        (if (member marker (list 1 2 3 4))
            (let* ((tr (transform marker))
                   (rr0 (- (- r (+ sep 1)) (quotient (rows tr) 2)))
                   (cc0 (- c (quotient (cols tr) 2))))
              (for*/fold ([acc out])
                         ([i (in-range (rows tr))]
                          [j (in-range (cols tr))])
                (let ((rr (+ rr0 i)) (cc (+ cc0 j)) (v (at tr i j)))
                  (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr cc out-h (cols g)))
                      (set-cell acc rr cc v)
                      acc))))
            out)))))

title: Route one shortest path through ordered waypoints
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Starting at 1, route a shortest path that visits 2, then 3, then 4, and finally reaches 6. Paint the traversed background cells cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (pos-of color) (first (find-color g color)))
    (define (path-between src dst)
      (define queue (list src))
      (define prev (make-hash))
      (hash-set! prev src #f)
      (define (search)
        (unless (or (empty? queue) (hash-has-key? prev dst))
          (define cur (first queue))
          (set! queue (rest queue))
          (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
            (define nr (+ (first cur) (first d)))
            (define nc (+ (second cur) (second d)))
            (define p (list nr nc))
            (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                       (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
