                        [(= control 2) (rotate shape 1)]
                        [(= control 3) (rotate shape 2)]
                        [else (reflect-v shape)]))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list trans)])
      (let ((r (+ (first anchor) (first p)))
            (c (+ (second anchor) (second p))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
                 (not (member? (at out r c) (list 6 1 2 3 4))))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Fill the band selected by the number of dots
written_solution: The grid contains nested rectangular frames made of blue(1). Count the red(2) dots. If there are k dots, fill the k-th band from the outside inward with cyan(8): inside frame k, but outside the next inner frame if one exists.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell<? a b)
      (or (< (first a) (first b))
          (and (= (first a) (first b)) (< (second a) (second b)))))
    (define (border-cells obj)
      (filter (lambda (p) (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                              (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
              (positions-in-rect (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
    (define frames
      (sort (filter (lambda (o) (and (= (obj-color o) 1)
                                     (equal? (sort (obj-cells o) cell<?) (sort (border-cells o) cell<?))))
                    (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b) (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b))))))
    (define idx (- (length (find-color g 2)) 1))
    (define selected (list-ref frames idx))
    (define inner (and (< (+ idx 1) (length frames)) (list-ref frames (+ idx 1))))
    (for*/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (+ (obj-r1 selected) 1) (obj-r2 selected))]
                          [c (in-range (+ (obj-c1 selected) 1) (obj-c2 selected))])
      (if (and (= (at out r c) 0)
               (or (not inner)
                   (not (and (>= r (obj-r1 inner)) (<= r (obj-r2 inner))
                             (>= c (obj-c1 inner)) (<= c (obj-c2 inner))))))
          (set-cell out r c 8)
          out))))

title: Keep cells present in exactly two normalized shapes
written_solution: Normalize the blue(1), red(2), and green(3) shapes to their own top-left corners. Output the cells that appear in exactly two of those three normalized shapes.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((s1 (normalize-cells (find-color g 1)))
         (s2 (normalize-cells (find-color g 2)))
         (s3 (normalize-cells (find-color g 3)))
         (union (remove-duplicates (append s1 s2 s3)))
         (exact2 (filter (lambda (p)
                           (= (+ (if (member? p s1) 1 0)
                                 (if (member? p s2) 1 0)
                                 (if (member? p s3) 1 0))
                              2))
                         union)))
    (if (empty? exact2)
        (empty-grid 1 1 0)
        (let* ((norm (normalize-cells exact2))
               (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm))))
               (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c) (if (member? (list r c) norm) 8 0)))))))

title: Voronoi-color the maze by distance to the seeds
written_solution: Gray(5) cells are walls. For every reachable black(0) cell, compare its shortest-path distance to the red(2) seed(2) and the green(3) seed(3). Color cells closer to the red(2) seed cyan(8), cells closer to the green(3) seed yellow(4), and leave ties black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((a (first (find-color g 2)))
         (b (first (find-color g 3))))
    (define (dist-from start)
      (define dist (make-hash))
      (define queue (list (cons (first start) (second start))))
      (hash-set! dist (first queue) 0)
      (let bfs ([fuel 0])
        (unless (empty? queue)
          (let ((cur (first queue)))
            (set! queue (rest queue))
            (for ([d (in-list cardinal-deltas)])
              (let ((nr (+ (car cur) (first d))) (nc (+ (cdr cur) (second d))))
                (when (and (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
                           (not (= (at g nr nc) 5))
                           (not (hash-has-key? dist (cons nr nc))))
                  (hash-set! dist (cons nr nc) (+ (hash-ref dist cur) 1))
                  (set! queue (append queue (list (cons nr nc))))))))
          (bfs (+ fuel 1))))
      dist)
    (define da (dist-from a))
    (define db (dist-from b))
    (grid-from-fn (rows g) (cols g)
      (lambda (r c)
        (if (and (= (at g r c) 0)
                 (hash-has-key? da (cons r c))
                 (hash-has-key? db (cons r c)))
            (cond [(< (hash-ref da (cons r c)) (hash-ref db (cons r c))) 8]
                  [(< (hash-ref db (cons r c)) (hash-ref da (cons r c))) 4]
                  [else 0])
            (at g r c))))))

title: Transform the shape, then translate it by the marker vector
written_solution: Take the magenta(6) object and normalize it. The control color selects the transform: blue(1) → identity, yellow(4) → flip horizontal, orange(7) → 180°, maroon(9) → flip vertical. The vector from red(2) marker to green(3) marker tells where to place the transformed copy relative to the original object's top-left corner. Draw the copy in cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rot90 cells)
      (let ((h (+ 1 (apply max (map first cells)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (second p) (- h 1 (first p)))) cells))))
    (define (rotate cells k)
      (let loop ([i 0] [cur (normalize-cells cells)])
        (if (= i (modulo k 4)) cur (loop (+ i 1) (rot90 cur)))))
    (define (reflect-h cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (h (+ 1 (apply max (map first norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (- h 1 (first p)) (second p))) norm))))
    (define (reflect-v cells)
      (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
             (w (+ 1 (apply max (map second norm)))))
        (normalize-cells (map (lambda (p) (list (first p) (- w 1 (second p)))) norm))))
    (define shape (find-color g 6))
    (define p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
    (define p3 (first (find-color g 3)))
    (define control (first (filter (lambda (color) (not (empty? (find-color g color)))) (list 1 4 7 9))))
    (define trans (cond [(= control 1) (normalize-cells shape)]
                        [(= control 4) (reflect-v shape)]
                        [(= control 7) (rotate shape 2)]
                        [else (reflect-h shape)]))
    (define bb (bbox-of-cells shape))
    (define dr (- (first p3) (first p2)))
    (define dc (- (second p3) (second p2)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([p (in-list trans)])
      (let ((r (+ (first bb) dr (first p)))
            (c (+ (second bb) dc (second p))))
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (= (at out r c) 0))
            (set-cell out r c 8)
            out)))))

title: Complete red T-tetrominoes into green rectangles
written_solution: Find every red(2) component that is exactly a T-tetromino: four cells whose normalized shape is a T in some rotation. Replace that whole 2x3 or 3x2 bbox with green(3). Leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (cell-count cells pred)
      (count-where pred cells))
    (define (t-tetromino? obj)
      (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
             (bb (obj-bbox obj))
             (r0 (first bb))
             (c0 (second bb))
             (r1 (third bb))
             (c1 (fourth bb))
             (height (+ (- r1 r0) 1))
             (width (+ (- c1 c0) 1)))
        (and (= (obj-color obj) 2)
             (= (obj-size obj) 4)
             (or
               (and (= height 2) (= width 3)
                    (or
                      (and (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (fst p) r0))) 3)
                           (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (fst p) r1))) 1)
                           (any? (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) r1) (= (snd p) (+ c0 1)))) cells))
                      (and (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (fst p) r1))) 3)
                           (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (fst p) r0))) 1)
                           (any? (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) r0) (= (snd p) (+ c0 1)))) cells))))
               (and (= height 3) (= width 2)
                    (or
                      (and (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (snd p) c0))) 3)
                           (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (snd p) c1))) 1)
                           (any? (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (+ r0 1)) (= (snd p) c1))) cells))
                      (and (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (snd p) c1))) 3)
                           (= (cell-count cells (lambda (p) (= (snd p) c0))) 1)
                           (any? (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (+ r0 1)) (= (snd p) c0))) cells))))))))
    (paint-cells
      g
      (flatmap
        (lambda (obj)
          (if (t-tetromino? obj)
              (let ((bb (obj-bbox obj)))
                (positions-in-rect (first bb) (second bb) (third bb) (fourth bb)))
              (list)))
        (objects g 0))
      3)))

title: Bridge matching endpoints into straight segments
written_solution: For each color that appears exactly twice, if the two cells lie in the same row or the same column and every cell between them is background, fill the whole segment between them with that color. Leave all other cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-color? color colors)
      (any? (lambda (v) (= v color)) colors))
    (define (color-order remaining acc)
      (if (empty? remaining)
          (reverse acc)
          (let ((v (third (first remaining))))
            (if (or (= v 0) (has-color? v acc))
                (color-order (cdr remaining) acc)
                (color-order (cdr remaining) (cons v acc))))))
    (paint-cells
      g
      (flatmap
        (lambda (color)
          (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
            (if (= (length cells) 2)
                (let* ((a (first cells))
                       (b (second cells))
                       (r1 (fst a))
                       (c1 (snd a))
                       (r2 (fst b))
                       (c2 (snd b)))
                  (cond
                    [(= r1 r2)
                     (let ((cmin (min c1 c2))
                           (cmax (max c1 c2)))
                       (if (all? (lambda (c) (= (cell-at g r1 c) 0)) (range (+ cmin 1) cmax))
                           (map (lambda (c) (list r1 c color)) (range cmin (+ cmax 1)))
                           (list)))]
                    [(= c1 c2)
                     (let ((rmin (min r1 r2))
                           (rmax (max r1 r2)))
                       (if (all? (lambda (r) (= (cell-at g r c1) 0)) (range (+ rmin 1) rmax))
                           (map (lambda (r) (list r c1 color)) (range rmin (+ rmax 1)))
                           (list)))]
                    [else (list)]))
                (list))))
        (color-order (grid-cells g) (list))))))

title: Recolor orange components that touch exactly one border
written_solution: Inspect each orange(7) component. If it touches exactly one of the four outer borders of the grid, recolor the entire component to cyan(8). Components touching zero borders or two or more borders stay orange(7).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (paint-cells
    g
    (flatmap
      (lambda (obj)
        (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj))
               (touches
                 (+ (if (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) 0)) cells) 1 0)
                    (if (any? (lambda (p) (= (fst p) (- h 1))) cells) 1 0)
                    (if (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) 0)) cells) 1 0)
                    (if (any? (lambda (p) (= (snd p) (- w 1))) cells) 1 0))))
          (if (and (= (obj-color obj) 7) (= touches 1)) cells (list))))
      (objects g 0))
    8))

title: Turn isolated red seeds into green diagonal Xs
written_solution: Every red(2) component of size 1 is a seed. Replace the seed and its four diagonal neighbors with green(3), clipping at the grid border. Larger red(2) components are distractors and stay as they are.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((seeds
          (map
            (lambda (obj) (first (obj-cells obj)))
            (filter (lambda (obj) (and (= (obj-color obj) 2) (= (obj-size obj) 1))) (objects g 0)))))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (or (= v 0) (= v 2))
                   (any?
                     (lambda (p)
                       (let ((dr (abs (- r (fst p))))
                             (dc (abs (- c (snd p)))))
                         (or (and (= dr 0) (= dc 0))
                             (and (= dr 1) (= dc 1)))))
                     seeds))
              3
              v))))))

title: Extract the smallest object
written_solution: Find the smallest non-background component in the input. Output only that object cropped to its own bbox, preserving its original color and shape.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-cell? cell cells)
      (any? (lambda (p) (and (= (fst p) (fst cell)) (= (snd p) (snd cell)))) cells))
    (let* ((objs
             (sort
               (objects g 0)
               (lambda (a b)
                 (let ((sa (obj-size a))
                       (sb (obj-size b))
                       (ba (obj-bbox a))
                       (bb (obj-bbox b)))
                   (or (< sa sb)
                       (and (= sa sb)
                            (or (< (first ba) (first bb))
                                (and (= (first ba) (first bb))
                                     (< (second ba) (second bb))))))))))
           (target (first objs))
           (cells (normalize-cells (obj-cells target)))
           (out-h (+ (max-list (map fst cells)) 1))
           (out-w (+ (max-list (map snd cells)) 1))
           (color (obj-color target)))
      (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
        (lambda (r c)
          (if (has-cell? (list r c) cells) color 0))))))

title: Fill the missing corner of each red rectangle
written_solution: The red(2) cells come in groups of three that mark three corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Add the missing fourth corner as green(3). Existing red(2) corners stay red(2).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((reds (find-color g 2)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (= v 0)
                   (any?
                     (lambda (rr)
                       (and (not (= rr r))
                            (any?
                              (lambda (cc)
                                (and (not (= cc c))
                                     (= (cell-at g r cc) 2)
                                     (= (cell-at g rr c) 2)
                                     (= (cell-at g rr cc) 2)))
                              (range w))))
                     (range h)))
              3
              v))))))

title: Fill the centers of hollow yellow 3x3 rings
written_solution: Whenever a 3x3 window contains a yellow(4) ring—eight yellow(4) cells around a single empty center—fill the center with cyan(8). Other yellow(4) patterns stay unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (cellmap g (r c v)
    (if (and (zero? v)
             (< 0 r (- h 1))
             (< 0 c (- w 1))
             (all? (lambda (d)
                     (= (at g (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d))) 4))
                   (append cardinal-deltas diagonal-deltas)))
        8
        v)))

title: Rotate a template according to the control cell and stamp it at the anchor
written_solution: Read the first rotation control value in the top row: 1 → identity, 2 → 90° clockwise, 3 → 180°, and 4 → 270 degrees. Take the first connected red(2) component in row-major order as the template, normalize and rotate it, then stamp it in green(3) with its top-left corner on the cyan(8) anchor. The output is otherwise background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (rotate-by cells code)
      (cond
        [(= code 2) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw cells))]
        [(= code 3) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw cells)))]
        [(= code 4) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw cells))))]
        [else (normalize-cells cells)]))
    (let* (;; The first top-row value in 1..4 is the rotation code.
           (control-hit (find-first (lambda (v) (member? v (list 1 2 3 4))) (row-at g 0)))
           (control (if control-hit control-hit 1))
           ;; The first cyan cell is the top-left anchor of the output stamp.
           (anchor (first (find-color g 8)))
           ;; Select the first red object in row-major object order.  When the
           ;; control is red(2), its top-row singleton is deliberately first.
           (template (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))
           (shape (rotate-by (normalize-cells (obj-cells template)) control)))
      ;; Stamp only the rotated template in green; every other cell is blank.
      (grid-from-fn h w
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((hit
                  (find-first
                    (lambda (p)
                      (and (= r (+ (fst anchor) (fst p)))
                           (= c (+ (snd anchor) (snd p)))))
                    shape)))
            (if hit 3 0)))))))

title: Draw the Manhattan ring selected by the control value
written_solution: The first top-row control value in {1,2,3} gives a Manhattan radius k. Use the first red(2) cell in row-major order as the seed, which may be the top-row control when it is 2. Mark every zero or red(2) cell at Manhattan distance exactly k from that seed with cyan(8), leaving other distractor colors unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define k
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (v) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3))) (row-at g 0))))
        (if hit hit 1)))
    (define seed (first (find-color g 2)))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
          (if (and (or (= v 0) (= v 2))
                   (= (+ (abs (- r (fst seed))) (abs (- c (snd seed)))) k))
              8
              v))))))

title: Draw rectangle borders from matching corner markers
written_solution: Each color that appears exactly twice marks opposite corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Draw that rectangle's border in the same color. Colors that do not appear exactly twice are distractors.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-color? color colors)
      (any? (lambda (c) (= c color)) colors))
    (define (color-order cells acc)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (reverse acc)
          (let ((v (third (first cells))))
            (if (or (= v 0) (has-color? v acc))
                (color-order (cdr cells) acc)
                (color-order (cdr cells) (cons v acc))))))
    (define colors (color-order (grid-cells g) (list)))
    (define (rect-for color)
      (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
        (if (= (length cells) 2)
            (let* ((a (first cells))
                   (b (second cells))
                   (r0 (min (fst a) (fst b)))
                   (r1 (max (fst a) (fst b)))
                   (c0 (min (snd a) (snd b)))
                   (c1 (max (snd a) (snd b))))
              (if (and (not (= r0 r1)) (not (= c0 c1)))
                  (list color r0 c0 r1 c1)
                  #f))
            #f)))
    (define rects (filter (lambda (x) x) (map rect-for colors)))
    (define (on-border? r c rect)
      (let ((r0 (second rect)) (c0 (third rect)) (r1 (fourth rect)) (c1 (nth rect 4)))
        (and (>= r r0) (<= r r1) (>= c c0) (<= c c1)
             (or (= r r0) (= r r1) (= c c0) (= c c1)))))
    (define (border-color r c)
      (foldl
        (lambda (rect acc)
          (if (on-border? r c rect) (first rect) acc))
        #f
        rects))
    (grid-from-fn h w
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((bc (border-color r c)))
          (if bc bc (cell-at g r c)))))))

title: Connect the two chamber markers with a shortest path
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Find the shortest 4-neighbor path from the red(2) marker to the green(3) marker without crossing walls, and color the intermediate path cells cyan(8). Keep the endpoints and the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (parent-of p parents)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (entry) (same-pos? p (first entry))) parents)))
        (if hit (second hit) #f)))
    (define (reconstruct goal parents)
      (let loop ((cur goal) (acc (list)))
        (let ((prev (parent-of cur parents)))
          (if prev (loop prev (cons cur acc)) (cons cur acc)))))
    (define (shortest-path start goal)
      (let loop ((visited (list)) (queue (list start)) (parents (list (list start #f))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            (list)
            (let ((cur (first queue)) (restq (cdr queue)))
              (cond
                [(pos-in? cur visited) (loop visited restq parents)]
                [(same-pos? cur goal) (reconstruct goal parents)]
                [else
                 (let* ((new-visited (cons cur visited))
                        (neighbors
                          (filter
                            (lambda (n)
                              (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
                                (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                     (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                     (not (pos-in? n new-visited))
                                     (not (pos-in? n restq)))))
                            (map
                              (lambda (d) (list (+ (fst cur) (fst d)) (+ (snd cur) (snd d))))
                              cardinal-deltas))))
                   (loop new-visited
                         (append restq neighbors)
                         (append parents (map (lambda (n) (list n cur)) neighbors))))])))))

    (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
           (goal (first (find-color g 3)))
           (path (shortest-path start goal))
           (interior
             (filter
               (lambda (p) (not (or (same-pos? p start) (same-pos? p goal))))
               path)))
      (grid-from-fn h w
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
            (if (and (= v 0) (pos-in? (list r c) interior)) 8 v)))))))

title: Pack objects into a row sorted by area
written_solution: Extract every non-background component, crop each one to its own bbox, and place the cropped pieces left to right in descending order of component area, separated by one background column. Preserve each object's original color and shape.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (and (= (fst p) (fst q)) (= (snd p) (snd q)))) cells))
    (define objs
      (sort (objects g 0)
        (lambda (a b)
          (cond
            [(> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) #t]
            [(< (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) #f]
            [(< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) #t]
            [(> (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) #f]
            [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))
    (define (total-width xs)
      (cond [(empty? xs) 0]
            [(empty? (cdr xs)) (obj-w (first xs))]
            [else (+ (obj-w (first xs)) 1 (total-width (cdr xs)))]))
    (define (placements xs x acc)
      (if (empty? xs)
          (reverse acc)
          (placements (cdr xs) (+ x (obj-w (first xs)) 1) (cons (list (first xs) x) acc))))
    (if (empty? objs)
        (list (list 0))
        (let* ((out-h (max-list (map obj-h objs)))
               (out-w (total-width objs))
               (placed (placements objs 0 (list))))
          (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((hit
                      (find-first
                        (lambda (entry)
                          (let* ((obj (first entry))
                                 (x (second entry))
                                 (lr r)
                                 (lc (- c x)))
                            (and (>= lc 0) (< lc (obj-w obj)) (< lr (obj-h obj))
                                 (has-cell? (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) lr) (+ (obj-c1 obj) lc)) (obj-cells obj)))))
                        placed)))
                (if hit (obj-color (first hit)) 0))))))))

title: Output the normalized XOR of the red and blue shapes
written_solution: Take the normalized red(2) shape and the normalized blue(1) shape. Compute their symmetric difference (cells that belong to exactly one of the shapes) and render that result as a minimal cyan(8) output grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define (render cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (list (list 0))
          (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
                 (bb (bbox-of-cells norm))
                 (out-h (+ 1 (third bb)))
                 (out-w (+ 1 (fourth bb))))
            (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
              (lambda (r c) (if (has-cell? (list r c) norm) 8 0))))))
    (let* ((blue (normalize-cells (obj-cells (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))))

(rule!

title: Connect checkpoints 1→2→3→4 through the maze
written_solution: Walls are gray(5). Connect checkpoint 1 to red(2), then 2 to green(3), then 3 to yellow(4) using shortest 4-neighbor paths through non-wall cells. Paint the intermediate route cells cyan(8), keeping the numbered checkpoints and the walls unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))

    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (parent-of p parents)
      (let ((hit (find-first (lambda (entry) (same-pos? p (first entry))) parents)))
        (if hit (second hit) #f)))
    (define (reconstruct goal parents)
      (let loop ((cur goal) (acc (list)))
        (let ((prev (parent-of cur parents)))
          (if prev
              (loop prev (cons cur acc))
              (cons cur acc)))))
    (define (shortest-path start goal)
      (let loop ((visited (list))
                 (queue (list start))
                 (parents (list (list start #f))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            (list)
            (let ((cur (first queue))
                  (restq (cdr queue)))
              (cond
                [(pos-in? cur visited) (loop visited restq parents)]
                [(same-pos? cur goal) (reconstruct goal parents)]
                [else
                 (let* ((new-visited (cons cur visited))
                        (r (fst cur))
                        (c (snd cur))
                        (neighbors
                          (filter
                            (lambda (n)
                              (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
                                (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w)
                                     (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5))
                                     (not (pos-in? n new-visited))
                                     (not (pos-in? n restq)))))
                            (map
                              (lambda (d) (list (+ r (fst d)) (+ c (snd d))))
                              cardinal-deltas))))
                   (loop new-visited
                         (append restq neighbors)
                         (append parents (map (lambda (n) (list n cur)) neighbors))))])))))

    (define (interior path start goal)
      (filter
        (lambda (p) (not (or (same-pos? p start) (same-pos? p goal))))
        path))
    (let* ((p1 (first (find-color g 1)))
           (p2 (first (find-color g 2)))
           (p3 (first (find-color g 3)))
           (p4 (first (find-color g 4)))
           (segments (list (list p1 p2) (list p2 p3) (list p3 p4)))
           (path-cells
             (flatmap
               (lambda (seg)
                 (let* ((start (first seg))
                        (goal (second seg))
                        (path (shortest-path start goal)))
                   (if (empty? path) (list) (interior path start goal))))
               segments)))
      (grid-from-fn h w
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
            (if (and (= v 0) (pos-in? (list r c) path-cells)) 8 v)))))))

title: Fill the selected band between nested frames
written_solution: The red(2) dots in the top row encode a band number k. Detect the nested rectangular yellow(4) frames. Fill the k-th band from the outside inward with cyan(8): band 1 is between the outermost and next frame, and the last band is the interior of the innermost frame.

(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (area obj)
      (* (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)))
    (define (frame-perimeter obj)
      (- (+ (* 2 (obj-h obj)) (* 2 (obj-w obj))) 4))

      (let ((r (first p))
            (c (second p))
            (r1 (first bbox))
            (c1 (second bbox))
            (r2 (third bbox))
            (c2 (fourth bbox)))
        (or (= r r1) (= r r2) (= c c1) (= c c2))))
    (define (rect-frame? obj)
      (let ((bbox (obj-bbox obj)))
        (and (= (obj-color obj) 4)

      (sort
        (filter rect-frame? (objects g 0))
        (lambda (a b)

              [(> aa ab) #t]
              [(< aa ab) #f]
              [(< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) #t]
              [(> (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)) #f]
              [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))])))))
    (define k (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 2)) (row-at g 0)))
    (if (or (empty? frames) (< k 1) (> k (length frames)))
        g
        (let* ((target (nth frames (- k 1)))
               (inner (if (< k (length frames)) (nth frames k) #f))
               (tr1 (obj-r1 target))
               (tc1 (obj-c1 target))
               (tr2 (obj-r2 target))
               (tc2 (obj-c2 target)))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
                (if (and (= v 0)
                         (> r tr1) (< r tr2) (> c tc1) (< c tc2)
                         (or (not inner)
                             (not (and (> r (obj-r1 inner)) (< r (obj-r2 inner))
                                       (> c (obj-c1 inner)) (< c (obj-c2 inner))))))
                    8
                    v))))))))

title: Rotate the blue shape, then apply the selected boolean op
written_solution: Read the first two nonzero cells in the top row as operation and rotation controls. The operation control selects 3 → union, 4 → intersection, 6 → xor, 7 → red(2)-minus-blue(1); any other operation marker defaults to xor. The rotation control selects 1 → identity, 2=90 degrees, 3=180°, 4=270 degrees; missing or invalid rotation defaults to identity. Take the first red(2) component and first blue(1) component in row-major order, normalize them, rotate the blue(1) component, apply the operation, and render the result as a minimal cyan(8) grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (has-cell? p cells)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) cells))
    (define (rotate-by cells code)
      (cond
        [(= code 2) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw cells))]
        [(= code 3) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw cells)))]
        [(= code 4) (normalize-cells (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw (rotate-cells-cw cells))))]
        [else (normalize-cells cells)]))
    (define (render cells)
      (if (empty? cells)
          (list (list 0))
          (let* ((norm (normalize-cells cells))
                 (bb (bbox-of-cells norm))
                 (out-h (+ 1 (third bb)))
                 (out-w (+ 1 (fourth bb))))
            (grid-from-fn out-h out-w
              (lambda (r c) (if (has-cell? (list r c) norm) 8 0))))))
    (let* ((nz (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row-at g 0)))
           (op-raw (if (empty? nz) 6 (first nz)))
           (rot-raw (if (> (length nz) 1) (second nz) 1))
           (op (if (member? op-raw (list 3 4 6 7)) op-raw 6))
           (rot-code (if (member? rot-raw (list 1 2 3 4)) rot-raw 1))
           (red-obj (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 2)) (objects g 0))))
           (blue-obj (first (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) 1)) (objects g 0))))
           (red (normalize-cells (obj-cells red-obj)))
           (blue (rotate-by (normalize-cells (obj-cells blue-obj)) rot-code))
           (result
             (cond
               [(= op 3) (append red (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p red))) blue))]
               [(= op 4) (filter (lambda (p) (has-cell? p blue)) red)]
               [(= op 6)
                (append
                  (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p blue))) red)
                  (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p red))) blue))]
               [else (filter (lambda (p) (not (has-cell? p blue))) red)])))
      (render result))))

title: Trace the mirror beam
written_solution: The source cell encodes the starting direction: 1 → up, 2 → right, 3 → down, 4 → left. A slash mirror 6 reflects the beam like '/', and a backslash mirror 7 reflects it like '\\'. Trace the beam until it leaves the grid, hits a gray(5) wall, or repeats a state, and color the traversed background cells cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (same-state? a b)
      (and (= (first a) (first b)) (= (second a) (second b))
           (= (third a) (third b)) (= (fourth a) (fourth b))))
    (define (pos-in? p lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-pos? p q)) lst))
    (define (state-in? s lst)
      (any? (lambda (q) (same-state? s q)) lst))
    (define (dir-for v)
      (cond [(= v 1) (list -1 0)] [(= v 2) (list 0 1)]
            [(= v 3) (list 1 0)] [else (list 0 -1)]))
    (define (slash d)
      (list (- 0 (snd d)) (- 0 (fst d))))
    (define (backslash d)
      (list (snd d) (fst d)))
    (define start-cell
      (find-first
        (lambda (p)
          (let ((v (third p))) (or (= v 1) (= v 2) (= v 3) (= v 4))))
        (grid-cells g)))
    (if (not start-cell)
        g
        (let* ((sr (first start-cell))
               (sc (second start-cell))
               (dir (dir-for (third start-cell)))
               (path
                 (let loop ((r sr) (c sc) (d dir) (seen (list)) (acc (list)))
                   (let ((state (list r c (fst d) (snd d))))
                     (if (state-in? state seen)
                         (reverse acc)
                         (let* ((nr (+ r (fst d)))
                                (nc (+ c (snd d))))
                           (if (not (in-bounds? nr nc h w))
                               (reverse acc)
                               (let ((cell (cell-at g nr nc)))
                                 (if (= cell 5)
                                     (reverse acc)
                                     (let ((next-dir (cond [(= cell 6) (slash d)]
                                                           [(= cell 7) (backslash d)]
                                                           [else d])))
                                       (loop nr nc next-dir (cons state seen) (cons (list nr nc) acc))))))))))))
          (grid-from-fn h w
            (lambda (r c)
              (let ((v (cell-at g r c)))
                (if (and (= v 0) (pos-in? (list r c) path)) 8 v))))))))

title: Mark the cells that lie on every shortest path
written_solution: Walls are gray(5); start is red(2); goal is green(3). Mark every cell that lies on at least one shortest path from start to goal through non-wall cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (same-pos? a b)
      (and (= (fst a) (fst b)) (= (snd a) (snd b))))
    (define (record-of p records)
      (find-first (lambda (rec) (same-pos? p (first rec))) records))
    (define (set-record-count p new-count records)
      (map
        (lambda (rec)
          (if (same-pos? p (first rec))
              (list (first rec) (second rec) new-count)
              rec))
        records))
    (define (neighbors p)
      (filter
        (lambda (n)
          (let ((nr (fst n)) (nc (snd n)))
            (and (in-bounds? nr nc h w) (not (= (cell-at g nr nc) 5)))))
        (map (lambda (d) (list (+ (fst p) (fst d)) (+ (snd p) (snd d)))) cardinal-deltas)))
    (define (dist-count start)
      (let loop ((queue (list start)) (records (list (list start 0 1))))
        (if (empty? queue)
            records
            (let* ((cur (first queue))
                   (restq (cdr queue))
                   (cur-rec (record-of cur records))
                   (cur-dist (second cur-rec))
                   (cur-count (third cur-rec)))
              (let update ((ns (neighbors cur)) (q restq) (recs records))
                (if (empty? ns)
                    (loop q recs)
                    (let* ((n (first ns))
                           (nd (+ cur-dist 1))
                           (hit (record-of n recs)))
                      (cond
                        [(not hit)
                         (update (cdr ns) (append q (list n)) (append recs (list (list n nd cur-count))))]
                        [(= (second hit) nd)
                         (update (cdr ns) q (set-record-count n (+ (third hit) cur-count) recs))]
                        [else (update (cdr ns) q recs)]))))))))
    (let* ((start (first (find-color g 2)))
           (goal (first (find-color g 3)))
           (from-start (dist-count start))
           (from-goal (dist-count goal))
           (goal-rec (record-of goal from-start)))
      (if (not goal-rec)
          g
          (let ((D (second goal-rec))
                (total (third goal-rec)))
            (grid-from-fn h w
              (lambda (r c)
                (let* ((v (cell-at g r c))
                       (p (list r c))
                       (rs (record-of p from-start))
                       (rg (record-of p from-goal)))
                  (if (and (= v 0) rs rg (= (+ (second rs) (second rg)) D)
                           (= (* (third rs) (third rg)) total))
                      8
                      v)))))))))

title: Fill Matching Border Lines Inside the Frame
written_solution: Identify the main rectangular frame. For each marker color, if that color appears on opposite left and right border cells in the same row, fill the interior row segment; if it appears on opposite top and bottom border cells in the same column, fill that interior column segment. At crossings of a filled row and filled column, colors paint in ascending order (columns then rows within a color), so the highest color wins.

  ;; ends of an interior row (its left AND right border cell) fills that row inside the frame;

  ;; ASCENDING order (columns then rows within each color), so crossings resolve to the highest
  ;; color deterministically.

         (r1 (first b)) (c1 (second b)) (r2 (third b)) (c2 (fourth b))
         (border (append (map (lambda (r) (at g r c1)) (range r1 (+ r2 1)))
                         (map (lambda (r) (at g r c2)) (range r1 (+ r2 1)))

        values
        (for/list ((name (in-list transform-names)))

            (if (and (= (rows ta) (rows b)) (= (cols ta) (cols b)))

title: Alternating Seed Rays
written_solution: The top row provides a two-color palette. Keep the input as-is, then from the unique seed cell draw rays up, down, left, and right. Color the first step with the first legend color, the second step with the second legend color, then repeat that two-color cycle until the border.

(rule!
  (let* ((palette (take (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0)) 2))
         (seed (first (find-color g 9))))
    (define dirs (list (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1)))
    (define (draw-dir out d)
      (let walk ([acc out]
                 [r (+ (first seed) (first d))]
                 [c (+ (second seed) (second d))]
                 [step 0])
        (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))

            acc)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([d (in-list dirs)])
      (draw-dir out d))))

title: Fill the Gap
written_solution: On each row, find colors that appear exactly twice. Fill every cell between the left and right occurrence of that color, inclusive, with that same color. Leave all other rows and cells unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; Rows are independent; inspect each foreground color in the original row.
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([r (in-range (rows g))])
    (for/fold ([acc out]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors (list (row g r)) 0))])
      ;; Exactly two occurrences define the inclusive horizontal fill span.
      (let ((cols-hit (for/list ([c (in-range (cols g))] #:when (= (at g r c) color)) c)))
        (if (= (length cols-hit) 2)
            (paint-cells acc
              (for/list ([c (in-range (apply min cols-hit) (+ (apply max cols-hit) 1))])
                (list r c))
              color)
            acc)))))

title: Mirror Across the Guide
written_solution: Find the full-width guide row made of a single non-background color. Copy every nonzero cell above that guide to the symmetric position below it, preserving color. Keep the original cells and the guide row.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((guide-row
         (first (filter (lambda (r)
                          (let ((vals (remove-duplicates (row g r))))
                            (and (= (length vals) 1) (not (= (first vals) 0)))))
                        (range 0 (rows g))))))
    (for*/fold ([out g])
               ([r (in-range guide-row)]
                [c (in-range (cols g))])
      (let ((v (at g r c))
            (rr (- (* 2 guide-row) r)))
        (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr c (rows g) (cols g)))
            (set-cell out rr c v)
            out)))))

title: Crop the Action
written_solution: Crop the grid to the tight bbox of all non-background cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (crop-to-content g))

title: Fourth Corner
written_solution: For each color, the input gives three of the four corners of an axis-aligned rectangle. Add the missing fourth corner of that same color and leave everything else unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
    (let ((cells (find-color g color)))
      (if (= (length cells) 3)
          (let* ((bb (bbox-of-cells cells))
                 (corners (list (list (first bb) (second bb))
                                (list (first bb) (fourth bb))
                                (list (third bb) (second bb))
                                (list (third bb) (fourth bb))))
                 (missing (filter (lambda (p) (not (member p cells))) corners)))
            (if (= (length missing) 1)
                (paint-cells out missing color)
                out))
          out))))

title: Commanded Trail
written_solution: The command cell encodes a direction: 1 up, 2 down, 3 left, 4 right. Starting from the unique non-command colored seed, extend that seed color in the commanded direction until the border. Keep the command and seed cells.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((cmd-cell (last (filter (lambda (cell) (member (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4)))
                                 (grid-cells g))))
         (seed-cell (last (filter (lambda (cell)
                                    (and (not (= (third cell) 0))
                                         (not (member (third cell) (list 1 2 3 4)))))
                                  (grid-cells g))))
         (code (third cmd-cell))
         (color (third seed-cell))
         (delta (cond [(= code 1) (list -1 0)]
                      [(= code 2) (list 1 0)]
                      [(= code 3) (list 0 -1)]
                      [else (list 0 1)])))
    (let walk ([out g]
               [r (+ (first seed-cell) (first delta))]
               [c (+ (second seed-cell) (second delta))])
      (if (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g))
          (walk (if (= (at out r c) 0) (set-cell out r c color) out)
                (+ r (first delta))
                (+ c (second delta)))
          out))))

title: Keep the Largest
written_solution: Find all nonzero connected components and keep only the largest one. Replace every other nonzero cell with black(0).
program_solution:
(rule!
  ;; 4-connected components (excluding background)
  (let* ((objs (objects g 0))
         (best (first (sort objs
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (cond [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))
                                     (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                    [(not (= (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b)))
                                     (< (obj-r1 a) (obj-r1 b))]
                                    [else (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b))]))))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells best) (obj-color best))))

title: Room-Limited Weave
written_solution: The top row gives a two-color palette and the frame walls are blue(1). Starting at the seed, draw alternating-color rays in the four cardinal directions, but only through the interior chamber reachable from the seed without crossing the frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((palette (take (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0)) 2))
         (seed (first (find-color g 9)))
         (mask (connected-region g (first seed) (second seed)
                 (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 1))) 4)))
    (define dirs (list (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1)))
    (define (draw-dir out d)
      (let walk ([acc out]
                 [r (+ (first seed) (first d))]
                 [c (+ (second seed) (second d))]
                 [step 0])
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (member (list r c) mask))
            (let ((next (if (= (at acc r c) 0)
                            (set-cell acc r c (nth palette (modulo step (length palette))))
                            acc)))
              (walk next (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)) (+ step 1)))
            acc)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([d (in-list dirs)])
      (draw-dir out d))))

title: Chamber Paint
written_solution: Each non-frame marker sits inside a chamber bounded by blue(1) walls. Flood fill that chamber with the marker’s color, keeping the frame intact. Do this independently for every chamber.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([marker (in-list (filter (lambda (cell)
                                                  (not (member (third cell) (list 0 1))))
                                                (grid-cells g)))])
    (let* ((color (third marker))
           (region (connected-region g (first marker) (second marker)
                     (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 1))) 4)))
      (paint-cells out region color))))

title: Legend Select Crop
written_solution: Read the top-left legend color. Among the remaining components, select the component of that color, crop it to its tight bbox, and output that normalized crop.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((target (at g 0 0))
         (source (set-cell g 0 0 0))
         (objs (filter (lambda (obj) (= (obj-color obj) target)) (objects source 0)))
         (chosen (first (sort objs (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b)))))))
    (grid-from-fn (obj-h chosen) (obj-w chosen)
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((p (list (+ (obj-r1 chosen) r) (+ (obj-c1 chosen) c))))
          (if (member p (obj-cells chosen)) (obj-color chosen) 0))))))

title: Commanded Transform
written_solution: Interpret the top-left code as a geometric transform, apply that transform to the nonzero object elsewhere in the grid, and output the transformed object cropped to its bbox.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((code (at g 0 0)))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (apply-cmd (crop-to-content (set-cell g 0 0 0)) code)))

title: Holes Decide the Color
written_solution: For each component, count the number of enclosed holes in its shape. Recolor the whole component according to that count: no holes becomes one color, one hole becomes another, and so on. Keep the geometry unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (let* ((holes (topo-count-holes g obj 0))
           (color (cond [(= holes 0) 3]
                        [(= holes 1) 4]
                        [(= holes 2) 5]
                        [else 6])))
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) color))))

title: Area Comparison Table
written_solution: Order the three components from left to right. Build a square matrix whose diagonal is a fixed self-comparison value and whose off-diagonal cells indicate whether the row object has larger area than the column object.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (< (obj-c1 a) (obj-c1 b)))))
         (n (length objs)))
    (grid-from-fn n n
      (lambda (r c)
        (let ((a (obj-size (nth objs r)))
              (b (obj-size (nth objs c))))
          (cond [(= r c) 2]
                [(> a b) 5]
                [else 0]))))))

title: Template Copies
written_solution: Extract the non-9 template from the top-left of the input. Keep the original template and stamp identical copies with their top-left corner anchored at every 9 marker location.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((markers (find-color g 9))
         (non9 (remove-color g 9 0))
         (template (crop-to-content non9))
         (bb (bbox-of-cells (filter-cells non9 (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 0))))))
         (positions (cons (list (first bb) (second bb)) markers)))
    (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
               ([pos (in-list positions)]
                [r (in-range (rows template))]
                [c (in-range (cols template))])
      (let ((v (at template r c))
            (rr (+ (first pos) r))
            (cc (+ (second pos) c)))
        (if (and (not (= v 0)) (in-bounds? rr cc (rows g) (cols g)))
            (set-cell out rr cc v)
            out)))))

title: Eight-Way Room Weave
written_solution: Read the three-color legend on the top row. From the seed, draw rays in all eight directions, cycling through the legend colors step by step, and clip the result to the chamber inside the frame.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((palette (take (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (row g 0)) 3))
         (seed (first (find-color g 9)))
         (mask (connected-region g (first seed) (second seed)
                 (lambda (r c v) (not (= v 1))) 4)))
    (define dirs (list (list -1 0) (list 1 0) (list 0 -1) (list 0 1)
                       (list -1 -1) (list -1 1) (list 1 -1) (list 1 1)))
    (define (draw-dir out d)
      (let walk ([acc out]
                 [r (+ (first seed) (first d))]
                 [c (+ (second seed) (second d))]
                 [step 0])
        (if (and (in-bounds? r c (rows g) (cols g)) (member (list r c) mask))
            (let ((next (if (= (at acc r c) 0)
                            (set-cell acc r c (nth palette (modulo step (length palette))))
                            acc)))
              (walk next (+ r (first d)) (+ c (second d)) (+ step 1)))
            acc)))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([d (in-list dirs)])
      (draw-dir out d))))

title: Transform Analogy
written_solution: Split the input into three panels. Infer which geometric transform maps panel A’s object to panel B’s object, then apply that same transform to panel C and output the transformed object cropped tight.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (define (zero-col? grid c)
      (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(zero-col? grid c) (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid)) (zero-col? grid stop))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (let* ((panels (map crop-to-content (split-panels g)))
           (a (first panels))
           (b (second panels))
           (c (third panels))
           (code (first (filter (lambda (k) (equal? (crop-to-content (apply-cmd a k)) b))
                                (range 1 8)))))
      (crop-to-content (apply-cmd c code)))))

title: Depth-Colored Frames
written_solution: The input contains nested rectangular frame components. Recolor the outermost frame with one color, the next frame inward with the next color, and continue by depth while keeping the frame geometry unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((objs (sort (objects g 0)
                     (lambda (a b)
                       (> (* (obj-h a) (obj-w a)) (* (obj-h b) (obj-w b)))))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)])
              ([obj (in-list objs)]
               [i (in-naturals 0)])
      (paint-cells out (obj-cells obj) (+ 2 i)))))

title: Path Overlap
written_solution: For each color, connect its two terminals using the fixed Manhattan L-path rule. Paint each path in its own color, but any cell used by more than one path becomes the overlap color.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (sorted-cells cells)
      (sort cells (lambda (a b)
                    (if (= (first a) (first b))
                        (< (second a) (second b))
                        (< (first a) (first b))))))
    (define (range-inclusive a b)
      (if (<= a b) (range a (+ b 1)) (range a (- b 1) -1)))
    (define (l-path a b)
      (append
        (for/list ([c (in-list (range-inclusive (second a) (second b)))])
          (list (first a) c))
        (for/list ([r (in-list (range-inclusive (+ (first a) (if (<= (first a) (first b)) 1 -1))
                                                (first b)))])
          (list r (second b)))))
    (define paths
      (for/list ([color (in-list (grid-colors g 0))])
        (let* ((pts (sorted-cells (find-color g color)))
               (cells (l-path (first pts) (second pts))))
          (list color cells))))
    (define all-path-cells (apply append (map second paths)))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([path (in-list paths)])
      (let ((color (first path))
            (cells (second path)))
        (for/fold ([acc out]) ([p (in-list cells)])
          (set-cell acc (first p) (second p)
                    (if (> (count-where (lambda (q) (equal? q p)) all-path-cells) 1)
                        8
                        color)))))))

title: Transform Code Tiling
written_solution: Extract the template from the left panel. For each command in the right-hand code matrix, transform the template accordingly and place the result in the matching tile position of the output grid.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (define (zero-col? grid c)
      (all? (lambda (r) (= (at grid r c) 0)) (range 0 (rows grid))))
    (define (split-panels grid)
      (let loop ([c 0] [panels (list)])
        (cond [(>= c (cols grid)) (reverse panels)]
              [(zero-col? grid c) (loop (+ c 1) panels)]
              [else
               (let scan ([stop c])
                 (if (or (>= stop (cols grid)) (zero-col? grid stop))
                     (loop (+ stop 1)
                           (cons (subgrid grid 0 c (- (rows grid) 1) (- stop 1)) panels))
                     (scan (+ stop 1))))])))
    (let* ((parts (split-panels g))
           ;; Crop to the non-background bounding box
           (template (crop-to-content (first parts)))
           (codes (second parts))
           (th (rows template))
           (tw (cols template)))
      (for*/fold ([out (empty-grid (* (rows codes) th) (* (cols codes) tw) 0)])
                 ([rr (in-range (rows codes))]
                  [cc (in-range (cols codes))]
                  [r (in-range th)]
                  [c (in-range tw)])
        ;; Crop to the non-background bounding box
        (let* ((tf (crop-to-content (apply-cmd template (at codes rr cc))))
               (v (at tf r c)))
          (if (not (= v 0))
              (set-cell out (+ (* rr th) r) (+ (* cc tw) c) v)
              out))))))

title: Sort by Holes and Pack
written_solution: For each component, count its holes, crop it to a tight bbox, and then sort the components by increasing hole count. Pack the normalized shapes left to right with one background column between them.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (norm obj)
      (grid-from-fn (obj-h obj) (obj-w obj)
        (lambda (r c)
          (let ((p (list (+ (obj-r1 obj) r) (+ (obj-c1 obj) c))))
            (if (member p (obj-cells obj)) (obj-color obj) 0)))))
    (define items
      (sort (map (lambda (obj) (list (topo-count-holes g obj 0) (obj-size obj) (norm obj)))
                 (objects g 0))
            (lambda (a b)
              (cond [(not (= (first a) (first b))) (< (first a) (first b))]
                    [else (< (second a) (second b))]))))
    (define max-h (apply max (map (lambda (item) (rows (third item))) items)))
    (define total-w (+ (apply + (map (lambda (item) (cols (third item))) items))
                       (max 0 (- (length items) 1))))
    (let pack ([remaining items] [left 0] [out (empty-grid max-h total-w 0)])
      (if (empty? remaining)
          out
          (let* ((shape (third (first remaining)))
                 (next-out
                  (for*/fold ([acc out])
                             ([r (in-range (rows shape))]
                              [c (in-range (cols shape))])
                    (let ((v (at shape r c)))
                      (if (not (= v 0)) (set-cell acc r (+ left c) v) acc)))))
            (pack (rest remaining) (+ left (cols shape) 1) next-out))))))

title: Remap Then Transform
written_solution: Read the top-row transform code and the aligned source-to-target color mapping in the first two rows. Recolor the object using that palette permutation, apply the commanded transform, and output the result cropped tight.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((code (at g 0 0)))
    (define (apply-cmd grid code)
      (cond [(= code 1) grid]
            [(= code 2) (rotate-cw grid)]
            [(= code 3) (rotate-180 grid)]
            [(= code 4) (rotate-ccw grid)]
            [(= code 5) (flip-lr grid)]
            [(= code 6) (flip-ud grid)]
            [else (transpose grid)]))
    (define (after-two xs) (rest (rest xs)))
    (define (lookup v pairs)
      (cond [(empty? pairs) #f]
            [(= v (first (first pairs))) (second (first pairs))]
            [else (lookup v (rest pairs))]))
    (define src (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (after-two (row g 0))))
    (define tgt (filter (lambda (v) (not (= v 0))) (after-two (row g 1))))
    (define mapping (map list src tgt))
    (define obj (crop-to-content (subgrid g 2 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))))
    (define remapped
      (grid-from-fn (rows obj) (cols obj)
        (lambda (r c)
          (let* ((v (at obj r c))
                 (hit (lookup v mapping)))
            (if (and (not (= v 0)) hit) hit v)))))
    (crop-to-content (apply-cmd remapped code))))

title: Keep Only the Boundary
written_solution: Treat each colored object separately. A cell stays if it lies on the object's boundary, meaning at least one of its four neighbors is outside the object. Interior cells are turned to black(0), so every solid rectangle becomes a hollow outline.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (paint-cells out (obj-boundary-cells obj) (obj-color obj))))

title: Fill Rectangular Frames
written_solution: Each object is a rectangular border. Detect its bbox, verify that the colored cells form the border of that box, and then fill the interior cells with cyan(8) while leaving the frame itself unchanged.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((dummy 0))
    (define (frame? obj)
      (let* ((h (obj-h obj))
             (w (obj-w obj))
             (perim (+ (* 2 w) (* 2 (- h 2)))))
        (and (>= h 3) (>= w 3)
             (= (obj-size obj) perim)
             (all? (lambda (p)
                     (or (= (first p) (obj-r1 obj)) (= (first p) (obj-r2 obj))
                         (= (second p) (obj-c1 obj)) (= (second p) (obj-c2 obj))))
                   (obj-cells obj)))))
    (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
      (if (frame? obj)
          (for/fold ([acc out])
                    ([p (in-list (positions-in-rect (+ (obj-r1 obj) 1) (+ (obj-c1 obj) 1)
                                                    (- (obj-r2 obj) 1) (- (obj-c2 obj) 1)))])
            (if (= (at acc (first p) (second p)) 0)
                (set-cell acc (first p) (second p) 8)
                acc))
          out))))

title: Crop the Smallest Object
written_solution: Among all non-zero connected components, select the one with the smallest area. Ignore the larger distractors and return only the chosen object, cropped to its own bbox.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (norm-grid obj) (let* ((cells (obj-cells obj)) (bb (bbox-of-cells cells)) (h (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb)))) (w (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb))))) (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0) (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells) cell<) (obj-color obj)))) (define best (first (sort (objects g 0) (lambda (a b) (if (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b)) (< (obj-color a) (obj-color b)) (< (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))) (norm-grid best)))

title: Mark Segment Endpoints
written_solution: For every straight line segment, keep the segment in place but recolor its endpoints. Horizontal segments use the leftmost and rightmost cells, and vertical segments use the topmost and bottommost cells.

(rule!
  (for/fold ([out g]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (cond [(and (= (obj-h obj) 1) (>= (obj-size obj) 2))
           (set-cell (set-cell out (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) 8) (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj) 8)]
          [(and (= (obj-w obj) 1) (>= (obj-size obj) 2))
           (set-cell (set-cell out (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj) 8) (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj) 8)]
          [else out])))

title: Move an Outline to the Anchor
written_solution: Find the anchor cell and the main non-anchor object. Compute the object's top-left bounding-box corner, keep only the boundary cells of the object, and translate those boundary cells so that corner aligns with the anchor. The output is otherwise background.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let* ((anchor (first (find-color g 1)))
         (comp (first (sort (filter (lambda (obj) (not (= (obj-color obj) 1))) (objects g 0))
                            (lambda (a b) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))))))
         (dr (- (first anchor) (obj-r1 comp)))
         (dc (- (second anchor) (obj-c1 comp))))
    (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([p (in-list (obj-boundary-cells comp))])
      (let ((nr (+ (first p) dr)) (nc (+ (second p) dc)))
        (if (in-bounds? nr nc (rows g) (cols g))
            (set-cell out nr nc (obj-color comp))
            out)))))

title: Mirror Dots Across the Axis
written_solution: The column of 5s is a mirror axis. Every non-zero non-axis cell gets copied to the reflected position on the other side of the axis, preserving color. Existing cells remain in place.
program_solution:
(rule!
  (let ((axis-col (first (filter (lambda (c)
                                   (all? (lambda (r) (= (at g r c) 5)) (range 0 (rows g))))
                                 (range 0 (cols g))))))
    (fold-cells g g
      (lambda (out r c v)
        (let ((mc (- (* 2 axis-col) c)))
          (if (and (not (= v 0)) (not (= v 5)) (not (= c axis-col))
                   (in-bounds? r mc (rows g) (cols g))
                   (= (at out r mc) 0))
              (set-cell out r mc v)
              out))))))

title: Bounding-Box Corners
written_solution: For each colored component, compute the minimum and maximum row and column it occupies. Paint only those four bounding-box corner cells and erase everything else.

(rule!
  (for/fold ([out (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0)]) ([obj (in-list (objects g 0))])
    (paint-cells out
                 (remove-duplicates (list (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                                          (list (obj-r1 obj) (obj-c2 obj))
                                          (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c1 obj))
                                          (list (obj-r2 obj) (obj-c2 obj))))
                 (obj-color obj))))

title: Largest Perimeter Wins
written_solution: Do not choose by area alone. Count boundary cells for each component and select the one with the largest perimeter-like boundary size. Copy only that object into a background grid and recolor it to cyan(8).

(rule!
  (let* ((best (first (sort (objects g 0)
                            (lambda (a b)
                              (cond [(not (= (length (obj-boundary-cells a)) (length (obj-boundary-cells b))))
                                     (> (length (obj-boundary-cells a)) (length (obj-boundary-cells b)))]
                                    [(not (= (obj-size a) (obj-size b))) (> (obj-size a) (obj-size b))]
                                    [else (> (obj-color a) (obj-color b))]))))))
    (paint-cells (empty-grid (rows g) (cols g) 0) (obj-cells best) 8)))

title: Fill Only Enclosed Holes
written_solution: Compute connected components of the background. Any zero-region that touches the outer border is still outside and stays black(0); any zero-region fully enclosed by colored cells is a hole and gets filled with cyan(8).
program_solution:
(rule!
  (fill-all-enclosed g 8 0))

title: Header Picks the Boundary Count
written_solution: The top row gives a target number. Compare that number to the boundary-cell counts of the body objects, choose the matching object, then crop tightly to it and keep only its boundary cells.
program_solution: (rule! (let ((dummy 0)) (define (norm-grid obj) (let* ((cells (obj-boundary-cells obj)) (bb (bbox-of-cells (obj-cells obj))) (h (+ 1 (- (third bb) (first bb)))) (w (+ 1 (- (fourth bb) (second bb))))) (paint-cells (empty-grid h w 0) (sort (map (lambda (p) (list (- (first p) (first bb)) (- (second p) (second bb)))) cells) cell<) (obj-color obj)))) (let* ((n (count-where (lambda (v) (= v 1)) (row g 0))) (body (subgrid g 1 0 (- (rows g) 1) (- (cols g) 1))) (best (find-first (lambda (obj) (= (length (obj-boundary-cells obj)) n)) (objects body 0)))) (norm-grid best))))

title: Rectangle from Diagonal Markers
written_solution: For each color, find its two marker cells. Use their rows and columns as the corners of a rectangle and paint the entire border of that rectangle in the same color.
